guide/src/content/docs/use/copying-and-m:
---
title: Copying and moving records
description: Use a saved model mapping to prepare records in another workspace and review what stays behind.
reader: steward
---

Copy records when another workspace needs its own data. Move them when the source records
should also be removed after the destination is ready. Both operations prepare change sets;
neither publishes automatically. Follow [Copy or move records to another workspace](/docs/guide/use/copy-or-move-records/).

A **model mapping** describes what source types, fields, parents and relationships become
in the destination. It can also identify existing destination records to update. Have a model
administrator prepare and check it; see [Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/).
This differs from a [mapping grid](/docs/use/mapping-grids/), which connects records inside
one workspace. Switching workspaces alone never copies records.

## Access and starting data

Open **Settings › Data operations › Copy and move**. You need access to read the source and
**Copy and move** for the destination; a move also needs **Work in change sets** for the
source deletion proposal. Review and
publication need their own workspace permissions. This page does not give you publication
rights. Background jobs and model administration must be enabled; otherwise the page explains
why copying and moving are read-only. Ask an administrator about absent workspaces or actions.

**Mappings** lists saved instructions. **Recent copies and moves** shows operations and waiting
dry runs. Check it before starting the same transfer again. The source and destination must
be different workspaces. Their model releases must match the releases used by the mapping.

## What is checked before starting

Choose **Copy** or **Move**, then the records to include: **Every mapped type**, **The whole
workspace**, **Chosen types** with optional filters, or **One record and everything under it**.
A subtree includes its descendants. A whole-workspace choice can leave out unmapped types;
read the report rather than assuming everything will transfer.

The dry run checks every selected record and relationship without writing them. Review records
created or updated, records that cannot transfer, relationships carried or dropped, and
**Values not carried**. A record can transfer while losing an unmapped field. Missing required
values, unsuitable parents, incompatible values and unresolved relationship ends need attention.
Ask the mapping owner to correct its choices; do not invent data just to pass a check.

![Copy dry run showing the two workspaces, selected scope, record counts and omissions](/docs/screens/use-copy-dry-run.png)

Changing the mapping or selection checks again. If **The mapping names other releases than
the workspaces run** appears, coordinate **Use the releases the workspaces run** with the
mapping owner, inspect the changes and obtain a fresh dry run. **Nothing to copy** or
**Nothing to move** means no selected record would be created or updated; confirmation cannot
make that empty selection useful.

## What happens after confirmation

**Copy** prepares a target change set and keeps the source. **Move** also prepares a source
deletion change set. A source record changed since the dry run, or required by records staying
behind, is kept with a reason. Publication of the source deletions is refused until the target
copy has been published. Review each proposal and its workspace's approval requirements separately.

The running job continues when you leave the page. Its actual result can differ from the dry
run after another person's changes. **Review the change set** opens the target proposal;
**Review the deletions** opens the source removal proposal where one was made. **The copy did
not complete** or **The move did not complete** needs inspection of the job and any retained
change sets before retrying. Read [Jobs](/docs/use/jobs/) for cancellation and retention;
stopping a job is not an undo of proposed chunks already written.

Copies keep their correspondence to the source. A later transfer can update the earlier copy;
a move back can update the original or recreate its original identity. Review matching decisions
and current values before repeating a transfer. This is a separate dataset, not a continuously
synchronised mirror.

## Change your mind

Before starting, cancel the confirmation to keep the dry run without loading records. After
loading, use the ordinary change-set controls to discard an unwanted proposal, after checking
for colleagues' edits. Do not publish its source deletions if you intend to retain the originals.
Once published, correcting data requires new reviewed changes; removing a saved mapping does
not reverse a transfer. Mapping changes and deletion belong to its administrator and affect
future operations, not already published copies.
guide/src/content/docs/use/appearance-an:
---
title: Appearance and devices
description: Adjust the display and use refiroo with a keyboard, touch screen or phone.
reader: steward
---

Make refiroo comfortable to read in this browser. Open **Settings › Appearance**; changes
apply immediately and need no Save button. Other browsers and devices keep their own choices.
Follow [Change how refiroo looks](/docs/guide/use/change-how-refiroo-looks/) for the steps.

## Display choices

| Setting | Choices and effect |
|---|---|
| Theme | **Current**, **Hearth**, **Studio**, **Instrument** or **Website purple** changes colours, title typeface, corners, type sizes, control height and the arrangement of the frame. Every theme works in light and dark. |
| Light or dark | **System**, **Light**, **Dark**. System follows your device's light or dark setting. |
| Table density | **Comfortable** or **Compact** sets the default; a table's own Display choice overrides it. |
| Type colours | **B: magenta and olive** or **A: plum and gold**. The palettes differ in their third and fourth colours. |
| Edit pencil | **On hover and focus** or **Always, faintly**. Touch screens always show edit hints. |

On a desktop, **Current**, **Hearth** and **Website purple** keep the applications in the top bar and lists in the sidebar. **Studio** puts the applications and lists in one side column beside a raised page. Its search remains above the page and the Live, change-set or publication band stays above the data. **Instrument** puts application tiles, Help, Inbox, Settings and your account in a narrow strip, with lists in the panel beside it. Search stays above the page; the data context appears along the bottom. Pages without search need no top bar in Instrument. On a phone, every theme uses the bar and navigation drawer.

Hearth, Studio and Instrument add short motions when surfaces open. These stop when your device requests reduced motion. A theme changes presentation; it does not change the model, records or permissions.

A table's **Display** menu controls visible columns, density, rows per page and column widths.
The identity column stays visible. These choices are remembered on this device for that view;
page size also travels in the address. **Reset display** restores its display defaults.
There is no column-reordering control in this menu.

Drag a panel's resize separator to change its width. Focus the separator and use Left/Right
for small changes, or Shift with those arrows for larger changes. Home chooses its minimum;
End chooses its maximum. Where reset is offered, Enter or double-click resets it.
**Resize record inspector** adjusts the inspection pane; **Resize record properties** adjusts
the record's properties. Availability and widths depend on the current layout.

## Keyboard operation

Opening a record collection or view puts focus on its page title; after deleting a record,
focus returns to the list heading. Tab then moves through controls with a visible focus indicator; Shift+Tab moves back. Use the skip
link at the beginning to reach the main content. Enter or Space activates a focused button.
Menus offer keyboard choices; Escape closes a menu or dialog. Enter saves a single-line inline
edit and Escape cancels it. Escape also clears the tree search or Notifications search. Dialogs keep Tab within them and
return focus when closed. Resolve an unsaved-input prompt before leaving an editor.

In a tree, Up/Down moves between visible records, Right expands or moves into children and
Left collapses or returns to the parent. Home/End reaches the first/last visible entry.
Shift+F10 opens the focused record's menu where available, as does right-click.
Use **Move to…** when dragging is inconvenient.

In tables, Up/Down moves row focus. Space toggles a focused selection checkbox; Shift extends
a range. Cmd/Ctrl+A inside a selectable table selects all matching records. Ctrl+Home and
Ctrl+End jump through long lists. These keys apply in their local controls. Press ⌘K on a Mac or Ctrl+K elsewhere to focus search. On Home it searches record names across your workspaces; within a workspace it also finds lists and places such as Settings under **Go to**. Use refiroo's search: the
browser's Find sees only drawn rows of long lists.

## On a phone or touch screen

The band beneath the top bar keeps workspace, application and Live/change-set/publication
choices within reach. Open the navigation drawer for collections. In Settings, use the
**Settings: …** toggle for the navigation and the Back link to return. Panels can stack or
use tabs rather than staying side by side. On narrow tables, **Show all … columns** reveals
extra columns and **Show fewer columns** hides them again.

Tap a record to open it. In an editable tree, hold a record still for about half a second to
start a drag; moving sooner scrolls instead. Drag near an edge to scroll. A stationary release
in the sidebar opens its node menu. Read-only and publication trees do not drag. See
[Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/) for permitted destinations.

Long text can be read on hover, focus or touch; Escape closes its full-text box. Record and
relationship labels accompany colours, and controls have accessible names. These facilities
describe how to operate the interface, rather than a guarantee for every browser or assistive
device combination.

![Appearance settings with Normal and Website purple themes, light or dark mode, density and edit hints](/docs/screens/use-appearance-themes.png)

Settings groups its pages under **You**, **Workspaces and models**, **People and access**,
**Connections** and **This instance**, with **About** last. Your permissions determine which pages and groups appear.
**Jobs** lets you inspect background work; **Import profiles** needs Bulk and import, and
**Copy and move** needs the corresponding permission. A missing navigation entry does not
grant access through a copied address. Ask an administrator about missing permissions.

![Phone application navigation drawer with collections and record search](/docs/screens/phone-navigation-drawer.png)

## Help beside your work

Choose **?** in the top bar, to the left of the bell, to open the documentation in a new tab.
The documentation and API reference share a header: the logo returns to the application,
**Documentation** and **API reference** switch between them, and the documentation has search.
The **System**, **Light** and **Dark** theme choice is shared with the application, including
other open tabs in this browser.

The initial choices are **Current**, **System**, **Comfortable**, **B: magenta and olive**
and **On hover and focus**. To return to those defaults, select them again. Clearing this
site's browser storage also loses display preferences, so keep any collection addresses you
need separately. Display preferences do not change your roles or the workspace model.
guide/src/content/docs/use/inbox-and-app:
---
title: Inbox and approvals
description: Read notifications and understand how change sets reach an approval decision.
reader: steward
---

The bell in the top bar opens your inbox. It tells you about work needing attention and results
of work you started. Approval notices lead an approver to a submitted change set.
Follow [Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/) for submitting and deciding.

## Read and manage notifications

The bell's count is the number of unread notices. Open it to see up to 20 unread notifications;
the panel indicates how many more remain. Use **See all notifications** for the rest.
**Mark all read** clears their unread state; **See all notifications** opens the full page.
You can also reach **Notifications** from the avatar menu.

![Inbox panel with unread notices, Mark all read and See all notifications](/docs/screens/use-inbox-panel.png)

*Above: Guide Admin has eight unread Batch finished notices from jobs they started.*

Notices include a change set waiting for your approval, approval or return of your submission,
a job that finished, failed or needs confirmation, and publications in workspaces you follow.
A notice is an invitation to inspect the result; a finished job may still have refused items.

![Notifications page with search, kind, workspace, read-state and sort controls](/docs/screens/use-notifications-page.png)

*Above: the reference account's notices are job results. One has been read; the others are highlighted.*

On **Notifications**, search by change set, comment, person or job. **Kind**, **Workspace** and
**Show** narrow the list; **Sort** chooses newest or oldest first. Filters cover the stored notices,
not just the rows you have scrolled to. Notices are kept for 90 days.

Opening a notice marks it read and opens its subject in the workspace it belongs to, where one
remains available. Completing a job’s confirmation also marks its notice read. A job notice
opens its state, result and items. An approval notice can remain after publication has consumed
the change set, so not every notice has an editable destination.

![A job opened from a Batch finished notice, showing its state and result](/docs/screens/use-notification-job.png)

*Above: the batch completed with 11 items already as asked and no changed items. Opening this job
marked its notice read.*

Tick notices to **Mark read**, **Mark unread** or **Delete** them. Shift selects a range; Cmd or
Ctrl adds one. **Select all** selects loaded notices, not every matching notice in storage.
At most 500 notices can be changed at once. Changing filters clears the selection.
**Delete all read…** opens **Delete all read notifications?**. Choose **Delete read
notifications** to permanently delete all your read notices, including those outside the
current filters, or **Cancel** to keep them. Unread notices and the jobs or change sets remain.
If an action fails, read the error and retry; clearing a notice does not fix its underlying job.

**Notification email settings** opens your mail choices. Where mail is configured and your account
has an email address, you can choose email notifications and their kinds. Turning mail off does
not turn off the inbox. If mail is unavailable, the settings page explains why.

![Notification email settings with mail unavailable and no followed workspaces](/docs/screens/settings-notifications.png)

*Above: mail is not configured on the reference instance, so the email choices are absent.
Workspaces I follow is empty; following starts from a workspace card on Home.*

## When a change needs approval

A workspace can require approval before publication and a different person to decide.
Administrators set these rules under [Approval policies](/docs/administer/approval-policies/).
To decide a request, you need **Approve publications**; the Data owner role includes it.
Check [Account](/docs/use/account/#what-you-can-do) for your own access.

![Workspace Approval tab with approval and second-person policy options](/docs/screens/use-approval-policy.png)

*Above: an earlier view of Graubünden’s Approval settings, with both policies off. The request
shown below uses approval with a second person required.*

With no approval requirement, people allowed to publish can do so directly. A person who prepares
work but cannot publish can submit it to an approver. When approval is required, direct publication
is available only to someone allowed to publish and approve their own work, with no second-person
requirement. That action records their approval as it publishes.

## From submission to decision

**Submit for publication** validates the change set and records its submitted version. An optional
comment gives the approver context. Submission does not change Live. The band says **waits for approval**. Open **Details** for the submitter and submitted version,
and the review’s **Decision** panel for the comment. The proposal cannot be edited while
it waits. **Withdraw request** ends the request and keeps the proposed work for editing; the
submitter or an authorised approver can withdraw it.

![Submitted change set with Waiting for approval, its comment and review and withdrawal controls](/docs/screens/appr-submitted.png)

*Above: Guide Admin submitted Guide approval example in Graubünden. Version 2 proposes a height
correction to Davos Platz; this earlier view keeps the submission comment in the banner.
In the current frame, read the comment in the review’s **Decision** panel.*

Approvers can find requests under **Waiting for your approval** on [Home](/docs/use/home/), or
through the bell's **Waiting for your approval** notice. Both lead to the review. Opening a
submitted change set also offers **Review and decide**.

![Approver's inbox with an unread Waiting for your approval notice](/docs/screens/appr-inbox-notice.png)

*Above: fictional approver Rita Approver receives a notice for Guide Admin's request.*

The review's **Decision** panel identifies who submitted which version and when, and shows their
comment. Below it, **Records** and **Relationships** show the proposed differences.

| Decision | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Approve and publish | Checks the current data again, applies the changes to Live and creates a publication immediately. Comment is optional. |
| Send back | Requires a Comment explaining what needs attention. Ends the pending request and keeps the change set for correction and another submission. Nothing is published. |

![Decision panel with submission details, Comment, Send back and Approve and publish above the changes](/docs/screens/appr-decision-panel.png)

*Above: Rita reviews Guide Admin's proposed change to Davos Platz. The empty Comment field says
Required to send back; approval does not require a comment.*

With the second-person rule on, the submitter sees **A second person must decide this request.**
instead of a Decision panel, even if they hold approval permission. They can inspect the changes
but must wait for another authorised approver.

## Sent back and submitted again

After **Send back**, the submitter receives a notice with the reason. The change-set banner names
the approver and repeats that reason. The proposal is editable again and **Submit for publication**
is available. The submitter can correct the work and submit again with a new comment. That is a
new request needing its own decision.

![Editable change set showing who sent it back and their reason](/docs/screens/appr-sent-back.png)

*Above: Rita asks Guide Admin to name the source of the new height. Review changes, Validate change
set and Submit for publication are available again; the correction has not reached Live.*

## Where the result appears

A successful approval publishes immediately and notifies the submitter. Under **Publications**,
the new snapshot is **Current** and names the person who published it. See
[Publications](/docs/use/publications/) for the saved result.

![Submitter's inbox with the approval notice above the earlier send-back notice](/docs/screens/appr-approved-notice.png)

*Above: Guide Admin's newest notice says Rita approved Guide approval example. The earlier
send-back notice remains below it; it is no longer the request's current state.*

Workspace **Activity** records the actions with who and when. Open **Settings**, **Workspaces**,
select the workspace and choose **Activity**. See [History](/docs/use/history/) for its filters.

![Workspace Activity showing change-set actions, the publication and the applied record correction](/docs/screens/appr-activity.png)

*Above: Graubünden's Activity after the submission, send back, resubmission and approval. The
visible latest entries include Publication 2 and Rita's published correction to Davos Platz.
Change-set actions use the general label Changed change set.*

Publication can still be refused because of a conflict or invalid combined data. A changed or
withdrawn request cannot be approved as the older submitted version. Reload, inspect the current
state and resolve the reported problem before retrying. The review also keeps the decision history.
Follow [Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/) for the steps, and
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) for how proposed work merges into Live.

## Email and following

Under **Settings › Notification email**, switch on **Email me when something arrives in my inbox**
to enable email where mail is configured and your account has an address. Choose **At once**,
**Digest** or **Off** for approval waiting, your approval decisions and your job notices.
Off stops only email; the inbox keeps receiving notices. Choose every morning or Mondays at
07:00 in your browser's time zone for digests, and check the next digest time shown. There is
no choice of another hour. A digest counts all eligible unread notices and lists the newest 50; if none remain, none is sent.

**Follow** on a Home workspace card adds notices when someone else publishes there. Your own
publications do not notify you through following. **Stop following** on Notification email ends
these notices; losing Browse access does too. If mail is unavailable or you have no address,
the page explains why and hides the email switch.

Administrators configure the publication rules on
[Approval policies](/docs/administer/approval-policies/). That page and its linked guide explain
saving the policy and establishing approvers; the submission and decision flow is above.

## When a notice has already been handled

Opening a job, move, migration or change-set review marks its notices read, including notices
arriving while you keep that subject open. A decision on a request, or confirmation or cancellation
of waiting work, also closes the waiting notice. A publication notice opens its publication
from Notifications or a digest while it is active and you have Browse. If it is no longer
active, it opens the workspace’s **Publications** instead. The bell also leads to
**Publications**. Opening marks the notice read; it does not restore lost Browse access.

For immediate email eligibility, digest counts and schedules, see
[Notification settings](/docs/use/notifications-settings/). A digest counts all eligible notices
but lists only the newest 50, and has no one-day cutoff. Job lines can include retained outcome
counts. **Stop following** removes a saved follow choice; losing access only suspends its notices.
Follow [Set up email notices](/docs/guide/use/set-up-email-notices/) or
[Follow a workspace](/docs/guide/use/follow-a-workspace/) to change these choices.

The **Submit for publication** dialog's **Comment (optional)** accepts up to 2,000 characters.
Choose **Submit** to validate and send the request, or **Cancel** to leave it editable.
**Submitted for publication. It waits for approval.** confirms submission. While waiting,
**Withdraw the request to edit it.** explains why controls are absent. **Request withdrawn.**
confirms that editing can resume; it does not discard the change set.

The change-set banner's ordinary write and model-version actions are explained in
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/#model-version-actions-on-the-banner).
For a person's activity, rather than inbox notices, see [History](/docs/use/history/).
guide/src/content/docs/use/mapping-grids:
---
title: Mapping grids
description: Understand source-to-target mappings, unmapped and ambiguous rows, replacement and removal.
reader: steward
---

Use a mapping grid to connect records on one side of a relationship to records on the other.
One use is connecting codes from another system to the records whose meaning they represent.
The model chooses both sides, their fields and the relationship; neither side has a fixed role
in refiroo. Follow [Map codes between systems](/docs/guide/use/map-codes-between-systems/) for the steps.

## Reading a mapping

Each row identifies a source record, its mapping state and its connected targets. Target chips use the target type’s colour and
show names with identifying fields chosen by the model. Read those fields before deciding that
two similar names mean the same thing.

Select the source record's name to open its record page. Each target chip opens that target's
record page. When editing is permitted, clicking elsewhere on the row opens **Change mapping**,
as do **Map** and **Change**.

The model may also show the name of a source record's nearest parent of a chosen type, even
several levels above it. The column heading is that type's name. Search looks at source names
and the source's displayed attributes, not these parent names.

Drag a column's right edge to change its width. With a keyboard, Tab to the edge and use the
Left or Right arrow key. refiroo remembers widths for this view in your browser on this device.
Rows keep their values on one line; a row with several targets lists them on separate lines.
If a value is cut off, point at the cell or move keyboard focus into it to see the full value
in a box beside the cell. The box usually appears below it and moves above when space is short.

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Unmapped | No target is connected through this view's relationship. |
| Mapped | At least one target is connected. When a row has several, the count says how many. |
| Ambiguous | More than one target is connected, on a view where a source may hold only one. |

A relationship decides what several targets mean. Where a source may hold many targets, such as
the "one" side of a one-to-many relationship, several targets are normal: the row is **Mapped**
with its count, and the view has no **Ambiguous** choice. **Ambiguous** appears only where a
source may hold at most one target, and describes multiple stored connections rather than
uncertainty about a suggested match. Decide whether one or several is correct for the data
before replacing anything. An unmapped row can be intentional.

![A mapping grid showing a source code mapped to two stops, other mapped codes and an unmapped code](/docs/screens/mapping-grid-codes-to-stops.png)

*Above: Codes to stops in Systems, searched for FICTIONAL, shows the invented Regional ticketing
system. T-0300 is Mapped (2), connected to Chur and Chur West; the other mapped codes each show
one stop. T-9999 is deliberately Unmapped, with Map available. This view allows several stops
per code, so its filters are All, Unmapped and Mapped. Select a name in the first column to open
the source record.*

**All**, **Unmapped**, **Mapped** and, where it applies, **Ambiguous** narrow the whole list, together with search.
An empty result says nothing about rows excluded by these conditions. A loading failure is not
an unmapped state; retry the read before editing.

## Choosing or clearing targets

**Map** on an unmapped row and **Change** on a filled row open **Change mapping**. Choosing a
target and saving sets that row's mapping to the chosen target. If several were connected,
the selection replaces them with one; it does not add another target alongside them.

Where offered, **Create new** followed by the target type opens a record creation form.
Creating a target and saving its mapping are distinct steps: review the selected target and
finish **Save**. Cancelling the mapping does not undo a target already created.

**Remove mapping**, where available, clears the connection rather than deleting either record.
A required connection cannot be cleared. Changes are saved together or refused, so an unsuccessful
replacement does not leave a half-changed mapping. See [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/)
for candidate restrictions and number limits.

A mapping grid works with voluntary associations, not parent containment or required ownership.
To create owned related records across columns, use a [relation matrix](/docs/use/relation-matrices/).
To keep several targets, use the record's relationship controls rather than replacing the set
with one selection in the grid.

## Permissions, context and conflicts

Reading needs **Browse**. Saving needs **Edit live** or **Work in change sets** for the relevant
data. Reader can inspect; Contributor can prepare change-set work; Data steward and Data owner
can also edit Live. Scoped grants can restrict the types you change. Publications and retired
workspaces are read-only. See [Record permissions](/docs/use/records/#who-may-read-and-change-records).

In Live, a saved mapping applies immediately. In a change set it remains proposed until publication.
If someone changes the mapping after you read it, **Mapping conflict** shows the current mapping.
Review it before continuing with your selection or cancelling. Publishing also checks intervening
live changes; see [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/).

The counts and **All**, **Unmapped**, **Mapped** and, where it applies, **Ambiguous** state choices describe the
whole matching list. Use them with search to find work beyond the visible rows. Target chips
preview the connected records so you can inspect identifying fields before replacing them.
An atomic replacement retains the existing relationship's identity and fields. Publishing a
change set refuses mappings that diverged from Live; review the current connections before
preparing another attempt.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*

## More targets and newly created records

**Mapping status** groups **All**, **Unmapped**, **Mapped** and, where it applies, **Ambiguous**. A mapping row
counts eligible sources plus sources already connected, so changing candidate conditions does
not hide existing mappings. **Show all … targets for …** expands a row's remaining targets.

Creating a missing target asks for its application. Parent choices belong to that application;
if no required parent can stand there, creation is refused. Create or select a suitable parent
rather than choosing one from another application. Creating the target selects it in the mapping
form but does not save the mapping: finish **Save** separately.

A replacement keeps the values of connections it retains when no new relationship values are
supplied. Explicit replacement values replace the whole collection of fields, and clearing
all is allowed only if the model accepts it. In the ordinary mapping picker, choosing a target
alone does not clear its existing relationship fields.

## Empty results and an unavailable view

**No results match these filters** means the mapping-state filter has no matching rows.
Choose **All** and clear other conditions to widen the list. **No results match this search**
means the search has no matches; change or clear it. **No … in this workspace yet** names the
source record type when there are no rows and neither a state filter nor search is applied.
Check that you are in the intended workspace and context before adding records.

**This mapping view references an object type that does not exist in the active model.**
means the view cannot be drawn. Reload after a model change. If it persists, give a model
administrator the view name and message so they can correct the model; changing mappings
cannot repair a missing type.

## Targets proposed by AI

**Propose targets** asks the configured AI provider to choose targets for unmapped sources.
It needs **Use AI proposals**, **Work in change sets**, a writable workspace and the send level
values. It is unavailable in a publication. Follow [Propose targets](/docs/guide/use/propose-targets/)
to prepare and review them.

Search and the chosen parent narrow which sources are considered. The provider receives source
and candidate target names and the fields this view shows. Only targets the grid permits are
candidates: all eligible targets when there are at most 100, otherwise each source's 20 closest
by name and searchable fields. Requests normally group 25 sources, or fewer for a small model
context. This shortlist can miss a good target; the proposal is help, not proof of a match.
Requests can cost money and their outcome is kept. See [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/)
for sending, access and retention.

Each accepted answer becomes an ordinary mapping in the chosen change set. Live data stays as
it was. **Proposed** under **Mapping status** shows sources with AI-proposed targets in that
change set. **Proposed by the AI** shows the confidence and reason; on a phone, open **Why?**
to read the reason. Confidence is the provider's estimate, not a guarantee. The operator sets
a minimum confidence, normally 0.5 out of 1; lower answers and invented or missing targets
are left unmapped.

![Proposed mappings in a change set, with suggested target stops and their confidence and reasons](/docs/screens/use-mapping-proposed.png)

Correct a wrong target through **Change** and **Save**, or remove the mapping if allowed.
Changing the target removes its AI mark because the replacement is your choice. Publishing
uses the usual approval and conflict checks. The published relationship's history keeps the
proposal's origin and model, and separately names the person who published it.

The job's result counts **Proposed**, **Left unmapped: no likely target** and **Changed meanwhile,
not touched**. It also reports refused or unanswered rows when present. Concurrently mapped
sources are left alone. Failed calls produce warnings; their rows are not proposed. Earlier
successful batches can remain after a later failure. **Stop** likewise keeps proposals already
written. Inspect the change set before publishing even when the job ended early.
guide/src/content/docs/use/jobs.md:
---
title: Jobs
description: Follow imports, exports and bulk work, inspect results and stop remaining work.
reader: steward
---

A job is work refiroo runs in the background, such as an import, export or change to many
records. Open **Settings › Data operations › Jobs** to find the jobs you may see across
workspaces, newest first. In **All jobs**, the list shows **Workspace**, **State**, **Items**, **Requested by**,
**Created**, **Finished** and **Actions**. Open a job to read its progress and results.

Follow [Follow and cancel a job](/docs/guide/use/follow-and-cancel-a-job/) for the steps.

## Jobs grouped under a task or a draft

Above the list, **Grouped** puts an assistant task's related work, including jobs queued by
its session, in one row. A model draft's jobs also form one row. A job with neither owner
remains a row of its own. **All jobs** shows the individual jobs instead. Your browser remembers
this choice when you return to Jobs.

The grouped table shows **Job or group**, **Workspace**, **Jobs**, **State**, **Latest** and
**Actions**. A group is labelled **Assistant task** or **Model draft** and named after its
workbook or draft. A workbook's extension appears beside its name. **Jobs** counts the group's
visible jobs; **State** gives counts for states with jobs, such as running, failed and completed.
**Latest** is the latest job time. These counts describe retained jobs you may see, not every
job ever started or every job in the instance.

Open the group name to see its jobs:

1. The heading names the workbook or draft. Above it, **Assistant task** or **Model draft**
   and the workspace identify the group; **‹ Jobs** returns to the main list.
2. **Summary of the group** gives the job count and latest time. **All** shows the total;
   state buttons show non-zero counts for **Running**, **Queued**, **Awaiting confirmation**,
   **Failed**, **Completed**, **Cancelled** or **Expired**. Select one to narrow the table;
   select **All** to restore every visible job. The selected state stays in the page's address.
3. The **Jobs** table shows **Job**, **State**, **Items**, **Requested by**, **Created**,
   **Finished** and **Actions**. Inspect processed, applied, rejected and unprocessed counts.
   **Refresh** reads again; **Load more jobs** continues the list. **Cancel** is offered
   for queued or running work where cancellation is available; it opens a confirmation.
4. **Open the task** or **Open the draft** opens the owning work. The button appears only
   after refiroo has confirmed you can read that task or draft. Seeing a group's jobs does
   not itself grant access to its owner; a missing button is not a stopped job.
5. Open a job to inspect its result. When opened from the group, its trail includes
   **‹ Assistant task: [name]** or **‹ Model draft: [name]**. Use that link to return to
   the group with the state choice preserved, or **Jobs** to return to the main list.

**Esc** goes up one level: job to the group it was opened from, then group to Jobs. A job
opened from the flat list returns directly to Jobs. Esc does not navigate while a dialog
is open or you are editing a field.

If the group says **This group has no jobs you can see**, its task or draft may have been
removed or its jobs may have expired. Return to Jobs. **No jobs in this state** means the
selected state has no visible rows; try **All** or **Refresh**. A read failure offers a retry;
it does not establish that the group is empty.

## States and results

A job can wait in the queue, run, wait for confirmation, complete, fail, be cancelled or expire.
**Cancel requested** means stopping has been requested, not that all work has stopped.
An import moves through **Reading the file**, **Previewing** and **Loading**. A waiting preview
has not applied its changes. **Load the file** confirms an import; **Apply** confirms a bulk
preview. Review the counts and item reasons before confirming.

Completion does not mean every row succeeded. Read applied, unchanged, rejected and unprocessed
counts and the item outcomes. A failure has **Why it failed**; a stopped job explains **What
stopped it**. Fix that cause before starting fresh work. A sample preview is informative, while
execution checks every item, the stored file, versions and the current context again.

An expired preview cannot be confirmed, even if a stale page still says it is waiting.
Start a new preview. The **Kept until** fact tells you when the job's retained results expire.
The list's **Limits** describes this deployment's batch, job and retention limits; do not rely
on a universal file size or item count.

## What a job's page shows

An import has its file/profile choices, row outcomes and column report. An export has **The
file**, with counts by type, format, size, checksum, context and **Download** after success.
An unsuccessful export has no file. Keep any file you need before its retention ends.

A copy or move shows records and relationships made, refused and not moved, breakdowns by type,
and outcomes filterable by reason. Source record names open in their original workspace.
Older retained jobs may lack relationship-type counts. A migration shows converted, type-changed,
removed and must-be-fixed counts. These operations are described under
[Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/) and [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/).
A job without item outcomes instead explains what it belongs to and links there where allowed.

## Cancellation and access

Cancel queued, running or waiting work with the offered cancel button and its confirmation.
Cancellation stops future work; it does not roll back already committed chunks. All-or-nothing
work commits as one unit, while independent work can leave partial results. A colleague's edit
to a shared change set between chunks can stop the next chunk; earlier chunks remain.

Jobs run with the requester's current rights. Deactivation or losing a required permission can
fail work at its next step. You see your own jobs and jobs your permissions allow; knowing a
job's address does not grant access. A retired workspace refuses new data changes.

The tab that starts work reports progress and completion while open. The inbox can also receive
waiting and finished-job notices. Opening a job marks its notices read, including notices that
arrive while it stays open. Closing a page does not itself stop a running job.

![Completed export with state, retention, counts, file details and Download](/docs/screens/job-results-and-file.png)

## Read the job labels

| State | Meaning and next action |
| --- | --- |
| Queued | Waiting to start. Cancel if the work is no longer wanted. |
| Running | Work is in progress. Follow its counts or leave it running in the background. |
| Awaiting confirmation | A preview is ready; review it before Apply or Load the file. |
| Completed | Processing ended. Check the result and refused items before relying on it. |
| Failed | Work stopped with an error. Read Why it failed and any applied counts. |
| Cancelled | Cancellation has finished. Check what was applied before it stopped. |
| Expired | Retention ended. Start new work if you need another preview or file. |

The result label is separate: **Every item applied**, **Partly applied** or **Nothing applied**.
A failed independent chunk is rolled back, while earlier committed chunks stay applied.
Cancelled all-or-nothing work rolls back its transaction completely. **Not reached** items
can mean cancellation, failure, a model change or a colleague changing the change set. With
all-or-nothing work, an otherwise valid item can be unwritten because another was refused.

The list distinguishes **Batch**, **Import**, **Export**, **Workbook for people**, **Profile**,
**Profile check**, **Dry run**, **Inference**, **Mapping proposal**, **Migration** and **Move**.
Some belong to model-administration tasks; their pages link to that work. **Refresh** reloads
the list and **Load more jobs** continues it. **New export** starts a file; **New import**
appears when your permissions allow importing.

**State** names the workspace and requester and shows creation, start and finish times.
For an export, **The file** also records **Sheets**, its Live/change-set/publication scope,
**Change feed position**, **Valid on** when chosen and **Checksum (SHA-256)**. Use those facts
to distinguish similar retained files; the checksum identifies the completed file's contents.

**Cancel this job?** offers **Stop the job** or **Keep the job**. If it finished first, read the
refusal and refreshed state rather than assuming it was cancelled. **The change was not applied**
after confirmation leaves the preview waiting: cancel it and create a fresh preview against
current data. The old result remains readable until retention ends.

Copies keep their source identity so a later copy can update its earlier counterpart instead
of making another one. Moving a copy back can update the original, or recreate its original
identity if it was removed. Inspect the source links and results before publishing. A move's
source deletions wait for the target copy to be published first; the deletion proposal cannot
be published ahead of the copy it depends on. See [Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/)
for mapping design, or [Copying and moving records](/docs/use/copying-and-moving/)
for preparing and reviewing a transfer.

On a waiting preview's own page, **Cancel this import?** offers **Discard the import**,
or **Cancel this preview?** offers **Discard the preview**. **Keep the import** or **Keep the
preview** returns to the preview. Discarding writes nothing and leaves the preview readable
until expiry. On the Jobs list, the confirmation button is **Cancel job** instead.
Results and files are normally kept for seven days; your deployment's **Limits** and the job's
**Kept until** give the applicable retention.

guide/src/content/docs/use/workspaces.md:
---
title: Workspaces
description: Choose the right dataset and understand its model, access and workspace management.
reader: steward
---

A **workspace** holds its own reference data, change sets and publications. Before editing,
check the workspace name and its model release. Follow [Switch workspace](/docs/guide/use/switch-workspace/)
to open another dataset.

## Each workspace runs its own model

Two workspaces can run the same model and hold different records. They can also run different
models, with different applications, types, fields and views. Changing one workspace's model
does not change another workspace's model. Switching workspaces copies and moves nothing.

[Home](/docs/use/home/) shows the workspaces you may browse, their models and releases, and their
application buttons. **Default** marks the instance's default workspace; it does not mean other
workspaces share its data. The workspace called Default need not be the default workspace.

![Home with workspace cards, model names, releases and application buttons](/docs/screens/use-home.png)

*Above: Graubünden is marked Default. The workspace named Default runs a different model.*

Within an application, **Workspace** in the sidebar names the dataset. The text beneath names its
model and release. The banner above the records identifies **Live**, a [change set](/docs/use/change-sets/)
or a [publication](/docs/use/publications/). Those are contexts within a workspace.

## The workspace's page

Choose a workspace's name on Home to open its page. **Find a record** searches names across its applications and lists. Up/Down chooses a result; Enter opens it. **Applications** offers each application's starting view and links straight to its lists.

**Your shelf** keeps the lists and other views you use most, from any application in this workspace. Choose **Add a list** and tick the lists, trees or matrices you want. You can also use the pin button in a list's header. A tile opens that view; its count, when available, is the number of live records of its source type, not a count of matrix cells or a filtered view.

Drag tiles to arrange them. For keyboard or touch use, open a tile's menu and choose **Move earlier** or **Move later**. Right-click also opens that menu. **Take off your shelf** removes the shortcut, leaving its data in place. The shelf and its order stay in this browser, separately for each workspace.

**Needs you** lists your waiting change sets. **What changed** groups recent activity by day; consecutive repeats of one kind of change fold with a count such as **4 in a row**. These are summaries, not a complete history. Workspace actions, including **Edit model**, appear only when your permissions allow them.

## Switching and access

The selector offers workspaces you may browse. **Other model** identifies a different model;
**Other release** identifies a different release of the same model. After switching, check the
applications and views again. The former view may not exist in the destination.
With only one available workspace, its name appears without a selector.

You need **Browse** access to read data, and the appropriate editing permissions to change it.
Reader can browse; Contributor can prepare changes in change sets; Data steward and Data owner
can also change Live. Custom grants can narrow writes to particular applications or record types.
See [What you can do](/docs/use/account/#what-you-can-do) for your own access.

If no workspace is offered, ask an administrator for access. A loading failure does not mean
there are no workspaces: retry the failed read first.

## Workspace administration

A retired workspace remains readable but refuses changes. Where your access permits it, open it
from **Settings › Workspaces**, rather than the active workspace selector. Creating, renaming,
retiring and deleting workspaces are described in
[Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/).

## A workspace from a workbook

Choose **New workspace from a workbook** on Home beside **Your workspaces**, in
**Settings › Workspaces**, or on a workspace's page. This creates a separate workspace;
it does not load into the workspace you have open.

The action appears when you hold **Workspace administration**, **Install a model** or
**Model release**, and **Bulk and import** at the instance, plus **Model authoring**.
Workspace administration, model administration and integration jobs must also be switched on
for the deployment. If any required access or capability is missing, the action is hidden.

1. Choose an XLSX workbook or CSV file in **Workbook**. **Name** starts with a name taken
   from the file; change it if needed. Choose **Read the workbook**. refiroo reads the file,
   finds its lists and checks every row before creating the workspace.
2. Review **What refiroo found**. Each list shows its source sheet where applicable, its row
   count, how many rows load, any rows skipped for want of a key, and why rows do not load.
   The total covers every row, not a sample. Choose **Create workspace** to install the
   model, create the workspace and start loading the workbook into Live. A refused row does
   not stop the other rows from loading.

**Adjust** keeps the draft and opens it in the model editor so you can change the structure
or how the workbook is read. If no list was found, or checking did not finish successfully,
**Create workspace** is unavailable; read any explanation and use **Adjust** to inspect the
draft. A read failure appears under **Not read**. A creation refusal appears under
**The workspace was not created**, with the problems to resolve.

**Cancel** closes the sheet and removes the draft made for the review. If removal fails,
the draft remains under **Settings › Model**. To start on an existing model instead, open
**More ways to start** in the file step and choose **New workspace on an installed model**.
From Home or a workspace's page this takes you to Settings › Workspaces; from Settings it
opens the **New workspace** form. You can also make a workspace without data that way.

After creation, the new workspace's page shows **Loading** with the file name and the
number of items processed, out of the total when available. When loading finishes, the
notice shows counts for **created**, **updated** and **unchanged**, followed by how many rows
did not load or that every row loaded. For refused rows, choose **See the rows** to open the
job's details. **Dismiss** removes the notice; it does not undo the load. If loading fails
or stops, the page shows the reason. The workspace already exists, so inspect the load in
**Settings › Jobs** before trying again. The notice is kept only for the current page load;
after a browser reload, find the job in Settings › Jobs.

## When a destination cannot open

The selector searches workspace labels; the page address keeps the workspace's key. Switching
can show a toast explaining that the destination runs another model or release.
**Not in this model** means the address names an application, collection or record type this
workspace lacks. Use the offered workspaces whose models contain it, or choose an available
application here. An unknown workspace or a release that cannot be served has its own explanation.
Read that reason and ask the operator to restore a supported release where needed; retrying a
record edit cannot make an unavailable model readable. Other workspaces can still be used.

## Refresh after the model changes

If the workspace changed release while your page was open, the message can say **… now runs ….
Nothing was saved.** or **Reload to see it.** Choose **Reload**, then review the current form
and context before editing. A stale screen must not overwrite data under a different model.

**Manage workspaces**, beside or inside the selector, opens its Settings entry where permitted.
Its **Applications · …** links open the workspace's applications. Loading the catalogue or an
individual workspace is distinct from an empty result; wait or retry the error.
Creating, renaming, setting the default, retiring, reactivating and deleting are administration
tasks. Their controls and deployment availability belong to
[Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/). **Capability groups** is an operator
status panel, not a setting a steward changes to gain access.

To open retired or unreadable data, follow
[Open a retired or unavailable workspace](/docs/guide/use/open-a-retired-or-unavailable-workspace/).
To read activity across workspaces, use [History](/docs/use/history/).

A retired workspace is marked **Retired · read only**. In Settings its **Overview** shows the
model, creation and last-change facts, and **Open workspace** leads to its start page. Wait
while **Loading workspace catalogue…** or **Loading workspace…** is shown; an error is not an
empty catalogue.

A missing model element can say **No other workspace's model has it.** Choose **Go back** or
the offered workspace start page, then choose a collection present in that model. If another
workspace is offered, its **Open in …** action changes the workspace as well as the page;
check the destination before making changes.

## Actions for this workspace

![Workspace menu offering Import, Export and Edit model beside the selected workspace](/docs/screens/workspace-actions-menu.png)

*Above: the menu for Graubünden while reading the Stops collection in Network. Its actions
apply to this workspace and the data context being viewed.*


The **⋯** menu beside the workspace selector offers **Import…**, **Export…** and **Edit model**
when your permissions and the current context allow them. Export starts from what the current
page shows; check the chosen columns, filters and data context in its dialog. See
[Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/) for what the file includes.

**Edit model** opens the workspace's model draft, returning to that draft on later visits.
It changes the structure rather than an individual record. Ask a model administrator when you
need that change; see [Models](/docs/model/models/). Applying a model shows its effect before
confirmation. If records must move, the migration preview must be confirmed before they move.

The workspace's Settings page offers **Overview**, **Access**, **Approval** and **Activity**
according to your permissions. Overview links to its applications; Activity shows changes newest
first, grouped by day. Access and Approval describe who can work here and how publication is
approved. They do not grant editing rights simply because you can read the workspace.

## A context that could not load

**Loading the model…**, **Loading change set…** or **Loading publication…** means the read
is still pending. **Could not load this content** reports a failed read, not an empty dataset.
Read its explanation and use **Retry** after correcting a connection or service problem.
**Return to Live**, where offered, leaves the failed snapshot view for this workspace's
current data. Check the context banner before continuing; changes made in Live take effect immediately.
guide/src/content/docs/use/history.md:
---
title: History
description: Find what changed on a record, across a workspace or in one person’s work.
reader: steward
---

Use history to find who changed data and when. Start from a record for one item's past,
a workspace for activity across records, or Home for your own work.
Follow [See who changed what](/docs/guide/use/see-who-changed-what/) for the steps.

## A record's History

In **Live**, a record page’s **History** shows the newest entries first.
The record History panel is absent inside a change set or publication. Use
[Review changes](/docs/guide/use/review-what-a-change-set-changes/) for a change set’s
prepared differences, or return to Live for the record’s history. **All**, **Values**,
**Relationships** and **Moves** select kinds of event. **By** narrows the entries to one person;
**Anyone** removes that restriction. Expand an entry with its arrow to see recorded details,
including previous values where available.

![A record's History with event kinds, author and time](/docs/screens/use-history-stop-changed.png)

*Above: Thusis Süd records the Abbreviation change and the later update applied by publication.
The details panel shows the current abbreviation, THSD.*

Creation, field changes, relationship changes and moves are different events. A successful Live
save appears in history; a refused save is not a saved correction. Work prepared in a change set
and work applied by publication have different contexts. Read the cause alongside the person
and time rather than assuming two lines mean two direct live edits.

History names the person or client responsible, using their current name. Earlier events recorded
before sign-in was recorded read **Before sign-in**. Renaming a person does not mean another person performed
the old action. Read access is limited to workspaces you may browse.

## Activity across a workspace

The workspace’s page shows **What changed**, grouped by day with consecutive repeats folded into a count. For more activity, where your access
opens workspace management, choose **Settings**, **Workspaces**, the workspace,
then **Activity**. Its **What** choices are **Everything**, **Records**, **Relationships**,
**Change sets** and **Publications**. Entries identify the action, person and time, and can also
name its change set or publication context.

![Workspace Activity with kind filters and changes across records](/docs/screens/use-history-activity.png)

*Above: Graubünden's Activity shows the creation and validation of the correction change set,
the record update and Publication 1, newest first.*

## A person's changes

On [Home](/docs/use/home/), **Your recent changes** gives a short list. **See all your changes**
opens **Your changes**. Consecutive steps on one model draft fold into one expandable line with their count. Expand it to read the individual steps. Choose **Workspace**, **What** and **Period** to narrow it. A person's
linked name can also lead to their changes, within the workspaces you may read.

![Your changes filtered by workspace with What and Period choices](/docs/screens/use-history-changes.png)

*Above: Guide Admin's changes in Graubünden include the published correction and earlier work.*

These lists help locate an action; they do not undo it. To correct current data, follow
[Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/). To read the saved result of a publish,
[browse a publication](/docs/guide/use/browse-a-publication/).

If a history read fails, retry it. If no entries match, remove the person, kind or
period filters. A filtered empty list does not prove that the record has never changed.

## Reading more and the limits of the list

History groups entries under day headings. It starts with the ten newest; **Load older history** reads
20 more and **Show fewer** shortens it again. Jobs are named as the cause of their changes;
changes applied by publication name that publication. A system's author name is marked **client**.
Where an earlier value was not recorded, the expanded entry says so rather than reconstructing it.

The person's **Changes** page helps find actions across workspaces. It shows no field values
and cannot be exported; open a record's History for values. It leaves out model-to-model mapping
operations. Older changes without a workspace are visible only to someone who reads every
workspace. Entries recorded before named sign-in say **Before sign-in**. Model-administration
entries also require Model authoring access.

## Empty results and continuing the list

**No history recorded yet.** means there are no retained record events. **No change matches.**
means the filters found none: remove **By** or the event-kind filter before concluding the
record never changed. **Show all history** clears a narrowed history. **Loading history…**
is still a pending read.

The person's Changes list groups actions by day and reads across workspaces you may browse.
**Load more** reads the next entries. **No change matches these filters.** calls for loosening
the filters; **You have not changed anything in the workspaces you can read yet.** describes
an empty personal list. A different person's page can be headed **Changes by …**. These activity
lists help locate changes without exposing the record's full before/after values.

## Authors, causes and destinations

Deactivated people and clients remain named using their current names. Changes made by refiroo
itself say **the engine**. For a job, the author is the person or client who requested it;
for publication changes, it is the person who published. A relationship entry identifies
the record at the other end. Publication and type-change entries may keep only the changed
values, so their earlier values can be unavailable.

The person's **Changes** page offers the last 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days and includes live
and change-set work, publications and permitted model work. Titles open the affected item
while it still exists; a deleted item has no current record to open.

A change set names its creator and the people who edited it. A publication names who
published and withdrew it. A job names its requester both in the list and on its page.
These names describe different responsibilities; the person publishing need not have prepared
every change.

A narrowed workspace Activity list offers **Show all activity** to clear its narrowing.
The wider result still includes only work you may read.

## What changed in a period

**What changed** above workspace **Activity** and a record's **History** can explain a period
in a few statements. It appears when a provider is enabled and you hold **Browse** and **Use
AI proposals** in the workspace. Opening the page sends nothing. Follow
[Explain a period in history](/docs/guide/use/explain-a-period-in-history/) to request an account
and check its sources.

The initial period is **Last 7 days** for a workspace and **Last 30 days** for a record.
**Choose dates** offers **From** and **To, included**; both chosen days are included, using your
browser's time zone. The first day must not follow the last. There is no fixed maximum period.

refiroo counts the live changes across the whole period: records created, changed, moved or
deleted by type, fields changed, relationships, jobs and publications, people, change-set events,
withdrawn publications and model activations. A publication can identify who prepared its work,
the preparation job and who published it. A staged record is counted when published, once;
record edits still sitting in an open change set are not counted as live changes. Events such
as creating or submitting that set can still be included. A record account concerns that
record's values, relationships and moves, rather than every record in the workspace. Counts can overlap: a record moved while a value
changed can appear in both counts. Do not add them as a total of different records.

**Explain this period** sends counts and model labels to the configured provider. Only the
values send level adds names of records, people, change sets and files. Names remain visible
in your fact lines whatever the send level. The explanation does not send record field values.
Requests may incur costs and are logged; [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) explains
permissions, content retention and provider privacy.

Each AI statement has numbered sources. A number leads to a fact counted by refiroo, not written
by the provider. **The facts** includes all facts, with **Show the other …** after the first ten.
The provider sees at most 40 facts of each kind and their true totals, so its short account is
not a replacement for the whole list. Statements without a valid source are removed and counted.
The note **Written by AI from the facts below** reminds you that the wording can be wrong.

![An account of a workspace period with numbered statements, facts and Show them](/docs/screens/use-history-explained.png)

**Show it** or **Show them** narrows Activity or the record's timeline to the changes counted
by that fact. Other facts offer **Open the change set** or **Open the job** where you may open
it. A job deleted after retention has no job link; a deleted record has no current name.
Use **Show all activity** or **Show all history** to leave the narrowing.

A period with no changes says so and sends nothing to AI. If **The account could not be written**
appears, the facts remain usable and **Try again** requests the wording again. A request that
cannot be made has its own error and retry. The same facts for the same period requested again within
an hour reuse the saved account without a second provider call. The preset periods end at the
time you ask: **Explain again** normally changes that end time and can make another paid call. The account itself is temporary,
not a permanent history entry. The browser's account is in English; it is not translated into
German. Requesting an explanation changes no record.

## Work prepared by an assistant

History separates who prepared work from who published it. Built-in assistant changes say
**Proposed by the AI assistant**, with the model when recorded, **Asked for by** the person who
requested the task, and **Edited by** a later editor when present. The mark survives later
edits of that prepared row and is kept in published history, including removals, after the
task expires. A task's proposal need not carry a confidence percentage. Mapping suggestions
can include confidence and a reason; replacing a mapping target removes that target's AI mark.

Work from an external connected assistant says **Prepared by an assistant:** followed by its
name, who asked and who edited when available. Its name is the one the assistant gave itself;
it is not proof of identity. The entry still names the person who published. The personal
Changes page has no separate assistant filter or mark, so inspect a record's History for this
detail. refiroo never turns an assistant's proposal into publication on its own.

![Live record history with an expanded update prepared by an assistant and attributed to a person](/docs/screens/use-history-assistant.png)

*Above: Chur Wiesental’s History attributes an Abbreviation update to Guide Admin and marks
it as prepared by Stops checker (guide). A separate entry below names changes made by that
assistant’s client.*

An external assistant can prepare and submit only change sets created by its own person or
client, not a colleague's. It can add or change records and relationships and set fields,
but cannot remove records or relationships, clear values, discard a set, withdraw a submission,
change the model, approve or publish. A person reviews the submitted work through
[change-set review](/docs/guide/use/review-what-a-change-set-changes/). Withdraw the request before editing a submitted change
set; a second-person policy still needs a different approver from
the person whose assistant submitted it. Correct mistaken additions yourself or have the
assistant prepare a new set. These external-assistant limits differ from the built-in workbook
task's fuller preparation abilities. See [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) before
allowing an assistant to read your workspace.
guide/src/content/docs/use/account.md:
---
title: Your account
description: Check your sign-in, manage your own browsers and see what your roles allow.
reader: steward
---

Open the avatar at the top right and choose **Account** to see who you are signed in as,
manage your sign-in methods and inspect your permissions.

## The account menu

The avatar menu shows your name and the roles you hold in the workspace currently open. **Account**, **Notifications** and **All settings**
open those pages. **Theme** offers **System**, **Light** and **Dark**. System follows your device;
the choice is saved in this browser. **Sign out** ends your current sign-in.

![The avatar menu with account links, theme choices and Sign out](/docs/screens/use-account-menu.png)

*Above: Guide Admin's menu shows their roles in Graubünden. Other people can have fewer roles.*

## Your identity and sign-in

The account card shows your name, e-mail address, how you signed in and when.
These details help you check that you are using the intended account. **Sign out** on the card
ends the current browser's sign-in.

![Account with identity, password, passkeys and authenticator setup](/docs/screens/use-account.png)

*Above: Guide Admin signed in with a password and has not set up an authenticator app.*

### When an administrator manages your sign-in

If Account says **An administrator manages the sign-in of this account.**, the password,
passkeys, authenticator app and **Where you’re signed in** sections are not shown. Your
profile and **Sign out** remain. You can sign out of this browser, but you cannot sign out
other browsers or sign out everywhere.

You cannot change your own password, set up, confirm or remove an authenticator app, make
new recovery codes, or add, rename or remove passkeys. Ask a security administrator for a
password-setting link or help with a lost device. **Forgotten your password?** gives the
usual response but sends no mail for this account. See
[Help someone who lost a device](/docs/guide/administer/help-someone-who-lost-a-device/).

### When you manage your own sign-in

The controls depend on how you signed in. If your organisation provides sign-in, its password
is managed there. The local Password control appears when you signed in with your refiroo password.

To change that password:

1. Choose **Change password**. Enter **Current password** and **New password**.
2. Choose **Save new password**. A successful save keeps this browser signed in and signs out
   your other browsers. **Cancel** closes the form without changing the password.
3. If a password is refused, read the reason beside the field and correct it. A failed save
   does not change your password.

Under **Passkeys**, choose **Add a passkey** and follow your browser or device's instructions.
A WebAuthn passkey uses your fingerprint, face or device PIN to sign in, or to provide the second step.
Registered passkeys can be renamed so you can tell them apart, or removed. Removal asks for your
password or a code from your authenticator app. If the device prompt is cancelled, no passkey is added.

An authenticator app supplies time-based one-time passwords (TOTP). Under **Authenticator app**, choose **Set up an authenticator app**. Scan the displayed code with
your app, or enter its key, then enter **Code from the app** to confirm setup. Keep the recovery
codes shown afterwards somewhere safe: each works once if you lose access to your phone.
They are shown once. **New recovery codes…** replaces the old codes after you prove your sign-in;
the old ones then stop working. If the instance requires a second factor with a password, removal is offered only when a
passkey provides another way to meet that requirement. Otherwise, ask a security administrator.

## Where you’re signed in

Each row names a signed-in browser or other sign-in session and shows when it last acted and
when it signed in. **This browser** marks the one you are using. Several rows can have the same
browser name; use their times to distinguish them.

![Signed-in sessions with last activity, sign-in times and individual Sign out buttons](/docs/screens/use-account-sessions.png)

*Above: the reference account has many sessions from browser work and automated captures.
A row labelled Python-urllib is not another person's browser.*

Choose a row's **Sign out** to end that session. Choosing it for This browser signs you out here.
For a lost device or an unfamiliar session, **Sign out everywhere** asks for confirmation and
ends all your sessions, including this one, at their next request. It does not delete your work.
If ending a session fails, retry after reading the error; do not assume it has ended.

## What you can do

The bottom of Account lists your roles by workspace and what they allow: reading, proposing
changes, changing Live, publishing and approving. Restrictions may name particular applications
or record types. Instance-wide roles appear separately under **Across the instance**.

![Account permissions grouped by workspace and instance-wide responsibilities](/docs/screens/use-account-permissions.png)

*Above: Guide Admin holds Data owner for every workspace and five instance-wide administrative roles.*

This is a view of your access, not a form for granting yourself roles. Ask an access administrator
if something you need is missing. To act on a proposal, follow
[Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) or
[Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/). For notices and their email options,
see [Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/).

Each role is listed once, with the groups through which you hold it. A limited permission is
shown as a count: open it to see the applications and record types covered, and the roles that
allow each. On a phone, the workspace sections stack vertically.

Use **Settings › Notification email** for email choices: switch on **Email me when something arrives
in my inbox**, then choose **At once**, **Digest** or **Off** for each kind. Digests run every
morning or on Mondays at 07:00 in your browser's time zone; the page shows the next one. No unread
notices means no digest. The email switch is absent if mail is not configured or you have no
email address; the page explains why. **Settings › Appearance** holds display preferences.
For administrator-managed sign-in and help with lost devices, see
[Sign-in and second factors](/docs/administer/sign-in/).

## Sign-in and password help

Opening a saved application address without a session shows the sign-in page, in this browser's
theme. Use your e-mail address and password, a passkey, or the offered organisation's provider.
After signing in you return to the requested page. An ended session sends you there again.
A wrong e-mail address or password does not reveal which was wrong. Repeated failures slow attempts;
they do not permanently lock your account. Wait before retrying rather than repeatedly submitting.

Sessions renew while you work, but still have idle and overall expiry limits set by the operator.
If sign-in keeps ending unexpectedly, sign in again and ask an administrator to inspect the
session rather than changing unrelated record data. Under **General › Account**, **Loading your
account** is a loading state, not missing identity; retry a failed read.
The identity card can say **Signed in with your password**, **Signed in with a passkey** or
**Signed in with …**, with **Since …** for this session's start. **Where you’re signed in**
counts browsers and shows **Active now** or last activity with sign-in time.

The normal password rule is 15–128 characters. Common passwords and your e-mail address are refused;
use a longer distinct password, not repeated guesses. A development instance can have a lower
minimum, so the displayed refusal is authoritative. The current password is needed to change
it. Use the reveal buttons to check the current or new password privately. If you forgot it,
use **Forgotten your password?** when offered, or ask an administrator for a password-setting
link. The response does not reveal whether an account exists. Your organisation manages its
provider password separately.

**Add a passkey** opens a separate refiroo page. Give the passkey a recognisable name and provide
**Your password, or a code from your app** before the browser's device prompt. This proof prevents
an unattended signed-in browser adding a lasting sign-in method. Cancellation adds nothing.
Passkeys belong to the host where they were made; moving refiroo to another host affects them.
Renaming changes their display name only. Removing the last second factor can be refused where
one is required: add another passkey or set up an authenticator app first.

For display steps, see [Appearance and devices](/docs/use/appearance-and-devices/).
For the next digest time and delivery choices, see
[Notification settings](/docs/use/notifications-settings/).

An account using only an organisation's provider cannot add refiroo passkeys or an
authenticator app to bypass that provider. Manage those sign-in protections with your
organisation. If proof for adding or removing a passkey is refused, correct the password or
use a current authenticator or unused recovery code; a slowed sign-in needs time before retrying.

Select the passkey's name where it stands to edit it. Choose **Save** after changing it; the notice offers **Undo**. **Remove …**
opens a separate confirmation with **Remove passkey**; it does not remove the device's other
passkeys. **New recovery codes…** asks for **Code from the app, or a recovery code**, then
**Rotate recovery codes**. Save the replacements: the old recovery codes stop working. Removing the
authenticator app uses **Remove the second factor** and **Remove it**; your recovery codes then
stop working too.

## Session limits and organisation sign-in

By default a session ends after 12 hours without use or 14 days in total, even if it has
continued renewing while you work. The operator can change these limits. Repeated failed
password attempts can delay another attempt by up to fifteen minutes; the account is not
locked permanently.

Your organisation can offer **Continue with** its OpenID Connect sign-in provider, such as
Microsoft Entra ID, Google or Keycloak. The provider handles its own second factors. On your
first sign-in, refiroo takes your name and email from the provider and updates membership of
its groups at sign-in. The roles granted to those groups determine what you can do here.

If you already had a local account, first provider sign-in can create a separate person.
Ask a security administrator to link the accounts so your existing roles and history stay
with the original person. Signing out of refiroo signs out of the provider too only when
that provider is configured to do so. If you can immediately sign in again without a password,
check whether the provider still has an open session.

**Forgotten your password?** asks for your e-mail address. It gives the same
response whether or not that account exists. A reset message is sent only for an account
with a local password and an email address whose sign-in is not managed by an administrator. For a provider account, reset your password with
the organisation instead. An administrator can supply a one-time password-setting link
when email recovery is unavailable.

## Sessions for an assistant

An external assistant you signed in for appears in **Where you’re signed in** as its name
followed by **(assistant)**. **Sign out** on that row ends its session, stopping it on its next
request. A blocked assistant also loses access; restoring it does not restore the ended session.
You must sign in for it again. Its sign-in page shows the name it claims and where it returns.
Check those details before allowing it. See [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/)
for what it may read, what it may prepare and why its provider privacy settings matter.

## Complete a second sign-in step

After your password, refiroo can ask for another proof of identity:
