1. If **Use a passkey** is offered, choose it and complete the device prompt. Cancelling the
   prompt leaves you at sign-in; it does not remove your passkey.
2. To use an authenticator app, enter its current six-digit **Code** or **Code from the app**.
   Choose **Sign in** or **Sign in with the code**, as shown. A refused code needs a new
   current code; repeated failed attempts can require a wait.
3. If you cannot use the app, choose **Use a recovery code instead**, enter one unused
   **Recovery code** and choose **Sign in**. That code cannot be used again. **Use the app's
   code** returns to the ordinary code entry. **Start again** returns to the first sign-in step.
4. If setup is required before you can continue, scan the displayed code with your app or
   copy the displayed key into it. Enter **Code from the app** and choose **Confirm and
   continue**. Save the recovery codes when they are shown.

If you have lost all usable proofs, ask a security administrator to help restore access.
After removing a passkey in refiroo, also remove its saved entry from your device or password
manager; the entry there is not deleted automatically.

![Second sign-in step offering a passkey, an authenticator code and recovery-code sign-in](/docs/screens/use-sign-in-second-step.png)
guide/src/content/docs/use/notifications:
---
title: Notification settings
description: Choose immediate email or digests, and manage the workspaces you follow.
reader: steward
---

Keep your inbox in refiroo and choose which notices also reach your email address. Open
**Settings › Notification email**, or **Notification email settings** on the Notifications
page. Follow [Set up email notices](/docs/guide/use/set-up-email-notices/) for the steps.
For the notices themselves, see [Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/).

## Email is your choice

**Email me when something arrives in my inbox** is off until you enable it. The page shows
the destination address. Under **How each kind reaches me**, choose **At once**, **Digest**
or **Off** for approval requests, decisions on your requests, jobs and other offered kinds.
These choices change only email: your inbox keeps every notice. Choices save as you make them;
read any error before assuming the new choice was stored.

If mail has not been configured or your account has no address, a sentence explains why no
email choice is offered. Ask an administrator about the missing setup or address. If email was
already on, the switch can remain visible so you can turn it off after mail becomes unavailable.
Email is for people's accounts, not clients used by other systems.

![Notification email for an account without an email address or followed workspaces](/docs/screens/notification-email-digest.png)

*Above: the reference account has no email address, so no email delivery choices are offered.
Its followed-workspaces list is also empty.*

**At once** sends an eligible unread notice once, provided it arrived since enabling email
and is less than 24 hours old. Previously read notices and notices from before enabling email
are not sent. Turning email off leaves inbox notices intact.

## A digest instead of separate messages

Choosing **Digest** for the first kind starts a daily schedule in your browser's time zone.
Under **The digest**, choose **Every morning at 07:00** or **Mondays at 07:00**. The page shows
the saved time zone and **Next digest**. There is no choice of another hour or an evening digest.
Enabling email recalculates its next time; changing the frequency or time zone moves it.
Saving the same schedule preserves its next time. With email off or no schedule, no next time
is shown. The browser supplies the time zone when you choose the schedule.

![Enabled notification email with delivery choices, digest frequency, time zone and next digest](/docs/screens/use-notification-email-digest-settings.png)

A digest counts all eligible unread, unhandled notices since email was enabled and lists the
newest 50, with links to the rest. Unlike immediate mail, it has no 24-hour cutoff. Job entries
can include applied and rejected counts while their results remain retained. Notices already
read or handled are omitted; nothing eligible means no message. A notice included in a digest
is not mailed again as a new digest entry.

Email uses fixed wording, kinds, times, counts and links. It contains no record, change-set,
workspace, person or file names. Digests do not require AI. If settings are refused, the prior
preferences remain; retry after checking the shown reason.

## Follow publication in a workspace

**Follow** on a workspace's Home card opts you into notices when someone else publishes a
change set there. Your own publication does not create a follower notice for you.
**Workspaces I follow** lists your choices with **Stop following**. Following requires Browse
and starts off. Selecting Follow again does not create duplicate subscriptions.

Losing Browse or deactivation stops notices while retaining your follow choice. Notices can
resume when access returns. Stop following to remove that choice deliberately. Following is
independent of whether email is available; its notices still appear in the inbox.
See [Follow a workspace](/docs/guide/use/follow-a-workspace/).

There is no browser view of a sent digest. Read the message in the receiving mailbox;
use **Notification email** to check its saved delivery choices and schedule.

## When email does not arrive

An unread notice alone is not enough: email must be enabled, the account active, a destination
address present and the instance able to send mail. A digest also needs a schedule and at
least one kind assigned to it. Choosing the first Digest kind saves a daily schedule with
your browser's time zone automatically. If that save is refused, your old choices remain;
read the error and retry rather than expecting a partly saved schedule.

Nothing eligible means no digest message. Check the inbox first: reading or handling a notice
can remove it from the next message. Turning a kind **Off** affects email only. There is no
interface-language or general account-locale chooser here; the digest time zone is a separate
schedule choice, not a language preference.

The unavailable-email messages are **Email is not set up for this installation, so there is
nothing to choose here.** and **Your account has no email address, so there is nothing to
choose here.** Neither means notifications are lost. Read them in **Notifications** and ask
an administrator to set up mail or correct your account's address.
guide/src/content/docs/use/relationships:
---
title: Relationships
description: Understand connections between records, allowed candidates, required relationships and removal.
reader: steward
---

Use a relationship to connect records with a named meaning. Its two ends can belong to different
applications in the same workspace. For the controls to add, replace and remove a connection,
see [Relate records](/docs/guide/use/relate-records/).

## Meaning, direction and number

The model defines each relationship's meaning in both directions, the record types it connects,
and how many connections each end may hold. The name you read depends on which record you open.
One connection appears from both ends; these are not two separately maintained copies.

A relationship can allow one record or several at either end. A section that allows one offers
**Set** when empty and **Change** when filled. A section allowing several offers **Add relationship**.
A connection may also hold fields of its own. These belong to this connection, rather than to
one of its records. The same record can have different values on different connections.

![A record with separate relationship tables and connected records](/docs/screens/relationships-stop.png)

*Above: Chur Wiesental in Network has Train under Modes, Rhätische Bahn under Operator, and two
System codes. The reference model allows several modes but exactly one operator per stop.*

The Relationships panel puts these values in columns after the related record's fields.
Open **Display** and find **Attributes of the relationship** to show or hide them. A panel
covering several allowed pairs can show a column that does not apply to every row. These
columns cannot sort this panel: sort by an offered field of the related record instead.
Use the relationship's edit action to change its values; this does not edit the related record.

![Rhätische Bahn operator record with Stops operated and its Display choices](/docs/screens/record-relationship-attribute-columns.png)

*Above: the Rhätische Bahn operator in the Graubünden workspace. Stops operated is filtered
to Chur W, showing Chur West with Local name Customer counter and Primary contact. Display
lists the record columns separately from Local name, Primary contact and Inspected on under
Attributes of the relationship; the column width is Narrow.*

For many connections at once, use a [relationships table](/docs/use/relationship-tables/).
Its grid can [change relationship values in bulk](/docs/guide/use/change-relationship-values-in-bulk/),
including links to several shown column records.

## Associations, ownership and containment

An **association** connects independent records. Removing the connection leaves both records.
A voluntary association can also be maintained through a [mapping grid](/docs/use/mapping-grids/).

An **owning relationship** makes a related record dependent on its owner. It must not be left
without its required owner. Deleting an owner can therefore remove the records it owns, including
records in another application. Review the deletion impact before confirming; see
[Deleting a record](/docs/use/records/#deleting-a-record).

**Containment** gives a record a parent and its place in a hierarchy. refiroo keeps the parent
connection consistent with that place. Change it by [moving the record](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/),
rather than adding or deleting the parent relationship separately.

## Which records you may choose

The records offered by a relationship search are its **candidates**. A candidate must be in the
same workspace and have an allowed record type. The model can further restrict choices using
the record's fields or fields of its ancestors. A hint below the search explains these conditions
where they apply. The record you are starting from may also have to meet conditions; a section
can explain why that record cannot hold the relationship.

An expected record can be absent because you are in another workspace or context, your search
does not match, or it fails those conditions. When replacing a single connection, the current
record is excluded from the replacement choices. Clear or shorten the search and check the hint
before asking a model administrator about the rule. Being offered a record does not guarantee
a save: number limits, required connections and uniqueness are checked when saving too.

Candidate conditions control new connections. If a record later changes so that it no longer
meets them, an existing connection is kept. Its presence is not a promise that the same record
would be offered for a new connection now.

## Required connections and removal

An optional connection may be removed on its own. A required connection cannot be removed while
its dependent record still needs it. Where only one related record is allowed, **Change** replaces
that record together in one save, avoiding a separate deletion followed by creation.

Choose **Remove relationship** to remove a permitted connection immediately. Both records remain, and the notice offers **Undo**. A required-relationship refusal leaves it in
place; do not delete an owner to work around the refusal. Review the intended data change first.

## Context, permissions and refused changes

Readers can inspect relationships with **Browse** access. Changes need **Edit live** in Live
or **Work in change sets** in a change set. Scoped grants may limit the records you can change.
See [Record permissions](/docs/use/records/#who-may-read-and-change-records). Publications and
retired workspaces are read-only; a view's configuration also determines its editing actions.

Live changes take effect immediately; proposed changes stay in the selected change set.
If a relationship changed after you read it, a replacement or edit can be refused. Read the
message, close and reopen the section to review the current connection before retrying.
A failed load is not an empty relationship list. Retry the read before deciding to add anything.

[Relation matrices](/docs/use/relation-matrices/) provide another way to inspect and maintain
connections across many records.

## Reading connections beside a tree

A record opened beside a tree lists related records under **Connected**. Each row follows a
relationship panel declared for the record, with chips that open the connected records.
Open the record's full page to manage those relationships in their tables.

Single-connection rows offer **Change** and **Delete** where permitted. A lock icon explains
connections that are required or managed through the parent. Use the row's edit icon to change
the relationship's own fields. Candidate conditions apply in every place that offers related
records, including creation forms, table cells, grids and matrices; a general record search
finding something does not make it an allowed relationship candidate.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*

## Connection limits and concurrent edits

A relationship's allowed type pairs determine which records it may connect. A one-to-one
relationship permits one at each end; one-to-many permits one owner at the many-record end;
many-to-one permits one target at the source end. Many-to-many has no single-record limit at
either end. The same directed connection of the same kind cannot be added twice, including
repeated connections in a creation form.

A model can also allow only one counting related record beneath each ancestor of a chosen
type. Where a condition decides which targets count, targets not meeting it do not use that
slot. This is separate from a unique field value. Review the conflicting record rather than
adding another connection with the same counting role. Live writes enforce the rule; a change
set may stage a scope conflict that validation or publication then refuses.

**Add …** can create an owned record with its required relationship already filled. Its
creation and connection succeed together. **Set relationship** fills an empty single-valued
connection; the form offers a search labelled with the related type's name and any fields on the connection, then **Set**. Other actions use **Add** followed by the type's name, **Change** or **Save** as appropriate. **Remove relationship** removes only the connection immediately, keeping both records; the notice offers **Undo**.

The picker labelled **Search by name or attribute…** supports arrows across pages and Enter
to choose; Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End reach its ends. Required choices still need a value.
If an edit conflicts, **Current saved relationship** shows its version and your input is
preserved. Review before saving again. If the relationship changed after the list was read,
close the dialog and reopen it to inspect the current connection.

For a whole set, use [Replace a record’s related records](/docs/guide/use/replace-a-records-related-records/).
A stale set replacement is refused. For several source records, use
[Change relationships of many records](/docs/guide/use/change-relationships-of-many-records/).

When candidate rules change, existing connections remain and no browser list automatically
flags all newly ineligible ones. Ask a model administrator to review a dry-run copy of the
workspace when those connections need auditing.

A related-record panel with all its rows loaded, five rows or fewer and no active search puts **Search**, **Display** and any available **Sort** in its ⋯ menu. Choose an item to reveal that control. Larger panels and panels with an active search keep the controls visible.

## Longer sets and actions on several records

A mapping's summary can preview only the first twenty targets while reporting the full count.
Use **Show all …** to expand it and continue reading the remaining targets. This differs from
an ordinary table column's **+N more**, which is a count of chips that do not fit its width.
Mapping coverage includes eligible sources as well as sources with relationships already held;
a changed candidate rule does not erase an existing connection.

For a selection of records, **Change relationships** offers allowed relationships in either
direction, except parent containment and required ownership. Single-valued connections offer
**Set to** or **Clear** where permitted; many-valued ones offer **Add**, **Remove** or
**Replace with**. Preview the additions, removals and refusals, then apply with the chosen
**Change the rest** or **Change none** policy. These actions and the selection's **Delete**
preview are described in [Changing many records](/docs/use/changing-many-records/).
guide/src/content/docs/use/change-sets.m:
---
title: Change sets
description: Understand coordinated changes, review, validation, publication, approvals and model versions.
reader: steward
---

A change set is a place to prepare related changes away from live data, review their combined
effect and publish them together. It belongs to a workspace. It can contain changes across that
workspace's applications, including new records, corrections, moves, relationships and deletions.

Use one when a group of changes needs to go live together or needs review before publication.
For an everyday correction that should be visible immediately, you can
[correct the record in Live](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/). Having an open change set does not
prevent direct live work, and changing many records does not by itself require a change set.

For the working sequence, see
[Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/).

For preparing specific kinds of change, see [Relate records](/docs/guide/use/relate-records/),
[Arrange records in a tree](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/),
[Map codes between systems](/docs/guide/use/map-codes-between-systems/) and
[Fill in a relation matrix](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/).


## Where a change set starts

A change set starts from a copy of data at a particular moment. Its source is shown alongside
its name, version and model release in the change-set list; inside it, open **Details** in the
band to read its source, creator, creation time, version and model.

| Source | What the change set initially contains |
| --- | --- |
| Current live data | Live records and relationships at creation, including direct corrections made since the last publication. |
| A publication | The records and relationships in that retained snapshot, using the model release it was published under. |

**New change set**, then **Start change set**, creates the first kind. The form asks for a name; **Options** shows its start point and, where your Model release access and installed releases allow a choice, its model version. A publication's menu offers
**Start a change set from this publication** for the second. Neither action changes live data or
creates a publication. See the
[starting instructions](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/#start-or-open-a-change-set).

Starting from an older publication does not restore it over current data. Only changes deliberately
made in the change set are applied when it publishes. Newer live records and corrections that
the change set leaves untouched remain in place.

![The change-set list with its source, version and creation details](/docs/screens/change-sets-list.png)

*Above: the Network application in the Graubünden workspace lists December 2026 timetable change.
It started from current live data. The button offers a separate new change set.*

## Working apart from Live

Inside a change set, lists and record pages show the starting copy with your proposed changes
applied. Later live edits do not refresh that copy. People reading Live continue to see live
data, and other people can keep correcting it while the change set is open.

The orange **Change set** band shows its name, number of changes and state in one row on a
computer. Edits stay in this change set until it is published. The green **Live** banner says that edits apply immediately in the
workspace. Check this context before saving. The ordinary record controls work in either context;
their destination is different. See
[Make the changes](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/#make-the-changes) and
[Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/).

![An open change set above a collection of records](/docs/screens/change-set-open.png)

*Above: December 2026 timetable change is open over the Stops list. The orange banner identifies
the proposed data and offers Review changes, Validate change set and Publish change set.*

A change set can be shared by people with access to the workspace. It has its own version,
so a save based on an older change-set version can be refused after another person changes it.
Refresh and review their work before retrying. This protection is separate from the record
version described in [Records](/docs/use/records/#versions-and-refused-saves).

## Review explains the differences

Opening a change set from the list opens **Changes in this change set**, which compares it
with its starting data. Choose **See the data with these changes** to browse or edit its lists.
A newly created change set, or your own open change set from Home’s **Continue where you left off**,
opens on the data. From there, **Review changes** in the band opens the comparison. **Records** shows additions,
changes and removals, including moves and type changes where applicable. A row identifies the
record and its path; expanding it shows the before and after details. **Relationships** shows
changes to connections. Filters help narrow the review to a kind of change or a type.

For a change set started from a publication, “before” means that publication. It does not mean
today's live data. Review describes what the change set proposes; validation and publishing also
check whether those proposals can be applied safely now.

Follow [Review and validate](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/#review-and-validate)
for the controls and the route back to editing.

![The Records tab of Review changes with changed fields and record paths](/docs/screens/change-set-review.png)

*Above: the timetable change proposes changes to Valid to (exclusive) on several stops.
The Records tab lists them; Relationships is a separate tab for connection changes.*

## Validation checks the whole proposal

**Validate now** in **More change set actions** (⋯) checks the complete proposed data against its model, including required
values and relationships, allowed structure and uniqueness rules. Some problems can only be
judged across the whole set of records. Individual successful saves do not replace this check.

Validation changes no live data and creates no publication. Problems identify what needs
attention. A successful check displays **Change set validation passed**. **Publish** also runs validation before opening a confirmation; a separate validation step is optional. A failed check publishes nothing and lists the problems with links to the affected records. After editing, publication checks the new version again.

A passed check is not a reservation of live data. Someone can still make a live edit or publish
another change set before you publish. Publishing checks the current situation again. For the
sequence, see [Review and validate](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/#review-and-validate).

## Publishing and intervening live work

Publishing applies the change set's changes over current live data and records the result as
the next publication. The whole operation succeeds together or changes nothing. There is no
partially published change set.

Unrelated live work survives. A new live record is kept if the change set has not changed it;
a live correction to a record left untouched by the change set is kept too. Publication is not
a replacement of Live with the older copy you have been editing.

If both Live and the change set changed the same record, publishing is refused and names the
conflict. This can happen even when different fields were changed. The combined result must
also satisfy the model: changes that are valid separately can conflict when brought together.
An invalid combined result publishes nothing.

The confirmation is also tied to the current publication and the change-set version that were
reviewed. If these have changed meanwhile, the stale attempt is refused. Live data and the change
set are kept. Review the reported conflicts and the latest live data before preparing another
attempt; retrying does not authorise overwriting another person's work.

The [Publish instructions](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/#publish) explain the
confirmation. Success is reported as **Published as Publication** followed by its number. The
change set's work is then live and represented by that publication.

![Successful validation behind a publication confirmation](/docs/screens/change-set-publish-confirm.png)

*Above: the timetable change has passed validation and the Publish this change set? confirmation
is open. The screenshot shows a proposal awaiting confirmation; nothing has been published.*

## When approval is required

A workspace can require approval and a second person to decide. The banner then offers
**Submit for publication** where appropriate; submission validates and waits for a decision,
without making changes live. These policies do not remove separately granted Live editing rights.
Administrators configure them under [Approval policies](/docs/administer/approval-policies/).

For waiting, withdrawal, sending back and resubmitting, see
[Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/#from-submission-to-decision).
Follow [Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/) for the working steps.

## Publications keep the result

A **publication** is a read-only snapshot of a workspace created by a successful publish. It
keeps the model release it was published under, rather than showing its records through today's
definitions. Later live corrections and model changes do not rewrite it.

Publications have numbers within the workspace. A new publication becomes **Current**, replacing
the previous one's current designation. Older snapshots remain available. Current means the
designated publication; it does not mean the snapshot includes live corrections made after it.

The **Publications** list offers **Open publication**, its model version, when and by whom it was
published, and its source and predecessor. Opening one is read-only. For the relationship between
publishing and the resulting snapshot, see
[Publish](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/#publish).

For snapshot rules, see [Publications](/docs/use/publications/). To open and inspect one, follow
[Browse a publication](/docs/guide/use/browse-a-publication/).

## Withdraw a request, discard a change set, or withdraw a publication

These actions have different effects:

| Action | What happens to the proposed work | What happens to Live and publications |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Withdraw request | Ends a pending submission; keeps the change set for further editing. | Nothing changes. |
| Discard change set | Removes the change set and its staged work after confirmation. | Live records and existing publications stay unchanged. |
| Withdraw publication | Keeps the snapshot, marking it Withdrawn and no longer Current. | Live records and history stay unchanged; no publication is current. |

**Discard** is on the change-set menu when the set is editable. A pending request
must first leave its submitted state. Discarding is still possible when the change set's model
release differs from the workspace's release. See the
[change-set guide](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) for the editing context.

**Withdraw publication** is offered for the current publication, with confirmation. It does not
restore older data, select an older publication as current, delete records or retire the workspace.
A retained publication can still be the source of a new change set, as described under
[Where a change set starts](#where-a-change-set-starts).

## Preparing for another model release

A change set uses a particular model release. With the necessary access, a new change set can
use an installed newer release while Live keeps using the workspace's current release. Its
forms, fields, rules and views then come from the selected release. Incompatible starting data
can prevent creation; refiroo reports the records that do not fit.

The change set cannot publish normally until its release matches the workspace's active release.
The banner explains a mismatch. A model administrator can activate the intended release when
the data is compatible. Where migration is available, the banner also offers a reviewed move of
the change set to the workspace's release, or a move of the workspace to the change set's release
with publication. These options depend on permissions and the deployment's available features.

**Change model version** can select another release when the existing content fits it. It does
not silently convert incompatible records. A refused change leaves the original release and
content in place. Discarding remains an alternative for work that is no longer needed.

For ordinary data changes, keep the current **Model version** in the
[creation form](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/#start-or-open-a-change-set).
Coordinate a different release with a model administrator before preparing work under it.

## Who may do what

Roles granted directly or through a group determine access in a workspace. Custom roles can
combine permissions differently from the predefined roles below.

| Permission | What it allows | Predefined roles that include it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browse | Open change sets, read their records, review differences and browse publications. | Reader, Contributor, Data steward, Data owner |
| Work in change sets | Create, edit, validate and discard change sets; submit for publication. | Contributor, Data steward, Data owner |
| Publish | Publish a change set directly, subject to approval policy; withdraw the current publication. | Data steward, Data owner |
| Approve publications | Decide a submitted change set: approve and publish, or send back. | Data owner |

Creating a new change set and opening an existing one need different permissions: opening and
reviewing are reads. A reviewer with **Browse** does not thereby gain approval rights. A person
with **Publish** alone does not gain **Approve publications**. In the browser, preparing a direct
publication also needs **Work in change sets** to run validation.

Write grants can be narrowed to applications or record types. This includes edits and publication;
permission for one type does not authorise publishing changes to other types. Reading is available
across the workspace where **Browse** is granted. Model administration and workspace administration
roles do not by themselves give the data permissions above. A retired workspace permits reads
but refuses change-set work and publication.

See [Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) for the
working flow and [Records](/docs/use/records/#who-may-read-and-change-records) for direct editing
permissions.

## Model-version actions on the banner

The amber strip's **More change set actions** menu holds model-version changes and discarding.
When the releases differ, **Move this change set to …** previews converting the proposal onto
the workspace's release. Review converted values, type changes, accepted removals and items
that must be fixed, then confirm **Move change set**. This changes no Live data or workspace
release. Unchanged records then read as they are live.

The alternative **Move … to … and publish…** moves the workspace to the change set's release.
It requires model-release access, model administration and background jobs. Review the migration,
explicitly accept any removals and resolve all items to fix, including live conflicts. Confirm
**Migrate and publish** only when ready: migration and publication happen together or neither
does. Opening either preview changes nothing. A stale review needs **Preview again**.

Policy configuration belongs to
[Approval policies](/docs/administer/approval-policies/). A pending request may be withdrawn by
its submitter or an authorised approver before editing resumes.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0.*

## Special review cases and recovery

The list shows each change set's version, source, model and creator. **Untitled change set**
is the fallback name. Use **Load more change sets** for older entries. **Empty bootstrap**
identifies a change set with no starting records; its initial changes are additions only.
The ordinary browser creation button starts from current Live, not an empty root.

A created record deleted again in the same proposal is omitted from review. A record saved
back to its original fields can still appear as **Saved unchanged**: publishing claims its
version and must still check for Live changes. In **Relationships**, **Show parent links**
reveals containment connections otherwise hidden because moves already appear as Parent changes.
**Clear filters** restores the complete review; **No changes yet** and **Nothing matches** have
different meanings. Follow [Review what a change set changes](/docs/guide/use/review-what-a-change-set-changes/).

Unique field values are checked immediately, including in a change set. A direct swap of two
held unique values is refused; plan an intermediate valid value where permitted. Some
ancestor-scoped relationship conflicts can be staged but fail validation or publication.
A profile deleting records absent from a file can load only into a change set.

Publishing coordinates with Live writes in the same workspace; unrelated change sets remain
available for work. If a colleague changes this change set between background-job chunks,
the job can stop at its next chunk and retain earlier applied chunks. Read its results on
[Jobs](/docs/use/jobs/) before retrying.

A submitted change set cannot be edited or moved to another release until its request is
withdrawn by the submitter or an approver. Open work is shared with authorised workers, not
reserved for its creator. **More change set actions** holds **Validate now**, **Change model version**, **Rename** and **Discard**. **Rename** opens a form for the name; it keeps the proposed data.

A release switch protects unsaved input and reloads the pinned model before enabling edits.
Old list positions are cleared; a disappeared page can lead to another model-declared view.
If **Model version changed, but the interface could not refresh…** appears, the release change
already succeeded. Reload and check the pinned release before editing. Other action failures
say **Change set action could not be completed** and keep the diagnostic reason.
See [Prepare under the next model version](/docs/guide/use/prepare-under-the-next-model-version/).

Other useful tasks are [Continue live work](/docs/guide/use/continue-live-work-while-a-change-set-is-open/),
[Start from an earlier publication](/docs/guide/use/start-from-an-earlier-publication/) and
[Propose a change](/docs/guide/use/propose-a-change/).
guide/src/content/docs/use/relation-matr:
---
title: Relation matrices
description: Compare related records across columns, understand cell states and find missing connections.
reader: steward
---

Use a relation matrix to compare many records against another set of records and see where
connections exist or are missing. For the steps to filter, create and correct cell records,
see [Fill in a relation matrix](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/).

## Rows, columns and the records in a cell

The model defines the row type, the column type and the relationship being read. Each cell
shows the row's related records that sit under that column record in their hierarchy, possibly
several levels below it. A chip shows the first of the view's chosen cell fields holding text or a number, or the related
record's name when none does.

A language can be a column, but so can a system or another model-defined type. A matrix does
not automatically translate anything or create missing records.

Drag the right edge of the row-heading column or any record column to change its width.
With a keyboard, Tab to the edge and use the Left or Right arrow key. refiroo remembers these
widths for this view in your browser on this device. If a cell value is cut off, point at the
cell or move keyboard focus into it to read the full value in a box. The box usually appears
below the cell, or above it when space is short. Opening the cell still opens its usual dialog.

On a narrow screen, the matrix keeps all the columns currently shown. Scroll sideways to reach
those outside the screen; use the column chooser to work with a smaller selection.

![A matrix comparing operators against languages, with filled and missing cells](/docs/screens/matrix-operator-names.png)

*Above: Operator names in Names compares operators against five languages. French and German
cells contain related name records; many English, Italian and Romansh cells are None.*

![A matrix comparing municipalities against systems instead of languages](/docs/screens/matrix-municipalities-by-system.png)

*Above: Municipalities by system in Systems uses systems as columns and System codes as the
related records. This is the same view kind with a different configuration.*

## Cell states

Read the legend above the table. A model may define a condition for a related record to count,
such as a Yes/No field. This condition is separate from a record's validity dates unless the
model's rules make that connection. Not all states apply to every configuration.

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| One | Exactly one related record counts in this cell. |
| Several | More than one related record counts. This may be allowed. |
| Inactive | Related records exist, but none meets the condition for counting. This state applies when the relationship defines such a condition. |
| History only | No related record is present now, but an earlier publication held one. |
| None | No related record is present and the cell has no earlier-publication record to show. |
| Conflict | More than one record counts where the model permits only one. Inspect and resolve the extra counting records. |

Live writes refuse a second counting record where only one is allowed. A change set can
hold two before validation: the cell then shows **Conflict** with its count. Resolve the
extra counting record or connection and validate again before publishing. This state comes
from the relationship's one-per-column counting rule. A relationship cardinality limit also
restricts creation, but does not by itself give the cell a **Conflict** label.

**One** does not prove that every field is complete or that its content is correct. **None**
does not mean an existing record merely has an empty text field. **History only** refers to an
earlier publication, rather than every past edit in a record's history. Historical content in
a cell is read-only; where offered, **Create from this** uses it to prepare a new record.

## Filters and coverage

Search narrows the rows. **Filter** offers **Cell state** and a column chooser named after the
column type, followed by **to show**. A state filter finds rows with that state in at least one
chosen column across the whole list, including rows not yet scrolled into view.

By default, the matrix includes all records of its column type, even those that do not concern
the rows you are working on. Use the column chooser on its own, with **Any state**, to show only
the columns you need; **Show all** followed by the column type's plural name clears that selection.

The choice belongs to the page you have open, not to the view's saved settings, and does not
change what other people see. The page's address keeps the chosen columns and cell state, so a
bookmark or shared link opens the same selection. Opening the view again from the navigation
clears that selection; **Hide empty columns** may still leave columns out.

**Hide empty columns**, beside **Filter**, leaves out columns with no related record in any row
left by the current search and scope. A scope limits the rows to those under one record. The check
includes all those rows, not just the ones on screen. The column navigation skips empty columns,
so they do not take up places on each page of columns.

The switch is off by default. Like column widths, its setting is remembered for this view in
this browser on this device, including after a reload. Another device starts with it off.
In a change set or publication, it checks that change set's or publication's own records.

![A matrix with Hide empty columns on: only the French and German columns remain and a line says three empty columns are hidden, with Show all](/docs/screens/matrix-hide-empty-columns.png)

When columns are left out, a line below the toolbar says **N empty columns hidden**, or
**1 empty column hidden** for one. **Show all** on this line turns the switch off.
If you have chosen columns in **Filter**, those columns are shown regardless of the switch.
The switch then says **No effect while columns are chosen in Filter**. Its setting is kept
and takes effect again when you clear the column selection.

![The same matrix with the English column chosen in Filter: the switch stays on and says it has no effect while columns are chosen](/docs/screens/matrix-hide-empty-columns-chosen.png)

Choose the columns before interpreting results for cells in state **None**. If no columns were explicitly selected,
choosing a state uses the columns currently shown. A result with no matching rows means no
matches for that search, state and column selection; it does not prove coverage in omitted columns.
**Any state** removes the state restriction. Clearing the column selection also clears the state
restriction. Up to 20 selected columns can be shown at once; unselected columns can be browsed
with the column navigation when available.

![The matrix Filter panel showing cell states and a searchable column chooser](/docs/screens/matrix-filter-panel.png)

*Above: Municipality names offers Languages to show. Its legend defines counting as Active is
Yes. The same state filter can be used with columns representing systems.*

## What you can change from a cell

The model chooses the available actions: create a related record, edit its displayed fields,
link an existing record, or unlink it. Opening a populated cell shows a table, even when it
contains only one record. Each row identifies a linked record. Its displayed fields come first,
then a tinted **Attributes of the relationship** group holds values of its connection to the
matrix row. This separates a record's content from facts about the connection.

Use the filter box to find a row by its record name or displayed record fields. It does not
search the relationship's values. **Open** leads to the record's full page. **Unlink** asks
within that row: **Keep** cancels; **Unlink** removes only the connection. A required owner
connection cannot be removed on its own.

Where editing is permitted, change a value where it stands. A Yes or no checkbox saves with
one click. Other fields open a small editor over the cell, keeping the table in place. Enter
submits an ordinary single-line value; Escape cancels. A click outside closes an unchanged
record-field editor. Relationship-value editors also attempt a save when focus leaves them.
Review any error before closing. A save refreshes the cell and leaves the table open.

![A populated matrix cell with record fields, tinted relationship values and a small editor open](/docs/screens/matrix-cell-relationship-table-editor.png)

*Above: Municipalities by system in the Graubünden workspace. The Schmitten (GR) cell under
wikidata-municipalities contains one System code, Q65399. Confirmed is ticked, and the Note
editor is open over “Merged municipality, old code kept”. Open and Unlink belong to that row.*

A populated cell offers **Create** beside **Link existing** when the view permits those
actions and the cell may hold several records. A filled cell does not offer Create when
uniqueness is scoped to the column type, or the relationship lets the row connect to only one
record. That includes one-to-one, many-to-one read from its source, and one-to-many read from
its target. Empty, inactive and history-only cells can still offer creation.

An empty cell explains which row and column have no related record and offers **Link existing**
or **Create** where permitted. A read-only cell keeps the table for inspection without editing.
Historical content names its publication and remains read-only.

Creation fixes the row and column and asks where under the column the new record belongs.
Only places where the new record can meet the relationship's rules are offered. If the rules
identify a single group and it is missing, saving creates it with the record. Otherwise the
group already holding the most records used by this view in the column is selected; a tie
leaves no selection. A group holding none is never selected automatically, even as the only one.

If neither rules nor data give a place, refiroo can propose a new group using the type and
name of groups this view uses in other columns. The proposed name is editable and an existing
group can be chosen instead. Saving creates the group and record together. This uses the
current model; no model change is needed. A proposal is offered only where the structure,
required fields and relationship rules allow it. If no suitable place is found, choose or
prepare one in the app. See
[When a new group is proposed](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/#when-a-new-group-is-proposed). The created record is listed in its container too.
The record and its connection are created together. Both Create and Link existing include **Attributes of the
relationship** when the pair carries values: fill these for the new connection, separately
from the record's fields. Linking instead uses an existing candidate. Where the relationship permits it, the same
record can be linked under several rows: these are separate connections to one shared record,
not copies. Disabled candidates explain why they cannot be linked. Unlinking keeps
the record, but cannot leave an owned record without a required owner.

For an inactive cell, inspect existing records before creating another. For a conflict, review
which records should count; do not assume several records are always wrong. All saves must satisfy
the model's rules, including any limit of one counting record per row and column. A refusal
explains that the row already has a record here and **only one may count**. Where offered,
**Open the … already here** takes you to that record; inspect it before creating another.

For example, a translation matrix can create a missing name under a language and allow only
one counting name for each row and language. A mapping matrix can instead reuse a code already
linked under another row, or create a separate code. These choices come from the model's
relationships and view actions. Connected systems see the new record and connection after
publication where their access exposes them. Reuse retains the record's identity under every
row; unlink removes a connection while leaving that record available elsewhere.

To work on the cells outside the browser, see
[Export records](/docs/guide/use/export-records/). The main matrix sheet loads only its cells;
clearing a cell does not remove its contents in refiroo. In a record-field workbook, cells
holding several records are skipped. A link workbook has value sheets for editing individual
records and loads non-empty lists of connections. See
[Matrix cells and new records](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#matrix-cells-and-new-records).

## Who may edit, and refused saves

**Browse** allows reading. **Edit live** or **Work in change sets** allows the corresponding
writes, subject to scoped grants and the actions configured for the view. A read-only cell may
therefore still be readable on a record's page. See
[Record permissions](/docs/use/records/#who-may-read-and-change-records).
Publications and retired workspaces cannot be edited.

Successful Live saves apply immediately; change-set saves remain proposed. A duplicate refusal
can offer **Open the … already here** to inspect the existing record. **Changed elsewhere**
means the cell has been refreshed after another change: review it and your preserved input before
retrying. If that record is no longer in the cell, the dialog returns to its current contents.
A load error does not mean the cell is empty; retry the read.

See [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/) for ownership and candidates and
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) for reviewing and publishing proposed work.

A model administrator adds the matrix to the applications that need it. Its row, column and
cell types must be listed there; the records themselves remain in their own applications.
Showing a matrix does not move or duplicate them. A table in another application can therefore
list fewer records than the matrix reads through its relationships.

To restore an inactive cell, inspect the existing record and change the field that determines
whether it counts. For a history-only cell, **Create from this**, where offered, prepares a new
record from historical content; it does not edit the earlier publication. Check the new values
and required connections before saving. Use **Link existing** for a record already present,
and unlink only when the relationship's rules permit it.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*

## Cell previews and editing details

A cell reports its full count but previews at most five records. Open the row's record to
inspect the complete relationship list. Conditions on the target end produce **Inactive** and
uniqueness **Conflict** states only when reading the relationship in its outgoing direction;
an incoming matrix does not apply those target-end states.

Focus a cell and press Enter or Space, or click it, to open its actions. The table offers inline value edits and row actions **Unlink** and **Open**; **Create …**,
**Link existing …** and **Create from this** appear where applicable.
When choosing a container, **Goes in** offers **Search places…**. Link or move choices can stay
visible but disabled with a reason such as **Already linked** or a cardinality limit.
**Does not count** identifies a candidate outside the cell's counting condition.

A conflict can say **Changed elsewhere** or **Not saved**, with a link to the affected record.
If a stale edit finds its record no longer belongs to this cell, the dialog explains and returns
to the cell's current actions. Inspect those before choosing another change. The page address
keeps search, column selection, state and row position. Leaving a dirty form asks whether to
discard unsaved changes; cancel that prompt to keep editing.

## Read the dialog and leave it safely

A conflict cell can show **Conflict (… )** with its count. Open the cell with Enter or Space.
Use **Open** on a row to inspect a record, or **Close** to leave its table. Link candidates can
stay visible but disabled with **Already linked** or a message that the record is already
linked to as many records as allowed. Choose another eligible candidate; searching again
does not remove that limit. **Does not count** identifies a record outside the counting condition.

**Not saved** reports a failed write; **Changed elsewhere** reports a conflict and refreshed
information. Inspect the current record before retrying. **Remove cell state …** and
**Remove chosen columns …** clear those restrictions. If leaving a changed form asks
**Discard your unsaved changes?**, stay to finish or confirm that you want to abandon the input.
The saved address retains matrix columns, state and position, rather than unsaved form values.
guide/src/content/docs/use/home.md:
---
title: Home
description: Find your workspaces, continue your work and see recent changes.
reader: steward
---

Select the refiroo name in the top bar to return to **Home**. It brings together the workspaces
you can read and the work waiting for you. **Waiting for your approval**, where you may approve, and **Your change sets** appear above the workspace cards.

![Home with a greeting, workspace cards, open change sets and recent changes](/docs/screens/use-home.png)

*Above: Guide Admin can browse two workspaces. Graubünden has an open change set; Default has none.*

## Find a record

Use **Find a record in any workspace** to search record names across every workspace you may browse. Results are grouped by workspace and show the record's type and where it stands. Press ⌘K on a Mac or Ctrl+K elsewhere to focus the search, Up/Down to choose a result and Enter to open it. Escape closes the results. Check the workspace after opening a result.

## Your workspaces

The default workspace comes first. Each card shows the workspace name, its model and release, your roles there and its applications.
The **Default** badge identifies the default workspace. Choose an application button to open its
starting view in that workspace. Follow [Switch workspace](/docs/guide/use/switch-workspace/)
and [Open an application](/docs/guide/use/open-an-application/) to check the destination.

The card's counts lead to your change sets or the open change sets available to publish. A count
of open work does not say that it is validated or ready for publication.
**Nothing open here** means there are no open change sets counted on that card.

Choose **Follow** to receive a notice when someone else publishes a change set in that workspace.
Your own publications do not send you a followed-workspace notice.
The button changes to **Following**; choose it again to stop following. Following neither grants
access nor changes the records. Notices appear in your [inbox](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/).

## Continue where you left off

After you have worked in an application, a **Continue where you left off** card can name the last
place and workspace. Select it to return there. Check the banner on arrival before editing:
access and available data may have changed since your last visit.

![Home with a Continue where you left off card](/docs/screens/use-home-continue.png)

*Above: the card returns Guide Admin to Domains in Default, the last place visited.*

## Work waiting for you

**Your change sets** lists your open proposals, newest change first, with how much each changes. Open one to continue editing
or reviewing it. Follow [Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/)
for validation, review and publication.

Where you may approve requests, **Waiting for your approval** lists submitted change sets, newest
first. Each entry names the change set, workspace and submitter, and shows when it was submitted.
Choose **Review** to open its changes and decision controls. An open-change-set count on a workspace
card does not mean those change sets have been submitted for approval.

![Home showing a submitted change set under Waiting for your approval](/docs/screens/appr-home-waiting.png)

*Above: fictional Rita Approver is a Data owner in Graubünden. Guide approval example was submitted
by Guide Admin; Review opens the request.*

Follow [Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/) to review, send back or approve
and publish. A person required to obtain a second person's approval cannot decide their own
request. The [inbox](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/) also carries notices of waiting requests and
of the decisions on your submissions.

**Your recent changes** shows your latest actions. Consecutive steps on one model draft fold into one expandable line with their count; expand it to read each step. **See all your changes** opens the longer list,
with workspace, kind and period filters. See [History](/docs/use/history/) for what those entries mean.

The greeting names you and shows your roles. For the workspace-by-workspace detail, open your
[Account](/docs/use/account/). The avatar also opens theme choices and Sign out. The bell shows
unread notices and opens your [inbox](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/).

If Home reports a loading failure, retry it. If no workspace is available, ask an administrator
for Browse access to the workspace you need.

A saved address naming a workspace, application or record opens that place directly instead of
Home. If you may browse no workspace, Home says there is none yet beneath the instance's name;
it does not mean your sign-in failed. Ask an administrator for Browse access.

To manage following later, open **Settings › Notification email** and use **Stop following** beside
a workspace. Losing Browse access also stops its publication notices.

Following starts off. Losing Browse or deactivation pauses notices without deleting your
choice, so they can resume if access returns. **Stop following** deliberately removes the
choice. Follow [Follow a workspace](/docs/guide/use/follow-a-workspace/) for the steps and
[Notification settings](/docs/use/notifications-settings/) for email copies and digests.

A card can say **This version cannot open the workspace's model.** instead of offering
application buttons. Your data has not been deleted. Follow
[Open a retired or unavailable workspace](/docs/guide/use/open-a-retired-or-unavailable-workspace/)
to read the reason and find the responsible administrator.
guide/src/content/docs/use/relationship-:
---
title: Relationships tables
description: Read and change the values of connections in rows or a grid.
reader: steward
---

Use a relationships table to work on connections between records, including values belonging
to each connection. A model administrator chooses the relationship, its directed pair of record
types, columns and layout. Any application can offer this view when its model declares it.
See [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/) for direction, ownership and allowed choices.

**Reference-data example:** the connection between a stop and an operator carries Local name,
Primary contact and Inspected on. The inspection date describes their connection. Changing it
does not change a date on the stop or the operator. The model chooses these fields.

## One row per relationship

Each row is one existing connection. It shows fields of the from record, fields of the to
record and the selected attributes of the relationship. A record with several connections
appears in several rows. Names open the corresponding records; endpoint columns identify the
records rather than editing them here.

Search narrows connections by their records. The view can offer equality filters on either
record's fields and the relationship's attributes, and sorting by the fields declared for the
view. Choose a sortable heading or **Sort**. A filter's empty choice removes that restriction.
The declared grouping can put rows beneath their from or to record, with a heading and count
of matching relationships. Scroll to continue reading the list; the heading can recur when a
window starts partway through a group.

**Display** chooses columns and the reading size. **Attributes of the relationship** separates
connection values from record fields. An editable relationship value opens its editor in the
cell; Enter submits a single-line value, leaving the editor attempts a save, and Escape cancels.
A Yes or no value saves when changed. A stale save shows the current saved relationship so you
can review it before retrying. Tick existing relationships to set one attribute across them;
see [Change relationship values in bulk](/docs/guide/use/change-relationship-values-in-bulk/#change-ticked-relationships-in-the-rows-layout).

![Relationships in rows with both endpoint fields, carried values and a counted group heading](/docs/screens/relationships-table-rows.png)

*Above: Stops and operators in the Network application of the Graubünden workspace, filtered
to Local name Station office and grouped by operator. Each group shows 5 relationships,
with Stop, Stop number and the relationship values alongside tickboxes.*

## Grid: each from record once

A grid puts each from record in one row. Each shown to record supplies a column group. Under
it are the relationship attributes chosen for this view. A group heading reads the record's
label followed by **n of m linked**, showing how many matching source records are connected
to that column record. These counts cover the filtered result, not just the rows on screen.
Both header rows stay visible while scrolling. Scroll sideways to reach further column groups.

A linked group shows its connection values. An empty value means that connection has no value
for the field; it is different from a hatched **Not linked** group. **+ Link** creates a
connection for that row and column where permitted. Linking still has to meet candidate and
number rules. It does not create either endpoint record.

Edit a linked value where it stands. A Yes or no checkbox saves in one click. Other values open
a small editor over the cell: Enter submits a single-line value, Escape cancels, and leaving
the editor attempts a save. The row refreshes after saving. If another person saved first,
review **Current saved relationship** before retrying; your stale value is not silently applied.

![Relationships grid with two header rows, linked counts and two stops selected](/docs/screens/relationships-grid-two-headers.png)

*Above: Stops by operator in the Graubünden workspace, filtered to Local name Station office.
Bus und Service AG (Chur) and Rhätische Bahn each show 5 of 10 linked. Two stops are ticked,
with 2 selected and Change relationship values in the selection bar. Hatched Not linked cells
include a + Link action; Operators and Display are above the grid.*

## Narrow rows and choose column records

The grid's row toolbar offers the from type's search and filter bar, with the same fields and
operators as that type's main view, plus the view's additional filter fields. Each non-JSON
relationship attribute shown by the view is also offered as a row filter. Such a filter finds
a row when a connection to a shown column record matches. With several relationship conditions,
the same connection must satisfy them together. Hidden column records do not supply a match.
See [Lists, search and filters](/docs/use/lists-and-filters/) for the operators.

Open the menu named after the to type's plural name to choose column records. It offers that
type's own search and filters and a searchable pick list under **… to show**. Choose particular
records or narrow their fields. At most 50 column groups appear at once. When more match, the
notice reports how many are shown out of the total; narrow the column-record filter to reach
the others. **Show all …** clears the column choices and restrictions, within that display limit.

**Display** chooses the from-record fields and the relationship attributes shown under each
column record. The row's name stays visible. Search, filters, column choices and display choices
belong to this page and stay in its address. They do not change the type's main view or another
person's view. Share or bookmark the address to return to those choices.

## Select records and change their connections together

Tick source rows, or select the loaded rows and choose **Select all N matching** when offered.
That includes matching records beyond those on screen; untick exceptions to leave them out.
**Change relationship values** sets or clears one attribute at all shown column records or one
chosen column record. Its preview distinguishes values that would change, values already held
and pairs that are not linked. Adding missing connections is a separate choice.
Follow [Change relationship values in bulk](/docs/guide/use/change-relationship-values-in-bulk/)
before applying a large selection.

## Live, change sets and publications

Live saves take effect immediately. In a change set, the grid marks affected connections as
**Proposed in this change set**. Proposed values remain in that change set until publication;
other readers of Live keep seeing Live values. A publication shows its frozen values and has
no editing or linking controls. Retired workspaces are also read-only.

Reading requires **Browse** access. Changing connections needs **Edit live**, or **Work in change
sets** in a change set, for a permitted endpoint, subject to scoped grants. Required ownership
and containment connections are managed by their record operations, rather than edited here as
independent connections. A view does not grant permission by displaying a value.

If editing or selection is absent, check your context, access and whether the model offers
editable relationship fields. Bulk selection also depends on the deployment's bulk-work
capabilities. JSON values do not appear in the grid's bulk-change attribute choices.

A failed read is not an empty grid. Retry before linking anything. A refused write keeps the
saved data unchanged; correct the named value, rule or stale version before retrying. In the
grid's bulk-change dialog, the preview and **Nothing was changed** notice name each refused
connection as **From record → To record: reason** when both names are known. Otherwise, the
line shows only the reason. The same connection and reason appear once. Each notice shows
at most five lines; the preview heading counts all distinct refusal lines. Narrow the selection
to investigate any others. If a bulk request is too large, narrow the rows or column groups
and apply smaller reviewed selections.
guide/src/content/docs/use/lists-and-fil:
---
title: Lists, search and filters
description: Understand search, filter conditions, sorting, columns and navigation through long collections.
reader: steward
---

Use a collection's search and filters to find records across its whole list. The workspace
and the **Live**, change-set or publication context determine which data you search.
Follow [Find records](/docs/guide/use/find-records/) to narrow a list, or
[Continue a long list](/docs/guide/use/continue-a-long-list/) to reach a distant result.

Use the pin button in the list's header to bring this view to **Your shelf** on the [workspace's page](/docs/use/workspaces/#the-workspaces-page). The shelf stays in this browser.

## Search and combine conditions

![A collection narrowed by a date condition and a named relationship, with both shown as removable pills](/docs/screens/list-filter-pills.png)

*Above: Stops in Network, Graubünden, narrowed by Valid from and Operated by. The footer
shows the total for these conditions; the related-record chips identify each stop’s operator.*


Search matches names and fields the model makes searchable. It works together with filters;
a record must match the search and the applied conditions. **＋ Filter** groups the fields and
relationships offered by this view. Its search finds a field in a long menu. Each active
condition appears as a pill: open it to change it, or use **×** to remove it. **Clear all**
removes the filters. When both search and filters are active, **Clear search and filters**
removes both.

Text can be compared exactly, by containing text or by its beginning. Numbers and dates offer
comparisons and ranges; Yes/No fields offer the two values. **More** holds further conditions.
A missing optional value differs from a stored empty value. A range can show separate lower
and upper conditions; check both pills if a record is unexpectedly excluded.

A relationship filter can mean **Is any of** the records ticked, **Has none**, or **Has any**.
**Has any under** and **Has none under** use one ancestor and consider related records at any
depth below it. Candidate restrictions set by the model can narrow the records offered.
In Live, **Created** and **Updated** filter when a record was made or last changed.
They are different from its business validity dates. The browser has no control for viewing
all data as valid on a chosen business date.

On a phone, the condition editor opens as a sheet. Its **Show …** button includes the matching
count. An empty result says **No results match these filters**; clear or loosen conditions.
An empty collection instead says there are no records in this workspace yet. A failed read
is an error: retry it before concluding that nothing matches.

## Show or hide inactive records

A table can use a Yes/No field to mark inactive records. When the model chooses **Active**,
a record with **No** keeps its place in the list, with its name in a quieter colour and a grey
**Inactive** pill after it. If the field has another name, the pill says **Not** followed by
that name in lower case. Only **No** gets this mark; a missing value does not.

These records are shown by default. Beside **Filter**, **Hide inactive (N)** lets you narrow
the list by hiding exactly those marked records. Records with no value stay visible.
For another field name, the switch says **Hide not** followed by that name. The number counts records with **No** in this list after its search and other
filters; it is not the total for the workspace. The number is shown even when it is **0**.
The label can appear without a number while the count is loading or if that count cannot be read.

Turn on the switch to add a filter pill, such as **Active: not No**. The filter stays
in the page address, like your other conditions. Turn the switch off, or remove the pill
with **×**, to stop applying it. Choosing **Yes** for the same field in the ordinary
**＋ Filter** menu is different: that keeps only records with **Yes**, excluding records
with no value. The switch does not use that condition. If a record seems missing, check
its filter pill along with your other filters.

The mark does not change editing permissions. Where you may edit, change the value in its
cell or on the record as usual. A change set or publication uses its own values for the same
mark and switch; a publication remains read-only. A table without this model setting has
neither the mark nor the switch. See [Records](/docs/use/records/#edit-a-value-or-create-a-record)
for editing and [Find records](/docs/guide/use/find-records/) for narrowing a list.

## Sort and show columns

There is one sort at a time. Choose it from the sort menu or a sortable heading, then choose
**Ascending** or **Descending**. Without another selected order the usual order is by name;
a view can declare its initial sort. Missing field values come last, including when a list
contains types without that field. Structured fields and computed paths do not sort.
Created and updated times are not available where that context has no recorded timestamps.

**Display** chooses the shown columns and table density. Resizing a column changes how much
fits. The name column stays whole; columns that do not fit fold behind **Columns · n of m**.
Choose it to show all columns, scrolling sideways if needed. Other values stay on one line; an ellipsis marks a cut value. Hover, focus or long press to read
it in full. A related-record column shows coloured chips and **+N more** when some do not fit.
That count is not a button: widen the column or open the record to see all its connections.
A column with at most one related record can sort by its name. Multi-record columns and columns
showing a related record's field do not sort; use a relationship filter to narrow them.

## Long lists and saved position

The rows scroll inside the table while its headings and footer remain visible. The footer
shows the current range and total, page entry and start/end controls. Where available,
**Go to** seeks a value in the selected sort. The address keeps your search, filters, sort and
position, including when you return using **←** and the list’s name above a record’s title. These controls also work in change
sets and publications.

Only visible and nearby rows are drawn. The browser's Find command searches those drawn rows;
use the collection's own search to find a record anywhere in it. A later page can fail
independently: use its retry action and keep your conditions.

For actions on the results, see [Changing many records](/docs/use/changing-many-records/).
An export keeps the collection's supported filters and columns, but does not include its text
search; see [Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/).

## Display details and limits

In **Display**, the identity column is fixed and marked **(record identity)**. Other columns
have checkboxes. **Density** offers Default, Comfortable and Compact; **Per page** offers
10, 20, 50, 100 and the view's default where applicable. **Column width** offers **Narrow**,
**Wide** and **Reset display**. Choices stay on this device per view; rows per page stays in
the address too. Created/updated stamps are filters in Live rather than default table columns.

**Not set**, **Cleared** and **Empty text** distinguish missing, stored null and empty text.
Related-record chips open those records. Opening a record can take you to the application
where it belongs, even if its type was listed in the application you started from.
On phones, **Show all … columns** and **Show fewer columns** control extra columns.
Selecting text does not open or edit a row. Full-text popups close with Escape.

There are no named saved searches, saved filters or saved views. Keep the page address instead.
There is no multi-column sort, grouping or aggregation in the list, and no cross-collection
search page. **Find any record** in the top bar searches record names across the workspace;
a collection’s search stays within that collection. See [Appearance and devices](/docs/use/appearance-and-devices/)
for local keyboard commands.

## Open, edit and recover a result

Choose a row to open its record; a related-record chip opens that connected record instead.
The record heading takes focus when the page opens. Choose **←** and the list’s name above
the title to return to the saved conditions and position. A failed panel can be retried without clearing the rest of the record.
For field and relationship edits from table cells, see [Records](/docs/use/records/#edit-a-value-or-create-a-record).
To select results for an action, see [Changing many records](/docs/use/changing-many-records/).

Numeric zero and **No** are actual values, not missing fields. Use the field's missing-value
condition when looking for records without a value. A view can offer several record types;
its search covers those types, rather than every collection in the application.

## Related values in columns

A related-record column can show the connected records' names, one of their fields, or a field
from an ancestor above them. The model chooses this presentation. A column showing a related
field does not sort. When a single-record column sorts by name, records without a connection
come last. These columns do not themselves offer filters; use the relationship conditions
in **＋ Filter** when the view declares them. Hiding a related-record column in **Display**
also stops reading its connections for that column.

Relationship chips follow the data context you are reading, including a change set or a
publication. The filter pill keeps the names of your chosen related records after a reload.
A Yes/No filter applies when you choose the value; other editors can require their apply action.

The sidebar scrolls independently of the table. Both short and long collections keep their
header and footer in view; the table fills the available height even with only a few records.

## Ask for filters in words

Where **Ask** is offered beside **Search**, you can describe the records you want and review
the ordinary filters the answer becomes. A partial answer waits for your acceptance. See
[Asking a list in words](/docs/use/ask-in-words/) and its
[step-by-step guide](/docs/guide/use/ask-a-list-in-words/). Your question and list definitions
go to the provider; short related lists can include names. Calls can incur costs and are
recorded: read [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) before sending.
---
title: Publications
description: Read saved workspace snapshots and understand Current and Withdrawn.
reader: steward
---

A **publication** keeps a workspace's records as they were after a successful publish. Open one
to read a saved result without changing Live. Follow
[Browse a publication](/docs/guide/use/browse-a-publication/) for the steps.

## What a publication keeps

Publishing a [change set](/docs/use/change-sets/) applies its authored changes over current live
data and creates a read-only snapshot. The snapshot retains the model release used for publication,
including the definitions and views for reading it. Later live corrections or model changes do
not rewrite its records. A publication is not an editable copy or a list of every earlier edit;
[History](/docs/use/history/) answers who changed what.

![Publications with a numbered snapshot, its model release, publisher and Current badge](/docs/screens/use-pub-list.png)

*Above: Publication 1 was created after Guide Admin published the correction to Thusis Süd.*

The **Publications** list is newest first. Each entry names its number within the workspace,
model version, publication time and publisher, along with:

- **Publication ID**, its stable identifier.
- **Started from**, the earlier publication the change set used, or Current live data.
- **Replaced as current**, the previous current publication, or No earlier publication.

Choose **Load older publications** when offered to read further back. **No publications yet**
means nothing has been published there; live data can still exist. A loading error needs a retry.

## Reading and status

**Open publication** opens the snapshot. Its purple banner names the publication and says it is
read-only. Search, filters and the views declared in that model help you inspect it. Editing
controls are unavailable. **Back to publications** returns to the list; **Live** returns to current data.
You need Browse access to the workspace to read its publications.

![A read-only publication searched for one record](/docs/screens/use-pub-snapshot.png)

*Above: Publication 1 shows Thusis Süd with Abbreviation THSD. The banner identifies the saved
model release and the read-only context.*

**Current** marks the designated publication. A newer publication replaces that designation;
older snapshots remain readable. Current does not mean that later direct live edits are included.
**Withdrawn** means an authorised person withdrew the current designation. Withdrawal keeps the
