snapshot and Live unchanged and leaves no publication current; it does not select an older one.
With Publish permission, **Withdraw publication** is on the current publication's menu and asks
for confirmation.

## Starting work from a snapshot

With Work in change sets permission, the publication menu offers **Start a change set from this
publication**. Enter a **Name**, then choose **Start change set**. The result is editable
and keeps the snapshot's model release. This does not restore Live: only changes you deliberately
author can be published later. If its model differs from the workspace's current model, resolve
that difference before publishing. See [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) and
[Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/).

For the actions on a saved snapshot, follow
[Start from an earlier publication](/docs/guide/use/start-from-an-earlier-publication/) or
[Withdraw a publication](/docs/guide/use/withdraw-a-publication/). Export is available where jobs
are enabled; Import and editing controls are absent. Snapshot pages do not show a Live History
panel. Reading the snapshot stays under its saved model even after later activations.
guide/src/content/docs/use/importing-and:
---
title: Importing and exporting
description: Choose a file for editing or exchange, preview its changes and load it safely.
reader: steward
---

Export data to read or edit outside refiroo, then import it with a preview. Export needs
**Browse** in the workspace. Import needs **Bulk and import** and permission to write the
target record types in Live or a change set. The deployment must allow new jobs. Publications
and retired workspaces can be exported but cannot receive an import.

Use [Export records](/docs/guide/use/export-records/),
[Edit in Excel and import back](/docs/guide/use/edit-in-excel-and-import-back/), or
[Import a file](/docs/guide/use/import-a-file/).

If a workbook should become a workspace of its own, see [A workspace from a workbook](/docs/use/workspaces/#a-workspace-from-a-workbook).

## What an export contains

Open **Workspace actions › Export**. On a view, **What** starts with **This view** and its
name. This takes the view's search, supported filters, parent scope and chosen columns,
including matching rows beyond those on screen. The count line names its context and size
when known: rows × columns for a matrix, records for a tree or mapping grid.

Choose **The type**, **The application** or **The whole workspace** for whole types rather
than the view's narrowed selection. From **Settings › Data operations › Jobs**, choose types
in a workspace. **Valid on** optionally limits an export by business date; ordinary browser
lists have no equivalent selector. When a page's search is not included, the dialog says so.
A filter on a relationship's own values is not carried into a view export; read that notice
before assuming the file contains exactly the connections left on screen.

**Kind of file** offers **For editing in a spreadsheet** and, for a table view or a selection
of types, **Technical**. Other view kinds export as an editing workbook.
Technical exports offer **Excel (XLSX)**, **CSV** and **JSON Lines**. Choose **Between exported
records**, **All their relationships** or **None** for relationships. All their relationships
can refer to records outside the chosen record scope. Everything is read at one instant.
The job's file summary records its scope, counts, size and checksum. Failed or cancelled exports
have no downloadable file. Downloads remain subject to job and file retention.

## Workbook layouts

**For editing in a spreadsheet** makes an Excel (XLSX) workbook. Its shape follows the selection:

| Selection | What the workbook holds | What loads back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Table view | The table's columns, labels and order, with optional related sheets. | Editable record values and relationships, according to the saved layout. |
| Matrix showing record fields | One row per row record; each column record has a group of cell fields, with hidden cell identities and versions. | The cell records only. Row labels are for reading. |
| Matrix showing links | One column per column record, listing linked records by a chosen text field, with dropdowns backed by a value sheet per column. | Connections within each row and column; value-sheet records where editing or creation is enabled. |
| Relationships table, rows | One row per connection, showing both records and the relationship's values. | Connection values; a new row without identities can connect two named records. |
| Relationships table, grid | One row per source record, with Linked and relationship values under each target. | Connection values; Yes can link a missing pair. No removes nothing. |
| Mapping grid | One row per source record, with its target in a relationship column. | The target relationship, as in a table workbook. |
| Tree | One sheet per type, with its parent by name. | Editable records and parent choices. |
| Type, application or workspace | One sheet per type, parents' types first, with fields, parents and relationships by name. | Editable values on each sheet; a connection between sheets loads from the later sheet only. |

A view enabling **Link existing** or **Unlink** uses the link-matrix layout, even when it also
enables **Create**. Otherwise the matrix shows its cell fields. Keep hidden identity and
version columns, including those that distinguish parents with the same name.

Every XLSX export, including a technical workbook, has **About this export** as its second
sheet. Read it for the view or scope, workspace, context, search and filters, export time,
counts, relationships and load-back rules. It is for reading and is ignored on import.
CSV and JSON Lines files have no sheets.

### Text in CSV files

In a CSV export, text beginning with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return gets one
extra leading single quote, so a spreadsheet shows it as text rather than a formula. The same
rule applies when one or more single quotes already precede that character. For example,
`=1+1` is written as `'=1+1`, and `'=1+1` as `''=1+1`.

Keep that added quote when returning an exported CSV. With **Profile: None**, import removes
exactly one protective quote from record names and text fields. Returning an unchanged export
therefore leaves the original values unchanged, including their original quotes. Other quotes
are kept. This reading applies to exported CSV layouts, not to an ordinary CSV read through a
stored profile. XLSX files are unaffected; their values need no added quote.

### Matrix cells and new records

Export does not ask where new matrix records go. The relationship's candidate rules limit
which groups can hold them. If the rules identify one group and it is missing, it is created
with the record. Otherwise the group holding the most of this view's records in the column
is used; a tie gives no choice. An unused group is never picked automatically, even if it is
the only one.

When neither the rules nor data give a place, refiroo can propose a new group named like the
groups this view uses in other columns, where the structure and rules allow it. In the browser,
review or edit its proposed name, or choose an existing group. An import preview says
**will create … under …**; confirming creates the group and record together. No model change
is needed. If no suitable place is found, a new record is refused with the column and reason.
Choose or prepare a group in the app before previewing again.

The main matrix sheet loads only its cells; value sheets load their records separately.
Empty or cleared cells change nothing; removing all
values or links in a cell is done in refiroo. In the record-field layout, a cell holding several
records is shown joined and not loaded back. Edit those records individually in the app.
In the link layout, a non-empty list replaces only that cell's connections: listed records are
linked, omitted records are unlinked, and other columns are left alone. Names containing a
semicolon are written and read with a comma instead. Keep that displayed form when editing.
Where the matrix also permits creation, an unknown value can create a record in the derived
or proposed group; otherwise the list must identify existing candidates.

### Value sheets and matching fields

For a link matrix, **What each cell lists** selects **Name** or a text field of its records.
The default is Name. The file records the field so it can be read back. A linked record with
no value in that field refuses the export; choose another field or supply the missing value.
The selected values need to distinguish records within each column for import to resolve them.

Each **Values · …** sheet lists the column's eligible and already-linked records, their fields
(except fields holding JSON), their group and hidden identities and versions. Its values back
the main-sheet dropdowns. With Edit or Create enabled, edits update by identity; where Create
is enabled, a new row creates a record. A row not selected in any cell still loads. With only
Link existing and Unlink, value sheets are for reading and do not load. A matrix showing the
record's own fields has no value sheets.

A main-cell value matching a value-sheet row refers to that record. Renames are recognised by
the new value and also the old one unless another sheet row now uses it. The same new value
in both places is one record. A value in neither the sheet nor existing records creates one
where allowed, supplying its name and the chosen field only. Other required values still
apply. Duplicate matching values are refused as ambiguous. Spreadsheet edits do not themselves
synchronise the two sheets; import resolves them together.

The preview's **How the file is read** shows matching fields, values matched, value-sheet
counts and where new records go. For an unrecorded reading, it guesses the field and marks
it **Guessed**, with a note when the choice is uncertain. Choosing another field runs the
preview again. **Save these fields in the profile**, where offered, keeps the reading for
later files. No records are written before **Load the file**. Follow
[Import a file](/docs/guide/use/import-a-file/#check-how-the-file-is-read).

For steps, see [Edit in Excel and import back](/docs/guide/use/edit-in-excel-and-import-back/).

## A workbook for people

For a table view, **For editing in a spreadsheet** makes a workbook shaped by your table: visible columns in their order,
readable labels and typed cells. **Advanced: columns and sheets** changes the columns, their
order, which field a relationship column shows and which relationships get separate sheets.
Related records are exported in full, even where the browser showed only a few chips.
Record identity and versions are held in hidden columns. Keep those columns and the workbook's
saved import information when editing. Cells choosing a single record offer dropdowns from
sheets of eligible records.

Columns marked **(not imported)** are for reading. A table relationship column that owns its
records is read-only; edit those records on their own sheet or in refiroo. An ambiguous or overlong relationship cell
becomes a read-only summary pointing to its sheet. Several owned records for one parent also
form a summary rather than an editable single value. Edit the appropriate sheet instead.

When imported with **Profile: None**, the workbook is read as exported. An untouched workbook
changes nothing; changed names, fields and added rows are loaded as edits. A record changed by
someone else since export is refused unless you deliberately choose the overwrite option.
A main-sheet relationship list replaces that whole set; connections still chosen keep their
identity and values. A relationship sheet adds or updates connections, but omitting a row does
not remove one.

**Blank ordinary field and owned-record cells leave values unchanged.** To clear such a value,
use refiroo's field editor. **An empty table cell replacing a relationship set empties that set**,
where its rules permit it. Check the preview carefully when clearing a relationship list.
A required connection still cannot be cleared.

An owned-record relationship can use **Columns per parent** to make a workbook for filling in.
Each chosen parent contributes columns for its owned record's fields. Filling an empty column
creates that record under its parent and connects it to the row's record. See
[Add a language with a workbook](/docs/guide/use/add-a-language-with-a-workbook/) for the generic
steps and an example. Excel permits at most 16,384 columns; a wider layout fails when the export
job runs. Reduce parents or fields and export again.

## Read a file through a profile

An import profile tells refiroo how sheets and columns become records, names, fields, parents
and relationships, and which values identify existing records. Choose the file first, or drop it onto the file field. The form selects a profile when exactly one valid profile fits; you can still choose **None** or another fitting profile. JSON Lines uses none; CSV accepts a profile with CSV settings or a single source, and a workbook accepts any valid profile for this workspace's model. Invalid profiles and profiles for other models are omitted. The three loading-policy choices are under **Options**. Profile setup belongs to
[Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/); a steward can
[load its next version](/docs/guide/use/load-the-next-version-of-a-workbook/).

Under **Settings › Data operations › Import profiles**, **Upload the next version…** stores
an XLSX or CSV file and starts a job to read its sheets and columns. While waiting, the page
says **Checking [file name]: profiling its sheets, then reading it through the profile…**.
This reading step writes no records. If **The file could not be read** appears, follow its
reason and upload a corrected file. A file that is too large or is neither XLSX nor CSV is
refused. Checking and loading must wait until its analysis is finished.

The profile page reports **Columns**, **Values**, **Records** and **Profile against the active
release**. To inspect the source's sheets, detected lists, header rows, column statistics
and cell ranges while changing the mapping, a model administrator uses the draft's
[source pane](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/#source-file-and-draft). Those statistics show
filled and distinct values, candidate keys, frequent values, placeholders and shared values
with other columns or records in the comparison workspace; they are evidence to review.

A newer upload supersedes the earlier file for this profile in this workspace. The earlier
file is kept for the job retention period after replacement, then deleted. It does not replace
another workspace's upload. The stored file is shared with its uploader and holders of
**Bulk and import** in its workspace; a file naming no workspace requires that access at the
instance. Keep your own original if it needs to outlive this retention.

A missing or ambiguous related name is refused. Parents can be resolved from existing records
or the same file, and are loaded before children. Repeated keys with compatible filled cells,
in one sheet or several sheets of the file, combine into one record; conflicting filled values refuse all contributing rows. Blank cells
do not conflict with another row's supplied value. A profile without a stable key warns that
later uploads may create new records instead of finding earlier ones.

A profile can keep or delete records missing from the next file. Deletion of missing records
is allowed only in a change set, so review those removals before publication. A profile must
still fit the workspace's model; ask its model administrator to fix named problems.

## Preview and load

The import always previews first in the browser. Choose whether to **Load the rows that can
load** or **Load nothing unless every row loads**, and whether found records may be updated.
The preview reports creations, updates, unchanged and refused rows. Its column report shows
empty, converted, mapped and refused cells, and found, missing or ambiguous record matches.
A large file may be sampled; the page says how much was tried. Loading checks the whole file
against current data, so the final result can differ.

**Load the file** confirms; **Cancel import** ends the preview without writes. Expired previews
cannot load. Correct refused rows in the original file and resend the whole file: already
loaded rows should preview unchanged when their data and matching choices are unchanged.
Refused rows are listed on the job page; there is no download of just the refused rows.

For an export from another workspace, **Load them as this workspace's own** creates separate
records with stable identities derived for the destination. Parents and relationships stay
together; resending the file finds those copies. They do not stay linked to the originals.
**Refuse them** instead reports the source workspace on the refused rows.

Read [Jobs](/docs/use/jobs/) for progress, cancellation, access and retention.

## Read the preview's evidence

**The preview** counts **Created**, **Updated**, **Unchanged**, **Deleted**, **Refused items**
and **Rows**. **A sample** means only part of the file was tried. In **Rows in the preview**,
choose **All rows**, **Refused** or **Not loaded**. Read **Outcome** and **Why, or what it does**
for the individual rows; a refused cell gives its column and reason.

**How the file was read** explains each sheet and column:

| Count | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| Bound to | The field, name, parent or relationship receiving this column. |
| Cells and Empty | Whether the expected rows supplied anything to read. |
| Read and Value-mapped | Values successfully read or translated through the profile's value choices. |
| Refused | Cells that could not be used; correct their stated cause before loading. |
| Found, Not found and Ambiguous | Whether a name or key identified exactly one existing record. |

A **Check** marker calls attention to a column. The **Read as exported** summary identifies a
workbook using its saved import information. **This import** records the chosen file, profile
and load policy. After confirmation, **The result** reports **Applied items**, **Refused items**
and **Not loaded**. Read that result even when the preview looked right.

![Import preview with one refused Height cell, 115 unchanged rows and per-column reading counts](/docs/screens/import-preview-columns.png)

*Above: one row in the reference Stops workbook is refused because Height (m) contains
“not a number”. The column counts show 115 height values read and one refused; the preview
has written nothing.*

## Profiles and recurring keys

In **Settings › Data operations › Import profiles**, **Valid** means the profile fits its
model; **Needs a fix** means a named problem must be resolved. Neither guarantees that every
row in the next file is valid. **Not loaded yet** means no retained last load is shown.
**Load more profiles** continues the catalogue. If there are no profiles, ask a model
administrator to prepare one through [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/).

**Last load** offers **Open the change set review** while its work is proposed, or
**Open the load's job** for the retained operation. A load can be missing here because it has
passed retention. Uploading the next file checks it without changing records. Accepting a
column rename or ignoring a new column changes the profile used for subsequent checks; review
those decisions with its owner. See [Load the next version of a workbook](/docs/guide/use/load-the-next-version-of-a-workbook/).

A matching key may combine several columns. Every component must be present and identify at
most one stored record. Fill incomplete keys or ask the profile owner to resolve ambiguous
combinations. Changing only a display name need not create a new record when a stable key still
finds the original.

An export uses one consistent reading of the data. If its worker restarts after a crash, it
starts the export again rather than appending new data to half of an old file. Follow the job
until it has a completed file. Home itself has no Import or Export action; open an application
or use Jobs. A record's History is a list of changes, not an earlier-state viewer, and offers
no restore or undo. See [History](/docs/use/history/).

## What the next file can change

A profile belongs to one model. Use it in a workspace running that model; a different model
needs its own suitable profile. A file carrying records from another workspace with a
different model cannot load them as counterparts: those rows are refused while other valid
rows can load under the chosen load policy.

The next-version check can recognise a renamed header when its column stays in the same
position and holds the same values. **Accept** saves that rename; **Ignore** saves the decision
not to load a new column. Each decision checks the file again before loading.

For a lookup allowing one related record, a changed value in the next file switches the
connection to the newly named record. Missing records are kept unless the profile says to
delete them. That deletion also removes their connections, but refuses a record that others
depend on. Review the refused items and the change set before publishing.

## File refusals and completion notices

A preview can refuse all rows participating in a parent cycle, rather than loading either
record into an invalid hierarchy. If the file cannot be read or does not fit the profile,
loading changes nothing. Correct the file or ask the profile owner to repair its mapping.

The tab that starts an import reports when its preview is ready and when loading finishes,
unless you already have that job open. A collection reloads after an import started in this
tab loads into it. For exports, the completion notice offers **Download** and the job page;
a failed or cancelled export instead reports that state. Keep the tab open for these notices,
or return to **Jobs** to inspect the result later.

A stored upload used by an import profile is visible to its uploader and to people allowed
to import in its workspace. Treat the file as shared with those workers when choosing what
to upload. Losing a write permission can stop a job at its next step; review its applied counts
before asking an authorised colleague to continue the work.

## Let the assistant prepare the import

When the assistant is enabled and you have the required access, **Import…** in the workspace
menu first opens **Load a workbook**. Give it one XLSX or CSV file, instructions, or both.
It proposes the model and load for review rather than publishing records. **Import without
the assistant…** opens the ordinary manual import. See
[Loading with the assistant](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/) and
[Load a workbook with the assistant](/docs/guide/use/load-a-workbook-with-the-assistant/).
The whole file and your words go to Claude Code, turns can incur costs, and task files are
retained; [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) explains those rules.

## Remove an uploaded file or an import profile

Open **Settings › Data operations › Import profiles** and select the profile. People with
**Bulk and import** are offered the deletion buttons; without that access the buttons are absent.
Deleting either item does not undo a load or remove records already loaded into a workspace.

- **Delete the file…** asks **Delete <file name>?**. **Delete the file** removes that upload,
  its stored cells and the analysis of its sheets and columns. This analysis is not the saved
  import profile that maps the columns. A check still reading it is
  asked to stop. The import profile stays. Upload the file again before checking or loading it.
- **Delete the profile…** asks **Delete the profile <profile name>?**. **Delete the profile**
  removes the saved instructions for reading the workbook and returns you to the profile list.
  Loading the workbook again needs a new profile saved by installing a model draft that holds it;
  ask a model administrator to prepare this through [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/).

Choose **Cancel** in either confirmation to keep the item. A refusal stays in the confirmation
with its reason. If someone changed the file or profile since you opened it, cancel, reload the
page and inspect the latest version before trying again. There is no undo button for either
deletion. Keep the original workbook outside refiroo if you need to upload it later.

![Import profile showing separate buttons to delete its uploaded file and the profile](/docs/screens/use-import-profile-delete-actions.png)

## Default file and preview limits

An import normally accepts a file of up to 200 MiB. Its preview tries at most 10,000 items;
**Load nothing unless every row loads** normally allows at most 10,000 items. Your operator
can change these limits. Read **Limits** on Jobs and the limit reported by the import form.
If a file exceeds the limit, split or reduce it, or agree a suitable limit with the operator.
If splitting a recurring workbook whose profile deletes missing records, ask its owner first:
each part could otherwise treat records in the other parts as missing.

Jobs and their downloadable files are normally retained for seven days. Download an export
before its **Kept until** time. A retained import profile can outlive its last load's job;
**Last load** is not an archive of every workbook loaded through it.

![Confirmation to remove an import profile while retaining previously loaded records](/docs/screens/use-import-profile-delete-confirm.png)
guide/src/content/docs/use/loading-with-:
---
title: Loading with the assistant
description: Understand assistant proposals, checked records, saved layouts and the steps from acceptance to publication.
reader: steward
---

Give the assistant a workbook, instructions about existing records, or both. It prepares work
for you to review. Use [Load a workbook with the assistant](/docs/guide/use/load-a-workbook-with-the-assistant/)
for a file, or [Change records with the assistant](/docs/guide/use/change-records-with-the-assistant/)
for instructions alone. A task is the saved work you return to as it proposes, checks and loads.

## Access and information sent

The built-in assistant must be enabled by your operator. It uses Claude Code, independently
of the AI provider used by Search / Ask and mapping suggestions. It needs the send level values,
**Use AI proposals**, **Bulk and import**, **Work in change sets** and enabled background jobs.
Model changes also need the model permissions; installing a new release needs **Model release**
at instance level. Retired workspaces and publications cannot receive imports.

Claude Code receives your words, the workspace's model and the whole file, if supplied. It can
read the workspace records it needs, within your permissions and their application and type
restrictions. It never approves, publishes or activates a model. Turns can incur charges or
consume a subscription allowance. Tasks, workbooks and session transcripts are retained while
the work can continue and then cleaned up; the normal task retention is 90 days. Read
[AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) for costs, sending and retention before starting.

## What the assistant prepares

The dialog takes one XLSX or CSV file, within the deployment's import size limit. Instructions
are limited to 4,000 characters. Without a file, instructions are required. Images and documents
are not data files for this task. You cannot attach several files, schedule a task or transfer
its session to a colleague. Its requester and the workspace's administrators can read it.

When no saved layout fits, one session reads the workbook, the current model and the workspace's
records. It changes the model draft where needed and turns the file into proposed records and
relationships. It finds existing records by reading them, so explain which fields identify a
record when names alone are ambiguous. The engine checks every proposed record and relationship
against the draft's model and workspace data without saving the changes. The assistant writes
no import profile. One file row can supply several records or relationships.

The same instructions can produce different proposed structures on separate runs; inspect each
proposal rather than assuming it repeats a previous design. An update can leave the model unchanged and prepare only record changes. Instructions can also
ask for relationships or a model change. The assistant is limited to capabilities refiroo supports;
its notes explain when it cannot complete a request. A turn that runs beyond the session limit (30 minutes unless the operator changed it) is stopped like your Stop,
and the task goes back to where you can tell the assistant to go on or try again. While other tasks hold the assistant, the page says how many are ahead.

## Review the proposal

**The assistant’s proposal** says what it understood and lists the types it adds, changes or
loads, with attributes and record counts. For a proposal with a model draft, **Show the model
change** expands **The model: what changes**, including changes such as a field becoming optional.
A words-only task that needs no model change says **No change to the model.** It has no model
draft, model-change detail or model editor button.
For a workbook, **What the load does** shows new records, existing records matched, new
relationships, refused items and rows read. The type table separates **New**, **Matched**,
**Changed**, **Refused** and **Linked to**. A matched record can be changed or unchanged. Open a
type's row with a click, Enter or Space for example records with their values, links and source
cells. Examples show only some of the records the engine checked.

**One name twice in one type** identifies a name shared by records touched by the load and says
whether they sit at the top level or under parents. It is a finding, not proof that the records
are unwanted duplicates. Check it against the file and your intent. Expand **Where each part of
the file goes** for sheet and cell ranges and what they become.

Under **Checks**, read every **Needs attention** item. Check types holding records that the
proposal leaves out, any filled cells left out and **Columns left out**. Compare new records
with matched ones: an unexpected new record can mean an intended update failed to find its
record. A successful engine check does not prove the design means what you intended. Empty
cells hold no value; they do not by themselves mean a row was skipped.

![Workbook proposal showing the checked load summary, results by type, questions and acceptance controls](/docs/screens/use-assistant-proposal.png)

*Above: the workbook proposal for the Graubünden reference data, scrolled to What the load does
and its results by type. Questions shows the assistant’s assumed answer and the other choices.
Accept and load to change set is available; nothing has been installed or loaded.*

**Questions** shows the answers the assistant assumed, only for what a person decides. Keep every choice and the answers are recorded without another turn; change a choice and use **Answer and
design again**. **Tell the assistant what to change** followed by **Send to the assistant**
continues the same session with your correction. When there is a draft, **Open in the model
editor** lets you edit it directly; the session reads it again before continuing. It cannot change a draft
held by another assistant task and must use its own. Close in the editor returns to the task. The draft’s history records who asked for the
assistant’s model steps; it does not mark every model element as Proposed.

If the draft changed after the check, **What the load does** warns that accepting checks every
record again first and loads nothing if any is refused. Ask the assistant for a revised proposal
if the shown records no longer describe your intended result. A saved-layout check that predates
an edit must be renewed before loading. Concurrent task changes reload the latest state and ask
you to check before trying again.

## Accepting, loading and publishing

For a workbook, **Accept and load to change set** makes the engine install a release if the model changed,
open a change set and load exactly the checked records and relationships as one batch. No
assistant turn runs. With no model change, the change set uses the workspace's current release.
No model is activated and no records are published by this acceptance.

If an edited draft fails its new check, nothing is installed or loaded. If the data changed
since checking and any item is refused during loading, none of the batch is loaded and its
change set is discarded. The task names the refused records and their source cells. Tell the
assistant what to correct, then review and accept its revised proposal. A release already
installed before a load refusal can remain installed.

For a words-only task with no model change, **Accept** lets the session prepare a new change set
on the workspace's current release. It installs and activates nothing. Model-only and record-move
proposals keep **Accept the model** and the migration or staged-move endings described below.
A file whose records are all stored already is a normal outcome: the check shows every record as
already there, **Accept** ends the task loaded with nothing new, and the change set it leaves is empty
(discard it from the task). A session that loads without the engine's check and names an empty
change set is not reported as a successful load.

The result names the change set and its counts. **Review the change set** opens its normal
review. Check the actual rows and relationships, validate, then submit for approval or publish
as your access and the workspace’s policy allow. If the load uses a different model version,
review offers a combined move of the workspace and publication. A model administrator with
publication permission reviews the migration preview and confirms **Migrate and publish**;
a separate activation first is not required. See [the workbook load’s publication step](/docs/guide/use/load-a-workbook-with-the-assistant/).
The assistant does not confirm it. A second-person approval rule still applies to the person
who asked for the work.

The saved-layout path has its own **What the load would do** check and load button. Read
**What confirming does, in this order**: when that path changes the model, **Activate the model
and load** explicitly activates it as your confirmed action before loading the change set.
A subsequent load failure does not undo that model activation. A record load always waits
for publication to reach Live.

A task's bar below the top bar names the current step and next action. It follows you into
the model editor and change-set review opened from the task. You can leave while a turn works
and return through its entry under **Settings › Data operations › Jobs**; its completion is announced.
See [Jobs grouped under a task or a draft](/docs/use/jobs/#jobs-grouped-under-a-task-or-a-draft)
for the group’s state counts and **Open the task**.

## The next file and the saved profile

A workbook loaded from the assistant's checked records and relationships saves no import
profile. Send the next file of the same layout to the assistant again. Explain how its contents
correspond to records already held so the proposal can match them correctly.

A separately saved import profile can still load a matching file without an assistant session
or AI cost.

A fitting saved profile takes the engine's own path: you still review its proposal and row
check, but no assistant session starts. Sheets also present in the earlier file but deliberately
left out by the profile do not prevent reuse. A new sheet needs the assistant to review it. After the earlier task and its file expire,
a sheet the profile left out can also require a new session because that comparison is no
longer available. A saved layout can ask its unresolved file-value questions again on each repeat.
If **The saved layout does not fit this file** appears, **Read it with the assistant** starts
a session on that task and file. The saved-layout check also offers **Back to the proposal**
and a correction box. See [Load the next version of a workbook](/docs/guide/use/load-the-next-version-of-a-workbook/).

## A model change that moves records

The workspace menu's **Change this model…** asks what should change, with an optional workbook.
It additionally needs **Model authoring** and **Model release**. The proposal says what becomes
what and shows existing record counts. Review the model in the
[model editor](/docs/model/the-model-editor/) if you need to inspect its structure.
For the model administrator’s full task, follow
[Change a model with the assistant](/docs/guide/model/change-a-model-with-the-assistant/).

For whole types becoming other types, acceptance installs a release but moves no records.
**Preview the migration** opens the migration with the proposed choices. You can go **Back to
the proposal**. A person with Model release confirms it: the records move live with their IDs,
values, relationships and history. There is no change set or its approval step for that migration.
When the request changes only the model and asks nothing of the records (for example, adding views), the task ends the same way with a migration that moves no type: confirming it puts the workspace on the new model and every record stays as it is.

A whole-type move and a partial move need separate tasks.

For part of a type moving, the task normally shows **Three steps are yours**: activate a release
holding old and new types, review and publish the change set under the usual approval rules,
then activate the final release to remove the emptied types. If old types remain in the final
model, it shows **Two steps are yours** instead. The first activation moves no records; publishing
moves them. A remaining record in a type being removed blocks the final activation. Each step
appears when it is ready; someone with Model release performs activation. A large split can be
slow because the records are changed individually. See [Model migrations](/docs/model/migrations/).
If the task expires before the final activation, the installed release remains available under
Settings › Model so an administrator can complete the step.

## Stop, correct or end a task

Follow [Continue or correct an assistant task](/docs/guide/use/continue-an-assistant-task/) for the
buttons. These states need different decisions:

| What you see | How to continue |
| --- | --- |
| Working on it or Loading | **Stop** ends the turn. You can also leave the page while it runs. |
| A stopped correction with an earlier proposal | The last proposal returns with a note. The draft may already contain changes from the stopped turn: inspect it before continuing. Stop does not rewind the draft. |
| A stopped load | The change set being loaded is discarded and its jobs stopped. Return to the accepted proposal and tell the assistant how to continue. |
| The assistant stopped or You stopped the assistant | Read the task's notes. Use the words box, **Try again as it was** or **Go on as it was**, open the draft, or **Discard this task**. Even a session that never started can be tried again with corrected words. |
| The engine could not apply this proposal | Read the reason above the correction box, then tell the assistant what to change. |
| A loaded change set that is wrong | Use **Not what you wanted? Tell the assistant** and **Discard and load again**. Confirmation removes that entire change set, including hand edits. For a workbook load, the same session revises and checks the proposal; review it and choose **Accept and load to change set** before loading again. |
| A load you want to abandon | **Discard the change set** ends the task and removes that prepared work. Live records are unchanged. |
| A refused migration or activation | Read the engine's reason on the task and tell the assistant what to change. |
| Your access no longer permits the next step | The page names the permission needed and lets you copy the task link for a workspace administrator. |
| Published | The task confirms publication and offers **Change this model…** and **Ask about these records…** where your access allows. Start new work to correct published data. |
| Discarded | The session has ended. Use **Start again** in the journey bar or return to the workspace. |
| Expired or unknown task | The page explains it is not kept or does not exist and offers **Go to the workspaces**. |

The newest three task notes are shown; older notes are folded. **Discard this proposal** removes
the proposal and its draft; closing the proposal keeps it for later. Discarding a loaded task
also discards its change set. Unused model releases installed by a session are retired at its
end; releases still in use are kept. Published changes and their assistant origin remain in
[history](/docs/use/history/#work-prepared-by-an-assistant) after the task expires.

A refused workbook batch leaves no record or relationship changes and discards its change set.
Other task paths can leave a prepared change set after failure. If the task says it loaded
changes before stopping and offers **Review the change set**, open it before retrying: a failed
turn does not prove that no proposed work remains. Live is unchanged until publication.
---
title: Asking a list in words
description: Turn a question into ordinary list filters and understand what the list can express.
reader: steward
---

Use **Ask** when you know which records you want but are unsure how to set their filters.
The answer becomes search text and ordinary filter pills. It changes which records you see;
it does not change any record. Follow [Ask a list in words](/docs/guide/use/ask-a-list-in-words/).

## Where Ask is offered

A table collection offers **Search** and **Ask** beside its search box when an AI provider is
enabled and you have **Browse** and **Use AI proposals** in the workspace. Ask works in Live,
a change set and a publication. It is absent from mapping grids, trees and the Changes page.
You can always use the list's ordinary [search and filters](/docs/use/lists-and-filters/).

## What a question can become

Ask can use the view's filter fields and every relationship of the listed record type,
including relationships absent from **＋ Filter**. In Live it also offers **Created** and
**Updated**. Those two times are unavailable in change sets and publications.

You can ask for field values, missing relationships, or records with a relationship below a
named ancestor at any depth. The result uses the list's existing conditions. Ask cannot
choose a sort order or find who changed a record. Use the sort controls or record History
for those tasks. Questions are limited to 500 characters.

When you name a related record, refiroo looks for an exact name, ignoring letter case, then
for a single name containing your words. No match or several matches means that part is not
expressed; it does not pick a record for you. Use a more complete name and ask again.
Choosing records by the meaning of their names needs the short-list names described below.
For larger lists, give an exact or unambiguous partial name.

## Read the result before relying on it

A complete answer applies its search and filters to the list, replacing the previous search
and filters. The line **Your question became these filters. Change or remove any of them.**
appears. Check each pill: the provider can misunderstand your intent. Open a pill to edit it,
remove it with **×**, or return to Search. The current sort stays as it was.

If any part cannot be expressed, the list stays as it was. A warning names the missing part
and shows **What it could do:** as dashed pills. **Use these filters** applies only that
partial answer. Review what was left out before choosing it. A failed request applies
nothing and keeps your question, so you can correct it, retry or use Search instead.

![Ask showing a part it cannot express and the filters available for review](/docs/screens/use-ask-partial.png)

## What is sent and kept

Your question, today's date, field names and relationship definitions go to the configured
provider when you press Enter, not as you type. At structure, no stored record names are
included. At samples or values, related-record and ancestor names are also included when
their type's list contains at most 50 records in this context. That short list is sent whole.
Your own words are sent at every level, so include only information you are allowed to send.

Requests can incur provider costs and are recorded with their outcome. Request and answer
text is kept in the call log only if the operator enables it. Read
[AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) for permissions, retention and provider privacy.
guide/src/content/docs/use/ai-and-your-d:
---
title: AI and your data
description: Understand who can use AI help, what is sent, the costs and what is kept.
reader: steward
---

Before asking AI for help, check that the task and the data suit your organisation's rules.
AI can misunderstand a question or propose the wrong change. You review its work before
publishing it. Asking a list changes its filters, not its records.

## Which help is available

refiroo offers three separate kinds of help. Your operator chooses which are enabled.

- An AI provider turns a question into list filters, proposes mapping targets and explains changes.
  The provider can use the Claude API or a compatible service, including a model run inside your organisation.
- The built-in assistant uses Claude Code to read a workbook or your instructions and prepare
  a model and records for review. It can be enabled without the provider.
- An external assistant can connect through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), if your organisation
  enables agent access. It acts within your access, limited to reading and preparing change sets.

The **Use AI proposals** permission is needed for built-in AI actions. The predefined
**Data steward**, **Data owner**, **Model administrator**, **Workspace administrator** and
**Integration administrator** roles include it. Your grant determines which workspaces it covers.
Other permissions still apply: AI access alone does not let you import, change a model or publish.
An absent action can mean the feature is disabled, the data allowed to be sent is insufficient,
or you do not have the required access.

## What leaves the instance

An operator sets a ceiling on what refiroo's AI features may send. These are the send levels
named by the screens:

| Send level | What it allows |
| --- | --- |
| structure | Names of types and fields, headers, their rules and counts; no stored record values. Your question or instructions are still sent. |
| samples | Also sample values, normally up to a limit chosen by the operator. Questions in words have the short-list exception below. |
| values | The record values the feature needs. The sample limit does not cap this level. |

[Asking a list](/docs/use/ask-in-words/) sends your question, today's date and the fields and
relationships the list can filter. At samples or values, it also sends related-record names when
that type's list has at most 50 records in the current context. Ancestor names can be included too.
Those short lists are sent whole, regardless of the ordinary sample limit. At structure, no
stored record names are included. Anything you type into the question is sent at every level.

[Proposed mapping targets](/docs/use/mapping-grids/#targets-proposed-by-ai) need values. The
provider receives source and candidate target names and the fields shown by the grid.
[The assistant](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/) also needs values: it receives your words,
the workspace's model and the whole workbook, if supplied, and reads the records its task needs.

[Explaining a period](/docs/use/history/#what-changed-in-a-period) sends counts and model labels.
Names of records, people, change sets and files are included only at values. Explaining a model
change sends the model's differences and counts, without record values. See
[Explain a model change](/docs/guide/model/explain-a-model-change/) for that model-administrator task.

Read the line beside an action before sending. An external provider receives the information
under your organisation's agreement with it. A local provider can keep it inside the organisation.
These send levels do not control what an external MCP assistant sends on after reading permitted data;
check that assistant's settings too.

## Costs and saved information

AI requests and assistant turns can incur charges or consume your organisation's subscription
allowance, even if they fail or you later discard the work. Your operator can see call records
under **Settings › Administration › AI**, including who asked, what for, the outcome, tokens and
reported cost. A missing cost means none was reported; it does not mean free usage. Provider
billing and Claude Code billing are separate. A saved workbook layout that fits the next file
can prepare it without another assistant session and without AI cost.

Call metadata is kept. Request and answer text is not kept in the call log by default; an operator
can enable it, normally for seven days. Assistant tasks keep instructions, proposals, checks and
the workbook for the configured retention period, normally 90 days after completion or the last
change. The session's working files and Claude Code transcript remain while the task can continue,
including after a failure, stop or load awaiting publication. They are removed when the completed
work is next checked, or on expiry. Turning off call-text logging does not remove those files.
Published records and their history remain when a task expires. The provider's own retention is
separate. See [AI operation and retention](/docs/run/ai/) for the full settings and limits.

## Your review stays necessary

Proposed mappings and loaded records wait in a change set. You correct them and follow the
workspace's normal approval and publication rules. The assistant cannot approve, publish or
activate a model. A whole-type model migration is different: a person's explicit migration
confirmation moves the records live. Read that preview before confirming it.

An external assistant cannot approve or publish either. If you sign in for one, refiroo's sign-in
page names the assistant and where it returns. That name is supplied by the assistant itself.
Check both before allowing it. Find its session in [your account](/docs/use/account/) to sign it out.
guide/src/content/docs/use/changing-many:
---
title: Changing many records
description: Select records, preview a bulk change and understand refusals before applying it.
reader: steward
---

Change fields or relationships across a collection, or delete selected records, after reviewing
a preview. These actions need **Bulk and import**, permission to write the selected types in the
current context, and a deployment that allows jobs. Publications and retired workspaces are
read-only. A Contributor works in a change set rather than Live.

## Choose exactly which records

Tick individual row checkboxes, use Shift for a range, or select the rows shown. The selection
bar counts them. **Select all … matching**, or Cmd+A when the collection selection handles the
shortcut, selects every record matching the search and filters, including rows not yet drawn.
Untick individual records to leave them out. **Clear selection** removes the selection.
Check whether the bar says a count or **All … matching except …** before starting an action.

The deployment limits how much one change can hold. An oversized selection reports its count,
the limit and what to do: narrow the list or select fewer records. A relationship change may
make several changes per selected record, so its limit can be reached sooner.

## Preview, then apply

- [Change values](/docs/guide/use/change-values-of-many-records/) sets or clears selected fields.
  Fields not added to the change keep their values.
- [Change relationships](/docs/guide/use/change-relationships-of-many-records/) adds, removes or
  replaces one kind of connection. It does not edit fields on the connections themselves.
- [Delete many records](/docs/guide/use/delete-many-records/) includes children and owned dependants.
  Independent connected records stay.

Choose whether a refusal should **Change the rest** or **Change none**. The all-or-nothing
choice has its own deployment limit and disappears when this change exceeds it. Deletion uses
the corresponding delete choices. Nothing is written by **Preview**. Read the counts of changes,
unchanged records and refusals, and open refused records to inspect their reasons.

**Apply** checks the records again. Someone else's saved changes are refused instead of
overwritten. A relationship change also checks that the connections have not changed since
preview. A deletion checks the exact impact, including children added in the meantime.
For a sampled deletion preview, only items whose impact was actually previewed are authorised;
other items need a new preview and may be refused during execution.

## Finish or leave the dialog

The result reports what actually changed, what did not need changing and what was refused.
**Preview again** retries against the data as it is now. The selection remains for another
change; deleted records leave it. Do not assume a finished job means every item succeeded.

Before applying, **Back**, closing the dialog or clicking outside cancels its waiting preview.
**View job** keeps the preview waiting on its [job page](/docs/use/jobs/), where you can apply
or cancel it. Once applying, **Keep running in the background** leaves the job working.
Stopping a job does not undo chunks it has already committed. If a colleague changes a shared
change set between chunks, the next chunk can fail while earlier chunks remain applied.

![Selected rows and selection bar, followed by a Change values preview with changed, unchanged and refused counts and Apply.](/docs/screens/bulk-selection-preview.png)

## Default limits

Normally one background change can hold up to 1,000,000 items, a preview tries at most
10,000 items, and **Change none** or **Delete none** can hold at most 10,000 items.
The operator can change these limits; use the count and limit shown by your dialog.
An item is a requested change, so one selected record can contribute several items to a
relationship change. A sampled preview is not a promise that all remaining items can succeed.

For **Delete**, the refusal choices are **Delete the rest** and **Delete none**. The first
allows valid deletions to continue when another item is refused. The second applies none
unless the whole operation can succeed within its limit.
guide/src/content/docs/use/records.md:
---
title: Records
description: Understand records, their fields and relationships, validity, versions, history and access.
reader: steward
---

A record is one item of reference data: something your organisation names, describes and connects
to other items. Its record type defines the fields it holds, the relationships it may have and
where it belongs. The model defines these types; your records are the data kept using them.

On a desktop, opening a table row shows the record beside its list, keeping your place. Choose **Expand to full page** to open the record's page. On a phone, the row opens the full page directly.

For the steps to locate and inspect one, see [Find records](/docs/guide/use/find-records/).

For choosing the dataset and view, see [Workspaces](/docs/use/workspaces/) and [Applications](/docs/use/applications/).
For connected records and placement, see [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/) and
[Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/). For coverage across records, see
[Relation matrices](/docs/use/relation-matrices/) and [Fill in a relation matrix](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/).


## Workspaces, applications and types

A **workspace** holds a set of reference data under a model release. An **application** groups
the types and views you work with. A **record type** defines one kind of item. The applications,
types and labels you see depend on your workspace's model.

A record belongs to a workspace and an application, and has a record type. A relationship may
connect it to a record in another application within the same workspace, where the model allows
that connection. Being in different applications does not make the records separate copies.

The workspace selector identifies the data you are working on. The context above the records
identifies **Live**, a **Change set**, or a publication. Live shows current data; a change set
holds proposed changes; a publication shows a saved, read-only snapshot. The same record can
therefore look different in these contexts. See [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) for how
they fit together.

![Home showing a workspace card with three applications](/docs/screens/home.png)

*Above: the Graubünden workspace offers Network, Systems and Names. These are applications in
the example model; other models can define different applications and record types.*

## What a record holds

A record has a stable **ID** as well as its displayed name. Renaming it keeps its identity,
relationships and place in the hierarchy. Its ID is separate from a business code stored in a
field: changing a code does not create a different record.

**Fields** hold typed values, such as text, numbers, dates and Yes/No values. Zero and No are
values, rather than empty fields. Depending on the model, a field may be required, read-only,
unique, or limited to a range. A save that breaks a rule is refused with a reason. A blank optional
field means that no value has been set.

A model can hide a field from record forms and the fields panel. A hidden field is absent,
rather than an empty field you should fill. Hiding it does not delete its stored value.
Ask the model administrator if information needed for your task is missing. Read any help
text below a form field: it explains that field's use. The model can give a field different
help for different record types. Read-only fields can be shown but cannot be changed.

The model also chooses how the record's page presents it. Fields may appear in the heading or
in a details panel; other panels show children, relationships and history. For ways to edit a
single value or several fields together, see [Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/).

![A record page with a heading, hierarchy path, fields and relationship tables](/docs/screens/stop-details.png)

*Above: Chur Wiesental is a Stop in the Network application of the Graubünden workspace.
Stop details holds its number, abbreviation and other fields; Modes and Operator show connected
records. This earlier view shows the ID and version directly in the heading; open **Details**
in the current header to see them.*

## Relationships and a place in the hierarchy

A **relationship** is a named connection between records. The model defines its meaning in each
direction, which types it connects, whether it is required and how many connections are allowed.
A connection can carry fields of its own. A relationship table shows connected records using
the fields and labels chosen by the model. In the Relationships panel, the connection's own
values follow the related record's columns. **Display** lists them under **Attributes of the
relationship**. They cannot be used to sort this panel; see [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/).

A **parent** gives a record its place in a hierarchy. Some types can stand at the top; others
need a parent of an allowed type. The line above a record’s title starts with **←** and the list’s name when you opened it from
a list, followed by its ancestors where the model shows them. Choose the list’s name to return. A parent is
more than an ordinary connection: changing it moves the record in the hierarchy and keeps the
parent connection consistent. An invalid parent or a move that creates a cycle is refused.

Relationships can express ownership or an association with an independent record. This matters
when deleting: a record that belongs to an owner can be removed with it, while an independent
record remains. The deletion section below explains the distinction.

See [Find records](/docs/guide/use/find-records/#inspect-the-record) for inspecting these panels, and
[Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/#change-several-fields-together) for the form
that includes **Parent**. The model determines which parents and related records are available.

## Records that belong to another record

A model can define records that belong to an owner through a required relationship. Each owned
record has its own fields, identity, version and history. Its owner can be in another application
in the same workspace. This is a general relationship rule, not a feature tied to one domain.

A relationship panel on the owner's page lists the connected records. **No relationships yet**
means none are connected there. A [relation matrix](/docs/use/relation-matrices/) can compare
owners against column records and show their owned records in the cells, where the model declares
that view. Follow [Create an owned related record](/docs/guide/use/relate-records/#create-an-owned-related-record)
or [Fill in a relation matrix](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/) for the steps.

![A record's related-record sections, one populated and one empty](/docs/screens/stop-relationships.png)

*Above: Chur Wiesental has two System codes and no Name translations. Regional ticketing
(FICTIONAL) is an invented example system; the other code belongs to Wikidata: stations.*

See [Translations as an example](/docs/examples/translations/) for one configuration of owned
records and a relation matrix. Languages, names and the rules connecting them come from that model.

## Validity periods

A record type can define a validity period using two date fields. The start is the first valid
date, including that day. The end is the first date on which the record is no longer valid,
excluding that day. An empty start leaves the beginning open; an empty end leaves the end open.
When both dates are set, the end must be later than the start.

For example, a stop with **Valid from** set to 1 April 2021 and **Valid to (exclusive)** set to
13 December 2026 is valid from 1 April 2021 through 12 December 2026. Those are the example
model's labels; other types can use different labels or have no validity period.

Validity describes the data's business dates. Setting an end date keeps the record, its identity
and its history. It does not delete the record or schedule a change set to publish on that date.
See [Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/) for editing a date and
[Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) for coordinating
several date changes.

## Versions and refused saves

The version under **Details** in a record’s header protects it from being overwritten by an older edit.
When you save, refiroo checks the version you read. If someone else saved a change first, your
save is refused, even if you changed a different field on the same record. Their saved change
remains in place.

The field editor keeps your attempted value and shows **Current saved value** alongside the
refusal. Review the refreshed record before deciding whether to save again or cancel. Another
change before the next save can cause another refusal. Follow
[If someone else changed it first](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/#if-someone-else-changed-it-first)
for the recovery steps.

![An Abbreviation edit refused because the record changed in another session](/docs/screens/save-conflict.png)

*Above: another session changed Chur Depot Sand's Designation before this Abbreviation save.
The editor preserves the attempted abbreviation, shows the current saved value and reports
“The value was not saved” and “Object version has changed”.*

A record version is different from a model release, which defines the data's structure, and from
a publication number, which identifies a workspace snapshot. Work in a shared change set is also
protected by the change set's version; a colleague's intervening change can require a refresh.

## History

**History** shows what changed, who changed it and when, newest first. Expand an entry to read
its details. See [History](/docs/use/history/) for record events and activity across records,
and [See who changed what](/docs/guide/use/see-who-changed-what/) for the steps and filters.

## Deleting a record

**Delete record** on the record menu opens one confirmation. It reads what deletion would remove before offering the delete button; opening it deletes nothing. The impact follows these rules:

- Descendants in the hierarchy are removed with their parent.
- Records owned through required relationships are removed with their owner, including dependants
  in another application. Their dependants are included too.
- Relationships to independent records are removed, but those records and their hierarchies remain.

The confirmation counts the records and relationships removed and names up to eight dependants with their types, followed by **and N more** where needed. Choose **Delete N records** when dependants are included, or **Delete** followed by the type's name for one record. Cancelling leaves everything in place. A failed impact read offers **Retry** and no delete button. If the record or impact changes before deletion, the stale attempt is refused and the refreshed impact must be reviewed and confirmed again. A required connection
cannot simply be removed on its own while leaving a dependant without its owner.

In Live, deletion takes effect immediately. In a change set, it remains a proposed deletion until
publication. Existing publications retain their snapshots. Ending a validity period is different
from deleting a record.

See [Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/) for the record menu and editing context, and
[Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) for applying
proposed removals together.

## Who may read and change records

Access comes from roles granted to you directly or through a group. A grant covers a workspace,
or the whole installation. The relevant permissions are **Browse**, **Edit live** and
**Work in change sets**.

| Predefined role | Read records and history | Create, change and delete in Live | Create, change and delete in change sets |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reader | Yes | No | No |
| Contributor | Yes | No | Yes |
| Data steward | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Data owner | Yes | Yes | Yes |

An administrator can also define custom roles. Write permissions may be limited to particular
applications or record types. A deletion must be allowed for the dependent types it removes too.
**Browse** covers the workspace's data as a whole; it is not narrowed to selected types.
An administrator role alone does not give permission to read or edit reference data.

Your available controls reflect your access. Publications are always read-only, and a retired
workspace remains readable but refuses changes. The workspace's publication approval policy
does not by itself require approval for a direct live correction. See
[Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/) for direct work and
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/#who-may-do-what) for publication permissions.

A narrowed grant permits a relationship change when you may write either connected record.
It does not permit changing unrelated records of a type outside your grant. A bulk load
refuses individual out-of-scope items; publishing a change set containing out-of-scope changes
refuses the publication as a whole. Check the proposal's types before asking someone to publish.

## Edit a value or create a record

Fields can hold text, long text, whole numbers, decimal numbers, Yes/No, dates, dates with times
or structured values. The model may require a value, limit a number's range, require at least
one of several fields, or require a unique value across the workspace. Separate relationship
rules can limit counting records beneath an ancestor; see [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/).
A missing value is different from No, zero or a deliberately stored empty value.

Click a value on the record page, or focus it and press Enter, to open its editor. Selecting
text to copy does not start an edit. Choose **Save** or press Enter to save where offered;
Escape cancels. The value becomes its field where it stands. Click an empty field to add a value. An editable Yes/No value in the details is a switch: changing it saves immediately. After saving a name or changing a field that already had a value, the save notice offers **Undo**. If the record changed again in the meantime, Undo is refused with “Undo was not possible: the record changed again in the meantime.” A field set for the first time has no previous value to restore. An optional value's trash button clears it immediately and offers **Undo** in the notice. Read-only fields have no editing control.

The header's title and subtitle edit the same way. An empty subtitle offers **Add**.
Open **Details** in the header for the record’s ID, its copy button and version.
**Copy ID** is also in the record’s **⋯** menu. Use **Edit record** in the **⋯** menu
for the form containing all fields. A new record form saves its fields, allowed parent and
required relationships together: complete all required choices before choosing **Add** followed by the type's name. Required fields come first; optional fields are under **More fields (n)**, remembered per type in this browser. Missing or wrongly typed values are explained beneath their fields. On a desktop, forms open as sheets beside the page; confirmations stay centred.
A refusal leaves the invalid record uncreated; correct the named field or connection.

In a table, use the cell's pencil to edit without opening the record. Optional values and
single relationships can have a trash button. These icons appear on hover and stay visible
on touch screens; the row's menu is the keyboard alternative. Clicking the value elsewhere
still opens the record. A success notice says whether you saved in Live or the open change set.
Ancestor fields, containment, owned relationships, computed fields and publications have no
cell editing icons. Relationship rows use tooltip-labelled icons for changing the other record,
editing the connection's fields or deleting it; a lock explains a required or parent-managed row.

There is no business-date filter in the browser. Validity fields describe business dates;
searching today's lists does not automatically select the records valid on another day.

## Propose instead of editing Live

A Contributor sees **Propose a change** on a record and **Propose a new …** on a collection.
The first use asks for a change-set name, then opens your proposal for editing. Later uses
continue your newest change set. The band names it, its change count and state. Open **Details**
for who started it, when, its version and model.
A Reader's band says **You can read this workspace** and whom to ask. With narrowed write
permissions, controls appear only on the allowed record types and the Live band names those types.

For several records, permitted collections offer selection and **Change values**,
**Change relationships** and **Delete** with a preview before applying. Deletion previews count
children and owned dependants by type, relationships removed and those reaching records that
stay. Review these separately from the number of selected records.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0.*

## Clearing, uniqueness and related cells

Required fields need non-empty values; empty text does not meet the requirement. A model's
default fills a missing value on creation, rather than replacing an existing value on every
save. Workspace-wide uniqueness prevents two records holding the same nonempty unique value;
missing values and empty text do not reserve one. A conditional relationship rule can further
limit which records count within an ancestor; see [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/).

To clear an optional field, use its remove-value button. It makes the value **Not set** and keeps the record, without asking for confirmation. The removal notice offers **Undo** to put it back. **No value** in the inline editor instead stores an explicit cleared value; it does not remove the field's stored entry. After any refusal or refresh problem, inspect the current saved state before another edit.

A multi-record relationship cell opens a checklist and saves additions and removals together.
See [Replace a record’s related records](/docs/guide/use/replace-a-records-related-records/).
For full workflows, use [Add a record](/docs/guide/use/add-a-record/),
[Delete a record](/docs/guide/use/delete-a-record/),
[Stop offering a value](/docs/guide/use/stop-offering-a-value/) or
[Propose a change](/docs/guide/use/propose-a-change/). For bulk policy and results, see
[Changing many records](/docs/use/changing-many-records/).

## When a record cannot open

**Record unavailable** is a failed read, not an empty record. Read its reason and choose
**Retry**, or **Back to list** to inspect another result. A record belonging to another
application follows that application's route where the model allows it. A record belonging
to another workspace cannot be read by silently substituting the workspace you have open.
Check the workspace and original address with its sender.

Read-only fields cannot be supplied on creation, changed later or cleared by an ordinary
edit. If a type requires **at least one of** several fields, keep one filled when changing
or removing another. For a related-record cell, a single-valued relationship opens its picker;
a many-valued one opens the complete checked set and saves its additions and removals together.
Computed fields, ancestor values, parent containment, ownership-managed connections and
publication cells have no ordinary table edit controls.

Different records' business validity periods may overlap. Ending a period does not turn the
ordinary list into a view of another date. Use **Valid on** when
[exporting a file](/docs/guide/use/export-records/) to request that business-date selection.
There is no record restore from History: review and save a new correction instead.
---
title: Applications
description: Understand the collections and the kinds of view an application can offer.
reader: steward
---

Open an application to reach the records and views you need in the current workspace.
Choose a workspace’s name or tile on Home to open its page: it offers record search, applications,
your shelf, waiting change sets and recent activity grouped by day. **Edit model** and the workspace’s **⋯**
menu offer the actions and Settings pages your access allows.
Follow [Open an application](/docs/guide/use/open-an-application/) for the steps.

An **application** groups record types and views. Its name, collections and starting view come
from the workspace's model. Applications are not fixed modules of refiroo: a model can rename,
replace or remove them. Any application can offer any of the view kinds when the model
declares the structure that view needs.

## Collections and views

Choose an application in the top bar, then a collection in the sidebar. In Studio the applications share the side column with the lists; Instrument puts application tiles in the narrow strip beside the lists. See [Appearance and devices](/docs/use/appearance-and-devices/) for the frame arrangements. A collection can have
several views, shown as tabs under the list’s title. Changing tabs changes how you inspect the records; it does not
copy them. The model can choose which view opens when you select a collection in the
sidebar or on a group page. That choice may differ from the application's starting view;
use the tabs to switch to another view when needed. **Browse records** offers another route to individual records through their hierarchy. Open it to browse; it starts folded and remembers your choice in this browser.

![An application with collections, record browsing and a table of records](/docs/screens/app-network.png)

*Above: Network in Graubünden shows the Stops table and the collections declared by its model.*

| View | What you can do |
| --- | --- |
| Table | Search, filter and sort records, then open one. See [Records](/docs/use/records/) and [Find records](/docs/guide/use/find-records/). |
| Tree | Browse parents and children and move records to an allowed place. See [Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/) and [Arrange records in a tree](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/). |
| Mapping grid | Inspect connections, missing connections and multiple targets. See [Mapping grids](/docs/use/mapping-grids/) and [Map codes between systems](/docs/guide/use/map-codes-between-systems/). |
| Relationships table | List one relationship's records and its own values (a weight, a flag) as rows. Declared by the model; in the model contract (`relationTable`). |
| Relation matrix | Compare related records across columns and find missing connections. See [Relation matrices](/docs/use/relation-matrices/) and [Fill in a relation matrix](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/). |

![A collection with a table and two mapping views](/docs/screens/app-systems.png)

*Above: System codes in Systems offers a table and mapping views. These are choices in the
example model, not features reserved for this application.*

A missing tab may mean the model does not declare that view. Ask a model administrator if you
need a different presentation. An empty table means no records match the current context and
filters; a loading error needs a retry before you can draw that conclusion.

## Shared workspace, different ways in

Applications in one [workspace](/docs/use/workspaces/) use that workspace's data. Relationships
may connect records across applications where the model allows it. The same record can appear
in a table, a hierarchy, a mapping grid and a relation matrix without becoming separate records.

The banner identifies **Live**, a **Change set**, or a publication. Live edits apply immediately;
a change set holds proposed changes; a publication is read-only. On a computer the band shows
only this data context, its explanation or change-set summary and the **Live · Change sets ·
Publications** switch. On a phone it also shows the workspace and application. Check the context before editing.
Your roles determine which actions are offered. A declared view does not grant permission to
change its records. See [Record permissions](/docs/use/records/#who-may-read-and-change-records).

For configurations of these capabilities, see [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
and [The starter model](/docs/examples/the-starter-model/).

## Collection groups and record pages

Ungrouped collections appear first. Expand or fold a labelled group with its arrow; your choice
is remembered in this browser. The model sets whether a group starts folded on your first visit. A folded group is marked when it contains the open collection.
Choose the group's name to open its page, search entries by name and open one in the same
Live, change-set or publication context.
