A relation matrix the model places in a group has its own entry, named after the matrix's
view. Its matrix symbol uses the row collection's colour. Choose it to open the matrix
directly, from either the sidebar or the group page. The row collection stays in the sidebar
and still offers the matrix among its view tabs. A matrix without its own group entry is
available through that collection. Groups have one level and show no record counts.

![Application sidebar with a relation matrix listed alongside a collection in a group](/docs/screens/app-navigation-matrix-entry.png)

*Above: the Graubünden example model places Municipalities by system in a navigation group.
The matrix opens directly; its row collection is still available.*

A record page combines panels for fields, children, relationships, tables, hierarchy and history.
The model chooses their arrangement. If it declares no detail layout, refiroo provides a default.
The collection views above are the supported kinds; dedicated form and dashboard views are
not available.

The group page's **Find a collection or matrix** searches collection and matrix names. **This group has no collections or relation matrices.**
describes an empty group, rather than no records in its collections. For the shared table
controls, see [Lists, search and filters](/docs/use/lists-and-filters/).

On a wide screen, each application has a coloured tile in the top bar. The open application
is underlined; hovering over its tab shows the model's description. The product mark returns
to **Home**, and the gear opens **Settings**. Applications that do not fit are under **More**.
Settings opens an index grouped by task. Inside Settings, **← Back to** followed by the workspace’s
name returns to its page. On a phone, choose the application from the band
beneath the top bar instead. See [Appearance and devices](/docs/use/appearance-and-devices/).

If a group says **No collection or relation matrix in this group matches “…”**, clear **Find a collection or matrix**
or press Escape in that search field. This search covers collection and matrix names, not records.
Opening a collection result uses its chosen starting view; opening a matrix result goes straight
to that matrix. Both keep the current data context.

### Find a list in the sidebar

Use the workspace search above the page to find a list by name, including lists in folded groups. Press ⌘K on a Mac or Ctrl+K elsewhere to focus it. Matching lists appear under **Lists**; select one to open its view. **Go to** offers matching places such as Home, Change sets and Settings. The sidebar no longer has a separate list search.

The same search finds record names across the workspace. Results are grouped by record type and show each record's place. Use the arrow keys to choose a record and Enter to open it. Workspace search opens records in **Live**; use a collection's own search to stay in a change set or publication. **Browse records** has no search box of its own. The group page's **Find a collection or matrix** searches only that group's entries.
guide/src/content/docs/use/hierarchies.m:
---
title: Hierarchies
description: Understand trees, parents and children, allowed placements and moves.
reader: steward
---

A hierarchy places records under parents so you can browse and maintain their structure. Use
[Arrange records in a tree](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/) to expand branches,
rename records and move them.

## Parents, children and branches

A record has at most one parent. Records directly inside it are its children; all the records
below it are its descendants. The path on a record's page shows its ancestors. A branch can
contain several record types, or repeat the same type through several levels.

The model defines which types may contain which others and which types may stand at the top
without a parent. A type label grouping records in a tree is navigation, not another record.
A tree view shows the roots and types chosen by the model; it need not show every record in the
workspace. The sidebar’s **Browse records** tree is another route to records. Open its folded
heading to browse; your choice is remembered in this browser. Use **Find any record** in the
top bar to search names across the workspace.

![A tree expanded from a canton through a district and municipality to stops](/docs/screens/tree-geography-chur.png)

*Above: Geography in Network follows Graubünden through Plessur and Chur to Chur's stops.
Cantons, Districts, Municipalities and Stops are type groups between record levels.*

![A tree in which parent and child records have the same type](/docs/screens/tree-modes.png)

*Above: Modes in the same application has Mode records below other Mode records. Rail-bound
contains Funicular, Metro, Rack railway, Train and Tram. This is another model-defined hierarchy.*

## What a move changes

Moving changes a record's parent. Its descendants move with it, keeping their places relative
to that record. The record keeps its identity and history. refiroo changes the parent and the
containment relationship together; ordinary relationship editing cannot change only one of them.

A move is refused if the destination has a disallowed type or would create a cycle, such as
moving a record into itself or one of its descendants. The **Move to…** dialog lists destinations
with a reason beside unavailable choices. **Top level** means no parent; it is available only
where the model and the view permit that placement. A record allowed at the top of the workspace
may still be outside the roots shown by this particular tree.

In Live, a move preserves the record's type. In a change set, a destination marked **Becomes**
can offer a type change. That opens a preview of the resulting types and fields before applying
it to the change set. Review what needs values and what is retained only in history. Live data
changes only when the change set is published. Do not use this route for an ordinary move unless
you intend to change the type too.

## Other tree actions

Where configured, a record's menu offers adding a child, renaming and changing availability.
The model chooses the allowed child types and whether an availability field exists. Renaming
keeps the record's identity. Availability is a field value; it does not remove the record.

Change sets can also offer restructuring actions such as **Change type…**, **Insert level above…**
and **Remove this level…** where allowed. These require reviewing their preview and the proposal
before publication. They are different from merely folding a branch or moving it.

Deleting a parent can delete its descendants. Review [record deletion](/docs/use/records/#deleting-a-record)
and the impact shown before confirming; collapsing a branch never deletes it.

## Access and recovery

**Browse** allows reading a tree. Editing needs **Edit live** or **Work in change sets** for the
records affected, and the view must offer the action. See
[Record permissions](/docs/use/records/#who-may-read-and-change-records). A publication or retired
workspace is read-only. A change set awaiting approval may need to be withdrawn before editing.

A move based on an older record version can be refused. Review the latest parent and values
before trying again. A loading error is not evidence that a branch has no children: retry it.
For related records that do not determine placement, see [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/).

## Browse and move several records

The sidebar tree handles hierarchies of any size and depth. Its search lists matching records
of every type with their paths. Type groups fold like records; a single top-level group starts
open. Expanding can also open its only child one level further. Long groups load as you scroll;
**Show earlier records** reads the part above a group opened midway through. Your sidebar place
is kept within the application and workspace.

Use Cmd or Ctrl to add or remove a record from selection, Shift for a range, Ctrl+Space to
select by keyboard and Shift+arrows to extend it. Escape clears selection. Drag the selected
records together or open **Move to…** with right click or Shift+F10. One confirmation moves
all selected records or none. On touch screens, hold still for half a second until the record
lifts; moving earlier scrolls. Rest near an edge while dragging to scroll to the destination.

Type groups normally start folded; the sole top-level group is the exception and starts open.
Expanding a group or record opens its only child one level further without repeatedly
expanding an entire branch. Loading more records keeps the sidebar's scroll position.
On touch screens, the drag preview stays above your finger. Letting go at the starting place
does not open the record; in the sidebar it opens the record's menu instead.

## Restructure in a change set

Besides **Becomes** destinations, the node menu can offer **Change type…**,
**Insert level above…**, **Remove this level…** and **Change type of all … in here…**.
Only model-permitted changes appear. A preview lists each resulting type, values and origin,
values still needed and anything with no place in the new structure. Content with no place is
kept in history. Records retain their IDs and history; the new structure reaches Live only
when the change set publishes. Cancel the preview if the result does not match your intent;
resolve missing values before proceeding.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*

## Ordering, limits and changing back

A parent must be in the same application and workspace. Its type must be allowed to contain
the child. A self-hierarchy can continue to any depth, but a record cannot become its own
ancestor. Moving beneath a new ancestor also rechecks uniqueness in that scope.
A tree drop chooses a parent or level, not a position among siblings; the model's order decides
that position. Moving several selected records together requires their types to stay unchanged.
Follow [Move several records together](/docs/guide/use/move-several-records-together/).

Restructuring carries fields between equal value types, and can widen text to long text or
whole numbers to decimal numbers without losing information. A value failing the destination's
rules becomes a required answer in the preview. Values and connections with no place remain
in history. A later type change can offer them back from effective earlier reclassifications
in the current or published change sets, keeping restored connections' identities. Deliberately
cleared values and discarded work are not restoration sources.

An operation can restructure at most 500 records. A larger subtree is refused with its limit;
choose a smaller operation and inspect its impact. The preview also becomes stale if the
change set changes before applying. Follow [Reshape a hierarchy](/docs/guide/use/reshape-a-hierarchy/).
Opening an old address for a retyped record follows its current type in the selected context;
review filters can match either the old or new type.

A tree view opens a record beside the list, with **Expand to full page** for its full page.
An explorer-tree record opens without a collection behind it. A table record instead offers
**←** and the list’s name in the line above its title, followed by its parents where shown. **Resize navigation rail** changes the rail width; see
[Appearance and devices](/docs/use/appearance-and-devices/) for keyboard resizing.

The rail is named **Browse application**, or **Application navigation** in its phone drawer.
A **Move to…** dialog for several selected records is headed **Move … records**. Search
**Search new locations**, or choose **Top level — No parent** where allowed. **Not every record
can move there** means the destination does not fit the whole selection; revise the selection
or choose another parent. **Could not save the change** leaves a failure to resolve; **Dismiss**
closes the message, without applying the refused change.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/continu:
---
title: Continue live work while a change set is open
description: Make immediate corrections and understand which ones can conflict with proposed work.
reader: steward
---

Live remains editable while a change set is open, if you hold Edit live. See
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/#publishing-and-intervening-live-work).

1. Leave the change-set context and choose **Live**. Check the green band before editing.
   Opening another browser tab can help keep the contexts distinct.
2. Make and save the immediate correction. It is visible in Live now; it does not update
   the starting copy inside the existing change set.
3. Return to the change set and review its changes. An unrelated new Live record or a Live
   correction to an untouched record is kept when the change set publishes.
4. Validate and attempt publication only after reviewing current work. If Live and the change
   set changed the same record, publication refuses the conflict even if different fields
   changed. Changed mapping sets and invalid combined relationships can also stop publication.
5. Read the conflict list. Both Live and the change set remain intact, and nothing is partially
   published. Prepare a new change set from current Live and reapply the intended corrections
   after reconciling them. There is no automatic rebase or forced overwrite through retry.

Another publication between review and confirmation can also make the attempt stale. Refresh
and inspect the current result before retrying.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/correct:
---
title: Correct a record
description: Save a correction, handle a refused save, and check who changed what.
reader: steward
---

Correct one value or several fields and check the saved result. See
[Records](/docs/use/records/) for field rules, versions and editing permissions.

To change connections, follow [Relate records](/docs/guide/use/relate-records/). For a move, follow
[Arrange records in a tree](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/).


## Change one value

1. Open an application in the current workspace and [find the record](/docs/guide/use/find-records/).
   Check its heading and hierarchy path before editing.
2. Choose **Live** for a correction that should take effect immediately. Check the green
   **Live** banner. To prepare work for later publication, [open a change set
   first](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/), then check its name in the orange banner.
3. Select the value you need to correct in the heading or a details panel. An editor opens for
   that field where the value stands. Enter the verified replacement using the text, number or date control. A Yes/No value is a switch that saves as soon as you change it. Where **No value** is offered, it stores an explicit cleared value. To make an optional field **Not set** instead, cancel this edit and use its remove-value button. Removal saves immediately and offers **Undo**.
4. Choose **Save**. On success, the editor closes and the saved value appears. Check it before
   leaving. The save notice offers **Undo** for a name or a field that had a value before. If the record changed again in the meantime, Undo is refused with “Undo was not possible: the record changed again in the meantime.” Choose **Cancel** instead to abandon an unsaved correction.

![One numeric field open for correction with Cancel and Save](/docs/screens/stop-edit-field.png)

*Above: Stop number (UIC) is open on Chur Wiesental in Network, in the Graubünden workspace.
Its current value is 8509006; the screenshot shows the editor before a correction is saved.*

If the value cannot be selected, check whether you are viewing a read-only publication. A field
may also be read-only or your access may not allow editing it. Ask a workspace administrator if
you need access. If a save is refused, read the message and correct the reported problem before
trying again. A refused save has not applied your input.

## Change several fields together

1. Open the **…** menu in the record’s header and choose **Edit record**.
   The record’s ID and version are under **Details**.
   The form is titled with the record's name and opens beside the page on a desktop, with the current values.
2. Correct the fields you need. **Name** identifies the record; the other fields describe it.
   Check each field's label rather than assuming similarly named fields change together.
3. Keep **In** followed by the current parent's name unless you intend to move the record. Choose **Change** to show **Parent**, then search
   for and select the intended parent, checking its path to distinguish matching names.
4. Scroll through the form and choose **Save**. On success, the form closes and the
   record page shows the result. If a message identifies an invalid or missing value, correct
   it and save again. Choose **Cancel** to leave without saving the form.

![The record editing form showing Parent, Name and other fields](/docs/screens/stop-edit-record.png)

*Above: Edit object for Chur Wiesental shows Chur as the selected Parent, followed by Name,
Designation, Stop number (UIC) and the other stop fields. The remaining fields and save control
are further down the form.*

## If someone else changed it first

1. If a single-field save reports **The value was not saved** and **Object version has changed**,
   leave the editor open. Your input is preserved. Read **Current saved value**, then review
   the refreshed record for the other person's changes, including changes to other fields.
2. Decide whether your correction still applies. Adjust the input if needed. Choose **Save**
   again only after reviewing the current values, or **Cancel** to abandon your correction.
3. Check the result. Another intervening edit can cause another refusal; review again rather
   than repeatedly pressing Save. If **Reload current value** appears, use it to load the
   current value before retrying.

![A refused field save with the current saved value and the user's preserved input](/docs/screens/save-conflict.png)

*Above: on Chur Depot Sand, another session changed Designation before this session tried to save
Abbreviation. The input CHSX is preserved, the current saved abbreviation DEPS is shown, and the
save is refused even though the other session edited a different field.*

For the reason a change to another field can refuse your save, see
[Versions and refused saves](/docs/use/records/#versions-and-refused-saves). If the whole-record
form reports a conflict, review the latest record and reapply only the corrections still needed;
do not assume the form's older values are current.

## Check the correction in its context

If you saved in a change set, choose **Review changes** in its orange banner. Under
**Records**, find the record and open its row to check the before and after values.
This shows the correction prepared for publication; it has not changed Live yet.
Follow [Review what a change set changes](/docs/guide/use/review-what-a-change-set-changes/)
for the full review. Record History is absent inside change sets and publications.

For a correction saved directly in **Live**, or after the change set has been published,
open the record in **Live** and check its History:

1. Scroll to **History** on the record's page. Each line identifies a change, the person who
   made it and the time. The newest changes appear first.
2. Choose **Values** for field changes, **Relationships** for connections, **Moves** for changes
   of place, or **All** to see every kind together.
3. Use **By** to narrow the history to one person. Choose **Anyone** to remove that restriction.
4. Open a history line with its arrow to inspect the change and its previous value, where
   recorded. If your correction is not visible, restore **All** and **Anyone** before looking
   again. A cancelled or refused correction is not a successful value change.

![Record history with change-kind tabs and a person filter](/docs/screens/stop-history.png)

*Above: Chur Wiesental's History shows its creation and added relationships by Guide Admin.
All, Values, Relationships, Moves and By control which events are shown; this capture does not
show a newly saved field correction.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/see-who:
---
title: See who changed what
description: Trace an edit from a record, workspace activity or your own changes.
reader: steward
---

Choose the view that matches your question. See [History](/docs/use/history/) for the meaning
of authors, event kinds and publication context.

## Check one record

1. [Find the record](/docs/guide/use/find-records/) in the intended workspace and open it.
2. Scroll to **History**. Start with **All** and **By: Anyone** to avoid hiding an event.
3. Choose **Values**, **Relationships** or **Moves** to narrow the list, or select a person in **By**.
4. Read the action, author and time. Expand the entry's arrow to inspect the stored detail,
   such as the previous and new field values where recorded.
5. Check whether the action was prepared in a change set or applied by a publication before
   comparing it with the current fields.

![Record history below its relationships, with author and time on each event](/docs/screens/use-history-stop-changed.png)

*Above: Thusis Süd's history shows the correction and its later publication. The current field is THSD.*

## Check activity across records

1. Where available to your role, open **Settings**, **Workspaces** and select the workspace.
2. Choose **Activity**. It lists the newest actions first.
3. Under **What**, choose **Records**, **Relationships**, **Change sets** or **Publications**.
   Return to **Everything** to see their sequence together.
4. Read who acted and the context beside the time. Follow a linked person's name to inspect
   their changes if you need to trace their other work.

![Workspace activity with Everything selected](/docs/screens/use-history-activity.png)

*Above: Graubünden's activity connects the correction change set with the resulting publication.*

## Find your own work

1. Select the refiroo name to open Home. Read **Your recent changes** for recent actions.
2. Choose **See all your changes**. The **Your changes** page opens.
3. Choose **Workspace**, **What** and **Period**. Read each result's action and context.
   Widen those filters if the expected action is missing.

![Your changes with workspace, kind and period filters](/docs/screens/use-history-changes.png)

*Above: the list is narrowed to Guide Admin's work in Graubünden.*

A failed read needs a retry; an empty filtered result needs broader filters. If workspace
management is unavailable, use the record's History or Your changes, or ask someone with the
necessary access to inspect workspace Activity. History cannot restore a value by itself:
follow [Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/) to make a new correction.

Under each day heading, read the newest entries first. On the record's History, use **Load older history**
to read 20 more after the initial ten and **Show fewer** to shorten the list. Check a job or
publication named as the cause; **client** marks a system's work, and **Before sign-in** marks an
older entry with no recorded author. Your changes has no value details or export: return to the
record's History for the saved values.

## Read an AI account or assistant origin

For a short explanation with links to the counted changes, follow
[Explain a period in history](/docs/guide/use/explain-a-period-in-history/). Opening History
sends nothing; asking for the account sends counts and, at values, names to the provider.
Calls can incur costs and are recorded; [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) explains
sending and retention.

On a record history entry, read **Proposed by the AI assistant** or **Prepared by an assistant**
alongside who asked, who edited and who published. These are different responsibilities.
An external assistant’s displayed name is its own claim. The personal Changes page has no
assistant filter; use [the record’s History](/docs/use/history/#work-prepared-by-an-assistant)
for the mark.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/change-:
---
title: Change relationships of many records
description: Add, remove, replace or clear one kind of relationship across selected records.
reader: steward
---

Use this when several records need the same connection changes. See
[Changing many records](/docs/use/changing-many-records/) and [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/).

1. Select records in an editable collection and choose **Change relationships**. Select the
   relationship's pill. Only relationships allowed for that record type appear; parent and
   owner connections are managed elsewhere.
2. Choose the offered action. **Add** adds the ticked records; **Remove** removes those ticked.
   **Replace with** makes the ticked records the complete set. **Set to** chooses the one record
   for a single-valued connection. **Clear** removes the set where optional. Required
   connections cannot be removed or cleared.
3. Search and tick the other records. **Remove** lists records the selection already holds and
   how many hold each. **Add** marks connections already held. Candidate rules may limit this
   list; read its explanation if an expected record is missing.
4. Read the number of changes. If it exceeds the deployment limit, reduce the selection or
   split the work. Choose **Change the rest** or, where available, **Change none**.
5. Choose **Preview**. Review additions, removals, unchanged connections and refused records.
   Use **Back** to revise, or **Apply** to proceed.
6. Read the actual result. Connections changed since preview are refused, preserving the
   newer work. Use **Preview again** after checking them, then **Done**.

The fields on each connection are not changed here. Open the record's relationship panel to
edit those fields. A replace operation removes connections you leave unticked, so review the
whole chosen set before applying.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/load-th:
---
title: Load the next version of a workbook
description: Check a recurring workbook against its profile and stage its differences in a change set.
reader: steward
---

Use a saved import profile to recognise a recurring workbook. This differs from creating a
model from a new workbook; that task belongs to
[Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/).

1. Open **Settings › Workspaces and models › Import profiles**. Select the profile and read its
   **Last load**: file, destination, row counts and whether its change set was published.
2. If your permissions offer **Upload the next version…**, choose it and upload the newer
   workbook. Choose the intended comparison workspace and wait while it is checked.
   The profile is checked and saved against that workspace’s model. Nothing is loaded
   into its records by this check.
3. Review new, missing and renamed columns, new values, changed names and missing records.
   Choose **Accept** on a **Renamed** row only where the proposed column really replaces the old one.
   Choose **Ignore** on a **New** row to leave that column out. Ask the profile's model administrator to
   fix ambiguous bindings or model problems; do not guess which field a column represents.
4. Check the missing-record choice. Keeping missing records leaves them; deleting them stages
   removals and is allowed only in a change set. A missing key means reliable recurring
   matching is not available: resolve it before relying on repeated uploads.
5. When the report allows loading, choose **Load into a change set…** and review the destination
   and proposed changes in its dialog. Loading creates a new change set containing differences.
6. Choose **Open the change set review** from the completed load or **Last load**. Review
   additions, corrections and removals before publishing or submitting for approval.

If the file could not be read or the profile could not be saved, correct the displayed cause
and check again. Missing controls can reflect your access; ask the responsible model
administrator. See [Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/) for row refusals.

![Import profile after a next-version check, with Accept and Ignore beside column differences, Needs a fix and disabled Load into a change set.](/docs/screens/import-profile-next-version.png)

The pictured profile still **Needs a fix**, so **Load into a change set…** is disabled. Resolve
the reported problems before loading.

In **Load … into a change set**, check the proposed name and workspace before choosing
**Load**. The steps **Open a change set** and **Load the rows** show what is happening.
The suggested name starts with **Load**, the file name and a date. If loading fails after the
change set was opened, inspect that change set and the load's job before starting again;
do not assume the first proposal disappeared.

## Use a saved profile through the assistant dialog

A workbook loaded from the assistant’s checked records and relationships saves no import
profile. For that route, send the next file to the assistant again and explain how to match
existing records; see [Loading with the assistant](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/#the-next-file-and-the-saved-profile).

If you already have a separately saved import profile, follow the steps above to reuse it.
Starting through **Import…** can also recognise that saved layout and prepare the file without
an assistant session or AI cost. You still review the proposal and row check. **The saved layout does not fit this file**
offers **Read it with the assistant**. That sends the file and instructions to Claude Code,
can incur costs and keeps task files; see [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/).
A new sheet or changed layout needs review, not an assumption that the previous mapping fits.

## Remove a file you no longer need

1. On the profile page, choose **Delete the file…** beside the upload and load actions.
2. Read **Delete <file name>?**. It removes the upload and its stored analysis, stops a check
   still reading it, and keeps the profile and already loaded records.
3. Choose **Delete the file** to continue or **Cancel** to keep it. After deletion, upload a
   file again to check it. A failed deletion leaves its reason in the dialog; resolve that
   cause before retrying.

To stop reusing the profile itself, choose **Delete the profile…** and confirm **Delete the
profile**. Read [what each deletion keeps](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#remove-an-uploaded-file-or-an-import-profile)
before confirming; deleting a profile does not reverse its earlier loads.

![Delete an uploaded workbook while keeping its import profile and loaded records](/docs/screens/use-import-file-delete-confirm.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/change-:
---
title: Change how refiroo looks
description: Choose this browser’s theme, table density, type colours and edit hints.
reader: steward
---

Adjust the display without changing the data. See
[Appearance and devices](/docs/use/appearance-and-devices/) for keyboard and phone use.

1. Open **All settings** from your account menu, then **Appearance** under **You**.
   On a phone, open **Settings: …** to reach the settings navigation.
2. Under **Theme**, choose **Current**, **Hearth**, **Studio**, **Instrument** or **Website purple** for the colours, typography and frame. Under **Light
   or dark**, choose **System**, **Light** or **Dark**. System follows the device. Every theme
   works in either mode. The page changes immediately; there is no Save button.
3. Under **Table density**, choose **Comfortable** for more space or **Compact** for more
   rows. If one table does not change, open its **Display** menu: its own density overrides
   this default. Choose Default there to use the browser preference again.
4. Under **Type colours**, choose **B: magenta and olive** or **A: plum and gold**. Read the
   record-type labels as well as colours when identifying records.
5. Under **Edit pencil**, choose **On hover and focus** or **Always, faintly**. On a touch
   screen, editable fields show their pencils regardless of this choice.

The choices stay in this browser. Repeat them on another device if needed. For individual
column visibility and widths, use the collection's **Display** menu rather than Appearance.

![Appearance showing its two colour themes separately from light or dark mode](/docs/screens/use-appearance-themes.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/start-f:
---
title: Start from an earlier publication
description: Use a retained snapshot as a proposal’s starting point without restoring it over Live.
reader: steward
---

Start a proposal from known published data. This is not a rollback. Read
[Publications](/docs/use/publications/) and [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/).

1. Open **Publications** in the intended workspace. Find the snapshot by its number, date
   and model version; open it first if you need to verify its content.
2. On its row, open **More actions** and choose **Start a change set from this publication**.
   You need Work in change sets; Browse alone cannot create it.
3. Give the change set a name and confirm the creation form. Open it and check that its
   source names the intended publication and its model release.
4. Make the changes you intend. **Review changes** compares them with this source snapshot.
   It does not describe all differences between that old snapshot and today's Live.
5. Validate and publish or submit as usual. Only changes made in this change set are merged
   into current Live. Newer untouched Live work survives; conflicts prevent publication.

If the proposal's release differs from the workspace's, coordinate with a model administrator
and follow [Prepare under the next model version](/docs/guide/use/prepare-under-the-next-model-version/).
Withdrawing a publication or starting from it never restores its records over Live.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/browse-:
---
title: Browse a publication
description: Open a saved snapshot, find a record and return to current data.
reader: steward
---

Use a publication to inspect records as published, even after Live changes.
See [Publications](/docs/use/publications/) for snapshot contents and status.

## Open the snapshot

1. [Open an application](/docs/guide/use/open-an-application/) in the intended workspace.
   Check **Workspace** in the sidebar.
2. Choose **Publications** above the records. The list is newest first. Read the number,
   model release, publication time and publisher; **Current** identifies the designated snapshot.
   Choose **Load older publications** if the one you need is further back.
3. Choose **Open publication** beside the intended entry. Check the purple banner for the
   publication number and model release. It says the records are read-only.

![The publication list with Open publication](/docs/screens/use-pub-list.png)

*Above: Graubünden has one publication, made after the abbreviation correction.*

## Find and inspect the record

1. Choose a collection or view in the snapshot's navigation. It uses the saved model's definitions,
   so its available views may differ from Live.
2. Search or filter as you would when [finding records](/docs/guide/use/find-records/).
   Open the record to read its fields and relationships. An empty result means no records match
   those filters in this snapshot; clear them before concluding the record was absent.
3. Use **Back to publications** to return to the list, or **Live** to inspect today's data.
   Check the banner again before making a correction in Live.

![A publication searched for a record, with its saved abbreviation visible](/docs/screens/use-pub-snapshot.png)

*Above: Thusis Süd reads THSD in Publication 1. The purple banner keeps the snapshot context visible.*

If the list says **No publications yet**, the workspace has not had a successful publication.
If loading fails, retry. If you need to prepare a correction based on a snapshot, use its menu's
**Start a change set from this publication** where permitted; opening the snapshot itself never
restores or changes live data. Follow [Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/)
for the editing and review that follows.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/open-an:
---
title: Open an application
description: Choose a workspace, open an application and select a view of its records.
reader: steward
---

Open the right data before searching or editing. See
[Applications](/docs/use/applications/) and [Workspaces](/docs/use/workspaces/) for how models,
datasets and views fit together.

## Start from Home

1. Select the refiroo name in the top bar to open Home. Under **Your workspaces**, find the
   intended workspace. Check the model name and release on its card; similar workspace names
   do not guarantee the same data or structure.
2. Choose the workspace’s name or tile to open its page, then choose an application. Its
   default view opens in that workspace. The application names come from the model. An
   application link on the Home card opens that application directly.
3. Check **Workspace** in the sidebar and the context banner above the records. Choose **Live**
   for current data, or open the intended change set or publication. A publication is read-only;
   Live saves apply immediately.

![Home showing workspace names, model releases and application buttons](/docs/screens/workspaces-home.png)

*Above: Graubünden offers Network, Systems and Names. Default offers RDM Master, RDM Systems
and RDM Translations under a different model.*

If no workspace is offered, ask an administrator for **Browse** access. If Home reports a loading
failure, retry it before concluding that no workspaces exist.

## Choose a collection and view

1. Select an application in the top bar, using **More** if it does not fit. On a phone,
   choose it in the band beneath the top bar. Read its sidebar collections; switching applications
   can change which collections are offered. If a collection group is folded, expand it.
2. Choose the collection you need. Check the page heading and description.
3. If tabs appear below the heading, choose the view that suits your task. A table helps
   [find records](/docs/guide/use/find-records/); a tree helps
   [arrange records](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/); a mapping grid helps
   [map records](/docs/guide/use/map-codes-between-systems/); a relation matrix helps
   [check coverage](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/).
4. Check the banner again before changing anything. Opening an application or changing a view
   does not itself save a data change.

![An application with multiple views of the selected collection](/docs/screens/app-systems.png)

*Above: System codes in Systems has a table and the Codes to stops and Codes to municipalities
mapping tabs. Other collections can offer different view kinds.*

A missing view may simply not be declared by the model. Ask a model administrator about the
intended configuration. An empty collection means there are no matching records in that context;
a reported loading error needs a retry instead.

## Switch workspace

Follow [Switch workspace](/docs/guide/use/switch-workspace/) to choose another dataset and check
its model, applications and context before editing.

## If the address does not fit this workspace

After switching, read the toast if the model or release differs. An old bookmark can open
**Not in this model**: the named application, collection or type is absent here. Choose one of
the offered workspaces whose model has it, or return Home and open an application this workspace
provides. If the workspace itself cannot be served, read the displayed reason and ask the
operator for help. Other workspaces remain available. A retired workspace can be opened through
**Settings › Workspaces** where permitted, but stays read-only.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/continu:
---
title: Continue or correct an assistant task
description: Resume a stopped task, correct a proposal or reload a wrong change set without losing sight of what is discarded.
reader: steward
---

Return to the task from **Settings › Jobs**, or use the task's bar when it accompanies the model
editor or change-set review. The same assistant session can continue while the task is retained.
For a task given in words, its Jobs group and page heading use the short title the assistant
writes with its first answer; any draft it makes is named **Assistant:** followed by that title.
Your full instructions stay under **You said:** on the proposal. Until the title arrives,
including after a stop or failure before an answer, the name uses your words, shortened at
a word boundary with “…” if needed. A workbook task keeps its file name.

Further turns can incur costs and read the task's workbook and permitted records again. See
[AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) for sending and retention, and
[task states](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/#stop-correct-or-end-a-task) for their rules.

## Correct a proposal

1. Read the latest notes, any **Checks**, **What the load does** or record counts, and any engine refusal. If you stopped a turn
   after it changed the draft, open the draft to inspect it: Stop does not undo those edits.
2. Under **Tell the assistant what to change**, describe the correction and choose **Send to
   the assistant**. The same session reads the current draft, if there is one, and proposes again.
3. Review the new proposal. For a workbook, inspect **What the load does**, open the type rows
   for example records and source cells, and read any repeated-name finding or refused items.
   Choose **Accept and load to change set** when those checked records and relationships match your intent.
   A draft edited after the check is checked again first; any refusal prevents the load.
   For words alone, choose **Accept** when the page says **No change to the model.**; model-only
   and record-move proposals keep **Accept the model**. If the task changed while you worked,
   inspect its latest state and try again; your old view cannot overwrite the newer work.

## Continue after a failure or Stop

1. On **The assistant stopped** or **You stopped the assistant**, read the reason in the task's
   notes. The newest three are shown; expand earlier notes if needed. If the message asks you
   to report a correlation ID, copy the ID shown with that warning for the operator.
2. Use **Tell the assistant how to go on** and **Send to the assistant** to supply corrected
   instructions. If the cause was temporary and the instructions are still right, use
   **Try again as it was** after failure or **Go on as it was** after Stop.
3. If needed, choose **Open the draft in the editor**. The draft and work so far are retained.
   If you stopped before the session had anything to resume, continuing starts it again on the
   same task with your words and any file.
4. Review the returned proposal. To end the work instead, choose **Discard this task**, which
   removes its draft and ends its session.

**Stop** while **Loading** discards the change set the load was making and returns to the
accepted proposal. Stop before any proposal leaves a stopped task that takes instructions.
Stopping a correction can return an earlier proposal whose draft already has newer edits;
read the warning before accepting anything.

![Task stopped before a proposal, with a words box, Go on as it was and Discard this task](/docs/screens/use-assistant-stopped.png)

## Correct a load before publication

1. On **Loaded into the change set**, choose **Review the change set** to understand what is
   wrong. If it can be corrected with small ordinary edits, you may make them there.
2. To ask the assistant to prepare it again, return to **Not what you wanted? Tell the assistant**.
   Describe the correction and choose **Discard and load again**.
3. Read **Discard this change set and load again?**. Confirming removes everything in that
   change set, including any edits you or others made there. Cancel to preserve it. Live data
   has not changed.
4. If you confirm a correction to a workbook load, the same session revises the proposal and
   has the engine check the records and relationships again. Review **What the load does** and
   choose **Accept and load to change set** to prepare the replacement change set. Review that change set
   before approval and publication. To abandon the work completely, use **Discard the change
   set** and confirm instead.

![A reload confirmation explaining that hand edits in the change set are removed](/docs/screens/use-assistant-reload.png)

After publication the task no longer takes corrections to that load. **Published** offers
**Change this model…** or **Ask about these records…** according to your access; use these to
prepare new work. A discarded task has ended: use **Start again** in its bar if available.

## Continue a saved layout or a model move

At a saved-layout row check, use **Back to the proposal** or the words box to have the assistant
read the file again. If **The saved layout does not fit this file** appears, choose **Read it
with the assistant**. Review its new proposal before loading.

For **The engine refused the migration** or **The engine would refuse the next step**, read
the reason on the task, then use **Tell the assistant what to change**. Review the revised
model and preview again. Whole-type migration confirmation moves records live; read the
[model-move rules](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/#a-model-change-that-moves-records)
before confirming it. The assistant cannot bypass the refusal or activate a release itself.

If you lost permission for a step, the page says which permission is required. Copy the task
link for a workspace administrator. If the task expired or does not exist, choose **Go to the
workspaces**. A task whose session has ended says so: start a new task if more work is needed.

If a workbook batch is refused at acceptance, none of its records or relationships is loaded
and its change set is discarded. Read the refused records and their source cells in the task's
notes, then tell the assistant what to correct. Review and accept the revised proposal.
A model release installed before the failed load can remain installed.

For other task paths, if a failed task says it loaded changes before it stopped, choose **Review the change set**
and inspect that retained proposal before retrying. This differs from **Stop** during loading,
which discards the load's change set. Do not publish a partial proposal merely because it exists.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/edit-in:
---
title: Edit in Excel and import back
description: Export a readable workbook and preview only the changes you intend to load.
reader: steward
---

Use an Excel (XLSX) workbook when you want to edit a view or a collection outside refiroo. Read
[Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#a-workbook-for-people) before clearing cells.

If **Load a workbook** opens because the assistant is enabled, choose **Import without the
assistant…** to reach the manual import form used below. That manual path does not send the
file to an AI assistant.

1. In the collection, open **Workspace actions › Export**. Keep **What** on **This view**
   to take its search, supported filters and layout, or select the type, application or workspace.
   Choose **For editing in a spreadsheet**. For a link matrix, choose **What each cell lists**:
   **Name** or a text field identifying its records. For a table, check **Advanced: columns
   and sheets**. Choose **Start export** and download the completed file.
2. Open it in Excel. Read the second sheet, **About this export**, for the file’s source and
   load-back rules. Keep its hidden identity and version columns and saved import information.
   Edit the names or ordinary values you intend to change; leave **(not imported)** columns
   alone. Read summary cells on their referenced sheet.
3. Follow the rules for the layout you exported, below. In an ordinary table workbook,
   review relationship lists carefully: the edited list replaces the whole set.
   An empty replacement cell clears it if allowed. In a matrix workbook, clearing a cell
   changes nothing. Blank ordinary field or owned-record cells
   leave values unchanged. Removing a relationship-sheet row does not delete the connection.
4. Back in the intended Live or change-set context, choose **Workspace actions › Import** and
   select the workbook. Leave **Profile** at **None** so refiroo reads its saved layout.
5. Keep **Only if unchanged since the export** unless you have reviewed a deliberate overwrite.
   **Update them anyway** deliberately replaces values from the file even where a record
   or relationship changed since export. Review the current data first: this choice ignores
   the workbook’s saved version checks.
   Choose the refusal policy and **Preview**. The job page identifies it as **Read as exported …**.
6. Review **How the file is read**: the field each column is matched by, the values matched,
   value-sheet counts and where new records go. Change **Matched by** where needed; this runs
   the preview again without loading records. See
   [Check how the file is read](/docs/guide/use/import-a-file/#check-how-the-file-is-read).
   Review creations, updates, unchanged rows and refusals. An untouched workbook should change
   nothing. With **Only if unchanged since the export**, a record edited by another person
   since export is refused. Reconcile those rows
   with the current records before retrying, or export a fresh workbook.
7. Choose **Load the file** when the preview is right. Inspect the final results; execution
   checks current data again. Correct refused rows in the file and resend it to preview again.

In a change set this prepares proposals for review and publication; it does not change Live.
Use **Cancel import** if the preview includes unexpected changes.

## Edit a matrix workbook

The main matrix sheet loads only its cells. Row names and identifying fields help you find
the right row; editing them here does not change those records. Value sheets, where present,
load their records separately as described below.

- In a matrix showing record fields, edit the intended field under the intended column.
  Filling an empty cell creates a record only when the view permits creation. The preview
  shows where it goes, including a group that **will be created**. If no suitable place can
  be found, the refusal names the column: choose or prepare a group by creating the first
  cell in the app, then preview the file again. There is no value sheet for this layout.
- A cell holding several records is shown joined and is not loaded back in this field layout.
  Open the cell in refiroo to edit the individual records.
- In a matrix showing links, choose a record from the cell's dropdown. A non-empty list
  replaces the links within that row and column: records added are linked, records left out
  are unlinked. Other columns are unaffected. A value found neither in that column's value
  sheet nor in existing records creates a record only if the view also permits creation. It supplies the name and, when different,
  the selected text field; other required fields still need values. Otherwise choose an
  existing record. Names containing a semicolon appear with a comma instead; keep that form
  when editing.
- An empty or cleared matrix cell changes nothing. To remove every value or every link in a
  cell, use refiroo.

### Edit the value sheets of a link matrix

1. Open **Values ·** followed by the column name. Each row holds a record's name and fields,
   its group for reading, and hidden identity and version columns. Keep those hidden columns.
   Fields marked **(not imported)** are for reading.
2. Where the view permits editing or creation, edit existing records on that sheet. The hidden
   identity updates the same record, even if you change its name. Its other connections see
   those record changes too. With only Link existing and Unlink enabled, value sheets are
   for reading and their edits do not load.
3. Where the view permits creation, add a row without an identity for a new record and fill
   its required fields. The group column does not choose where it goes: check the import
   preview. A row not selected in any main-sheet cell is still created or updated.
4. In a main-sheet cell, use the chosen field's value from the value sheet. If you rename a
   record there, its old main-sheet value still identifies it unless another value-sheet row
   now uses that value. The same new value in both sheets identifies one new record. Two
   records with the same chosen value make the reference ambiguous; correct the values or
   the selected matching field in the preview.
5. Preview the workbook in refiroo. A spreadsheet cannot synchronise the main sheet's text
   and value-sheet records itself; import resolves them together. Review both value-sheet
   counts and main-sheet connections before choosing **Load the file**.

For example, a translation matrix workbook can fill missing names under language columns.
A mapping matrix workbook can link an existing code instead. Both create connections; reuse
keeps the existing record's identity. In a change set, connected systems see the accepted
changes after publication, according to what they are allowed to read.

## Edit other view workbooks

A relationships table exported as rows lets you edit connection values or add a row connecting
two named records. Removing a row does not delete its connection. In its grid layout, **Linked**
is Yes or No: Yes can add a missing connection, and No does not remove an existing one.
A table column showing a relationship that owns its records is for reading; edit the owned
records on their own sheet or in the app. Follow the file's **About this export** instructions.

A tree or a wider type selection has one sheet per type, with parents identified by name.
Keep the hidden columns where names alone would be ambiguous. A mapping grid uses a
relationship column for the target. See
[Workbook layouts](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#workbook-layouts) for the differences.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/propose:
---
title: Propose targets
description: Ask for mapping suggestions, review the proposed targets and publish the mappings you keep.
reader: steward
---

Use this to prepare mappings for unmapped records. You need **Use AI proposals** and **Work in
change sets**, an enabled AI provider and permission to send record values. Read
[Mapping grids](/docs/use/mapping-grids/#targets-proposed-by-ai) for candidate and confidence limits.
Names and displayed fields go to the provider; requests can incur costs and are recorded.
See [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) for details.

1. Open a mapping grid in the current workspace. Apply search or choose a parent if you want
   only those sources considered. Open **Propose targets**. The dialog counts the unmapped
   sources and states what is sent. If none remain, close it and change the scope if necessary.
2. Under **Into change set**, use the current change set or choose **New change set** and name
   it. Without an open change set, enter **Name of the new change set**. No suggestion writes Live.
3. Choose **Propose**. **Proposing targets…** shows progress. You can **Close** the dialog and
   the job continues; its end is announced. **Stop** ends further work but keeps mappings already
   proposed. If someone changed the change set before the request started, review it and propose
   again against its current state.
4. Read the result counts and warnings. **Left unmapped: no likely target** needs your own
   investigation. **Changed meanwhile, not touched** means someone changed the source while the
   answer was being prepared. A failed or unanswered batch is not a decision that no target exists.
5. When at least one target was proposed, choose **Show proposed** to open the change set's grid with **Proposed** selected. Inspect
   each target, its displayed fields, confidence and reason. On a phone, expand **Why?**.
   Use **Change** and **Save** to replace a wrong target. Its AI mark disappears.
   If no target was proposed, **Show proposed** is absent. Choose **Close** and investigate
   the unmapped sources manually.
6. Review the whole change set, including any earlier work in it. Follow
   [Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) to validate,
   obtain any required approval and publish. The published history says which mappings were
   proposed by AI and who published them.

![A finished proposal job with no proposed targets, one source left unmapped and Close](/docs/screens/use-mapping-proposal-result.png)

If the provider fails, read the warning and review any proposals already saved. You can prepare
mappings manually through [Map codes between systems](/docs/guide/use/map-codes-between-systems/).
If the action disappears, ask an administrator whether the provider, send level or your access changed.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/map-cod:
---
title: Map codes between systems
description: Find unmapped or ambiguous rows and choose, replace or remove a mapping.
reader: steward
---

Connect each source record to the intended target using a mapping grid. Codes from another
system are one example. See [Mapping grids](/docs/use/mapping-grids/) for states, limits and
permissions.

## Find the rows that need attention

1. Open an application in the current workspace and choose a collection with a mapping grid.
   Select the mapping tab. Check the heading and the source and target types in its description.
2. Check the banner. Choose **Live** for immediate changes, or
   [open a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) to prepare them together.
3. Search for the source records you need. Read their codes and other identifying fields.
   Select **Unmapped** for rows without a connection, **Mapped** for rows with a
   target, or, on a view where a source may hold only one, **Ambiguous** for rows with several. **All** removes the state restriction.
4. Inspect each target's name and identifying fields. Select a source name or target chip to
   open that record's page for a closer look. Decide whether the current state needs changing.
   Clear search and select **All** if an expected row is absent. A read error needs
   a retry; it does not mean a row is unmapped.

## Choose or replace a target

1. Choose **Map** on an unmapped row or **Change** on a filled row. **Change mapping** opens
   with the source name in its heading and the current targets, or **Not mapped**, under
   **Currently**. Check these before searching.
2. Search for the intended target and inspect its identifying fields. Select its radio button.
   If nothing matches, shorten the search and check the model's candidate rules. Do not select
   a similar name merely to fill the row.
3. Choose **Save**. This sets the row to the selected target, replacing any previous
   targets, including all targets of an ambiguous row. Check the refreshed target and state.
   If the row no longer matches the active state filter, switch to **All** and find it again.
4. Choose **Cancel** if no correction is needed. Where **Save and next** is offered, it saves
   this choice and opens the next row; check that new source before choosing again.

![A mapping dialog for an unmapped row with target radio choices and a creation action](/docs/screens/mapping-grid-map-dialog.png)

*Above: T-9999, the fictional special day pass, is deliberately unmapped. The dialog shows
Not mapped and offers stop candidates and Create new stop. It was cancelled; the screenshot
does not suggest that this pass needs a stop mapping.*

To retain several valid targets, use the record's [relationship controls](/docs/guide/use/relate-records/).
Saving one selection in this dialog resolves the row to one target.

## If the target does not exist

1. Search carefully first. If a new record is needed, choose **Create new** followed by its
   type name. The target creation form opens.
2. Check its application and parent where offered, then fill **Name** and the required fields.
   Choose **Add** followed by the target type's name, or **Cancel** to return without creating a target.
3. After creation, review the selected target in the mapping dialog and choose **Save**.
   Creating a record does not itself finish the mapping. If you cancel now, the new record remains.

## Remove a mapping

1. Choose **Change** on the row and review **Currently**.
2. Choose **Remove mapping** inside the form where offered. This clears the row's mapping and keeps the source
   and target records. Check **Unmapped**, using **All** if your previous filter hides the row.
3. If the dialog says the mapping is required, choose an allowed replacement instead of clearing
   it. **Cancel** keeps the current mapping.

## Handle a refused save

If **Mapping conflict** appears, read **Current mapping** and compare it with your intended
selection. Choose **Cancel** to leave it as it now stands. Choose **Continue with my selection**
only after reviewing the other change, then save again. A further intervening change can cause
another refusal. Other **Save failed** messages name a rule to resolve before retrying.

If editing actions are missing, check your context and permissions. Reader can inspect; Contributor
works in change sets; direct Live writes need **Edit live**. Publishing proposed mappings has its
own conflict checks; see [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/).

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/import-:
---
title: Import a file
description: Choose a file, review its preview and load the rows you approve.
reader: steward
---

Load into Live or a change set after checking exactly what the file means. See
[Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/) for file and profile rules.

If **Load a workbook** opens because the assistant is enabled, choose **Import without the
assistant…** to reach the manual import form used below. That manual path does not send the
file to an AI assistant.

1. Open the intended workspace and collection. Choose **Workspace actions › Import**. To
   choose another destination, open **Settings › This instance › Jobs › New import** and
   choose the workspace and **Load into** context.
2. Choose **File**, or drop the file onto that field. The chooser accepts Excel workbooks, CSV and supported technical export
   files. After choosing the file, check **Profile**: refiroo selects it when exactly one valid profile fits. You may choose **None** or another fitting profile. A JSON Lines file takes none; CSV offers profiles with CSV settings or one source; a workbook offers any valid profile for this workspace's model. Invalid profiles and other models' profiles are omitted. Use **None** for a file exported by refiroo. Read any profile problems before continuing. For an exported CSV,
   keep the protective single quotes added to formula-like text. With **None**, import removes
   exactly one such quote from names and text fields; an unchanged export changes nothing.
   XLSX is unaffected. See [CSV text rules](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#text-in-csv-files).
3. Open **Options**. Under **Rows that cannot load**, choose **Load the rows that can load** or **Load nothing
   unless every row loads**. Under **Records the file finds**, decide whether to update or
   refuse them. For an export, **Only if unchanged since the export** protects newer work;
   **Update them anyway** deliberately relaxes that protection.
4. If the file names another workspace's records, choose **Load them as this workspace's own**
   for separate destination records, or **Refuse them**. Check this choice before continuing.
5. Choose **Preview**. The job page opens while the file is read. Check its context, counts,
   column report, **How the file is read** where shown, and refused rows. Each failing cell identifies its column and reason.
   If only part of a large file was tried, its sample is not a promise about every row.
6. Choose **Load the file**, or **Cancel import** if the result is wrong. Loading checks
   current data and can refuse rows that passed preview. Read the final applied and refused counts.
7. Correct refused rows in the file and import it again. Resend the whole file: rows already
   loaded should be unchanged when their values and matching rules are unchanged.

## Check how the file is read

1. In the preview, open **How the file is read** where offered. Each matrix or relationship
   column shows **Matched by**, **Values matched** and **New records go into**. For a workbook
   exported by refiroo, the file records the matching field. When a file does not record it,
   refiroo compares its values with existing records and marks its choice **Guessed**. Read
   any note about an uncertain choice; do not assume a high match count proves it is right.
2. Check each column's field against what its values mean. Where a selector is offered under
   **Matched by**, choose the intended field. This starts a new preview of the same file;
   wait for it and review its counts and refusals again. Nothing is loaded by either preview.
3. For a link matrix with value sheets, check how many rows update existing records and how
   many are new. The main columns also report values found on value sheets and new values.
   An unselected value-sheet row can still create or update a record; review it too.
4. Check **New records go into**. A proposed or rule-defined missing group says
   **will create … under …**. Confirming the load creates that group with its records.
   If there is no suitable place, follow the reason and prepare the place in the app before
   previewing again. You do not need a model change to accept a proposed group.
5. When using a stored profile, choose **Save these fields in the profile** if this reading
   should apply to later files. Saving the reading does not load the file. Review all changes
   and refused rows, then choose **Load the file** only when the preview is right.

For the workbook editing rules, see
[Edit in Excel and import back](/docs/guide/use/edit-in-excel-and-import-back/#edit-the-value-sheets-of-a-link-matrix).

A malformed file or invalid profile changes nothing. Ask a model administrator about profile
rules you cannot fix. A profile deleting records absent from the file must load into a change
set. An expired preview needs a new import preview, rather than another confirmation attempt.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/propose:
---
title: Propose a change
description: Prepare a correction as a Contributor without changing Live.
reader: steward
---

A Contributor prepares changes in a change set for someone authorised to publish.
Read [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) for shared work and publication.

1. In Live, open the record and choose **Propose a change**, or choose **Propose a new …**
   on a collection to add a record. These offers depend on your permission for that type.
2. If you have no open change set of your own, the **Propose a change** dialog asks for
   **Change set name**. Give the work a recognisable name, then choose **Start and edit**.
   **Cancel** leaves Live unchanged. If one already exists, refiroo continues your newest
   open change set instead of asking for another name.
3. Check the amber band for the change-set name. The Live band can also identify **Your change
   set** and its count. Make the correction with the ordinary field or record form; the save
   goes into the change set.
4. Open **Review changes** and check every proposed record and relationship. Your change set
   is shared with other authorised workers, so it can contain work beyond your latest edit.
5. Submit it for publication where offered, or ask someone holding Publish in this workspace
   to publish it. Submission freezes editing until withdrawal or send-back.

![Propose a change dialog with a change-set name and Start and edit above a record in Live](/docs/screens/contributor-propose-change.png)

*Above: a Contributor proposes a correction to Chur Wiesental in the Network application,
Graubünden workspace. Cancel closes the dialog without starting a change set.*

A Reader sees **You can read this workspace** and whom to ask, rather than proposal controls.
Narrowed permissions show actions only for the covered types. Check **Account › What you can do**
if an expected offer is absent. A publication and a retired workspace remain read-only.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/prepare:
---
title: Prepare under the next model version
description: Coordinate a proposal’s model release with the workspace before publishing.
reader: steward
---

A change set can use an installed release while Live still uses another. Coordinate this
with a model administrator. See [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) and
[Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/) for the reviewed conversion process.

1. When creating a change set, open **Options**, then choose **Model version** if your Model release access and the available releases offer a choice. The starting
   records must fit it. A refusal leaves Live unchanged; inspect the named incompatibilities.
2. In an editable change set, use **More change set actions › Change model version** to choose
   a **Target release** where the existing content fits without a conversion. Resolve unsaved
   input before switching. Wait for the new model to load before editing further.
3. If the releases differ, read **This change set uses a different model version**. Ordinary
   publication needs matching releases. **Move this change set to …** instead previews
   converting your proposal to the workspace's release, with no change to Live.
4. Review converted values, changed types, removals and items requiring a fix. Resolve refusals
   and explicitly accept losses before confirming **Move change set**. If the review is stale,
   choose **Preview again**. This move needs background jobs and suitable change-set rights.
5. The alternative **Move … to … and publish…** previews moving the workspace to the proposal's
   release. It needs model-release and publication rights and follows the same approval policy
   as publication. Have the responsible model administrator review it. **Migrate and publish**
   changes the workspace and publishes together, or does neither.

A submitted change set is frozen, including release changes. Its submitter or an authorised
approver must withdraw the request before editing. A changed model reload clears obsolete list
positions and can open another declared view if the old page disappeared. If the release change
succeeded but refreshing failed, reload and check the pinned release before saving; repeating
the move blindly is not recovery.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/withdra:
---
title: Withdraw a publication
description: Remove the current designation while retaining the snapshot and Live data.
reader: steward
---

Withdraw when a publication should no longer be designated current. You need Publish in the
workspace. See [Publications](/docs/use/publications/) for what the designation means.

1. Open **Publications** and locate the row marked **Current**. Check its number and workspace.
2. Open the row's **More actions** and choose **Withdraw publication**.
3. Read **Withdraw Publication …?**. Confirm with **Withdraw publication**, or cancel to keep
   the current designation.
4. Check that the snapshot is **Withdrawn** and no publication is current. Live data, earlier
   publications and history remain. An earlier snapshot is not made current automatically.

If another publication became current meanwhile, the stale withdrawal can be refused. Reload
and review the current row before deciding again. This action does not retire the workspace,
delete the snapshot or undo its data changes. To prepare work from it, use
[Start from an earlier publication](/docs/guide/use/start-from-an-earlier-publication/).
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/delete-:
---
title: Delete many records
description: Preview all dependent records and removed relationships before deleting a selection.
reader: steward
---

Deletion can remove more records than you selected. Read
[Changing many records](/docs/use/changing-many-records/) for permissions and
[Records](/docs/use/records/#deleting-a-record) for ownership rules.

1. Select the records in an editable collection. Check the workspace and whether you are in
   **Live** or a change set. Choose **Delete** in the selection bar.
2. Read the dialog and choose **Delete the rest** to continue with valid deletions despite
   refusals, or **Delete none** to require all items to pass, where that choice is available. Choose **Preview**.
3. Review selected records, children and owned dependants by type, relationships removed,
   and the connections reaching records that stay. A selected record may already be included
   beneath another selected record; do not count it twice.
4. Check the final total on **Delete … records**. This includes dependent records, not only
   selected rows. Use **Back** or cancel if the impact is wrong.
5. Confirm with **Delete … records**. Review the result and reasons for refusals. A new child
   or intervening edit can invalidate an item's preview. Use **Preview again** for refused or
   unprocessed items. For records refused because their version changed, the new preview
   uses their current versions. Review its updated dependent records and relationships
   before confirming again; the earlier preview no longer describes the whole impact.

Live removals take effect immediately. In a change set they remain proposals until publication.
History and earlier publications remain. A sampled preview cannot authorise deletion of items
it did not inspect. Cancellation stops remaining work and leaves already committed removals in place.

![Delete preview for two stops, showing ten relationships to surviving records and the Delete 2 records action.](/docs/screens/bulk-delete-impact.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/change-:
---
title: Change relationship values in bulk
description: Preview and apply one value across selected connections in a relationships table.
reader: steward
---

Use a [relationships table](/docs/use/relationship-tables/) when the value belongs to a connection
rather than a record. You need **Edit live** in Live, or **Work in change sets** in a change set,
with access to change the connections. A publication is read-only.

## Prepare the grid selection

1. Open an application in the current workspace and choose its relationships table. Check that
   it uses grid layout. Read the direction below the heading: rows are from records and column
   groups are to records.
2. Check **Live** or the selected change set. Open a change set first if these values need review
   before publication. The following steps then create proposed changes.
3. Use the row search and **Filter** to narrow the source records. A relationship-value filter
   matches through a connection to one of the shown column records. Check the column selection
   before interpreting how many rows match.
4. Open the menu named for the column record type. Search, filter or tick the records whose
   connections you intend to change. At most 50 column groups are shown. A count such as
   “Showing … of …” means other column records are omitted; narrow the filter if you need them.
5. Tick the intended rows. The header checkbox selects loaded rows. When all loaded rows are
   selected and more match, choose **Select all N matching** to include the whole filtered list.
   Untick individual exceptions. Read the selection count above the grid, then choose
   **Change relationship values**. Changing the search or filters starts a new selection.

## Choose and preview the value

1. In **Attribute of the relationship**, choose the field. The choices come from this view's
   relationship attributes; JSON fields are not offered for this bulk operation.
2. In **At …**, choose **All N shown …** or one named column record. “All” means the shown
   column records, not every record of that type in the workspace.
3. Choose **Set to** and enter a value using the field's own control, or choose **Clear** to
   remove the held value. No is a Yes or no value; Clear removes the value instead.
4. Wait for **The preview**. **Would change** counts linked pairs with a different value;
   **Already …** counts those holding the requested value; **Not linked to the …** counts
   selected row/column pairs without a connection. Nothing has been written yet.
5. If missing pairs should also become connections, select **Also link them, with …**. Leave
   it unticked to change existing connections only. Review the refreshed preview: new links
   must meet the same candidate, number and ownership rules as any other new connection.
6. Read the refusal notice, if shown. Each line names the row record and column record as
   **From record → To record: reason**. The same connection refused for the same reason appears
   once. The heading **N would be refused, so nothing can be changed yet** counts those lines,
   but only the first five are shown. If a record's name is unavailable, a line shows only the
   reason; this can happen with matching rows the grid has not read. Narrow the selection to
   investigate. Check the number beside **Applying changes … relationships**. **Apply**
   stays unavailable while the value is missing or invalid, the preview is loading or failed,
   nothing would change, or any pair would be refused. Correct the value or selection; do not
   assume the remaining pairs will be applied around a refusal.

![Change relationship values dialog with attribute, shown column scope, Set to or Clear and preview counts](/docs/screens/relationships-grid-change-preview.png)

*Above: 10 stops selected in Stops by operator in the Graubünden workspace. Primary contact
is ticked under Set to, at All 2 shown operators. The preview reads Would change 6, Already
Yes 4 and Not linked to the operator 10. Also link them is unticked, so Applying changes
6 relationships counts only existing connections. Apply has not been chosen.*

## Apply and check

1. Choose **Apply**. The operation checks the current data again and writes all changes together.
   Either every intended change succeeds, or none does. A preview does not reserve the data
   against another person's edits.
2. On success, the dialog closes and the grid refreshes. Check a changed cell and the counts.
   A filter on the old value may hide changed rows; clear that filter to inspect them.
3. In a change set, look for **Proposed in this change set**, then
   [review and publish](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) when ready. Applying
   this dialog alone does not publish the change set.

**Nothing was changed** means Apply was refused. Its list uses the same record names and
reasons as the preview, with up to five lines and only the reason when a name is unavailable.
