Check the named connections and current values, then retry with corrected choices. Narrow the
selection if you need to investigate refusals beyond those shown. **Cancel** closes without
applying the preview.

The deployment limits how many source records can be selected and how many relationships one
atomic change can write. One source row can affect many column groups, so a selection can fit
the row limit yet exceed the write limit. If the preview reports too many, narrow the row filter,
choose fewer rows, or choose one column record. Apply smaller reviewed selections, or ask the
operator about the configured limit. Do not keep retrying the same oversized selection.

## Change ticked relationships in the rows layout

The rows layout changes connections that already exist. It does not offer the grid's choice
to add missing pairs or its preview dialog.

1. Search or filter the relationship list and tick the particular relationships to change.
   A source appearing in several rows represents separate connections; tick each intended one.
2. In the selection bar, choose **Attribute to set** and enter the value. A Yes or no field
   offers Yes and No. Leave a non-boolean value empty to clear it.
3. Read the button, **Set … to …**, which names the field and value, then choose it. The bar's
   **Clear** abandons the selection; it does not clear stored values.
4. The ticked connections are saved together using their read versions. Success clears the
   selection and refreshes the list. A refusal displays **Nothing was changed** and the affected
   connections. Review current values before trying again. Split an oversized selection.

This layout also writes proposed changes when a change set is selected, and remains read-only
in a publication.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/reshape:
---
title: Reshape a hierarchy
description: Preview a type change or inserted or removed level inside a change set.
reader: steward
---

Restructuring changes the meaning or levels of a hierarchy. It is available in a change set,
where the model permits it. For a parent-only move, use
[Arrange records in a tree](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/).

1. Open a change set and locate the record in its tree. Open its node menu with its actions button
   or Shift+F10. Choose the offered **Change type…**, **Insert level above…**, **Remove this
   level…** or **Change type of all … in here…**. A move to a **Becomes …** destination opens
   the same kind of reviewed restructuring.
2. Choose **New type**, or **Type of the new level** and **Name of the new level**, as the
   selected action requires. Review any records included beneath the level.
3. Read the plan's counts and open **By record** to inspect the affected records. **By type**
   compares their types and fields. Use **Show** to filter by **Needing input**, **Refused**,
   **Changing type**, **With something left without a place** or **With something restored**
   to inspect the relevant records.
4. Supply values and required connections where the new type needs them. Choose the source
   of a value where the plan offers alternatives. Values that fail the destination's rules
   need input rather than being silently carried over. Something without a place remains
   in history; it is not an editable field of the new type.
5. Resolve all refusals and missing input. **Ready to apply** means the preview can proceed.
   Choose **Apply to the change set**. If **The plan changed** appears, review its new preview
   before applying again.
6. Choose **Review the change set**. Inspect changed types, fields and paths, then validate
   and publish or submit through the usual process. Live retains the earlier structure until
   publication.

Records keep their identity and history. There is no general Undo for data edits; restructuring
can offer compatible values back from effective earlier type changes. It does not restore
intentional clears or discarded work. See [Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/).

![Insert a level above a record: one move and one new record, a required Mode code still empty, and Apply to the change set disabled.](/docs/screens/hierarchy-restructure-plan.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/fill-in:
---
title: Fill in a relation matrix
description: Check coverage, find missing cells, create related records and correct existing ones.
reader: steward
---

Use a relation matrix to find empty cells and maintain the records behind its cells. The rows, columns,
fields and actions come from your model. See [Relation matrices](/docs/use/relation-matrices/)
for cell states, limits and permissions.

## Read the matrix

1. Open an application in the current workspace and choose a collection with a relation matrix.
   Select its matrix view where tabs are offered. Check the heading, row type and column headings.
2. Check the banner. Choose **Live** for immediate changes, or
   [open a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) to stage them. A publication
   is read-only.
3. Read the legend above the table. **One** and **Several** count related records under the
   model's rule. **Inactive** means records exist but none counts. **None** means no related record is present and no earlier-publication record is available to show; **History
   only** has content from an earlier publication; **Conflict** needs inspection because more
   than one record counts where only one is allowed.
4. Search for a row and check its identifying fields. Open a cell under the intended column.
   The dialog heading combines the row and column, so check both before changing anything.
   You can focus the matrix and use arrow keys between cells, then Enter to open one.

![A relation matrix with operators as rows and languages as columns](/docs/screens/matrix-operator-names.png)

*Above: Operator names in Names has many None cells. French and German contain name records.
The legend explains Active is Yes as the condition for counting in this example.*

The same steps apply when columns represent something else:

![A relation matrix with municipalities as rows and systems as columns](/docs/screens/matrix-municipalities-by-system.png)

*Above: Municipalities by system in Systems compares System codes under their systems. One
means exactly one related record here, without the name matrix's Active condition.*

## Choose which columns to show

A matrix includes all records of its column type by default, even those that do not concern the
rows you are working on. Hide empty columns automatically, or choose specific columns yourself.

### Hide empty columns

1. Set the row search and scope to the rows you want to work on, then turn on **Hide empty columns**
   beside **Filter**. The matrix keeps columns with a related record in at least one of those rows,
   including rows not yet on screen. Use the column navigation to reach more columns; empty columns
   do not take up places on its pages.
2. If the switch says **No effect while columns are chosen in Filter**, open **Filter**, choose
   **Show all** followed by the column type's plural name, then **Done**. This clears the chosen
   columns and any cell-state restriction, allowing the switch to take effect.
3. When columns are hidden, read the **N empty columns hidden** line below the toolbar. Choose
   **Show all** on that line, or turn the switch off, to bring them back.

The switch is remembered for this view in this browser. Before checking for missing connections,
turn it off or choose the columns to check explicitly, so wholly empty columns are included.
See [Filters and coverage](/docs/use/relation-matrices/#filters-and-coverage) for how the setting
works with search, scope, change sets and publications.

### Choose specific columns

1. Choose **Filter**. In the section named after the column type followed by **to show**,
   search for and select the columns you need. You can select up to 20; deselect one before
   adding another if you reach the limit.
2. Leave **Cell state** on **Any state**, or choose it to remove an existing state restriction.
   Choose **Done**. The matrix shows only your selected columns.
3. To clear your selection, open **Filter** and choose **Show all** followed by the column
   type's plural name, then **Done**. Use the column navigation if they do not all fit on one page.
   This also clears any cell-state restriction. If **Hide empty columns** is on, it takes effect
   again; turn it off to bring every column back.

Your choice belongs to the page you have open; it is not saved as a setting for the view and
does not change what other people see. Bookmark or share the page's address to reopen the same
column selection. Opening the view again from the navigation clears that selection, but keeps
your **Hide empty columns** setting.

## Find empty cells across the list

1. Clear the row search if you intend to check the whole list, then choose **Filter**.
2. In the section named after the column type followed by **to show**, search for and select
   the columns to check. The chooser can show up to 20 selected columns at once.
3. Under **Cell state**, choose **None**, then **Done**. Rows remain when at least one chosen
   column has that state, across the whole list. If you choose a state without selecting
   columns first, it applies to the columns currently shown.
4. Inspect the result. **No rows match these filters** means no matches within this search
   and column selection. Check omitted columns separately before concluding coverage is complete.
5. To inspect existing records that do not count, choose **Inactive** where offered. Choose
   **Any state** or remove the state pill with **×** to remove the state restriction. Clearing
   the column selection also clears that restriction.

![The Filter panel with cell-state choices and a column search](/docs/screens/matrix-filter-panel.png)

*Above: Municipality names offers Languages to show, with English, French, German, Italian
and Romansh. The state filter tests the chosen or shown languages, not hidden languages.*

## Fill an empty cell

1. Open the intended **None** cell. Check the row and column in the heading and the message
   that no related record exists yet.
2. Choose **Create** followed by the related type's name, where offered. The form identifies
   the row and column under **For** and **under**.
3. Check **Name**, which identifies the new record. Review the proposed name rather than
   treating it as the field content. Under **Goes in**, check where it will belong. The relationship's rules can fix a group;
   otherwise refiroo selects the group already holding the most records used by this view
   in this column. A tie leaves the choice open. An unused group is never selected just
   because it is the only one. Use **Search places…** to choose another offered group.
4. Fill the type's content fields. Set any checkbox or field that determines whether it counts
   according to the legend. Fill **Attributes of the relationship**, if shown: these describe
   the new connection rather than the record itself. Choose the form's **Add** action followed by the cell type's name. On success, the dialog closes
   and the cell refreshes; check its state and displayed content.
5. Use **Back** to abandon the creation form and return to the cell, then **Close** to leave
   without creating anything. If creation is refused, correct the named problem before retrying.

![A searched matrix showing one missing cell beside four filled cells](/docs/screens/matrix-missing-name.png)

*Above: Bonaduz in Municipality names has One in four languages and None in Romansh. The empty cell
was prepared for these captures and filled again afterwards; it is not the reference data's current state.*

![An empty cell dialog offering creation of the missing related record](/docs/screens/matrix-missing-name-cell.png)

*Above: Bonaduz · rm says None · no name translation yet and offers Create name translation.*

![A creation form with a proposed name, selected container, content field and current flag](/docs/screens/matrix-missing-name-add.png)

*Above: For Bonaduz under rm fixes the cell. Name is proposed as Bonaduz rm; Goes in is Romansh.
Translated name is empty and Active is selected. Back was used without saving this form.*

If **Link existing** followed by a type name is offered, use it when the desired record already
exists. Search, inspect the candidate and any refusal reason, select an eligible record, fill
**Attributes of the relationship** if offered, and choose **Link**. This adds a connection instead of creating another record.

## When a new group is proposed

If the relationship's rules identify one group and it is missing, **Goes in** says **(will be
created)**. Saving creates that group, the record and its connection together.

When neither the rules nor existing records give a place, refiroo can propose a new group
named like the groups this view uses in other columns. Review **Name of the new …** and change
it if needed. Submit the creation form once to create both group and record. Where offered,
**Use an existing group instead** opens the group choices. Only places compatible with the
relationship's rules are offered. If no proposal or suitable place is available, resolve the
missing place in the app before creating the record. No model change is needed to accept a
proposed group.

## Add another record or reuse one

1. Open a filled cell and inspect the records already connected to the row. If the cell allows
   several records and the view permits creation, **Create** appears beside **Link existing**.
2. Choose **Create** when this is a new record. Choose its **Goes in** container and fill its
   fields as for an empty cell. The record is also listed in that container; it is not stored
   only inside the matrix.
3. Choose **Link existing** when the record already exists under this column. Search the
   candidates and read any reason beside a disabled choice. An existing link or a relationship
   limit can prevent selection. Select an eligible record, fill any **Attributes of the
   relationship**, then choose **Link**.
4. Check the refreshed cell. Linking adds a relationship to the existing record. Where the
   relationship permits reuse, that record can appear under several rows. Editing its own
   fields affects that shared record; each connection keeps its own relationship values.

**Example: a mapping matrix.** A code already connected to one row can also be linked to another
where the model permits it. Reuse keeps the same record identity. Create makes a separate record
and a new connection. After publication, connected systems see the corresponding connections
where their access includes them.

A filled cell that may hold only one record does not offer **Create**. Inspect or edit the
record already there. Empty, inactive and history-only cells can still offer creation where
configured. For example, a translation matrix may permit one counting name per language:
create a missing name, and edit an existing one rather than adding another counting name.
Publishing makes the new record and its connection available to connected systems that expose them.

## Correct an existing cell record

1. Remove a missing-cell filter before searching for an existing record. Find the row and open
   the cell under the intended column.
2. The cell opens a table with one row per linked record. Use its filter box to narrow record
   names and displayed record fields. Read the record's columns first, then the tinted
   **Attributes of the relationship** columns. Choose **Open** for its full page and history.
3. Edit the intended value in place. A Yes or no checkbox saves with one click. For another
   field, open its small editor and enter the value; Enter saves an ordinary single-line field,
   and Escape cancels. Clicking outside an unchanged record-field editor closes it. Leaving
   a relationship-value editor also attempts to save. Check the refreshed value and any error.
4. Check the condition for counting before switching an availability checkbox off: the cell
   can become Inactive without removing the record. Successful inline saves leave the table
   open. If a row disappears from a state-filtered matrix, select **Any state** to find it again.
5. To remove a permitted connection, choose **Unlink** on its row. Read the confirmation there:
   **Keep** cancels, **Unlink** confirms and keeps the related record. Choose **Close** when done.

![Cell table separating record fields from relationship values, with a value editor open](/docs/screens/matrix-cell-relationship-table-editor.png)

*Above: the Schmitten (GR) cell under wikidata-municipalities in Municipalities by system in
the Graubünden workspace. One code, Q65399, has Confirmed ticked and the Note editor open
with “Merged municipality, old code kept”. These values belong to its connection to the municipality.*

![An existing cell record open for editing with a content field and Active checkbox](/docs/screens/matrix-cell-editor.png)

*Above: Chur · rm opens the Romansh name Cuira with Active selected. Open Chur (rm) leads to the
full name record. Cancel leaves its fields unchanged.*

In a one-per-column counting rule, a change set can temporarily hold two counting records
for one cell. It shows **Conflict** with the count. Open it and inspect both records. Correct
which records meet the counting condition, or **Unlink** an unintended connection where
permitted. Unlink keeps the record. Validate the change set again before publishing; resolve
any remaining refusal through the affected record's full page. Live writes refuse a second
counting record. A conflict in proposed work is not a published extra value.
See [Cell states](/docs/use/relation-matrices/#cell-states).

For an **Inactive** cell, review existing records before adding another. For **Several**,
inspect the records before deciding whether anything needs changing; several may be allowed.
For **Conflict**, resolve the extra counting records before publication. Where **Unlink** is
offered, it asks for confirmation and keeps the related record; required ownership cannot be
removed this way. To add an owned record from its owner's full page instead, follow
[Create an owned related record](/docs/guide/use/relate-records/#create-an-owned-related-record).

For **History only**, inspect the read-only content from the named earlier publication.
Where **Create from this** is offered, it opens creation with those values supplied. Review
Name, container and fields before creating a new record; it does not undo a deletion or restore
the old record's identity and history.

## When a save or read fails

A duplicate refusal can offer **Open the … already here**. Inspect that record instead of
creating another. If **Changed elsewhere** appears, review the refreshed cell and your retained
input before retrying. If the record moved out of the cell, inspect the current contents first.
A loading failure needs a retry, not a new record to fill an apparently empty cell.

If actions are missing, check that the context is editable, you have **Edit live** or **Work
in change sets** as appropriate, and the model offers the intended action. Reader can inspect
cells. A matrix is not a promise that every visible cell can be edited.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/export-:
---
title: Export records
description: Export the view you are using, or choose a type, an application or the whole workspace.
reader: steward
---

Take a file of the data you need. Read
[Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/) for file shapes and workbook rules.

1. Open the intended view in the current workspace and **Live**, change set or publication.
   Set its search, filters, parent scope and chosen columns before opening Export.
2. Open **Workspace actions › Export**. Under **What**, the first choice is **This view**
   followed by its name. Keep it to export the view with its search and supported filters.
   Read the count line and context: a matrix reports rows × columns; a tree or mapping grid
   reports records. Counts are shown when the page knows them. This includes matching rows
   beyond those currently on screen.
3. To take a wider selection, choose **The type**, **The application** or **The whole workspace**.
   These choices select whole types rather than the current view's narrowed rows. Check
   **Record types** and **Where** where offered. You can also start an export from
   **Settings › This instance › Jobs**.
4. Choose **Kind of file**. **For editing in a spreadsheet** makes an Excel (XLSX) workbook
   shaped for the chosen view or types. **Technical** is offered for a table view, a type,
   an application or the workspace; it offers **Excel (XLSX)**, **CSV** or **JSON Lines**
   under **Format**. A matrix, tree, mapping grid or relationships table exports its view
   as a workbook for editing. In CSV, text that could start a spreadsheet formula receives
   one extra leading single quote, even when single quotes already precede the formula character.
   Keep it if you return the CSV; import reads back the original text. XLSX is unaffected.
   See [CSV text rules](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#text-in-csv-files).
5. Read any notice about filters not carried into the file. A filter on a relationship's own
   values is not carried. The file can therefore include connections that filter hid.
   For a table workbook, **Advanced: columns and sheets** adjusts its columns and related sheets.
6. For a matrix listing linked records, check **What each cell lists**. Under **Each linked
   record is listed by its**, keep **Name** or choose a text field of those records. Choose a
   field whose values distinguish the records in each column. The file records this choice
   so import reads the cells the same way. If linked records have no value in that field,
   the export is refused; fill those values or choose another field.
   Each column also gets a value sheet with its records and fields. New records use the
   relationship's rules and existing groups when imported; there is no group choice in Export.
7. Where offered, choose **Relationships**: **Between exported records**, **All their
   relationships**, or **None**. Use **Valid on** only when you need a business-date extract.
   Check the selection and context, then choose **Start export**.
8. Open **View job** from the notification to follow progress. When completed, choose
   **Download** before retention ends. Failed or cancelled exports have no file; correct
   the stated reason and start another export.
9. In an XLSX file, read the second sheet, **About this export**. It explains the source,
   counts, relationships, what loads back and, for a creating matrix, where new records go.
   Check it before editing: a matrix workbook loads its cells, not changes to its row labels.

For a workbook to edit and return, follow
[Edit in Excel and import back](/docs/guide/use/edit-in-excel-and-import-back/).

![Export dialog showing This view, its count and What each cell lists](/docs/screens/export-for-people.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/approve:
---
title: Approve a change set
description: Submit proposed work, review a request and publish it or send it back.
reader: steward
---

Use this task when a proposal needs someone else's decision. You need **Approve publications**
to decide a request. A workspace can require a second person, even if the submitter holds that
permission. See [Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/) for the policy and notices.

## Submit your work

1. [Prepare the change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/), then check its
   workspace in the sidebar and name in the band. Open **Details** for its version.
   Review the proposed records and relationships.
2. Choose **Submit for publication** where offered. The dialog explains that refiroo validates
   the change set and that it cannot be edited while it waits. Add a comment if the approver
   needs context, then choose **Submit**. **Cancel** leaves it unsubmitted.
3. If validation fails, fix the reported problems and submit again. Success says
   **Submitted for publication. It waits for approval.** The approvers receive a notice.
4. Check that the band now says **waits for approval**. Open **Details** for the submitted
   version and your name; read your comment in the review’s **Decision** panel. To change your proposal while it waits, choose **Withdraw request** first. The proposed work
   stays in the change set and becomes editable. After correction, submit a new request.

![Submitted change set showing Waiting for approval, version, comment and Withdraw request](/docs/screens/appr-submitted.png)

*Above: Guide Admin's Guide approval example waits in Graubünden. Its submitted version is 2;
the proposed height correction is still separate from Live.*

If **Publish** is offered instead, your permissions and the policy allow direct
publication. Use the [publish steps](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/#publish).
Do not change workspace policy merely to make a button appear; ask an administrator if the
available actions do not match your responsibility.

## Open and review a request

1. Open the bell and choose **Waiting for your approval**, or open the request from Home's
   **Waiting for your approval** section using **Review**. The Home list shows the change-set
   name, workspace, submitter and submission time, newest first. You can also open a submitted change set and choose
   **Review and decide**.
2. Check the workspace, change-set name, submitted version, submitter and their comment.
   Review all proposed changes, not just the first visible record.
3. On **Records**, expand changed entries to inspect before and after values. Review created
   and deleted records as well. On **Relationships**, inspect added, changed and removed connections.

![Approver's Home with Waiting for your approval and a Review button](/docs/screens/appr-home-waiting.png)

*Above: fictional approver Rita Approver has Data owner access in Graubünden. Guide Admin's
request appears below her workspace card.*

![Review changes with a Decision panel above the proposed record change](/docs/screens/appr-decision-panel.png)

*Above: Rita sees who submitted version 2, when it was submitted and the comment about Davos
Platz's height. Expand the record below the panel to inspect the correction before deciding.*

If you open your own request while a second person is required, there is no **Decision** panel.
The review says **A second person must decide this request.** You can read the changes, but another
authorised approver must decide.

![Submitter's own review with the second-person message and no Decision panel](/docs/screens/appr-own-approval.png)

*Above: Guide Admin can inspect the Davos Platz change but cannot approve this request themselves.*

## Decide

1. Read **Decision** and confirm it names the version you reviewed. If the screen says the
   proposal changed since submission, choose **Reload** and inspect its current state. Do not
   decide an older version as though it were the current proposal.
2. To accept it, add an optional **Comment** and choose **Approve and publish**. This immediately
   attempts publication. On success, the change set is consumed, Live contains its authored
   changes and a new publication holds the result. The submitter is notified.
3. To request corrections, enter a **Comment** saying what needs attention and choose **Send back**.
   A blank comment is refused. Success returns the change set to its submitter for editing and
   another submission, without publishing it.
4. If publication reports a conflict or validation failure, read the reason and refresh the
   review. Have the proposal corrected and resubmitted where necessary. A refused decision is
   not a successful publication.

![Decision panel with a reason entered before sending the request back](/docs/screens/appr-send-back-reason.png)

*Above: Rita asks for the source of the new height. The reason is entered, but Send back has not
yet been pressed.*

If the request was withdrawn or already decided, reload to see its new state.

## Correct work that was sent back

1. Open the returned change set from your notice or the change-set list. The notice says
   **Sent back** and names the request; its detail includes the reason and approver.
2. Read the reason in the notice below the change-set band. The request is no longer waiting
   and the change set is editable again. From **Changes in this change set**, choose **See the
   data with these changes** to inspect and correct the affected records and relationships.
3. Review the whole result, then choose **Submit for publication** again. In **Comment (optional)**,
   explain what you corrected or add the context the approver requested. Choose **Submit**.
   The change set is validated again and waits for a new decision. **Cancel** leaves it editable.

![Submitter's inbox with the send-back reason and approver](/docs/screens/appr-sent-back-notice.png)

*Above: Guide Admin's newest notice carries Rita's request for a source.*

![Returned change set with the approver's reason and preparation controls](/docs/screens/appr-sent-back.png)

*Above: Guide approval example is open for correction. The banner shows Rita's reason and offers
Submit for publication again.*

![Submit for publication dialog with a new comment for resubmission](/docs/screens/appr-resubmit.png)

*Above: Guide Admin adds the source of the height in a new submission comment. The dialog explains
that the change set cannot be edited while it waits.*

## Approve the revised request and check the result

1. As the approver, open the new request from Home or the inbox. Read the current **Decision**
   details and the new submission comment. Review the records and relationships again; the earlier
   review does not approve later edits.
2. If the proposal is ready, choose **Approve and publish**. Wait for success. If it is refused,
   resolve the reported conflict or invalid data as described under [Decide](#decide).
3. Open **Publications** in the application. The new publication is **Current** and names the
   approver as the person who published it. Choose **Open publication** to inspect the snapshot.
   Check the changed records in **Live** too.
4. As the submitter, open the bell. The approval notice confirms the decision. Earlier notices
   can remain in the inbox; read the newest result rather than treating a previous send back as
   still pending.
5. To trace the work, open **Settings**, **Workspaces**, select the workspace and choose
   **Activity**. Read the actions, people and times. See [History](/docs/use/history/) for filtering.

![Approver's Decision panel showing the resubmission comment before approval](/docs/screens/appr-approve.png)

*Above: Rita reviews the new source comment before choosing Approve and publish.*

![Publications with the new current snapshot and the previous publication](/docs/screens/appr-publication.png)

*Above: Publication 2 in Graubünden is Current and was published by Rita. Publication 1 is no
longer current; it is also marked Withdrawn in this example.*

![Submitter's inbox showing the approval notice](/docs/screens/appr-approved-notice.png)

*Above: Guide Admin receives the approval result above the earlier send-back notice.*

Follow [Browse a publication](/docs/guide/use/browse-a-publication/) for inspecting the saved result.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/copy-or:
---
title: Copy or move records to another workspace
description: Choose an approved mapping, inspect the dry run and publish the destination before source deletions.
reader: steward
---

Use a saved mapping prepared for the two workspace models. See
[Copying and moving records](/docs/use/copying-and-moving/) for access, retained identities,
omissions and the difference between Copy and Move. For mapping design, ask a model
administrator to follow [Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/).

1. Open **Settings › Workspaces and models › Copy and move**. Check **Recent copies and moves**
   for an existing operation before choosing **New copy or move…**.
2. Choose **From workspace** and **To workspace**. Check their model names and releases.
   Under **Mapping**, select the agreed saved mapping. If none fits, stop and have its owner
   prepare one; **A new mapping, proposed** is a suggestion requiring design review.
3. Choose **Open the editor**. Select **Copy** to retain the source, or **Move** to prepare
   source deletions as well. Nothing has reached Live in either workspace.
4. Beside **What to copy** or **What to move**, choose **Change…**. Choose the intended scope,
   fill its types, filters or starting record, then choose **Dry run this selection**.
   Wait for the check of all selected items.
5. Inspect creates, updates, omissions, **Values not carried** and **What cannot be copied**
   or **What cannot move**. Open the reasons and affected records. Ask the mapping owner to
   correct unexpected losses, required values or placement problems before proceeding.
6. Choose **Start the copy…** or **Start the move…**. Read the confirmation and enter
   **Name of the change set of workspace …** for the destination. Choose **Start the copy**
   or **Start the move** to load the proposal; **Cancel** keeps the work unstarted.
7. Read the actual result and refused or kept records. Choose **Review the change set** for
   the destination. Review records and relationships, correct problems, validate, and
   [publish or submit for approval](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/).
8. For Move, publish that destination first. Then choose **Review the deletions** and inspect
   the source proposal. Check which records were kept and why. Publish or obtain approval
   there separately. Publishing the copy has not itself deleted the originals.

![Finished move linking to the destination change set and source deletion proposal](/docs/screens/use-move-review-change-sets.png)

If the mapping or workspace release changed after the dry run, inspect the current mapping
and check again. A refused start is not permission to use the older preview. If the running
operation fails, open its [job](/docs/use/jobs/) and any produced change sets before repeating
it. If no items can transfer, revise the scope or ask the mapping owner to fix the report's
reasons. Closing a running operation's page leaves it working in the background.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/ask-a-l:
---
title: Ask a list in words
description: Ask a table collection a question, review its filters and correct an incomplete answer.
reader: steward
---

Use this to find records by describing the conditions you need. You need a table collection,
an enabled AI provider, and **Browse** and **Use AI proposals** in the workspace.
See [Asking a list in words](/docs/use/ask-in-words/) for the supported questions.
Your words and the list's definitions are sent to AI; short related lists can include names.
Requests can cost money and their outcome is kept. Read [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/)
before sending sensitive information.

1. Open a table collection in the current workspace. Check whether you are reading **Live**,
   a change set or a publication: Ask searches that context.
2. Choose **Ask** beside the search box. In **Ask in words**, describe the records you want,
   using field and relationship names you recognise. For example, with the reference data:
   “Stops updated last month with no operator” asks for a Live date condition and a missing relationship.
3. Press **Enter**. **Asking…** appears with **Cancel**. Cancel stops waiting for the answer;
   do not assume it reverses a provider request already sent or its cost.
4. When the question is fully expressed, read **Your question became these filters. Change or
   remove any of them.** Check the pills and search text against your question. They replace
   the earlier search and filters. Open a pill to adjust its condition or use **×** to remove it.
   The results update as with manually chosen filters.
5. If **This list cannot answer all of that, so nothing was applied.** appears, read each
   **Not possible here:** line. Dashed pills under **What it could do:** are only a proposal.
   Choose **Use these filters** if that smaller question is useful, or rewrite the question and
   press Enter again. To disambiguate a record, use more of its name.
6. If an error appears, your words stay and the earlier list remains. Retry after the cause is
   addressed, or choose **Search** and set filters yourself. An unavailable Created or Updated
   condition needs Live; asking from a snapshot cannot supply those times.

![A table list after a question becomes ordinary editable filter pills](/docs/screens/use-ask-filters.png)

*Above: the reference Stops list after a question becomes filters. The pills, rather than the
wording of the question, determine which stops are shown.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/arrange:
---
title: Arrange records in a tree
description: Browse branches, rename a record and move it to an allowed parent.
reader: steward
---

Use a tree view to inspect where records belong and move them to an allowed place. See
[Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/) for parents, type rules and the effect on descendants.

## Browse a branch

1. Open an application in the current workspace. Choose a collection and its tree view, where
   offered. Check the heading and the banner: **Live**, a named change set or a publication.
2. Expand the arrow beside a type group or record. Its children appear below it. Continue
   down to the branch you need; collapse an arrow to hide that branch without changing data.
3. Use **Find a record** to search, checking names, types and paths before selecting a match.
   Clear the search to return to browsing. A branch loads more records as you scroll.
4. For keyboard browsing, focus the tree and use arrow keys to move through it and expand
   or collapse branches. Open the record when you need its full fields and relationships.

![A hierarchy expanded through several record types to a municipality's stops](/docs/screens/tree-geography-chur.png)

*Above: Geography in Network is expanded through Graubünden, Plessur and Chur. Stops appears
as a type group above the stop records.*

![A hierarchy with records nested under others of the same type](/docs/screens/tree-modes.png)

*Above: Modes groups Train and Tram under Rail-bound, and Bus under Road. The record type is
Mode at both levels; a tree is not limited to a chain of different types.*

If a branch reports a loading failure, retry it. A failed read does not mean the parent has
no children. If the tree is empty, check its workspace, context and search before adding data.

## Move a record

1. Choose **Live** for an immediate move, or [open a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/)
   to stage it. Check the banner and the record's current ancestors.
2. Open the record's **…** menu and choose **Move to…**. You can also open the menu with a
   right click or **Shift+F10** while the record has focus. The dialog names the record and
   shows **Now in** followed by its current path.
3. Search by name for the new parent. Check the path below each candidate to distinguish
   repeated names. Select its radio button; typing a name alone is not a selection.
4. Use **Top level** only if you intend to remove the parent and the choice is available.
   Unavailable destinations state their reason. If no destination matches, shorten the search
   and check the model's allowed placements before continuing.
5. Check the selected destination and choose **Move to** followed by its name, or
   **Move to the top level**. Before selection the button reads **Move**. Wait for completion,
   then inspect the new branch or the record's path. The descendants move with the record.
   **Cancel** leaves its placement unchanged.

![A move dialog showing the present path, candidate parents and an unavailable top level](/docs/screens/tree-move-dialog.png)

*Above: Move 85 Garage Chur shows its current place under Graubünden / Plessur / Chur and offers
other municipalities. Top level explains why it is unavailable in this tree. The dialog was cancelled.*

A choice marked **Becomes** changes the record's type in a change set. Its button opens a type
change preview instead of making an ordinary move; review the resulting fields and missing
values before applying it. Cancel if you only intended to change the parent.

Dragging a record onto a parent is another way to move it. Review the destination and any
confirmation before proceeding. On touch screens, hold the record still until it lifts, then
drag. Beginning to move your finger before it lifts scrolls the tree instead.

## Add the first top-level record

In an editable tree, choose **Add …** for the intended top-level type in the header or empty
view. Complete the new record’s name and required fields, then choose **Add** followed by the record type's name. This form
has no parent field: the record starts at the top of this tree. Add children from its menu
afterwards. The action appears only for types allowed at the top, when the view allows creation
and your permissions allow writing that type.

## Rename or add a child

1. Open the record's menu and choose its rename action, or press **F2** on the focused record.
   Enter the intended name and confirm the rename. Check the new label; the record retains
   its identity and connections.
2. To add within a parent, choose the menu's add-child action for an offered type. Complete
   the new record form, check its parent and choose **Add** followed by the record type's name. If the needed type is absent,
   ask a model administrator about the permitted children.
3. Where an availability action is offered, use it only to change whether the record is
   available under that model's rule. It does not delete the record.

If a move or rename is refused, read the reason and review the current record before retrying.
Another person's change can make your version stale. If editing controls are absent, check
[permissions](/docs/use/records/#who-may-read-and-change-records) and the configured actions;
publications and retired workspaces are read-only. For permanent removal and its impact, see
[Deleting a record](/docs/use/records/#deleting-a-record).

## Move a selection together

1. In the sidebar tree or tree view, use Cmd or Ctrl to select individual records, or Shift
   for a range. With the keyboard, use Ctrl+Space and Shift+arrows. Escape clears the selection.
2. Open the selection's menu with right click or Shift+F10 and choose **Move to…**, or drag
   the selected records together onto the new parent.
3. Read the destination and confirmation for the whole selection. Confirm only when every
   selected record belongs there. If any cannot move, none moves; correct the selection or
   destination and try again.

In a long branch opened partway down, use **Show earlier records** to read those above it.
For **Change type…**, **Insert level above…**, **Remove this level…** or
**Change type of all … in here…**, first open a change set. Review the preview's types,
values, missing values and content kept only in history before applying; see
[Restructuring](/docs/use/hierarchies/#restructure-in-a-change-set).

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/relate-:
---
title: Relate records
description: Connect records, replace a single connection and remove an optional relationship.
reader: steward
---

Connect two records using a relationship declared by the model. See
[Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/) for candidates, ownership and required connections.

## Open the relationship section

1. Open an application in the current workspace and [find the record](/docs/guide/use/find-records/).
   Check its name, identifying fields and path.
2. Check **Live** for an immediate change, or [open a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/)
   to prepare work for publication. Check the banner before editing.
3. Scroll to the relationship section you need. Its heading describes the connected records.
   Read existing entries before adding another. **No relationships yet** means the section is
   empty; a loading error needs a retry instead.

![Relationship sections with add, change and delete controls](/docs/screens/relationships-stop.png)

*Above: Chur Wiesental in Network has Modes, Operator and System codes sections. Modes permits
several connections; Operator permits one. Further sections continue below the capture.*

## Connect an existing record

1. Choose **Add relationship**, or **Set** followed by the relationship name when the empty
   section permits just one. The connection form opens beside the page on a desktop.
2. Where the relationship is known, the form says **Add a** followed by the related type **to** this record (or **Add an** where appropriate). Read the relationship named beneath it. If several choices are offered, choose the intended type and relationship under **What to add** before searching.
3. Under the related record type's name, type part of the related record's name or a searchable field. Read any
   hint explaining which records are offered. Select a result, checking its path. Typing alone
   leaves **Nothing selected** and does not enable saving.
4. Fill any fields carried by the relationship. These describe the connection, rather than
   changing the other record's fields.
5. Choose **Add** followed by the related type's name, or **Set** in the single-connection form. On success the dialog closes;
   check that the connected record appears in the section. **Cancel** abandons the connection;
   if asked to discard unsaved changes, confirm only if that is what you intend.

![The Connect an object dialog with a relationship choice and candidate search](/docs/screens/relationship-picker-mode.png)

*Above: Add relationship in Chur Wiesental's Modes panel offers Served by mode (outgoing) and
candidate modes such as Boat and Bus. Nothing is selected; this dialog was cancelled.*

If a record is missing, clear or shorten the search and check the workspace, context, type and
candidate hint. A model can limit candidates by their own or their ancestors' fields. Ask a
model administrator about the rule if the expected record is still unavailable. A refused save
may report a duplicate, a number limit or changed data; resolve that reason before retrying.

## Replace a single connection

1. In a section that allows one related record, choose its **Change** action. Read **Now:**
   to confirm the connection you intend to replace.
2. Search and select the replacement under the related type's name. Check its identifying fields and path.
   The currently connected record is not offered as its own replacement.
3. Choose **Change**. The replacement is saved together; check the section's new entry.
   Choose **Cancel** to keep the existing connection.
4. If the dialog says the relationship changed after the list was read, close it and review
   the refreshed section. Reopen **Change** only if replacement is still appropriate.

![A replacement dialog identifying the current record and offering other candidates](/docs/screens/relationship-picker-operator.png)

*Above: Operated by currently connects Chur Wiesental to Rhätische Bahn. The dialog offers
replacement operators. It was cancelled, leaving Rhätische Bahn connected.*

Where a relationship has its own fields, its **Edit** action opens those fields. Correct them
and choose **Save**; use **Change** when replacing the related record itself. A version refusal
requires reviewing the current saved connection before saving again.

## Remove an optional connection

1. Find the exact relationship row and check both record names, especially where a section contains several connections.
2. Choose **Remove relationship**. It removes the connection immediately, without a confirmation; both records remain.
3. Check the refreshed section. The removal notice offers **Undo** to create the connection again. If removal is refused because it is required, review the intended correction and use a replacement where allowed.

![The Delete relationship confirmation explaining that both records remain](/docs/screens/relationship-delete-confirm.png)

*Above: deleting Chur Wiesental's Served by mode connection would leave both the stop and Train.
The confirmation was cancelled, so the connection remains.*

To change containment, [move the record](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/).
Deleting a record has a different impact; see [Records](/docs/use/records/#deleting-a-record).

## Create an owned related record

Some sections offer an add action named after the related type rather than connecting an
existing record. Use it when you need a new dependent record.

1. Choose that section's add action. Check the new record form and its already supplied
   connection to the source record.
2. Under **Parent**, search and select the intended container where requested. Check the
   selected path; search text alone does not select it.
3. Fill **Name** and the type's other fields. Set any field that determines whether the record
   counts as current according to the model's rule.
4. Choose **Add** followed by the new record type's name and check the new entry in the original section. Correct any reported
   missing values or duplicate before retrying. **Cancel** leaves without creating the record.

![A new related record form with parent choices and its owner already supplied](/docs/screens/stop-add-translation.png)

*Above: Add Name translation on Chur Wiesental opens a form with Translates already set to
that stop. Parent offers languages; Name, Translated name and Active describe the new record.
The form was cancelled. This is an example of creating an owned record.*

If editing actions are absent, check your context and
[record permissions](/docs/use/records/#who-may-read-and-change-records). A publication is read-only;
a Reader can inspect connections but cannot change them.

A lock on a row explains why it cannot be deleted or changed independently. Parent connections
are maintained by moving the record. Beside a tree, **Connected** chips open related records;
open the full record page to use the relationship tables and their tooltip-labelled icons.

*Screenshot data: Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of
Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. See [The example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/)
for sources and fictional additions.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/delete-:
---
title: Delete a record
description: Review dependent records and relationships before confirming a permanent removal.
reader: steward
---

Delete only when the record should be removed. To keep it for history and stop offering it,
see [Stop offering a value](/docs/guide/use/stop-offering-a-value/). Read
[Records](/docs/use/records/#deleting-a-record) for ownership rules.

1. Open the record and check its workspace and Live or change-set band. Open **⋯** and choose
   **Delete record**. You need permission for the record and dependants the deletion removes.
2. Read **Delete …?**. Wait while **Checking what deleting it would take…** is shown. Nothing is deleted while refiroo reads the impact. If that read fails, choose **Retry** after resolving the stated problem, or **Cancel** to leave it.
3. Review the counts of records and relationships removed. Dependants are named with their types, up to eight names followed by **and N more** for a longer list. Children and owned dependants
   go with the record, including owned records in another application. Independent records
   and their hierarchies remain.
4. Confirm once, only when that is the intended impact. The button says **Delete N records** when dependants are included, or **Delete** followed by the record type's name for a single record. **Cancel** leaves everything in place.
5. After success, the list opens. In Live the removal is immediate; in a change set it stays
   proposed until publication. Earlier publications and history are not erased.

If someone changes the record or adds a dependant before confirmation, the stale deletion
is refused. The confirmation refreshes the impact and says **The record changed after this was shown**. Review the new impact before confirming again; it does not silently delete a larger set. If the refresh fails, resolve that error before proceeding.

![Single-record deletion impact showing dependent names/types, relationships removed, independent connections retained and Confirm deletion.](/docs/screens/record-delete-impact.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/change-:
---
title: Change values of many records
description: Set or clear fields on selected records after reviewing a preview.
reader: steward
---

Use this for the same field correction on several records. Read
[Changing many records](/docs/use/changing-many-records/) for selection, access and limits.

1. In an editable collection, tick the records or choose **Select all … matching**. Check the
   count and any exclusions in the selection bar, then choose **Change values**.
2. Choose **Change a field** and select a field. Choose **Set to** and enter its new value,
   or **Clear** for an optional field. Required fields cannot be cleared. Read-only and hidden
   fields are not offered. Repeat to change more fields together.
3. Leave a field out to keep its value. To remove a field you added, use its **Do not change …**
   button. This form does not need a Keep choice on every field.
4. Choose **Change the rest** to apply records that can change despite other refusals, or
   **Change none** to require every item to pass. If the second option is unavailable, the
   dialog explains the deployment's all-or-nothing limit.
5. Choose **Preview**. Read how many records would change, already hold the values, or would
   be refused. Open a refused record to understand its reason. Use **Back** to revise the change.
6. Choose **Apply**, then read the actual result. A record changed by someone else is refused.
   **Preview again** checks remaining work against current values. Choose **Done** when finished.

**View job** leaves a preview waiting on its job page. Closing the preview otherwise cancels
it. If the model changed, reload before making a fresh change; if the change set changed,
preview again. A successful preview never reserves a record against another editor.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/review-:
---
title: Review what a change set changes
description: Inspect record and relationship differences before validation or a publication decision.
reader: steward
---

Compare proposed work with the data the change set started from. See
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/#review-explains-the-differences).

1. From **Change sets**, choose **Open change set** to open **Changes in this change set**.
   If you are already browsing its data, choose **Review changes** in the amber band. Confirm
   its name; open **Details** for its source. If it started from a publication, the earlier values come from that publication,
   not today's Live.
2. Under **Records**, filter by change kind or record type. Open a row to read before/after
   values and paths. A moved record names both parents. A type-change filter can match either
   its old or new type, so check the difference itself.
3. Open **Relationships** and inspect additions, changes and removals separately. A record
   review alone does not account for every changed connection.
4. Scroll or jump through the lists. The address retains the tab, filters and position so
   you can return to the same part of the review.
5. Choose **See the data with these changes** to return to editing for corrections, then
   choose **More change set actions › Validate now**. You can also choose **Publish**, which checks before confirmation. Resolve its named
   problems and validate the new version again before publishing or submitting.

A record created and deleted in the same change set contributes no remaining change and is
omitted. A record edited back to its original values can still count as changed, because
publication still checks the version it claims. A successful validation is not protection
against later Live conflicts; publication checks again.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/find-re:
---
title: Find records
description: Find a record, narrow and sort the results, and inspect its fields and relationships.
reader: steward
---

Find a record and check its fields and connections. See [Records](/docs/use/records/) for
background on records, workspaces and applications.

For choosing a dataset or view, follow [Open an application](/docs/guide/use/open-an-application/).
For the connected records you inspect, see [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/).


## Open the right list

1. On Home, find the workspace you need under **Your workspaces**. Choose its name or tile
   to open its page, then choose an application. An application link on its card opens it directly.
2. Check **Workspace** in the sidebar. If it names a different workspace, select the intended
   one before searching: a record with the same name elsewhere may hold different data.
3. Choose the collection you need under **Collections**. To find a list by name, use the search above the page and choose a result under **Lists**. Press ⌘K on a Mac or Ctrl+K elsewhere to focus search. See [Applications](/docs/use/applications/#find-a-list-in-the-sidebar) for lists and places in search. The collection's heading identifies the list. Available collections and their
   labels depend on your workspace's model.
4. Choose **Live** at the top to search current data. Check the green **Live** banner. To
   inspect proposed or previously published data, open that change set or publication instead;
   check the context before interpreting the results.

![Home showing workspace cards and their application buttons](/docs/screens/home.png)

*Above: the Graubünden workspace card offers Network, Systems and Names. Network contains the
Stops collection used in the following screenshots.*

## Search for a record

1. To search names across the workspace, use **Find a record in this workspace** above the page or **Find a
   record** on the workspace’s page. Check the list and path beside a result; use the arrow
   keys and Enter to open one in **Live**. To stay in a change set or publication, or search
   just this collection, type all or part of the record’s name in the search box above the list. Wait for the results
   to update. Use a shorter part of the name if you are unsure of its spelling.
2. Check the result names and identifying fields before opening one. Several records may have
   similar names; a number, date or related record can distinguish them.
3. If the record is missing, check the workspace, application and context first. Clear filters
   that may exclude it. Clear the search text to see the list without that search. If the list
   reports a loading failure, use its retry control rather than treating it as an empty result.

![A record list narrowed by text in its search box](/docs/screens/stops-search-chur.png)

*Above: searching Stops for Chur in Network, in the Graubünden workspace, returns matching stops.
The number and operator columns help distinguish similar names.*

## Filter and sort the results

1. Choose **＋ Filter** beside the search box. The menu lists the fields and relationships
   available for this list. Use its search box to find an option if the menu is long.
2. To find an exact field value, select the field, choose **Is** where offered, enter the value,
   and choose **Apply**. Use a number for a numeric field or a date for a date field. A pill
   above the results shows the filter. Search text still narrows the same results; clear it
   if you are now looking by a number rather than a name.
3. To filter by a connection, select a relationship under **Relationships**. Search the offered
   records, select the one you need, and choose **Apply**. The pill identifies the chosen
   connection. If the record is not offered, check the relationship and try a shorter search.
4. Open the sort button, marked with up and down arrows beside **Display**. Choose a field.
   Open it again and choose **Ascending** or **Descending**. Ascending puts earlier dates or
   smaller numbers first; descending puts later dates or larger numbers first. The column
   heading's arrow shows the direction.
5. Check the results and the total at the bottom. Remove an unwanted filter with its pill's
   **×**. **Clear search and filters** clears both when search and filters are active. If no records match, remove
   conditions one at a time to find which one excludes the record.

If the table offers **Hide inactive (N)** beside **Filter**, turn it on to hide the records
marked **Inactive**, whose chosen Yes/No field is **No**. Check the added pill, such as
**Active: not No**. Records with no value have no mark and stay visible. To bring back the
hidden records, turn the switch off or remove the pill with **×**. Choosing **Yes** in
**＋ Filter** instead keeps only Yes records and excludes those with no value. Other field
names change the mark and switch wording. See
[Show or hide inactive records](/docs/use/lists-and-filters/#show-or-hide-inactive-records)
for the count and rules.

![The filter menu listing fields and relationships](/docs/screens/stops-filter-menu.png)

*Above: the Stops filter menu offers Stop number (UIC), date fields and the Operated by
relationship. In this example, a number filter of 8509006 identifies Chur Wiesental.*

![Filtered records sorted by a date field in descending order](/docs/screens/stops-filtered-sorted.png)

*Above: in Network in the Graubünden workspace, search Chur and Operated by Rhätische Bahn leave
eight stops. Valid from is sorted newest first; Chur Wiesental is among the results.*

## Inspect the record

1. Choose the result's name. On a desktop, the record opens beside its list with a heading and identifying fields. Choose **Expand to full page** for the full record page. On a phone, it opens the page directly. Check the
   path above the heading to confirm its place in the hierarchy, especially if names repeat.
2. Read the fields in the heading and details panels. The labels depend on the record type.
   An unset value differs from zero or No; see [Records](/docs/use/records/#what-a-record-holds)
   if you need to interpret a field.
3. Read the relationship sections for connected records. Scroll down to find further sections.
   **No relationships yet** means that section has no connections. If a panel reports an error,
   retry that panel; the error does not mean there are no related records.
4. Choose **←** and the list’s name above the title when finished. Your search, filters, sort and position are preserved,
   so you can inspect the next result. To make a correction, follow
   [Correct a record](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/).

![A record page with its fields, hierarchy path and relationship sections](/docs/screens/stop-details.png)

*Above: Chur Wiesental in Network has its fields under Stop details. Modes shows Train and
Operator shows Rhätische Bahn. Its path places the stop under Chur.*

![Further relationship sections, including an empty section](/docs/screens/stop-relationships.png)

*Above: further down Chur Wiesental's page, System codes holds two codes from other systems.
Name translations has no relationships yet.*

## Choose the right relationship condition

1. Open **＋ Filter** and choose a relationship under **Relationships**. Select **Is any of**
   to tick one or more related records: a match to any of them keeps the row.
2. Choose **Has none** to find records without that relationship, or **Has any** to find
   records with at least one, without selecting particular records.
3. Where the related records sit under parents, **Has none under** and **Has any under**
   let you select one ancestor. They check related records at any depth beneath it.
4. Choose **Apply**, then inspect the filter pill and results. Open a pill to edit it or
   choose its **×** to remove it. On a phone, the editor opens as a sheet; its **Show …** button
   includes the number of matching records. Check that count before applying.

Other filter groups depend on the view. Text, number, date and Yes/No fields get suitable
conditions; **More** holds additional conditions. In Live, **Created** and **Updated** can narrow
by when records were made or changed. A missing optional value and a stored empty value can be
separate conditions: choose the one matching your question.

## Reach a distant row and read related columns

1. Scroll inside the list to read more records. The header and footer stay in view, including
   the range and total. Use the footer's page field to jump to a page, **Go to** to seek a
   sorted value where offered, or **Go to start** and **Go to end** for the ends of the list.
2. In a related-record column, read the chips. **+N more** counts records that do not fit on
   the line; widen the column to see more, or open the row's record to inspect the full
   relationship table. The count itself is not an expand button.
3. A column that holds only one related record can sort by that record's name, with missing
   connections last. Columns holding several related records or showing their fields do not
   sort. Use a relationship filter rather than trying to filter a chip column.
4. Use **Display** to change shown columns. A one-line value ending in an ellipsis can be read
   in full on hover, focus or long press. If columns have folded, choose **Columns · n of m**
   to show them all. Return using **←** and the list’s name above the title after inspecting a record;
   the address preserves search, filters, the single sort and your position.

The same list navigation works in Live, change sets and publications. If a jump or later page
fails to load, retry the failed read before treating the result as empty.

## Keep a search you need again

1. Copy the page address after choosing the search, filters, order and position. Opening that
   address later reads the same collection state in the named workspace and context.
2. Use the collection's search to look beyond the visible rows. The browser's Find command
   sees only rows currently drawn, so it can miss a record elsewhere in the list.
3. Without a selected sort, records normally appear by name; a view can choose a different
   initial order. Only one sort applies. Computed paths and structured values cannot sort;
   creation and update times are unavailable in contexts without those recorded timestamps.

There is no named saved-search list. **Clear all** removes filter conditions; where search
and filters are both active, **Clear search and filters** removes both together.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/explain:
---
title: Explain a period in history
description: Ask for an account of changes, check its facts and open the underlying work.
reader: steward
---

Use this for a workspace's changes or one record's past. You need a configured AI provider and
**Browse** and **Use AI proposals** in the workspace. Counts and model labels go to the provider;
at values, names go too. Requests can incur costs and are recorded. Read
[AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) and
[What changed in a period](/docs/use/history/#what-changed-in-a-period) for privacy and counting rules.

1. Open a record in **Live** and its **History**, or open **Settings › Workspaces**, choose the
   workspace and open **Activity**. Opening **What changed** sends nothing to AI.
2. In **Period**, keep **Last 7 days** or **Last 30 days**, or choose **Choose dates**.
   Set **From** and **To, included**. Both dates count; the first must not be after the last.
   A workspace starts with seven days and a record with thirty.
3. Read the sending line, then choose **Explain this period**. **Writing the account** appears.
   A period without changes reports that nothing changed and nothing was sent to AI.
4. Read the statements and follow each numbered source to its fact. Expand **Show the other …**
   to inspect all the facts. The warning that AI can be wrong applies even when a source exists:
   check that the statement says what its numbers support.
5. Choose **Show it** or **Show them** beside a fact to narrow the current Activity or History.
   Use **Open the change set** or **Open the job** to inspect its preparation where offered.
   A missing job link can mean the job is no longer retained or you cannot open it.
6. Use **Show all activity** or **Show all history** to restore the full list. Change the period
   and ask again for a different interval, or use **Explain again** to refresh it. The same facts
   for exactly the same period within an hour reuse the earlier account without another provider
   call. Preset periods end at the time you ask, so **Explain again** can make a new paid call.

![A record's What changed section with date controls, statements and cited facts](/docs/screens/use-record-history-explained.png)

If **The account could not be written** appears, read the facts anyway and use **Try again**
when appropriate. If the request itself fails, its error also offers **Try again**. Neither
failure changes your records. For exact values and individual actions, use the normal
[History controls](/docs/guide/use/see-who-changed-what/); an account counts published changes,
not the record edits still waiting in an open change set.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/prepare:
---
title: Prepare and publish a change set
description: Prepare related changes, review and validate them, then publish them together.
reader: steward
---

Prepare changes away from Live, review them and publish them together. See
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) for how starting data, live work and publications fit together.

For changes beyond fields, follow [Relate records](/docs/guide/use/relate-records/),
[Arrange records in a tree](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/),
[Map codes between systems](/docs/guide/use/map-codes-between-systems/) or
[Fill in a relation matrix](/docs/guide/use/fill-in-a-relation-matrix/).


## Start or open a change set

1. Open an application in the current workspace. Check **Workspace** in the sidebar, then
   choose **Change sets** at the top. The list identifies existing change sets by name and
   shows their versions, starting data and creators.
2. To continue existing work, find its name and choose **Open change set**. **Changes in this
   change set** opens first. Choose **See the data with these changes** to reach its lists,
   and check the name in the band before editing. Opening a change set does not publish it.
3. To start separate work, choose **New change set**. Enter a **Name**
   that helps other people recognise the work. **Options** shows the starting point, today's live data. A **Model version** choice appears there when you have Model release access and another release is available. Keep the workspace's version for ordinary corrections; coordinate a different choice with a model administrator.
4. Choose **Start change set**. The new set opens with a copy of the current live data.
   If creation is refused, read the message and resolve the named problem before retrying.
   Choose **Cancel** if you do not intend to create it.

![The change-set list with controls to open existing work or start a new set](/docs/screens/change-sets-list.png)

*Above: Network in the Graubünden workspace lists December 2026 timetable change. Open change set
continues that work; Start from current live data begins a separate proposal.*

If creation controls are unavailable, check your access with a workspace administrator. Opening
and reading an existing set does not itself give permission to change or publish it.

## Make the changes

1. Check the orange **Change set** band. It names the intended set, its number of changes
   and state. Open **Details** for its creator, creation time, version and model. If the band
   says **Live**, open your change set
   before making staged corrections.
2. Choose a collection and find a record. [Correct its fields](/docs/guide/use/correct-a-record/)
   and save using the ordinary record controls. Check that the saved values appear in the
   change set, then repeat for the other records in your proposal.
3. If you switch applications or inspect **Live**, check the banner again before the next edit.
   Return to the named change set to continue preparing it. Later live corrections do not
   refresh its starting copy.
4. If a save is refused, read the message and review the current record or change-set version
   before retrying. If the band says **waits for approval**, open **Details** for the submission
   and withdraw the request before editing.

![An open change set with its name, context banner and preparation controls](/docs/screens/change-set-open.png)

*Above: December 2026 timetable change is open over Stops in Network. The orange banner offers
Review changes, Validate change set and Publish change set. The example proposal changes
Valid to (exclusive) on several stops: the first date on which each stop is no longer valid.*

## Review and validate

1. Choose **Review changes** in the banner. On **Records**, inspect every intended addition,
   change or removal. Expand a row with its arrow to compare the before and after values.
   Check names and paths to confirm that you changed the intended records.
2. Choose **Relationships** and review the connection changes too. If a long review is hard to
   inspect, use **Filter** to narrow it, then remove the restriction to check the remaining work.
   An empty filtered review does not mean the whole proposal is empty.
3. Choose **See the data with these changes** to correct anything unexpected. Save those corrections and
   review again before proceeding.
4. Open **More change set actions** (⋯) and choose **Validate now**. If problems are reported, use the named records and reasons
   to correct them in the change set, then validate again. Do not proceed while problems remain.
5. Check for **Change set validation passed**. You can also go straight to **Publish**, which validates the current proposal before asking for confirmation. After further edits, the next publication attempt checks them again.

![The record review with changed fields, record paths and a Relationships tab](/docs/screens/change-set-review.png)

*Above: the timetable change's Records tab lists stops with Changed: Valid to (exclusive).
The arrows open the differences; Relationships provides a separate connection review.*

If publication remains unavailable after validation, read the banner for a model-version or
approval requirement and check your permissions. If **Submit for publication** is offered,
follow [Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/#submit-your-work). Submission leaves
the proposal waiting for a decision; it does not make the changes live.

## Publish

These steps apply when **Publish** is offered. When approval is needed, the banner
instead offers **Submit for publication**. Follow [Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/)
for submission, corrections and the approver's decision. See
[Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/) for the rules and notices.

1. Choose **Publish**. refiroo checks the proposal first. If it fails, nothing is published; use the reported problems and record links to correct it. A passed check opens **Publish this change set?**.
2. Read the confirmation. It names how many records and relationships become live, explains that unrelated live changes stay, and that a conflicting live edit publishes nothing. Follow **Review changes** if you need another look. Choose **Cancel** if you are
   not ready; the change set stays available for preparation.
3. To apply the reviewed changes, choose **Publish** in the confirmation. Wait for
   the result. Success is reported as **Published as Publication** followed by its number.
   Check the changed records in **Live** and find the resulting snapshot under **Publications**.
4. If publication is refused, read the reported reason. For conflicts, compare the named records
   with **Live** and agree which corrections are needed before changing the proposal. Review
   and validate the revised work before attempting publication again. A conflict or failed
   check publishes nothing; the proposed work remains available.

![The publication confirmation after validation has passed](/docs/screens/change-set-publish-confirm.png)

*Above: December 2026 timetable change has passed validation and its confirmation is open.
No publication has been confirmed in this screenshot; Cancel leaves it unpublished.*

An intervening live edit can still prevent publication after validation. See
[Publishing and intervening live work](/docs/use/change-sets/#publishing-and-intervening-live-work)
for what conflicts and what is preserved. A refusal needs review before another attempt.

## Discard work you no longer need

1. Open the change set and check all its proposed changes, including work by colleagues.
   If it is waiting for approval, its submitter or an approver must **Withdraw request** first.
2. Open **More change set actions** and choose **Discard**.
3. Read **Discard this change set?**. **Discard change set** removes all staged work in it.
   Choose **Cancel** to keep it. Live records and existing publications stay unchanged.
4. If the action fails, read its reason and refresh the change set before trying again.
   There is no undo for discarded work; a fresh change set does not recover those edits.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/switch-:
---
title: Switch workspace
description: Open another workspace and check its model, applications and data context.
reader: steward
---

Switch workspaces to work with another dataset. It does not copy or move records.
See [Workspaces](/docs/use/workspaces/) for models, access and retired workspaces.

## Choose from the sidebar

1. Check the current **Workspace** and the model and release beneath it.
2. Open the workspace selector. Search for the workspace if necessary. Check its model before
   selecting it: **Other model** means a different structure, and **Other release** means another
   release of the same model.
3. Choose the destination. Check the workspace name after it opens. If the previous application
   or view is unavailable there, choose one of the destination's applications and collections.
4. Read the context banner before editing. **Live** saves apply immediately; a change set holds
   proposed work; a publication is read-only. Open the intended context in the new workspace.

![The workspace selector with an Other model marker](/docs/screens/workspace-switcher.png)

*Above: Default is marked Other model while Network is open in Graubünden.*

![The destination workspace showing its different applications and an empty collection](/docs/screens/use-workspace-default.png)

*Above: choosing Default opens RDM Master and its Domains collection. The toast explains that
Default runs a different model from Graubünden. No records were copied.*
