## Choose from Home

1. Select the refiroo name in the top bar.
2. Under **Your workspaces**, check the destination card's model and release.
3. Choose the workspace’s name or tile to open its page, then choose an application.
   Check the sidebar and banner in the application that opens.
   Continue with [Open an application](/docs/guide/use/open-an-application/).

If the selector is absent, only one workspace is available. If the intended workspace is missing,
ask an administrator about Browse access or retirement. Where permitted, **Manage workspaces**
opens the full management list; a retired workspace opened there is read-only.
If switching reports an error, retry and confirm which workspace is open before changing data.

## If the address does not fit this workspace

After switching, read the toast if the model or release differs. An old bookmark can open
**Not in this model**: the named application, collection or type is absent here. Choose one of
the offered workspaces whose model has it, or return Home and open an application this workspace
provides. If the workspace itself cannot be served, read the displayed reason and ask the
operator for help. Other workspaces remain available. A retired workspace can be opened through
**Settings › Workspaces** where permitted, but stays read-only.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/follow-:
---
title: Follow a workspace
description: Receive publication notices for a workspace and stop them when no longer needed.
reader: steward
---

Follow a workspace to hear when someone else publishes a change set there. You need Browse
access. See [Notification settings](/docs/use/notifications-settings/#follow-publication-in-a-workspace).

1. Open **Home** and find the intended card under **Your workspaces**. Check the name and model
   before choosing **Follow**.
2. Check that the control reads **Following**. Your inbox now receives a notice for each
   eligible publication by another person. Your own publications do not notify you this way.
3. Open the notice from the bell or Notifications page. It opens the publication while that
   publication is active and you can browse it. A publication that is no longer active leads
   to the workspace’s **Publications** instead. The bell opens **Publications** too. Opening
   marks the notice read; if access is no longer available, it does not restore access.
   A digest link uses the Notifications page’s opening behavior.
4. For email copies, open **Settings › Notification email** and choose delivery for publication
   notices. Following itself works without mail.
5. To stop following, toggle **Following** on Home, or choose **Stop following** under
   **Workspaces I follow** in Notification email settings. Check the list after the change.

If you lose access or your account is deactivated, notices stop but the follow choice stays.
It can resume when access returns. If the toggle fails, read the error and retry rather than
assuming your preference changed.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/set-up-:
---
title: Set up email notices
description: Turn on email, choose notice kinds and check your digest schedule.
reader: steward
---

Choose email copies without changing your inbox. See
[Notification settings](/docs/use/notifications-settings/) for eligibility and limits.

1. Open **Settings › Notification email**, or choose **Notification email settings** from
   the Notifications page. Check the address under **Email**.
2. Turn on **Email me when something arrives in my inbox**. If no switch is offered, read the
   reason: mail may not be set up or your account may have no address. Ask an administrator
   to resolve it; following workspaces can still work without mail.
3. Under **How each kind reaches me**, choose **At once**, **Digest** or **Off** for each kind.
   Changes save immediately. If an error appears, correct the cause and try again.
4. For a digest, choose **Every morning at 07:00** or **Mondays at 07:00** under **The digest**.
   Read the displayed time zone and **Next digest**. The browser supplies the zone; the hour
   is fixed. The first kind put into Digest starts a daily schedule automatically.
5. Return to **Notifications** for the full inbox. Reading a notice before its digest is sent
   leaves it out. Nothing eligible means no digest; older unread notices are not excluded
   merely because they are more than a day old.

To stop all email, turn the master switch off. To stop just one kind, choose **Off** beside
it. Inbox notices remain either way. Immediate mail does not backfill notices from before
you enabled email and only sends unread notices less than a day old.

![Notification email enabled with one kind assigned to a daily digest and its next time visible](/docs/screens/use-notification-email-digest-settings.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/move-se:
---
title: Move several records together
description: Select records in a tree and move them to one parent as a single confirmed change.
reader: steward
---

Move several records together while keeping their types. See
[Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/) for allowed placement and descendants.

1. Open an editable tree in Live or a change set. Use Cmd or Ctrl to add or remove records
   from selection, or Shift for a range. By keyboard, use Ctrl+Space and Shift+arrows.
   Selection does not itself open a different record; Escape clears it.
2. Drag the selected records to the intended parent, or right-click the selection (Shift+F10
   by keyboard) and choose **Move to…**.
3. In the move dialog, search for the parent and read disabled choices' reasons. The destination
   must allow every selected record without a type change. A place needing **Becomes …** is
   for an individual restructuring operation, not this multi-record move.
4. Review the destination and selected records, then confirm the move. They move together or
   none moves. Their descendants stay beneath them; IDs and history are kept.
5. Check their new paths. Live moves are immediate; change-set moves await publication.

On touch, hold a record still for half a second until it lifts. Moving first scrolls; a short
tap opens. Drag near an edge to scroll. In the sidebar, releasing where you lifted opens the
node menu and offers Move to. Read-only trees and publication trees do not drag.

A drop chooses a parent or level, not a manual position among siblings. The view's order
controls sibling positions. If records changed meanwhile, review the refreshed state and try
again rather than assuming the first destination is still valid.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/replace:
---
title: Replace a record’s related records
description: Review a complete relationship set and save its additions and removals together.
reader: steward
---

Choose exactly which records should stay connected. This applies where the table offers
editing for a multi-record relationship. See [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/).

1. In an editable table, find the record's relationship column and choose its pencil, or the
   corresponding row-menu action. The dialog identifies **Related records of …** and the
   relationship. Parent, ownership, computed and read-only columns have no such editor.
2. Review the ticked records, pinned first and counted. They are the current set, not merely
   the first few chips shown in the table.
3. Search for eligible records and tick additions. Untick records to remove their connections.
   Review the whole ticked set, including choices outside the current search. Unticking removes
   the connection, not the related record.
4. Choose **Save**. Additions and removals save together as one operation; there is no partial
   replacement if a rule refuses it. Connections still selected keep their identity and fields.
5. Check the refreshed column and save notice. If **Nothing was changed** appears, read the
   cause and reopen the current set before trying again. Another person's intervening change
   must be reviewed rather than overwritten.

For a single-valued relationship, use **Set relationship** or **Change** to choose its one
record instead. To replace sets on several records, use
[Change relationships of many records](/docs/guide/use/change-relationships-of-many-records/).
The ordinary relationship panel otherwise maintains connections one at a time.

![Relationship editor with one checked record, two matching unchecked candidates, the selected count and Save disabled.](/docs/screens/replace-related-records.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/stop-of:
---
title: Stop offering a value
description: Keep a record and its history while marking it unavailable or ending its validity.
reader: steward
---

Keep the record when it must remain identifiable for older references. The model must provide
an availability field or validity dates; these controls do not exist on every type.
Read [Records](/docs/use/records/#validity-periods).

1. Find and open the record. Check its workspace and whether the change should be immediate
   in **Live** or proposed in a change set.
2. If the model provides an availability field, edit it to **No** and save. In an editable
   tree, the availability switch or **Mark not …** menu action can change the same field.
   The label comes from the model. The record remains, even if a view filters it out.
3. If the type has validity dates, set its end to the first day on which it must no longer be
   valid. The end is exclusive: an end of 13 December means the last valid day is 12 December.
   If both dates are present, the end must be later than the start. Save the field.
4. Check the saved value and history, or review and publish the change set when ready.
   If the record disappears from a filtered view, clear its availability filter to inspect it.

Setting an end date does not schedule publication or remove the record. The browser has no
business-date selector for browsing an earlier state; a validity field filter is not a
whole-workspace date view. Ask the model administrator if the type offers neither mechanism.
Do not delete a record simply because its availability control is absent.

An availability flag does not automatically hide the value from every consuming system.
Each system's agreed reading rules decide whether unavailable records are included. If the
record still appears elsewhere, check that agreement with the integration owner rather than
deleting the record to make it disappear.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/add-a-l:
---
title: Add a language with a workbook
description: Fill empty columns to create owned records under selected parents.
reader: steward
---

Fill in records that belong to each exported row, arranged as columns beneath chosen parents.
This works for any model declaring that ownership and placement; languages are one example.
Read [Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#a-workbook-for-people).

1. Open the owner records' collection. Choose **Workspace actions › Export** and **For editing in a spreadsheet**.
2. Open **Advanced: columns and sheets**. Select the owned-record relationship and choose
   **Columns per parent** for its layout. Choose the fields to fill.
3. Under **More columns for these …**, search for and select the additional parent records.
   Existing parents arrive automatically; added parents contribute empty columns. The parent
   must already be available to the model and workspace.
4. Choose **Start export**, then download the completed workbook. Check each column heading:
   it identifies the parent and any higher level used to distinguish it.
5. Fill the empty cells for the intended rows. Each filled owned-record entry becomes a record
   under that column's parent, connected to its row's owner. Leave cells blank where you want
   no addition; blank cells do not remove existing ordinary values.
6. Import with **Profile: None**. Check the **Read as exported …** preview, creations and
   refused cells, then choose **Load the file**. Review the actual results and, if working in
   a change set, publish through the usual review process.

**Example:** in the reference data, a parent groups stop names in a language. Adding that parent
as columns lets a steward fill names for the exported stops. This layout comes from ownership
and hierarchy rules, rather than a special language feature.

If the workbook would exceed Excel's 16,384 columns, the export job fails. Choose fewer parents
or fields and export again. If a cell summarises several owned records, edit their sheet instead.

![Workbook export showing Columns per parent, fields and an additional parent](/docs/screens/workbook-columns-per-parent.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/open-a-:
---
title: Open a retired or unavailable workspace
description: Read a retired workspace and understand why another workspace cannot be opened.
reader: steward
---

A retired workspace is readable history. An unavailable workspace cannot currently be served.
See [Workspaces](/docs/use/workspaces/) for choosing a dataset.

1. For a retired workspace, open **Settings › Workspaces** where your access offers it.
   Select the workspace and choose **Open workspace**. It may be absent from the active
   workspace selector. Check the **Retired · read only** mark and the context band’s
   **Retired: read only.** message.
2. Browse its applications, records and retained publications. Editing records, relationships,
   change sets and migrations is refused. Ask the workspace administrator about reactivation;
   do not try to work around read-only status.
3. If the destination says **Workspace … cannot be opened** or **Cannot be opened**, read its
   reason. The model's language can be too old or too new, or its release can be invalid.
   Other workspaces are not affected and nothing was changed by opening the address.
4. Send the reason to the responsible model administrator or operator. **Bring it up to date**
   and **Review the change**, when offered to an authorised administrator, belong to
   [Model language versions](/docs/model/model-language-versions/). A steward should choose
   another readable workspace while that is resolved.
5. If the page instead says **No workspace …**, check the address with its sender. If an
   application or type **is not in this workspace's model**, use **Workspaces whose model has …**
   to select a suitable destination, or **Go back**. If none exists, the page says **No other workspace's model has it.**

![Unavailable example workspace with its model-language reason, recovery review and other workspaces](/docs/screens/workspace-cannot-open.png)

An unavailable model is different from missing Browse access. Ask about the displayed reason;
repeatedly retrying a record save does not repair it.

For a missing application, collection or record type, the suggested destination button reads
**Open in …** with the workspace name. It opens that workspace; recheck its model and context
on arrival. The start-page button instead keeps you in the workspace already named.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/add-a-r:
---
title: Add a record
description: Create a record with its fields, parent and required relationships in one save.
reader: steward
---

Create one item of the type declared by your model. See [Records](/docs/use/records/) for
field rules and [Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/) for placement.

1. Open the intended workspace, application and collection. Check **Live** or the named change
   set before choosing **Add …**. If you see **Propose a new …**, follow
   [Propose a change](/docs/guide/use/propose-a-change/) first.
2. The **New …** form opens beside the page on a desktop. Enter the name and required fields first; optional fields wait under **More fields (n)**. That choice is remembered per type in this browser. Required fields must have
   values, including at least one field where the form gives that rule. Read-only fields
   cannot be filled through this form. Keep numbers, dates and Yes/No values in their proper controls.
   Read help below the fields before filling them. Fields hidden by the model are omitted;
   ask the model administrator if a required piece of information cannot be supplied.
3. If the page already supplies the parent, the form says **In** followed by its name; choose **Change** only to pick another. Where **Parent** is offered, select the allowed parent type and search for the record.
   Some types require a parent and cannot be created at the top. **No parent available** means
   you must first provide an allowed parent. Open the hierarchy view and use **Add …**
   for its top-level type, then add the child records beneath it. If that action is absent,
   check your editing access and ask the model administrator about the view’s actions and placement rules.
4. Complete required relationships in the same form. Search only offers eligible records in
   this workspace and context. A general search result elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility.
5. Choose **Add** followed by the record type's name. Fields, parent and required relationships save together. A refusal leaves
   no partially created record. Missing and wrongly typed values are explained below their fields; correct the named missing value, duplicate value, invalid date
   period, placement or relationship and try again.
6. Check the new record's path, fields and save notice. A Live save takes effect immediately;
   a change-set save stays proposed until publication.

If the workspace's model changed while the form was open, reload and review the new form.
Do not remove required information merely to get past a refusal.

![New record form with name, typed fields, required parent and relationship, Create and a visible context.](/docs/screens/new-record-required-connections.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/continu:
---
title: Continue a long list
description: Jump through a collection and return to the same search and position.
reader: steward
---

Find a distant row without scrolling through every earlier result. See
[Lists, search and filters](/docs/use/lists-and-filters/) for what the controls mean.

1. Open a collection and check its workspace and context. Search, filter and sort before
   choosing a position: a different condition changes which records occupy that position.
2. Scroll the rows inside the table. The footer shows your range and the full matching total.
   Scroll back up to read earlier rows; where an append-style list offers **Show earlier records**,
   choose it to read the preceding group.
3. To reach a numbered page, enter the number in **Page** and press Enter. Check the range after
   it loads. Use **Go to start** or **Go to end** for either end. With the list focused,
   Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End reach those ends too.
4. Where **Go to** is offered, enter a value for the current sort and submit it. This seeks the
   value's place in that ordering; it does not add a filter. Check nearby names and identifying
   fields if there is no exact match.
5. Open a record. Choose **←** and the list’s name above the title to return with your search, filters, sort and position.
   Save or share the address if you need to return later. Changes to the underlying data can
   change the records at that position.

If a jump fails, retry the failed read. Do not clear your search just because a page failed.
Use the list's own search rather than the browser's Find command: Find sees only drawn rows.

![A collection footer with range, total, Page, Go to and start/end controls; a noninitial position is loaded.](/docs/screens/list-position-and-seek.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/change-:
---
title: Change records with the assistant
description: Give instructions without a workbook and review the prepared changes before publication.
reader: steward
---

Use this to ask the assistant to prepare changes to records the workspace already holds.
It needs **Use AI proposals**, **Bulk and import**, **Work in change sets**, available jobs
and an enabled assistant at the values send level. Your words and the workspace model go
to Claude Code, which reads records as needed. Turns can incur costs and task files are
retained. See [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) and
[Loading with the assistant](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/) for the rules.

1. Open the current workspace's **⋯** menu and choose **Ask about these records…** where it is
   offered. You can also choose **Import…** and leave **Workbook** empty in **Load a workbook**.
   Confirm **Into** names the intended workspace.
2. In **Tell the assistant about this file (optional)**, say which records should change, how to
   find them and the desired result. Words are required when there is no workbook. For example,
   with the reference data: “Set the Abbreviation of the stop ‘Thusis Süd’ to ‘THSD-REVIEW’.” Use the names of fields and relationships in your
   model. Instructions are limited to 4,000 characters.
3. Read the sending note and choose **Ask the assistant**. This starts a saved task; it is
   different from **Ask** on a table list, which only chooses filters. Until a proposal exists,
   the journey bar and trail say **Change with the assistant**. With a proposal, they say
   **Change records** if the model stays unchanged, or **Change this model** if it changes.
   The task heading gets a short title with the assistant’s first answer; any draft it makes
   is named **Assistant:** followed by that title. Your full instructions stay under **You said:**
   on the proposal. Until the title arrives, including after a stop or failure before an answer,
   the heading uses your words, shortened at a word boundary with “…” if needed.
4. Read the proposal and any counts or checks shown. Check that it affects the intended
   records and reuses existing types and records where appropriate. Answer any **Questions** with **Answer and
   design again**, or use **Tell the assistant what to change** and **Send to the assistant**.
   If the task proposes a model change, inspect **Show the model change** and involve a model
   administrator before accepting it. If the summary says **No type, attribute or relationship
   changes**, open the draft in the model editor: it may still change views or layout.
   When a task without a workbook says **No change to the model.**, there
   is no model draft, model-change detail or model editor button.
5. When the proposal and any checks match your request, choose **Accept** for words alone
   with no model change. The session prepares a new change set on the workspace’s current
   release; it installs and activates nothing. It changes no Live record.
   If the proposal also changes the model or moves records between types, follow
   [Change a model with the assistant](/docs/guide/model/change-a-model-with-the-assistant/)
   for its **Accept the model** and migration or staged-move steps. A workbook proposal showing
   **What the load does** uses **Accept and load to change set**: the engine loads the checked records and
   relationships as one batch without another assistant turn.
   If the assistant cannot do the task, read its reason and correct the instructions rather
   than assuming a partial or empty load completed the request.
6. Choose **Review the change set**. Review the actual differences, validate and follow the
   [approval and publication steps](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/).
   The workspace's normal approval rules apply, including a second person where required.

![Record-change proposal showing No change to the model, Accept and the correction box](/docs/screens/use-assistant-words.png)

*Above: the proposal changes the Abbreviation of Chur Wiesental in the reference data. Accepting prepares a change set for review; nothing is published.*

For a wrong result, [continue or correct the same task](/docs/guide/use/continue-an-assistant-task/)
while its session is available. Instructions about stored records do not create a reusable file
layout. A workbook loaded from the assistant's checked records and relationships saves no
import profile either; send the next file to the assistant again.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/load-a-: --- title: Load a workbook with the assistant description: Send a workbook, review the model and checked records, then load a change set for publication. reader: steward --- Use this when a file needs interpretation before it can load. You need the assistant enabled, permission to send values, **Use AI proposals**, **Bulk and import**, **Work in change sets** and available background jobs. A model change needs a model administrator's access too. The whole workbook, your words and the workspace model go to Claude Code; it can read records as needed. Turns can incur costs and the task and session files are retained. Read [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) and [Loading with the assistant](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/) before starting. 1. Open an application in the current workspace and check that it is writable. Open the workspace's **⋯** menu and choose **Import…**. When the assistant is offered, **Load a workbook** opens first. To use a known manual import instead, choose **Import without the assistant…** and follow [Import a file](/docs/guide/use/import-a-file/). 2. In **Workbook**, choose one XLSX or CSV file, or drop it onto the field. To follow the illustrated example, download the example workbook, a fictional operator’s stop list from the guide’s reference data. Check **Into** names the intended workspace. In **Tell the assistant about this file (optional)**, explain the result you need: for an update, say how rows correspond to the records already held and what must stay unchanged. Read the sending note, then choose **Read the workbook**. If the file exceeds the instance's size limit, reduce it or ask the operator about that limit; nothing has been loaded. 3. The task page shows **Working on it** and the steps actually completed. You can leave and return from **Settings › Jobs**, or choose **Stop**. A fitting saved profile can prepare the file without starting AI; the page then follows that saved layout. 4. Read **The assistant’s proposal** and **What the load does**. Check the totals for new records, existing records matched, new relationships, refused items and rows read. New relationships include the links of new records to their parents; the summary says how many of those links it includes. Open each type's row to inspect example records, their values, relationships and source cells. Read **One name twice in one type** if shown, and expand **Where each part of the file goes**. Check **Show the model change**, **Checks** and **Columns left out**. Unexpected new records instead of matches, unexplained repeated names and omitted filled cells need a correction. 5. Under **Questions**, inspect the assumed choices. Change wrong ones and choose **Answer and design again**. For other corrections, use **Tell the assistant what to change** and **Send to the assistant**. **Open in the model editor** opens the draft if you need to edit it. Close the editor to return. If the draft changed after the check, accepting checks every record and relationship again first. Ask for a revised proposal if the shown examples no longer describe what you intend. 6. When the proposal matches your intent, choose **Accept and load to change set**. The engine installs the model if it changed and loads exactly the checked records and relationships into a new change set, as one batch. No assistant turn runs and nothing is published or activated. If any item is refused, none of the batch is loaded and its change set is discarded. Read the task's reason, then tell the assistant what to correct and review its new proposal. A release already installed before a load failure can remain installed. A saved-layout task instead shows **What the load would do** and a load button: inspect the per-sheet figures, expand changed records, read refused row examples and **What confirming does, in this order** before loading. Its button explicitly says when it also activates a model; that activation is not undone if the subsequent load fails. 7. On **Loaded into the change set**, compare the actual record and relationship counts with the checked result: the same relationships, including parent links, are counted in both. A load prepared by the assistant does not save an import profile. Send the next file of the same layout to the assistant again. 8. Choose **Review the change set**. Check the actual record and relationship changes, validate, obtain any required approval and publish through [Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/). If the change set uses a different model version, review offers **Move** followed by the workspace name, the proposed version and **and publish…**. A model administrator with publication permission can use this to preview the migration and choose **Migrate and publish**. This moves the workspace to that model and publishes the change set together; a separate activation first is not required. Follow [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) to inspect the preview and resolve any blockers or approval requirement. Loaded records reach Live only when published. ![The workbook dialog with Workbook, Into, instructions and the sending note](/docs/screens/use-assistant-workbook.png) ![A loaded assistant task naming the change set](/docs/screens/use-assistant-loaded.png) If the proposal or load is wrong, use [Continue or correct an assistant task](/docs/guide/use/continue-an-assistant-task/). For the next file, start another assistant task and explain how it should match existing records. If you already have a separately saved import profile, use [Load the next version of a workbook](/docs/guide/use/load-the-next-version-of-a-workbook/).
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/follow-:
---
title: Follow and cancel a job
description: Read a background operation’s progress and results, or stop remaining work.
reader: steward
---

Follow work after leaving its collection or import dialog. See [Jobs](/docs/use/jobs/) for
states, access and retention.

1. Open **View job** in the starting notification, or go to **Settings › This instance › Jobs**
   and open the job; a group of related jobs opens first, and its jobs under it. Check **Workspace**
   and **Requested by** before acting.
2. Read **State** and progress. A preview waiting for confirmation has not written its proposed
   changes. Review the items before choosing **Load the file** for an import or **Apply** for
   a bulk preview. A running job updates while the page stays open.
3. To stop remaining work, use **Cancel job**, **Cancel import** for a waiting import,
   or **Cancel preview** for a waiting batch preview.
   Read the confirmation, then choose **Stop the job** for running work or **Discard the
   import** / **Discard the preview** for a waiting preview. From the Jobs list, choose **Cancel
   job** in its confirmation. **Keep the job**, **Keep the preview** or **Keep the import**
   dismisses that confirmation.
4. Wait for the state to settle. **Cancel requested** is still pending. Already committed
   chunks remain applied: inspect the final counts rather than assuming cancellation undoes them.
5. For an export that completed, read **The file** and choose **Download**. For an import or
   batch, read refused and unprocessed items and their reasons. Fix the source and preview
   again before retrying work.

If the job failed, read **Why it failed**. Loss of the requester's permissions can stop a job;
a changed change set can stop its next chunk. Expired previews require a fresh preview.
Retained results and files disappear after their retention; download what you need in time.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/edit-:
---
title: Edit a workspace’s model
description: Reopen its saved draft and apply the reviewed definitions to that workspace.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this path when changing the model for a particular workspace. You need **Model authoring**,
**Model release** there and **Browse**, with model administration enabled. A retired workspace
does not offer this action. See [Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/).

1. Open **Settings › Workspaces**, then the workspace. Check its current model and choose
   **Edit model**. The workspace's menu also offers this action where your access allows it.
2. Read **Applies to** in the editor. It identifies the destination. Later visits reopen the
   saved workspace draft; closing keeps the work rather than applying it.
3. Make the intended changes and review **History**, **Issues** and preview. No live record
   or active definition changes merely because a draft step was saved.
4. Choose **Apply to this workspace…**. Read the model changes, data and consumer checks,
   old change sets left behind and other workspaces left unchanged.
5. **Not valid** needs model fixes. **Nothing to apply yet** means no applicable change.
   **Your records stay as they are** means no data conversion is required. **Some records
   must move first** offers **Preview what happens to the records…**; follow
   [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) for the separate review.
6. Confirm only after checking the named workspace. On success inspect its model and applications.
   On **Not applied**, read the reason, reload the current state and check again before retrying.

![Workspace overview with Edit model](/docs/screens/model-workspace-edit-model.png)

![Apply dialog listing the workspace, changes and compatibility](/docs/screens/model-workspace-apply-dialog.png)

To choose an already installed release instead, follow
[Change a workspace’s model](/docs/guide/model/change-a-workspaces-model/).

A workspace remembers at most one current draft. If its model changes elsewhere, that older
draft is detached from the workspace rather than deleted. Reopen **Edit model** to obtain the
current draft instead of applying an old tab without review. If installation succeeded but
activation failed, the flow retries against the installed release; inspect the reported state
rather than installing the same release again.

## Ask for a change in words

The workspace menu also offers **Change this model…** when the assistant and your rights
allow it. Follow [Change a model with the assistant](/docs/guide/model/change-a-model-with-the-assistant/)
to review its draft and complete the record moves. Apply can separately
[explain the change](/docs/guide/model/explain-a-model-change/) through the configured provider.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/creat:
---
title: Create a model draft
description: Start editable model work from an installed release or an empty model.
reader: model-admin
---

Create a draft to shape definitions without changing a workspace yet. You need **Model authoring**.
Read [Models](/docs/model/models/) for the difference between a draft, release and activation.

## Start from a release or an empty model

1. Open **Settings**, then **Model**. Find the model you intend to extend. Check which workspace
   runs it; another workspace may use a different model.
2. Choose **New draft**. Enter a **Draft name** that identifies the work rather than an installed
   version. The draft name can differ from the model's name.
3. For **Starting document**, choose **Installed release** to retain its applications, types and
   views, then select the intended **Base release**. Choose **Empty model** for a new model with
   no applications or types. An empty draft needs those elements added before people can use it.
4. Choose **Create draft**. Wait for the editor and check its name, base release and version in
   the header. If creation is refused, read the reason and correct the named problem. A missing
   base release or empty draft name prevents creation. **Cancel** closes the dialog without
   creating a draft.

![Create draft dialog with a name, starting document and base release](/docs/screens/model-draft-new-dialog.png)

*Above: Guide draft is named and an installed Graubünden release is selected. This captured dialog
was cancelled; it did not create a draft.*

From a model's overview, **New draft from** its release starts the same flow. On an installed
release's own page, use **Create draft from release**. On **Drafts**, select a saved draft to
continue existing work instead of creating another.

## Start from a workspace

1. Open **Settings**, **Workspaces**, then the workspace you intend to change.
2. On **Overview**, check **Model**, then choose **Edit model**. This opens its existing current
   draft where one is available, or prepares one from its running release.
3. Check **Applies to** in the editor header. Its main action is **Apply to this workspace…**;
   opening the editor has not applied anything.

![Workspace model editor identifying the workspace it applies to](/docs/screens/model-workspace-edit-model.png)

*Above: Guide draft applies to Graubünden and offers Apply to this workspace….*

This route needs model authoring and release access for that workspace. If it is unavailable,
ask an administrator to check access and whether the workspace is retired.

## Continue the draft

Choose an application or type in the model pane, or add one with the plus button. Follow
[Add a record type and fields](/docs/guide/model/add-a-record-type-and-fields/).
**Close** leaves the saved draft available for later; it does not discard your work or activate it.

If the starting material is a spreadsheet, choose **New from a workbook** instead and follow
[Load a workbook](/docs/guide/model/start-a-draft-from-a-workbook/). That guide covers the source and proposals.

For an existing model document, choose **Import JSON** under **Starting document**. A specialist
model author can paste it in **JSON document** or use **Or choose a JSON file** (or drop the file onto that field), then create the
draft. Read validation issues before installing; importing does not activate it. For ordinary
changes, starting from a release and using the model editor keeps the work in named controls.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/retir:
---
title: Retire or delete a workspace
description: Take a dataset out of active use while preserving its history, or delete an eligible empty one.
reader: model-admin
---

Open **Settings › Workspaces** with **Workspace administration**. See
[Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/) for active and retired states.

1. Open the workspace and check its name, key and default status. The default cannot be
   retired or deleted; [make another workspace default](/docs/guide/model/make-a-workspace-the-default/) first.
2. To keep the data but stop changes, choose **Retire…**. Read the confirmation and choose
   **Retire workspace**, or cancel. It leaves the active selector and becomes read-only.
   Records, change sets, publications and history remain readable through workspace management.
3. To resume work later, open the retired workspace in this list and choose **Reactivate**.
   Check the active state. Reactivation does not change its model release. Retirement also
   suspends its active webhook subscriptions; ask their administrator to resume them separately
   after reactivation.
4. Use **Delete…** only for an empty workspace that has never been published and has no change
   sets or webhook subscriptions. Read the page's explanation of anything preventing deletion.
   Even an emptied workspace with past publications must be retired instead.
5. If eligible and no longer needed, read the deletion confirmation's name and key, then
   choose **Delete workspace**. Cancel preserves it. Do not treat deletion as reversible retirement.

![Retire workspace confirmation](/docs/screens/workspace-retire-dialog.png)

If an action fails or reports a newer workspace version, review the current state before
retrying. A missing action can also mean insufficient permissions or disabled administration.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/edit-:
---
title: Edit a mapping row
description: Set a target type, field, relationship or typed default and review its dry run.
reader: model-admin
---

Open a copy or move in **Settings › Copy and move** with the necessary workspace access.
See [Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/) for how mappings and record matching work.

1. On **Mapping**, check **From**, **To**, the saved mapping and its version. **Change…**
   beside Mapping selects another mapping; it is different from changing one row.
2. Focus or select a row and read **Why this step**. Evidence and alternatives explain a
   **Proposed** choice. No numeric score is displayed. Select an alternative only if its
   meaning is right, not simply because its labels look similar.
3. Choose the target type for a source type. For an excluded type, use **Map … to…**. Then
   inspect each attribute, parent, relationship direction and matching rule under it.
4. Select a target field or **Not carried (reported)**. Review **Records already in the target**:
   finding only previously moved records differs from matching by a unique target field.
5. For a target field without a source value, use **Set a default…** and enter a value of its
   declared type. Use **Change…** to edit it or **Clear** to remove it. Supply a meaningful
   default rather than an arbitrary value just to satisfy a required field.
6. Read any problem beside the row. A refused step leaves that choice unapplied. **Undo** and
   **Redo** revisit mapping steps. A manual row says **This row is yours**; Undo can restore
   the proposal where available.
7. Wait for the new dry run. Inspect **Values not carried**, dropped relationships and records
   that cannot go. **The dry run waits for the mapping** is not a successful check; correct
   mapping problems first. After **The dry run did not run**, read why and **Dry run again**.

![Mapping choices and the evidence for a selected row](/docs/screens/model-mapping-why.png)

![Typed default editor for a target field](/docs/screens/moves-set-default.png)

If the mapping names releases other than the workspaces run, choose **Use the releases the
workspaces run**, inspect the choices and check again. A read-only notice means this deployment
or your access prevents edits. Saving rows alone copies or moves no records.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/chang:
---
title: Change a workspace’s model
description: Choose an installed release and read its data and consumer compatibility checks.
reader: model-admin
---

Choose an installed release for one workspace with **Model release** there. The release must
be usable on this instance. See [Releases](/docs/model/releases/) and [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/).

1. Open **Settings › Model**, select the model and its **Overview**. Beside the workspace choose
   **Change model…**. Alternatively open a release and choose **Activate in a workspace…**.
2. Check **Workspace** and its current model. Under **Release**, choose the target version.
   Expand another model only if you intend to replace the workspace's definitions with it.
3. Wait for the check and read its result:

   | Result | What to do |
   | --- | --- |
   | Compatible with the workspace's data | No record, value or relationship needs migration. Review the destination before activating. |
   | A migration is needed | The same model's definitions require data changes. Use the offered migration preview. |
   | A different model | The different model does not fit the data unchanged. Review its reasons and the migration preview where available. |
   | A consumer API needs a higher contract version | Correct or version the named contract in a draft before activating. |
   | Could not be checked | Correct the stated failure and check again. This is not a compatible result. |

4. Read the listed open change sets left on the old release and other workspaces left unchanged.
   If compatible, confirm activation. If conversion is needed, use **Preview the migration…**
   and follow [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/).
5. After success, reopen the workspace and inspect its applications. Reload a page reporting a
   model change before editing. A bookmark to a missing application or type shows **Not in this
   model**; choose a collection declared by this workspace's current model.

![Activation dialog selecting a release for one workspace](/docs/screens/model-release-activate-dialog.png)

**Not activated** means the switch failed. Read why, refresh the workspace and check again.
Choosing an older version runs the same checks; it does not restore older record values.


## Check which consumer versions stay available

Compare the target release with the workspace’s current contract, including any earlier
versions it serves. A higher current number does not itself prove every existing consumer
can continue: the target release must retain the earlier definitions. An older installed
release or publication does not keep their live routes available.

A finding ending **a kept version is served as it was: restore it, or stop serving it**
means an earlier contract would read differently. Prepare a corrected draft that restores
that definition and its sources, or coordinate stopping it, then install a new release.
Raising the current contract again does not repair the retained version.

The activation dialog shows blocking consumer differences, and a warning when an earlier
version **stops serving**, naming the version and that its consumers get
`CONTRACT_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`. Agree that removal with all consuming teams
before activating. That version’s reads and feed stop. Webhooks bound to
it can suspend; the integration administrator must check the receiver before resuming on
the current contract. If the version remains retained, its consumers and webhooks continue
in its own shape. A **Sunset day** announces an end but never stops service automatically.

To change which versions the target release retains, use
[Raise a contract version](/docs/guide/model/raise-a-contract-version/) or
[Stop serving an earlier contract version](/docs/guide/model/stop-serving-an-earlier-contract-version/)
in a draft. Releases themselves are immutable. **Cancel** leaves the workspace on its
current release; a draft undo does not reverse an activation already completed.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/delet:
---
title: Delete a draft
description: Remove an editable draft while keeping installed releases.
reader: model-admin
---

Delete a draft only when its saved design work and attached source are no longer needed.
You need **Model authoring**. See [Models](/docs/model/models/) for the distinction between a draft and a release.

1. Open the draft and inspect **About this draft** and **History** to identify it. If you need
   a copy of its model document, use **JSON**, then **Export JSON**, before deleting.
2. In the editor's **More actions** menu choose **Delete draft…**.
3. Read **Delete this draft?**. This removes the editable draft, its proposals, history and
   attached workbook. Installed releases are not changed. Choose **Cancel** to keep it.
4. Confirm deletion only for the intended draft. Return to **Settings › Model** and check the
   remaining drafts. If deletion fails, read the notice and reload the list before retrying.

![Editor menu with Delete draft and workbook actions](/docs/screens/model-more-actions.png)

Deletion is not an undo of activation or a removal of records. To stop offering a release for
new use, see [Retire or delete a release](/docs/guide/model/retire-or-delete-a-release/).
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/choos:
---
title: Choose what moves
description: Select mapped types, filtered types, a whole workspace or a contained branch for a dry run.
reader: model-admin
---

Open a mapping for the source and target workspaces. Choose **Copy** to keep source data or
**Move** to also prepare source deletions. See [Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/).

1. Check the source and target, then choose **Change…** beside **What to copy** or **What to move**.
2. Under **Records**, choose the scope:

   | Choice | What it includes |
   | --- | --- |
   | Every mapped type | Records of each source type the mapping handles. |
   | The whole workspace | All source types, with excluded types reported as not copied or moved. |
   | Chosen types | Selected types and, where set, only records matching their filters. |
   | One record and everything under it | A starting record and all its contained descendants. |

3. For **Chosen types**, tick the types and review their filters. For a branch, set **Type
   of the record**, then find **The record** in the source workspace. A similar name elsewhere
   does not identify the same branch.
4. Choose **Dry run this selection**. Cancel keeps the previous selection. Wait for the fresh
   report and inspect creates, updates, records refused and relationships carried or dropped.
5. Open **What cannot be copied** or **What cannot move** for reasons and affected items. A
   relationship whose target cannot be resolved may be dropped even if a record can go.
   Inspect **Values not carried** too. Correct the mapping or deliberately narrow the scope.

![Selection dialog with type, whole-workspace and contained-branch options](/docs/screens/model-mapping-selection-dialog.png)

Changing the selection runs the check again. Nothing eligible prevents starting. When ready,
follow [Move records to another model](/docs/guide/model/move-records-to-another-model/) for
confirmation and publication of the resulting change sets.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/map-a:
---
title: Map a workbook column
description: Choose what a column feeds, how references match and which values are ignored or replaced.
reader: model-admin
---

Open a draft with an attached workbook and **Model authoring**. See
[Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/) for the source and profile.

1. Select the sheet, then a column in **Source**. Read its status, **Feeds**, **Read as**,
   **Matched by** and **Statistics**. Filled and distinct values help assess a mapping; they
   do not prove the column's meaning. Review frequent values, placeholders and delimiters.
2. Choose **Map to…**, or drag the column onto a type. Select the type whose rows are being
   read and **What the column holds**: a name, attribute, parent, lookup, related record,
   relationship flag, or an ignored column. The form changes with this choice.
3. For a new attribute, review **Attribute name**, proposed **Value type** and **Unique**.
   For a parent or relationship, choose the offered destination. A missing parent type or
   relationship must be modelled first; the form explains when there is none.
4. For a lookup, set **Matched by**. A unique attribute can find existing records; only name
   matching can create missing named records. Enable **Create the records a cell names that
   do not exist** only when those names really define records you want to maintain.
5. For a related record, choose what the column fills and its parent. Choose a fixed named
   parent or **The one each row names in** and **The column naming it**. A fixed parent and
   a column cannot both supply the same source's parent. Name matching for that record is
   under the chosen parent, rather than a search across every parent.
6. For a flag, check **The record a Y relates the row to**. Its default comes from the header;
   change it if that is not the intended record. For a multi-value lookup, set **Split a cell
   on** only when each part names a separate record; **Do not split** keeps the cell whole.
7. Choose **Map**. **Not mapped** leaves the attempted mapping unapplied; correct the stated
   problem. **Ignore** or **Ignore the column** excludes values you do not intend to load.
8. Back in the column panel, use **Add a value map…** or **Edit value map…**. Pair **Text in
   the file** with **Becomes**, including intended placeholder handling. Remove a row to stop
   that replacement. This changes reading instructions, not the original spreadsheet.
9. Choose **Save the value map** to keep its replacements, or **Cancel** to leave them unchanged.
   Check **Key** before **Use as the key of the rows**. A non-unique column explains why it
   cannot serve as a key. Review [the refreshed dry run](/docs/guide/model/check-a-workbook-with-a-dry-run/).

![Workbook column statistics and the model it feeds](/docs/screens/use-wb-source-namen.png)

The mapping form shows the selected source column and its destination. A value map changes
how the file is read before matching or conversion.

![UIC-Nr column mapped to an existing integer attribute, with row type, column meaning and key choice](/docs/screens/model-workbook-map-column.png)

![Value map with an unsaved J-to-true replacement and placeholder entries that become empty](/docs/screens/model-workbook-value-map.png)

If none of a sheet belongs in the load, open its Source menu and choose **Ignore this sheet**.
It removes that sheet’s reading sources, not its cells or live records. Check other sheets’
lookups and the refreshed dry run; use Undo if excluding the sheet was unintended.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/add-a:
---
title: Add a relationship
description: Allow two record types to connect, with forward and reverse names and the intended limits.
reader: model-admin
---

Allow a relationship in a draft before people can create it between records. You need **Model
authoring**. A relation type gives the connection its meaning; an allowed pair determines which
types it may join. See [Types, attributes and relations](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/).

## Inspect existing connections

1. Open the draft and select the type at the intended **from** end.
2. Choose **Relations**. Read **From → to**, **Cardinality**, **Required** and **Which records**.
   The list includes incoming as well as outgoing relationships, so use the direction column
   rather than assuming every row starts from the selected type.
3. If the connection already exists, inspect its row instead of creating a second relation type
   with the same meaning. **Which records** can limit the permitted endpoints beyond their types.

![Relations table showing directions, cardinalities, requirements and endpoint restrictions](/docs/screens/model-relations.png)

*Above: Stop has outgoing relationships to Mode and Operator, incoming containment from Municipality
and incoming system-code relationships restricted by their parent systems.*

## Allow the pair

1. Choose **Allow a relation…**. Select **To**, the target record type.
2. Under **Relation type**, reuse an existing meaning where appropriate, or choose **A new relation
   type**. For a new one, enter **Name (from …)** and **Reverse name**. Read them as sentences from
   both ends so people understand the same relationship whichever record they open.
3. Set **Cardinality** using the from and to types shown below. Do not infer it from the plural
   wording of a label.
4. Review **Required**. This is a dependent-ownership rule, not a general request that every source
   record have a target. For the supported required one-to-one or one-to-many connection, the
   target is created with its owner relationship. **Many to one** cannot be required. Leave it
   unticked for an optional association.
5. Choose **Add relation**. Check the new row's direction and limits, its **New** mark and the saved
   history step. If refused, correct the named combination or migration problem. **Cancel**
   leaves the draft unchanged.

| Cardinality | What it permits |
| --- | --- |
| Many to one | Each source has at most one target; a target may serve many sources. |
| One to many | A source may have many targets; each target has at most one source. |
| One to one | At most one at each end. |
| Many to many | Neither end is limited to one by this setting. |

![Allow a relation dialog with target, forward and reverse names and cardinality](/docs/screens/model-relation-dialog.png)

*Above: Stop to Operator is given the new names Inspected by and Inspects, with Many to one and
Required unticked. It is separate from the existing Operated by relationship.*

![Relations table with the newly allowed relationship marked New](/docs/screens/model-relation-added.png)

*Above: Inspected by now appears beside Stop's released relationships. No actual inspection
relationship between records was created by this draft step.*

## Check the whole structure

Choose **Open the relationship matrix**, or **Relationship matrix** in the model pane. Rows are
from types and columns are to types. Select a cell for that ordered pair. Arrow keys move between
cells and Enter selects a pair. Containment is labelled **contains**.

![Relationship matrix with from types as rows and to types as columns](/docs/screens/model-matrix.png)

*Above: Guide draft's matrix shows the containment chain and permitted system-code mappings. The
new Inspected by relation is also listed in the model pane.*

For parent-child hierarchy, use the type's **Stands** and containment controls described in
[Add a record type and fields](/docs/guide/model/add-a-record-type-and-fields/).
Then [check issues](/docs/guide/model/fix-issues-before-installing/) and preview the type's generated
relationship panels before activation.

## Limit which records can be chosen

1. On **Relations**, open the **Which records** cell, or the row menu's
   **Which records may be chosen…**. The criteria editor separates the two ends; check which
   type's choices you are changing.
2. Add criteria on the name, a field or a field of an ancestor. Choose the condition and value
   for the intended end. Several criteria are combined with “and”; several **is** choices on
   one field are alternatives.
3. Choose **Save** and inspect the row's summary. These conditions restrict new choices in
   every record picker, not just one panel. Existing relationships remain if a record later
   stops meeting the condition. Recheck Issues before activation.

A relation type's names and reverse name describe the connection from both ends. Its key and
reverse key are stable once released; changing its wording does not create a new identity.
In **Relationship matrix**, selecting a pair opens its relations' menus and the action to allow
another; resize the selected-pair panel if the choices need more room.

## Choose what each relationship carries

1. On **Relations**, edit the pair’s **Carries** cell or choose **Attributes of the relationship…**
   from its menu. If there are no attribute types, create the shared definitions first.
2. Select the **Attributes** whose values belong to the connection itself, then **Apply**.
   Carries now names them; an empty selection reads **Nothing**. Endpoints’ fields are unchanged.
   Select shared definitions of the right value type: a date stays a date, and a Yes or no value
   becomes a checkbox. Check the from and to types in the popover title: this choice applies to
   that directed pair, not every pair using the relation type.
3. To revise limits together, choose **Cardinality and required…** and choose **Save** for the intended
   combination. Released pairs may withhold these structural actions. Use the refusal and
   compatibility check to decide whether a migration is necessary.
4. Select the shared **Relation type** to review both names and its **Settings**. Change
   **Oriented** only after reviewing its effect on record deletion; see
   [relationship settings](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/#visibility-help-and-relationship-settings).

![Allowed relationship showing Carries beside number limits and candidate criteria](/docs/screens/model-relation-carries.png)

After installation, check the relationship's columns on a record or in a matrix cell. To give
people a dedicated view for these values, [add a relationships table](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relationships-table/).
To expose them to another system, [choose them in a consumer API's related block](/docs/guide/model/define-a-consumer-api/).
Each connection holds its own values; selecting Carries creates no values on existing connections.

**Remove relation type** also stops allowing that relation between its listed pairs. Read the
confirmation’s pair list before accepting. Removing a definition from a draft does not delete
live connections immediately; stored use can prevent the change or require a migration.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/expor:
---
title: Export a release
description: Download the immutable model document and identify its exact release.
reader: model-admin
---

Use export to hand a model document to a specialist author or keep a copy of its definitions.
It exports the model, not workspace records. See [Releases](/docs/model/releases/).

1. Open **Settings › Model**, the model's **Releases**, then the intended version. Check its
   name, version and **Immutable release** state rather than opening a similarly named draft.
2. Choose **Export JSON** and keep the downloaded document. The installed release is unchanged.
   Export is also available for historical definitions the current editor cannot interpret.
3. If you need to identify it precisely, open **Technical details**. Use **Copy** beside
   **Release ID** and **Content hash**. The hash identifies the content; the displayed version
   is a human-facing release label.
4. To edit a copy, use **Create draft from release** or the draft creation dialog's **Import
   JSON** option. Importing a document does not activate it. For data backup, use the operator's
   backup procedure instead of treating this file as a workspace export.

![Immutable release with export and draft creation actions](/docs/screens/model-release-detail.png)

![Technical details identifying the release and its content hash](/docs/screens/release-technical-details.png)

If the download fails, read the displayed failure and retry after correcting its cause.
The downloaded file alone does not include records, access grants or publication history.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/choos:
---
title: Choose table columns, filters and sort
description: Choose a table's fields, related-record columns, available filters and initial order.
reader: model-admin
---

Choose what a type's table shows and how it starts when people open it. You need
**Model authoring** and an open draft. The choices become the table's model defaults after
activation; they do not change stored records or save one person's search.

See [Record pages and tables](/docs/model/record-pages-and-tables/) for how table columns
differ from the columns inside a record-page panel.

## Open the table layout

1. Select a type in the model editor and choose **Preview**, then **Edit layout**.
2. Choose **Table**. If there is more than one table view, use **View** to select it.
3. Check that you have a declared table view to arrange. **The draft declares no table view**
   means there is none for this type. Return to the application and use **Add a view…**,
   **Table: the records of one type in rows** to [add one](/docs/guide/model/add-a-view/).

![Table layout with column frames and the Columns, Filters and Default sort controls](/docs/screens/model-layout-table-tab.png)

If the draft is invalid, use **Show issues** and correct the definitions before opening
the layout. Follow [Preview a type](/docs/guide/model/preview-a-type/) for the workspace and
record choices.

## Choose columns, including fields of related records

1. Choose **Columns…**. The popover lists **Name**, the type's fields and its relationships,
   including its parent relationship where applicable. Check the columns you want to show.
2. Check a relationship to show the names of related records as a column. To show one of
   their fields, open **Fields of** followed by the relationship's name beneath that choice.
   Opening the list does not select the relationship or its fields.
3. Select a field of the related records. Each checked field becomes a separate column;
   you can keep the relationship's name column as well, or leave it unchecked.
4. To show information from a containing record, look under **Where they sit ·** followed
   by a type's name. Choose its **Name** or one of its fields. These choices include types
   further up the related records' hierarchy. Fields holding JSON are not offered here.
5. Choose **Apply**. Check the resulting column frames. A field column's heading combines
   the relationship name and the field label. Its cells show the related records' values,
   with **—** where a related record has no value. These columns cannot sort.
6. Reorder frames by their grips, or open a column's menu and use **Move left** or
   **Move right**. **Remove column** takes it out of this view without deleting any values.

![Table Columns dialog with Has name translation unfolded and Language code selected](/docs/screens/model-table-columns-related-fields.png)

Above: the Stops table in the guide's Graubünden model. **Fields of Has name translation**
shows the translation fields and **Where they sit · Language**. Selecting **Language code**
adds **Has name translation · Language code**, showing the language of each related translation.

These choices read fields of records at the other end, or of their containing records.
Fields stored on the relationship itself cannot be columns. If you need the containing
record's name inside a record-page panel, use that panel's
[Columns… menu](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-record-page/#choose-a-panels-columns-and-sort).

## Choose available filters

1. Choose **Filters…** and select the fields and relationships people may filter by.
   Choose the relationship itself to offer a relationship filter. The popover does not unfold
   its fields: a related-field column does not provide a filter on that field.
2. Choose **Apply** and check the selection. This defines available filters; it does not
   restrict everyone's table to particular values. In the live table, a relationship filter
   can find records linked to selected records, linked to any record, or with no link.

Keep at least one column and one filter field. An ordinary field must allow filtering and
must not hold JSON. If **Not applied** appears, read its reason, adjust the choices and apply
again; a refused step changes nothing.

## Choose how the table marks inactive records

1. In the **Table** layout, choose **Inactive records…**, beside **Filters…** and
   **Sort menu and page size…**. The popover is titled **Inactive records of** followed by
   the view's name.
2. Under **A record is inactive when this is No**, select a Yes/No field of this record type.
   Choose **None** if this table should have no inactive mark or switch. If the field you
   need is missing, check that it belongs to this type and is Yes/No. A field of another
   type, or a field with another kind of value, is refused for this setting.
3. Choose **Save**. This saves a draft step; it does not change any record's value or make
   a read-only field editable. The field does not need to be selected in **Filters…**.
   If **Not applied** appears, read the reason, correct the choice and apply again. Use
   **Undo** to reverse an unwanted draft step.
4. Review **Issues** before [installing and activating the release](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/).
   In the active table, records with **No** stay in their usual order with a quieter name
   and a grey **Inactive** pill if the field is called Active. For another field name,
   the pill says **Not** followed by that name in lower case. Records with no value have
   no inactive mark.
5. Check **Hide inactive (N)** beside **Filter**. It starts off unless the page address
   already applies its filter. Turn it on and check the added pill, such as **Active: not No**:
   only marked records disappear, and records with no value stay visible. Turn it off or
   remove the pill to restore the results. The number counts **No** values after the list's
   search and other filters, including **0** when none match. Choosing **Yes** in the ordinary
   **＋ Filter** menu instead excludes records with no value; it does not turn this switch on.

The setting belongs to the selected table view. The same mark and switch use a change set's
or publication's own values; publications remain read-only. See
[Mark inactive records in a table](/docs/model/record-pages-and-tables/#mark-inactive-records-in-a-table)
for the rules and [Lists, search and filters](/docs/use/lists-and-filters/#show-or-hide-inactive-records)
for the reader's controls.

## Set the initial order and check the table

1. Choose **Default sort**, whose control shows the current field and direction arrow.
2. Select **Sorted by** from the view's allowed sort fields. Check **Descending** to reverse
   the order. Related-field columns cannot be chosen as the initial sort.
3. Choose **Save** and check the arrow on the control.
4. Return to preview and inspect real records, including ones with several related records
   and ones with none. An empty table explains what it will show; it does not mean the view
   is broken. Use **Undo** for an unwanted step and review **Issues** before
   [installing and activating the release](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/).

![Table default sort dialog with Sorted by and Descending choices](/docs/screens/model-layout-sort-dialog.png)

People continue to see the active layout until activation. Tree and mapping-grid settings are
in the application’s view menu; see [Add a view](/docs/guide/model/add-a-view/).

## Set the sort menu and reading size

1. In the Table layout, choose **Sort menu and page size…**.
2. Select **Fields a reader can sort by**. Name, existing choices and attributes marked
   Sortable are offered. To add another attribute, first enable Sortable on its shared
   definition. Ordinary field columns can still sort from their headers.
3. Keep at least one choice. If the current default is removed, the first selected field
   becomes the default; if you uncheck everything, the current list is retained.
4. Choose **Rows on a page** and **Apply**. The choices are 10, 20, 25, 50 and 100, plus an
   existing different size. This is the amount read at once, not a total-result limit.
5. Review **Default sort** again, and check the preview and Issues before activation.

![Table Sort menu and page size dialog](/docs/screens/model-table-menu-size.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/previ:
---
title: Preview a type
description: Check a draft record page and table without changing live records.
reader: model-admin
---

Use preview to check a draft's appearance before applying it. You need **Model authoring**.
See [Record pages and tables](/docs/model/record-pages-and-tables/) for what preview reads.

1. Select the type in the model pane and choose **Preview**. A type listed in several applications
   is previewed in the application whose row you selected (a type another application only borrows
   for a relation view opens on the application that holds its records); when none is selected, in the one
   that holds the workspace's records of the type. Choose the application in the band to switch.
   If **The draft has … issues, so
   it cannot be previewed** appears, choose **Show issues**, fix the errors and return.
2. Choose **Workspace** and **Record**. The record's live values are drawn using the draft's
   definition. Check that the workspace is the one whose records you intend to inspect.
3. Use **Show an empty record** to see unfilled fields, especially for a new type. No value
   in a preview does not itself mean that the field or type is invalid.
4. Inspect **Record page** and **Table**, including long labels and records with missing optional
   values. Controls that would change data are disabled. Previewing does not save a record.
5. Choose **Edit layout** to change the draft's presentation, or **Back to definition** to
   return to the selected type. Review Issues after layout changes.

![Draft type preview over a selected live record](/docs/screens/model-type-preview.png)

Preview shows individual screens. The separate activation check decides whether all stored data
fits the release; a good-looking preview does not replace it.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/arran:
---
title: Arrange applications and views
description: Create an application, list shared types and choose the next navigation or layout task.
reader: model-admin
---

Arrange a draft so people can find the types and views they need. You need **Model authoring**.
Any application can use a view when its structure fits. See
[Applications and views](/docs/model/applications-and-views/) for listings and view rules.

1. In the model pane, choose **Add**, **Application…**. Enter **Name** and, if useful,
   **Description**, then choose **Add application**. In an existing application, select its row instead.
2. Check **Object types** and **Stands** to see what it lists and where records belong. Use
   **Object type** to create a definition, or **List an existing type…** to list a shared type
   here. Check the intended type before applying: listing it does not copy its records.
3. Open a listed type's menu. Use **Stop listing in this application** where offered to remove
   only that listing. For containment or a move between applications, use
   [Split, merge and move types](/docs/guide/model/split-merge-and-move-types/) instead. Released
   listings and placements can be refused when data uses them; read the impact before proceeding.
4. Inspect **Views**, including each view's kind, **Shows** and state. **Rename…** changes a
   view's label. To add or configure a relation matrix, follow
   [Add a relation matrix](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relation-matrix/).
5. Use [Group collections in navigation](/docs/guide/model/group-collections-in-navigation/) for
   sidebar sections, their order and initial folded state. This does not change record parents.
6. Use [Preview a type](/docs/guide/model/preview-a-type/), then
   [Edit a record page](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-record-page/) or
   [Choose table columns, filters and sort](/docs/guide/model/choose-table-columns-filters-and-sort/)
   for screen layout. Use [Add a table, tree or mapping grid](/docs/guide/model/add-a-view/)
   for the other view forms.
7. Check **Issues** and review the saved steps before installing. A **Not applied** notice means
   the attempted step was refused; correct its named problem. **Undo** reverses unwanted saved work.

![Application editor listing types, views and navigation groups](/docs/screens/model-editor-application.png)

![Application view list with table, tree, mapping-grid and relation-matrix kinds](/docs/screens/model-editor-systems-views.png)

*Example: an application in the Graubünden model declares all four view kinds. These are choices
in that model, rather than features reserved for the subject of that application.*

The live workspace keeps its current navigation and layouts until the release is activated.

To choose the opening view, edit **Default view** under the application’s **Settings**, select
one of its views, then **Save**. To remove a non-matrix view, choose **Remove view**. Read
“Types only it needed stop being listed here.” before confirming: review the application’s
listings as well as the view list afterwards. Removal changes navigation, not the stored
records. Restore an unwanted draft change with **Undo**.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/chang:
---
title: Change a model with the assistant
description: Describe a model change, review the proposal and complete a migration or a staged record move.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this task to change the structure of an active workspace from words. Read
[Model changes with the assistant](/docs/model/ai-model-changes/) for permissions and the two
ways records can move. You need the assistant enabled, permission to send the data it needs,
and the rights to author, install and release the model and work in change sets.

Your words, the model and any whole workbook you attach go to Claude Code; it can read workspace
records as needed. Turns can cost money, and tasks, files and session transcripts are kept for
the configured retention periods. [About AI in refiroo](/docs/run/ai/) explains access, costs
and retention in full. Check your organisation's policy before sending a file.

## Describe and review

1. Open the intended workspace. Open its **⋯** menu beside the workspace selector and choose
   **Change this model…**. Check the workspace named in **Change this model**.
2. Enter **What should change?**. Say which types or fields change and what should happen to
   existing records. The field allows up to 4,000 characters. Use **A workbook (optional)**
   to attach an XLSX or CSV file when it helps explain the change.
3. Read the disclosure of what is sent. Choose **Ask the assistant**, or **Cancel** to leave
   without starting a task. Wait on the task page; **Stop** pauses the work without discarding
   the task. Before a proposal exists, the journey bar and trail say **Change with the assistant**
   for a task without a workbook. They become **Change this model** when the proposal changes
   the model, or **Change records** when it leaves the model unchanged.
   For words alone, the task heading gets a short title with the assistant’s first answer;
   any draft it makes is named **Assistant:** followed by that title. Your full instructions
   stay under **You said:** on the proposal. Until the title arrives, including after a stop
   or failure before an answer, the heading uses your words, shortened at a word boundary
   with “…” if needed. With a workbook, the heading keeps the file name.
4. Read **The assistant’s proposal**. Check every type it adds or changes, **Checks**, questions
   and the records that move. For a whole-type move, check both the destination type and the
   number of records. Open **Show the model change**. **No type, attribute or relationship
   changes** does not mean the draft is unchanged: it can still change views or layout. Use
   **Open in the model editor** to inspect those changes. A task without a workbook or a
   model draft instead says **No change to the model.**
   Do not accept merely because the summary sounds plausible.
5. Answer questions and use **Tell the assistant what to change** for corrections. Choose
   **Open in the model editor** to inspect or edit the draft directly. Return to the task;
   the assistant rereads the draft when it continues. For a workbook proposal, inspect
   **What the load does**, open each type's row for examples with source cells, and read any
   repeated-name finding. A draft changed after that check is checked again before loading.
6. For a model-only change or a record move, choose **Accept the model** only when the proposed
   structure and treatment of records are right. **Accept the model** in the journey bar
   takes you to the page’s acceptance button; choose that button to confirm.
   A workbook load showing **What the load does**
   uses **Accept and load to change set**: the engine installs a changed model and loads exactly the checked
   records and relationships into a change set as one batch, without another assistant turn.
   It does not activate or publish. Follow
   [Review the assistant's workbook design](/docs/guide/model/review-an-assistants-workbook-design/)
   for loading, refusals and publication. **Discard this proposal** removes the proposal and its
   draft instead. **Close** keeps the proposal for later.

*Example: a model for transport stops might split a general stop type by a field that distinguishes
bus and rail stops. The instruction should say whether the old type remains and which values
