select each new type. These choices belong to the model, not to a built-in transport feature.*

![Change this model dialog with the workspace, instruction and optional workbook](/docs/screens/model-assistant-change-dialog.png)

## Finish a model-only change or a whole-type move

When only the model changes, such as adding a view, acceptance installs a release and prepares
a migration that moves no type. Preview and confirm it as below to put the workspace on the
new model. No change set is created and every record stays as it is.

Whatever you ask the assistant to reshape, all your data comes through: every record, value,
relationship and translation. The only exception is what your own words explicitly ask to
remove. The assistant lists that removal with your words, and the proposal states it in plain
words with the engine's counts before you accept, for example "As you asked, the Drug list is
deleted, deleting 16 records." If the change would lose anything else, the assistant does not
offer it: the task ends with a note naming what would be lost per type, and nothing is changed.

1. For a whole-type move, review the list under **Move the records to the new model** of what
   becomes what, or which application each type moves to when its key stays. The migration
   takes what the draft changes against the workspace's model, together with the moves the
   assistant named. For a model-only change, there are no type moves to review. Accepting has
   installed a release; nothing has moved yet.
2. Choose **Preview the migration**. The migration page opens with the assistant's type choices.
   Follow [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) to inspect converted,
   removed and blocked items. **Back to the proposal** returns to the task.
3. If a mapping is wrong or the engine refuses it, return to the task and use
   **Tell the assistant what to change**. The assistant can revise the model before confirmation.
4. Confirm only the reviewed migration, with **Model release** in this workspace. This changes
   live records and the running release together. There is no change set or separate change-set
   approval for this path. Return to the task to see that the workspace runs the new model.

![Accepted whole-type move with record counts and Preview the migration](/docs/screens/model-assistant-whole-type-move.png)

## Finish a partial move

Before accepting, read how the proposal moves the selected records and what acceptance
prepares: a release with the old types beside the new ones, a change set that moves the
records, and the final release that removes the emptied types. The removal note names the
record moves and their destination types; removing the emptied types does not delete those
records. You do not need to prepare the releases or move the records by hand.

Choose **Accept the model** when this matches your request. Once preparation finishes, the
task links the releases and change set under **Three steps are yours**, with **Next** beside
the available step.

1. Under **1. Add the new types to the workspace**, choose **Open the release**. Activate the
   release holding both the old and new shapes in the intended workspace. No records move.
2. Return to the task. Under **2. Review and publish the change set**, choose
   **Review the change set**. Inspect its record changes and validation, then submit for approval
   and publish according to the workspace's rules. Publication moves the selected records.
3. Return to the task. Under **3. Remove the emptied types**, choose **Open the release** and
   activate the final release. This removes the old types only when they are empty. If new
   records were added to one meanwhile, resolve them and check again.

If the accepted model keeps the old types, **Two steps are yours** omits the removal step.
Someone without **Model release** is told that a holder of that right must activate the release.
A split of thousands of top-level records can take time; avoid starting a duplicate task while
it is working.

![Partial move showing the three steps, with the first complete and review next](/docs/screens/model-assistant-partial-move.png)

## If you cannot continue

Read the reason on the task. A refused migration or next activation is also reported there.
Tell the assistant how to correct the proposal; an explanation cannot waive an engine rule.
After a failure, **Try again as it was** continues without a new instruction. A stopped task
can **Go on as it was**. See [Stop, correct or discard](/docs/model/ai-model-changes/#stop-correct-or-discard)
for what is kept or removed at each stage.

If an action disappears because your permissions changed, ask an administrator to restore the
needed right or give the task link to the person named by the page. An expired or missing task
leads back to the workspaces; start a new task if its proposal is no longer kept. A confirmed
migration has no automatic undo; inspect its history before planning a further model change.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/migra:
---
title: Migrate a workspace
description: Review every converted or removed item and confirm a model switch with accepted loss.
reader: model-admin
---

Start from a draft's install or Apply review, or an activation check that says the data needs
migration. You need **Model release**
in the workspace, with model administration and jobs enabled. See [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/).

1. From **Install and activate…**, read **Activation needs a migration** and choose **Install …
   and preview the migration…**. From **Apply to this workspace…**, choose **Preview what happens
   to the records…**. For an installed release, choose **Preview the migration…** where offered.
   Check the workspace and target release on the migration page. **Nothing has changed yet**
   refers to workspace data: the editor flow has installed the release, but has not activated it.
   Wait for every record to be checked, or **Cancel the preview**. Leaving keeps the job running.
2. For an editor proposal, read **What the draft proposes**. Each row shows **Records of**,
   **Become**, **In**, **Under**, **Records** and a **Proposed** mark for the draft's choice.
   Check the destination type, application and parent placement, plus the split, list-conversion
   or relationship-key lines below. Change **Become** in place if another destination is intended;
   it previews again without changing the draft. Under **What … no longer has**, review any
   remaining missing type or field and select **Became …** only for its genuine replacement.
   Type mappings retain record IDs and history. **Not kept** removes the type's records and
   relationships or the field's values. Each choice previews again.
3. Open each outcome: **Converted**, **Type changed**, **Removed**, **Must be fixed** and, when
   shown, **Created**. Created lists the records and relationships a split or list conversion
   makes. Read the item lists, including before and after values. These count items, not just
   records. Check top-level moves for the removal of the old parent connection; tighter rules
   can leave records under Must be fixed even when their proposed destination is correct.
4. Fix every blocking item in the named workspace or change set. Required values, required
   relationships, parent placement, uniqueness and publication conflicts cannot be waived by
   accepting loss. Choose **Preview again** and review the refreshed lists.
5. If **Removed** contains items, inspect them. While **Must be fixed** contains blocking
   items, the acceptance checkbox is hidden and the migration button is disabled. Resolve
   those items first, then tick **I accept that …** to accept the listed removal.
   Choose **Cancel** to keep the current data; a release already installed remains installed.
6. Check the final action. **Migrate … to …** changes the workspace. **Move change set** changes
   only the named change set onto the workspace's current release. **Migrate and publish** also
   publishes the named change set and needs publication permission and any required approval.
7. Confirm only the reviewed action. If a stale notice appears, **Close** or **Preview again**;
   nothing was migrated by that refusal. Review the new result before another confirmation.
8. Read the success counts and destination. For a workspace migration, inspect its applications
   and arrange to move or discard old change sets. For a change-set move, choose **Open the
   change set** and review and validate it. For migration and publication, inspect the named publication.

![Migration preview with a Proposed destination row and outcome counts](/docs/screens/model-migration-proposed.png)

*Above: the draft proposes moving 12 Stop code records from Network to the top level of Systems. The row is marked Proposed, and Type changed counts 12 records; nothing has changed yet.*

![Migration preview with split and list-conversion proposals and the Created outcome selected](/docs/screens/model-migration-created.png)

*Above: the draft splits Code system from Stop code and turns Code kind values into list records. Created lists 28 new records and relationships across both changes; nothing has changed in the workspace yet.*

![Migration preview with outcomes and choices for missing types and fields](/docs/screens/model-migration-review.png)

![Removed items in a blocked migration preview, with three items to fix and the migration button disabled](/docs/screens/model-migration-loss-confirm.png)

![Stale migration review asking for another preview after the workspace changed](/docs/screens/model-migration-stale.png)

A failed execution leaves data and the release switch unapplied together. Read **Not migrated**
or **Not moved**, correct its cause and preview again. History retains removed content, but
migration has no automatic reverse button.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/undo-:
---
title: Undo and review the draft history
description: Inspect saved steps and undo changes with their dependent steps.
reader: model-admin
---

Use history to understand and correct a draft before releasing it. You need **Model authoring**.
The [model editor](/docs/model/the-model-editor/) saves actions as steps; an installed release stays fixed.

1. Expand **Issues and history**, or **Issues, history and dry run** with a workbook. Choose
   **History**. Steps appear newest first with their author, time and state: **Applied**,
   **Undone** or **JSON edit**. One step may include several related changes. A released-element
   change that affects stored data also shows **Needs a migration**, with the records, values
   and relationships that hold the element. A released key change needs a migration even when
   those counts are zero; integrations naming the key must change with it.
2. Use **Earlier steps** to read older entries. **No steps yet.** means there is no saved step
   in this history. A document edit appears as **JSON edit**, rather than a list of visual actions.
3. To reverse the latest step, choose **Undo** in the header. To reverse an older step, use
   its **Undo** action in History. Check the resulting model and Issues afterwards.
4. If **Undo the steps that depend on it too?** appears, read every dependent step. Confirm
   only if all those reversals are wanted. Cancel keeps them. A field added later cannot stay
   attached to a type whose creation is being undone.
5. Choose **Redo** to restore the available undone step. A new edit clears redo history.
   If the draft changes elsewhere, review its newer history before retrying.

![History showing an applied move, its Needs a migration mark and affected data counts](/docs/screens/model-history.png)

*Above: moving Stop code to the top level of Systems is marked Needs a migration, with 12 records, 36 values and 12 relationships holding the type. Undo is available.*

![History after Undo with the move and its migration mark crossed out and Redo available](/docs/screens/model-history-undone.png)

*Above: the move is Undone and its migration mark is crossed out. Stop code is back under Stop in Network in the draft; Redo is available.*

![Confirmation listing steps dependent on the step being undone](/docs/screens/model-history-undo-dependants.png)

Undo changes the draft and takes the undone step's part out of the proposed migration. Redo
restores it; the install or Apply review reflects the steps that stand now. A migration mark
records a step's impact; activation checks the workspace's current data again. See
[Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/) before installing marked steps.

Undo neither changes an installed release nor reverses published records.
For concurrent edits, see [Work on a draft with others](/docs/guide/model/work-on-a-draft-with-others/).
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/start: --- title: Start a draft from a workbook description: Review a proposed model and its source mapping, check refused rows and load into a change set. reader: model-admin --- Use this task when a workbook needs a new model, an additional application or new fields and types. See [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/) for what the draft, source and dry run keep. You need the permissions to administer the model, activate it in the target workspace and load records there. ## Get the example workbook You can use your own file. To follow the illustrated example, download Haltestellen_Busbetrieb_Nord.xlsx. Save the file, then select it in **Workbook** in step 2 below. It has three sheets: **Haltestellen** (stops), **Namen** (names) and **Lokale Codes** (local codes). This is a deliberately messy workbook from a fictional bus company. Stop names and numbers come from the guide's [example data](/docs/examples/the-example-data/); lines, local codes and fare zones are invented. Review its proposals rather than treating them as an approved model. Dry-run counts and refused rows depend on your mappings and comparison workspace; they may differ from the pictures. For the next-upload exercise, a second file is available in [Propose again with a newer workbook](/docs/guide/model/propose-again-with-a-newer-workbook/#get-the-example-update). ## Start the draft 1. Open **Settings**, **Model**. Choose **New from a workbook**. **New draft** starts model authoring without this workbook proposal task. 2. Enter **Draft name** and choose the **Workbook**, an Excel workbook or CSV file, or drop it onto the field. 3. Under **Propose**, choose **A new application**, **A new model**, **Additions to the model** or **Nothing: I will map it by hand**. Read the explanations: a new application adds to the starting model, while a new model starts empty. Set **Application name** where offered. 4. Choose **Compare with the records of**. The dry run uses that workspace; choose the intended data, not simply a similarly named workspace. Check **Starting document** and **Base release** where offered so the draft starts from the definitions you intend. 5. Choose **Create and propose**, or **Cancel** to leave without creating the draft. Wait for the file to be read and the editor to open. If the upload fails, correct the reported file problem and try again before proceeding. ![Model list with New from a workbook and New draft](/docs/screens/use-wb-model-list.png) *Above: Model lists the releases and drafts installed or saved on the reference instance.* ![Workbook dialog with a selected file, proposal mode and starting release](/docs/screens/use-wb-dialog.png) *Above: Haltestellen_Busbetrieb_Nord.xlsx is a fictional operator file. The capture cancels this dialog.* ## Inspect the source and proposals 1. In the source pane, open each sheet tab. Read the columns, their filled and distinct counts, and the source's header row. Distinguish sheet rows from the data rows actually loaded. 2. Select a proposed type in the model tree. Read **Proposed because** and choose **Evidence** to inspect the values that support it. Check that the proposed key identifies the intended record, and that names, fields, parents and related records have the intended meaning. 3. Select a source column to inspect its mapping. Use its menu's **Map to…** to change what it feeds, or drag it onto a type. Check any splitting of multi-value cells, replacements of placeholders and creation of missing related records. Ignore columns you do not intend to load. 4. Open **Issues, history and dry run**, then **History**, to review the steps. Use **Undo** to reverse an unwanted step and **Redo** to restore it. Closing the editor keeps the saved draft. ![Source pane on the second sheet showing column statistics and Proposed marks](/docs/screens/use-wb-source-namen.png) *Above: Namen is the second sheet of the fictional workbook. Its columns need their own review; a reasonable mapping on the first sheet does not establish that this sheet is correct.* For an explanation of proposal marks and key evidence, see [Proposed steps](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/#proposed-steps-are-decisions-to-review). [How workbook proposals are made](/docs/model/workbook-proposals/) explains the patterns, recognition limits and alternatives behind the evidence. ## Resolve issues and check every source 1. In the bottom panel, choose **Issues**. Fix or undo the steps causing reported issues. **No issues** establishes that the draft is valid, not that every row loads. 2. Choose **Dry run**. Check the draft version and comparison workspace. Wait for the current check to finish; a failed or outdated result is not a result for your latest mapping. 3. Read every source's counts. Select a figure to inspect the rows behind it. Open the red refused-row figure to read each reason. 4. Correct a wrong mapping, unresolved reference or source value. After a source-file correction, use the editor menu's **Upload a newer workbook…**. **Propose again…** can reconsider the file while retaining your edits. Review any new issues and the refreshed dry run. 5. Continue only when you understand the predicted changes and any rows that remain refused. Nothing has been written to the workspace's records by the dry run. ![Dry-run refused rows with their reason and source row numbers](/docs/screens/use-wb-dry-refused.png) *Above: nine Namen rows in the fictional workbook have no matching reference. They would be refused; a valid model does not resolve those references automatically.* When the mapping and dry run are ready, follow [Load a workbook into a change set](/docs/guide/model/load-a-workbook-into-a-change-set/). ## Correct list ranges and column instructions 1. If a sheet contains several lists, choose **Lists** and open each detected list. Read its range and **Loads**. Choose **Adjust list…** to correct the header, last row, first column and last column, then check the range before applying. 2. Use **Don't load this list** for a range to exclude, **Load as a list…** to choose its interpretation, or choose the proposal alternative **Read these N lists as one list under their headers** for at least three lists of the same shape under one title (or no title). These are source instructions; they do not edit cells in the original workbook. 3. Open a column and choose **Map to…**. Review whether it supplies a name, attribute, parent, related record or relationship flag. Check **Matched by**, any naming column and whether missing related records may be created. Select **Ignore** for columns to leave out. 4. Set **Split a cell on** only for genuinely separate values. Open **Add a value map…** or **Edit value map…** to map **Text in the file** to **Becomes**. Check that placeholders are treated as intended, rather than becoming real values. 5. Inspect **Key** and its uniqueness message before **Use as the key of the rows**. Reopen **Dry run** for every source tab. **was** compares a figure with the previous result; open refused rows and use their sheet, row number and reason to make a correction. A workbook describing a model, lists laid out for reading and repeated-parent tables can lead to different proposals. Check the inferred structure rather than assuming one sheet means one type. [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/) explains those choices. ## Use the assistant instead If the built-in assistant is enabled, you can [review its proposed workbook design](/docs/guide/model/review-an-assistants-workbook-design/) before accepting a model and load. The rules-based draft route above does not call AI or offer AI naming suggestions.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/remov:
---
title: Remove an element
description: Review the scope and stored-data impact before removing a model definition.
reader: model-admin
---

Remove unused definitions in a draft with **Model authoring**. See
[Types, attributes and relations](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/) for released-element limits.

1. Select the element, inspect its uses, then open its operations menu. Choose the specific
   removal: **Remove type**, **Remove application**, an attribute's **Detach from …**, or the
   removal offered for that definition. These actions have different scopes.
2. Read the confirmation. Removing a type removes its views, detail page and relationships
   at either end. Detaching an attribute removes its use in that type's views and panels.
   Removing a navigation group leaves its collections available outside the group.
3. Cancel if any named effect is unwanted. Otherwise confirm, inspect the remaining model
   and open **Issues** for references that now need repair. Use **Undo** for an unwanted draft step.
4. A removal of released structure that stored data uses applies to the draft. **History** marks
   it **Needs a migration**, with the records, values and relationships that hold it. The counts
   include Live and open change sets in workspaces running this model. With nothing holding the
   element, the structural step has no migration mark; activation checks stored data again.
5. When installing, review **Activation needs a migration**, then **Install … and preview the
   migration…**. Inspect **Removed** for the records, values and relationships that would be lost.
   Resolve **Must be fixed** items first, then explicitly accept the listed loss only if intended.
   [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) explains confirmation.
   Cancel the review to leave workspace data unchanged.

![Type removal confirmation naming the views, page and relationships removed](/docs/screens/model-type-remove-confirm.png)

![Removal preview with Not kept selected, Removed items listed and loss acceptance ticked](/docs/screens/model-migration-loss.png)

*Above: Stop code is Not kept, and Removed lists 12 items. Must be fixed is zero and the loss acceptance is ticked, making Migrate available. The migration has not been confirmed.*

To hide a collection in one application, use **Stop listing in this application** where offered.
That is different from removing its type and records. A released listing can also need migration.
No removal in a saved draft alone changes the active workspace's records.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/renam:
---
title: Rename or re-key an element
description: Rename a label or change an identifying key with a reviewed migration after release.
reader: model-admin
---

A name is what people read. A key identifies a definition across releases. Changing a released
key needs a migration, even when there are no records; integrations naming it must change too. See [Types, attributes and relations](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/).

1. Open the element in a draft with **Model authoring**. Read **Key editable until released**
   or **Released: a key change needs a migration** in its facts.
2. To change the displayed words, choose **Rename…** or select the editable title. The short form opens beneath the control. Enter **Name**;
   a record type also offers **Plural name**. Save, then check navigation and views using it.
   A shared attribute rename appears on every type that attaches it.
3. To change identity, choose **Change key…** and enter the new key. Relation types offer
   **Change keys…**. Save and inspect the affected definitions and **Issues**. The editor follows
   references in the draft; check documents and external systems you maintain separately.
4. For a released key, read **Needs a migration when installed: integrations naming the key must change**.
   The step applies and **History** marks it **Needs a migration**. When installing, review the key
   change and the consumer APIs of the base release naming it. Coordinate integrations before
   confirming the [migration](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/). A label-only rename does
   not change the key.
5. If a save is refused, read **Not applied**. A key already in use needs a different key;
   for a newer draft, review [concurrent changes](/docs/guide/model/work-on-a-draft-with-others/).

![Rename a type with separate singular and plural names](/docs/screens/model-type-rename-dialog.png)

![Change key dialog for an unreleased type](/docs/screens/model-type-change-key-dialog.png)

![Install review naming a changed released key, its consumer API and a blocking contract-version finding](/docs/screens/model-install-key-change.png)

*Above: the key change for Stop number (UIC) names Stops API among the consumers that must change. The Consumer APIs check needs version 2, so installation cannot continue from this review.*

New keys are suggested from labels: lower-case words separated by hyphens, with accents removed.
A clash adds a number such as -2 or -3. Review the suggestion while it is editable; changing a
label after release does not generate a new identity.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/stop-:
---
title: Stop serving an earlier contract version
description: Announce an earlier consumer contract’s end, remove it in a draft and activate the change.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this task after consuming teams have moved off an earlier version. You need **Model authoring**
to edit and **Model release** in each workspace where you activate the change. Stopping a version
removes its reads without deleting records or stopping the other versions. Read
[Earlier versions](/docs/model/consumer-apis/#keep-an-earlier-version-available) before starting.

## Announce the end date

1. Open a draft based on the workspace’s active release. Select **Consumer APIs**, the API,
   then **Types and related**. In **Earlier versions**, check **Version** and **Superseded**
   to identify the version you intend to retire. This table does not stop the current version;
   [raise it first](/docs/guide/model/raise-a-contract-version/) if it needs a replacement.
2. Agree a notice period with every consuming team, including owners of webhook receivers.
   You choose that period; refiroo does not enforce a minimum for your consumer contracts.
3. Select that row's **Sunset day** value or its pencil. In **Sunset day (YYYY-MM-DD)**,
   enter the agreed calendar date and choose **Save**. Clear it and save to withdraw the
   announcement; the table shows a dash when no day is set. A date that is not a valid
   calendar day stays in the form with **Not saved** and the reason; the previously saved
   value remains unchanged. Correct it and save, or **Cancel**. The date announces the end
   in the response's Sunset header after activation; the version stays served until you
   stop it explicitly, whatever the day.
4. Review and [install and activate](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/) the
   announcement in the intended workspaces. Integrators then see the planned end date in
   the contract’s documents and responses. The date alone never turns the version off.

![Earlier versions with Superseded, Sunset day and Stop serving](/docs/screens/model-consumer-earlier-versions.png)

## Remove the version when consumers are ready

1. Open a new draft from the release that still serves the earlier version. Check the API
   and the intended row in **Earlier versions** again.
2. Choose that row’s **Stop serving**. Read the confirmation naming the version and warning
   that its consumers lose access once the draft is active. Choose **Cancel** to keep the
   row, or confirm **Stop serving** to remove it from this draft. Live workspaces are unchanged.
3. If you removed the wrong row, choose **Undo** or use the draft’s **History** to undo that
   saved step. Check that the version and its sunset day are back before continuing.
4. Review **Issues**, then open **Install and activate…**. Its Consumer APIs list names the API
   and says it **stops serving version …** and its consumers get `CONTRACT_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`,
   not **Compatible**; the activation dialog of each workspace says the same. Confirm that
   this is the removal you agreed. A finding that a kept version changed needs repair;
   raising the current version again does not repair it.
5. Install and activate the release in each intended workspace. Installation alone does
   not stop reads. Check each workspace’s active release; a workspace left on the old
   release keeps serving the version.
6. Ask the integration administrator to review affected webhooks with their receiver owners.
   A webhook whose accepted version stopped is suspended. Resuming accepts the current
   version after its events and filters pass validation; the receiver must be ready for
   that shape. Follow [Find out why a webhook paused](/docs/guide/administer/find-out-why-a-webhook-paused/).

An earlier version’s reads and change feed stop after activation. Keeping an older release
installed or an older publication does not keep that route available. Other served versions
continue reading the same stored data.

## Restore service after activation

Draft **Undo** alone cannot change a live workspace. Prepare a release that retains the original
definition and its model sources again, review its compatibility against the workspace, then
activate it. Do not reuse the earlier number for a different contract. Check suspended webhooks
separately; a restored route does not itself resume delivery. If the required source fields or
relationships have been removed, restore them too or agree a different recovery with the consumers.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/expla:
---
title: Explain a model change
description: Ask for an account before activation and follow its statements back to the engine's facts.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this task before activating a release or applying a draft to a workspace. You need
**Model release** and **Use AI proposals** in that workspace, and a configured AI provider.
The Claude Code assistant alone does not provide this explanation.

Your request sends the model's changes and record counts, without record values or names.
It may incur provider charges. Successful accounts are reused for the same inputs for up to
an hour; call records remain, with content kept only if enabled by the operator. See
[About AI in refiroo](/docs/run/ai/) for full costs, access and retention details, and
[Accounts of model changes](/docs/model/model-change-accounts/) for how the facts are prepared.

1. Open the release under **Settings › Model** and choose **Activate in a workspace…**, then select the
   workspace. Alternatively, open the workspace's draft and choose **Apply to this workspace**.
   Check the workspace, release and comparison before proceeding.
2. Wait for the data and consumer API checks. Opening the dialog does not ask the provider
   or spend AI usage. Read any compatibility notice first.
3. Find **What this change does**. Read the line saying what goes to the provider, then choose
   **Explain this change**. Wait for the account; asking does not activate or apply the model.
4. Read the statements and their AI-written note. Select a numbered citation to move to the
   fact it rests on. A citation to a hidden fact opens the rest of the list. **+** refers to
   the other facts of a kind.
5. Review **The facts**, including counts and blocking reasons. Choose **Show the other …**
   when more facts are available. Check the original compatibility and consumer notices too:
   the account cannot certify that a change is safe.
6. Decide what to do using the dialog's normal action. Cancel if the result is wrong, fix the
   draft, or follow the migration route if needed. Ask again after a new check; the old account
   is cleared. For migration, follow [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/).

![Activation dialog showing What this change does before an account is requested](/docs/screens/model-account-before-request.png)

![Activation dialog with an AI-written account, numbered citations and the engine's facts](/docs/screens/model-account-facts.png)

If **The account could not be written** appears, read the facts below it. **Try again** asks
the provider again; it is not required to continue reviewing the model. If the account could
not be asked for, use the reason shown to resolve the request failure. Fix an invalid draft's
issues or reload a newer draft version before another attempt.

![Provider failure with facts still available and Try again](/docs/screens/model-account-provider-failure.png)

If the section is absent, ask an administrator to check provider setup and your workspace
permissions. It is absent from the install dialog and migration page by design. You can still
read those screens' checks and outcomes without an AI account.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/load-:
---
title: Load a workbook into a change set
description: Apply the workbook's model and profile, load its rows and review the unpublished result.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this for the manual workbook route in the model editor, which loads through an import
profile. For an assistant's proposal, use
[Review the assistant's workbook design](/docs/guide/model/review-an-assistants-workbook-design/):
**Accept and load to change set** loads its checked records and relationships without saving an import
profile or activating the model. The steps below apply to the manual route.

First [start a draft from a workbook](/docs/guide/model/start-a-draft-from-a-workbook/) and
check every source's mapping and dry run. See
[Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/) for the separate model and data stages.
You need the release permissions for any activation and the import and change-set permissions
in the destination workspace. Loading does not publish the records.

## Load and review


1. Choose **Load into a change set…**. Check the dry-run version and summary at the top.
2. Read stage 1. If the model changed, check the release's **Release key**, **Version** and
   **Name**. Installing and activating changes the target workspace's model before loading rows.
   If the model is unchanged, this stage keeps it and saves the profile.
3. Under **Open a change set**, set **Change set name** and **Workspace**. Verify the destination
   before proceeding, especially if it differs from the comparison workspace.
4. Review **Load the rows**. Found records are updated through the saved profile. Choose
   **Install, activate and load**, or **Load** when no activation is needed. **Cancel** leaves
   the dialog without starting these stages.
5. Wait as the stages run in order. Completed steps are marked; the button shows **Installing…**,
   **Opening the change set…** or **Loading…**. During the row load, read the processed-item count
   under **Load the rows**. The dialog's actions are unavailable while it works.
6. If it stops, read which stages completed and why it stopped. An installed release can remain
   installed after a later failure; inspect the reported state before retrying. If the profile
   or model has issues, return to **Issues** and resolve them.
7. At **Loaded into the change set**, read all four counts: **created**, **updated**, **unchanged**
   and **refused**. They cover records and relationships. A finished load with refused items is
   not a complete import of every source row. Compare the result with the dry run and resolve
   unexpected refusals before publishing.

![Load dialog showing release details and the chosen change-set workspace](/docs/screens/wbload-dialog.png)

*Above: the fictional operator workbook is about to install release 1.0.1, open a change set in
Guide workbook test and load the rows. This is the destination chosen for this example.*

![Load in progress with completed installation and change-set stages](/docs/screens/wbload-running.png)

*Above: the first two stages are done. Loading has begun at 0 of 420 items; the button says Loading….*

![Completed load with its four counts and Open the change set review](/docs/screens/wbload-finished.png)

*Above: the fictional workbook load created 258 records and relationships, updated 108, left 45
unchanged and refused 9. The result is in a change set, ready to review.*

## Inspect the loaded changes

1. Choose **Open the change set review**. Check its workspace and change-set name against the
   destination you chose. On **Records**, read the kinds of change and expand entries to inspect
   the loaded details. Use **Filter** if needed, then remove it to check the rest.
2. Open **Relationships** and inspect the connections. Compare the proposed changes with what
   you intended to load. Unchanged records do not count as differences; refused rows have not
   become successful record changes. The dry run's refused-row details explain its known refusals.
3. Choose **Back to change set**. Open a collection and inspect the records' fields and
   relationships. Check the orange **Change set** banner before correcting anything; the load
   has not published the records.
4. If the result is ready, [review, validate and publish the change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/),
   or [submit it for approval](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/#submit-your-work).
   **Close** in the finished load dialog leaves the loaded proposal unpublished; it does not undo it.

![Review changes showing added records from the workbook load](/docs/screens/wbload-review.png)

*Above: the load's review in Guide workbook test includes new lookup values and local codes.
Each arrow opens the record's details; Relationships has its own tab.*

![Loaded collection of records inside the load's open change set](/docs/screens/wbload-records.png)

*Above: Haltestellens lists 51 proposed records in the fictional workbook's application. The
change-set banner remains visible above the list; the records have not been published.*

Keep the draft if you need to revisit its mapping. To remove it, choose **Delete draft…** on the
editor menu and read the confirmation. Deletion removes its proposals, steps and attached workbook
permanently; installed releases remain. Cancelling deletion keeps the draft.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/work-:
---
title: Work on a draft with others
description: Recover an edit refused because another person saved a newer draft.
reader: model-admin
---

Several model authors can open the same draft. Each save checks the version it was based on,
so an older edit cannot silently replace a newer one. See [The model editor](/docs/model/the-model-editor/).

1. When **Another change came first** appears, stop repeating the original action. Your change
   was not applied. The notice lists steps applied since you opened the draft, and the model
   beneath it shows the newer version. A rename names both the old and new name, so you
   can identify the definition before deciding whether to retry.
2. Read those steps and inspect the affected definitions. Check whether your intended change
   is still needed and whether its target still means the same thing.
3. Choose **Apply mine again** to try your change against that version, or **Discard mine**
   to leave it out. A further edit by someone else can refuse the retry too; review again.
4. Open **History** to confirm the saved result and **Issues** to check its validity.

![Newer draft notice with applied steps and retry or discard actions](/docs/screens/model-conflict-editor.png)

In the specialist [JSON view](/docs/model/json-view/), **A newer draft version exists** preserves
your local text. Choose **Copy local JSON** before **Reload saved version** if you need that text.
Reloading reads the saved draft; it does not merge your local text into it. Review and reapply
only the changes still needed, then save against the current version.

![JSON editor preserving local work after a version conflict](/docs/screens/model-json-newer-version.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/add-a:
---
title: Add a table, tree or mapping grid
description: Add a collection view and choose its hierarchy or matching relationship.
reader: model-admin
---

Work in a draft with **Model authoring**. A view gives people a way to work with existing
types; adding it does not create records. Read [Applications and views](/docs/model/applications-and-views/)
for the structural rules. For cells at row and column intersections, use
[Add a relation matrix](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relation-matrix/) instead.

## Start with the application

1. Select the application and choose **Add a view…** from its menu.
2. Choose **Kind of view**. Only suitable kinds are offered. A table needs a type; a tree
   needs a listed type that permits records without a parent; a mapping grid needs an optional
   non-containment relationship. Add those definitions first if the kind is missing.
3. Complete the form for that kind below. Enter **Name**, then **Add view**. Check **Views** and
   **Issues**. **Not applied** means the step was refused: read its reason and revise the
   choices. **Cancel** leaves the draft unchanged.

## Table

Choose **Table: the records of one type in rows**, select **Type**, and enter **Name**.
The application also lists the type if necessary. Columns, filters and sorting start from
its attributes. After adding it, select the type and open **Preview**, **Edit layout**, **Table**;
choose this view in **View** to [arrange it](/docs/guide/model/choose-table-columns-filters-and-sort/).

## Tree

1. Choose **Tree: records under the records that contain them**.
2. Select **Top of the tree**. These are types that can stand without a parent. The tree
   includes the types beneath them that this application lists. List missing child types in
   the application before adding the tree.
3. Set **Each record reads** to Name or a field shared by every shown type. **Second line**
   adds another shared field; **None** removes it.
4. Set **Records under a record are ordered by**. The form applies that one field to child
   types. It starts with Name. More detailed per-type or descending ordering needs a specialist.
5. For an on/off control, choose a common Yes or no field in **Switch a record on and off with**.
   Choose None for no availability action. A read-only field cannot support this action.
6. Enter the name and choose **Add view**. Review Issues. The form sets availability actions only; do not
   expect Create, Rename or Move just from choosing a tree. Ask a specialist to declare those
   separately when needed.

![Add a view with Tree selected and roots, label, second line, order and availability choices](/docs/screens/model-add-tree-view.png)

## Mapping grid

1. Choose **Mapping grid: records of one type matched to records of another**.
2. In **Matches records through**, choose the permitted relationship and its two types.
   Containment and required ownership are not offered.
3. In **Rows are**, choose the first or second type. This decides which end chooses records
   at the other end. Changing the relationship or row end resets the column and search choices
   to Name: select them again afterwards.
4. Choose and order **Columns of a row** and **Columns of the matched record**. Keep at
   least one in each list. Fields holding JSON are not offered. In **Columns of a row**,
   **From the parents** offers the types the row can stand beneath. Add one to show the name
   of each row record's nearest parent of that type, even several levels above it. The type's
   name heads the column. These parent names give context but are not searched when people
   search the grid's rows.
5. Choose **Find a record to match by**. Name and searchable attributes of the matched type
   are offered. This controls candidate searching, not a relationship’s eligibility rules.
6. Enter the name, choose **Add view** and check the resulting view and type listings. The new grid starts
   with 20 rows per page. A specialist can change that reading size.

![Add a view with Mapping grid selected, relationship, row end and display/search fields](/docs/screens/model-add-mapping-grid.png)

## Change or remove a view

In **Views**, open a tree or mapping grid’s menu and choose **Change…**. Choose **Save** and
review the saved step. On a tree, the form rebuilds actions from its availability choice:
review any actions a specialist had previously declared. New trees start with 50 records per
branch page; the change form preserves an existing reading size.

**Rename…** changes the label. **Remove view** removes the view and can stop listing types
only it needed. Review the confirmation and remaining listings. Stored data remains. Use
**Undo** to restore the draft step. Review the application’s **Default view** in Settings
when changing its views, then [install and activate](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/)
when the draft is ready. People keep the current views until activation.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/defin:
---
title: Define a consumer API
description: Choose what other systems read and review how each editor choice changes their answers.
reader: model-admin
---

Define a consumer API when another system needs an agreed view of your workspace's data.
Open a model draft with **Model authoring** and agree the required information with the
consuming team. You choose the public record shape, the operations and the filters;
a security administrator separately grants a client access in each workspace.

See [Consumer APIs in the model](/docs/model/consumer-apis/) for the rules. The marked
examples below use the reference Stops API. They explain the result of your choices; the integrator’s request examples are linked separately.

## Choose the records and their public shape

1. Select **Consumer APIs** in the model pane, then the add button's **Consumer API…**.
   Enter **Name**, review **Key** and choose **Types to expose**. A blank key is made from
   the name. Choose **Add consumer API**. The initial definition includes identifiers, names, attached
   attributes, Get by ID and a list per type. Inspect these starting choices before sharing
   the contract: exposing a type does not mean every attached field belongs in a public API.
2. On **Types and related**, inspect each type's public name. Use **Expose a type…** to add
   another type. Consumers receive that public name as the object's type. Choose only the
   types they need as business objects; related blocks can carry information from other
   types without exposing those records as business objects in their own right.
3. On **Fields**, open **Parent, path and hierarchy…** if consumers need containment information. The
   parent is the immediate containing record; a path or hierarchy names ancestors from
   the root down, excluding the current record. Review those outputs as part of the contract.
4. Use **Add related…** to include information reached through a relationship. Set
   **Output name**, **Via** and **Fields**. Each related field pairs a public name with a
   value on the related record. Check the relationship's direction and whether it serves
   one record or several: the answer is respectively an object or an array. A missing
   relationship gives null or an empty array, rather than an invented related record. The
   field picker's group **Attributes of the relationship** lists the values stored on the
   relationship itself, when the relation's binding carries any. Give each selected value a
   public output name and check its served type in **Schema**. A connection without that value
   answers null; the same value can differ on two connections to the same related record.
5. To add these values to an existing block, use its **Fields…** and select from **Attributes
   of the relationship**. If the group is empty, review **Via** and the pair's **Carries** in
   [Add a relationship](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relationship/#choose-what-each-relationship-carries).
   Do not add connection values to the main object's Fields: they need the related block's context.

![New consumer API dialog with name, key and types to expose](/docs/screens/model-consumer-add-dialog.png)

Above: creating a consumer API in the reference model.

**Example result.** Stops API exposes Stop, Municipality, Operator and Mode. Its Stop
object includes an `operator` object and a `modes` array. The parent names the municipality;
the path is `Graubünden/Plessur/Chur` for the Chur stop. These are outputs chosen in
**Types and related** and **Fields**, not extra records copied into the stop. Compare the
[complete business object](/docs/model/consumer-apis/#the-business-object-consumers-read).

![Related-block field picker with the Attributes of the relationship group and selected outputs](/docs/screens/model-consumer-relationship-field-picker.png)

*Above: Stops API’s Add related dialog in a reference-model draft, with output operatorLinks
and Operated by (forward), from Stop to Operator. The fields are name, localName and isPrimary.
The open source list for isPrimary separates Built in, Attributes of the exposed types and
Attributes of the relationship. Primary contact is selected beside the Local name and
Inspected on choices. This dialog has not been applied.*

## Add values and related records to the parent

Use this when a consumer needs the containing record's values alongside each child. For
example, a catalogue item can return its category's approval flag and external codes. This
avoids a second read, but a parent's related block repeats for every child in a list.

1. On **Fields**, choose **Parent, path and hierarchy…**, select **Serve the parent
   (objectType, id, code, name)** and choose **Save**. The **Parent** section appears below
   the object's fields. If it is already served, open that section directly.
2. Review the parent's **Output name**. Select **Fields**, or choose **Parent fields…**,
   to open **Fields of the parent**. Each row pairs a public name with the source it reads.
   Choose built-in values or attributes from **Attributes of the parent types** and review
   the proposed camelCase name. Edit that name if consumers need another one, then choose **Save**.
   The Parent table shows name=source where they differ. These sources belong to types that
   directly contain exposed records, rather than to the child. A missing or unbound value
   answers null unless a default supplies a value; with no parent, the whole output is null.
   Existing short lists remain valid: built-in fields keep their role's output name, and
   other sources become camelCase words, such as categoryCode for category-code. Editing
   writes the parent fields out with explicit output names.
3. Under **Parent's related records**, choose **Add related**, or open the consumer API's
   ⋯ menu and choose **Add related to the parent…** to open the same dialog. Give the block an **Output
   name**, choose **Via**, and select **Fields**, including their public output names.
   The offered relationships start from the possible parent types. Choose **Add related block** and inspect the
   new row. Its block sits inside the parent's answer; do not add a parent prefix to its
   output name here.
4. In **Served**, choose **Always** to return that block in ordinary answers, or **On request**
   to return it only when a consumer asks. You can also set Served in the add dialog.
   The related table on **Types and related** has the same choices for the object's blocks.
   Use **Fields** on a parent block to adjust what it shows.
5. Open **Operations**. If any block is on request, **Include** shows the accepted choices,
   with the parent's blocks distinguished by a parent prefix. This list is generated from
   Served; there is nothing to enter here. Share it with the consuming team. An omitted
   block is absent, rather than null or an empty list; when requested it uses the usual
   object-or-list shape.
6. To filter through the parent's block, open **Filters**, choose **Add filter…**, set
   **Verb** to **On related**, and select the parent's entry in **Related block**. Choose
   **Name** and **Matches on**. Select **Keep only matching records** if children whose
   parent has no matching item should disappear. Leave it clear to trim only the block.
   The filter still works when the block is not requested. Leave **Crosswalk** clear:
   a parent's block cannot be a crosswalk target. The parameter used by Include is
   reserved for requesting blocks; choose a different filter name.
7. Review **Issues**, **Schema**, **Message example** and compatibility. The parent has
   one level; another parent, path or hierarchy cannot be added inside it. Values from the
   parent's ancestors are supported through specialist editing, rather than new choices
   in the parent field picker. An invalid field or relationship must be corrected before
   activation. Changing **Always** to **On request** on a released block needs a higher
   contract version because the block leaves the ordinary answer.

![Consumer API Operations tab with Include choices for an object block and a parent block](/docs/screens/model-consumer-include.png)

The Include list is generated from the two related tables' **Served** choices.
See [the parent's rules](/docs/model/consumer-apis/#the-parent-can-carry-its-own-values) and
[requests with optional blocks](/docs/integrate/reading-business-objects/#ask-for-a-related-block)
when reviewing the contract with integrators.

## Choose the fields and fallbacks

1. On **Fields**, inspect **Output name**, **Role**, **Sources (first non-empty)**,
   **Served type** and **Default**. Output names are the names consumers receive;
   sources are where their values come from. Use **Add field…** to add a public field.
2. Use **Sources…** on an existing field to order its fallbacks. The first non-empty
   value wins. Zero and false count as values. **Move up** and **Move down** order
   supported items; **Remove** takes an item out.
3. Choose **Role** for an identity, code, name or validity output where needed. The identity
   reads the record's stable ID. Keep any business identifier as a separate field. Check
   **Served type** after changing sources; incompatible types or conflicting roles appear
   in **Issues** and need correction.
4. Select an editable **Default** cell to provide a fallback only when all sources have
   no value. Save the value or cancel. Use the served type: a text fallback cannot stand
   in for a number. A default changes the consumer answer, not the stored record.

![Public field dialog with output name, sources and role](/docs/screens/model-consumer-add-field.png)

Above: adding a public field to a consumer API in the reference model.

**Reference-data example:** the code field tries the stop identifier, then the operator code, then the mode code. Chur’s stop shows its stop identifier while its operator shows SBB. The stop number is an integer. A default abbreviation applies only to a record without one; Chur’s existing CH takes precedence. See [Sources and defaults](/docs/model/consumer-apis/#sources-and-defaults).

## Offer the operations and filters

1. On **Operations**, review **Get by ID**, **XREF** and **Resolve**. Get by ID reads a
   stable record ID; XREF matches values such as a code or name. Resolve performs many
   such reads in a batch and needs both Get by ID and XREF. Leave off operations the
   contract does not need: consumers cannot use an undeclared operation.
2. Use **Add list…** and set **Key**, **Of**, **Within the filter** and **Sorted by**.
   **Of** selects a type; sorting selects its order. None for Within gives the list no
   special parent parameter. With an Under filter, a consumer can supply a parent ID to
   list records below it. Omitting that parameter still returns the whole type.
3. Enable XREF if needed, then use **Add XREF rule…**. Review the fields with
   **Matches on…** and **Fields…** where offered. **Exact** and **Contains** are numeric
   weights, not mutually exclusive modes. Give reliable identifiers stronger weights
   than broad name fragments. Contains applies to text terms of at least three characters.
4. Use **Add a match through a related block…** when related data should help identify an
   exposed record. Review **Also match through**, **First of** and **Prefers**. A match
   through a system code can identify its owning record; a shared code can identify several.
   Use that row’s **Preferred types…**, select **Prefer records of these types**, and choose **Apply** in the popover
   to prefer exposed owner types; select none to remove the preference. Review ties with the
   consuming team rather than relying on the first result.
5. On **Filters**, choose **Add filter…**, **Name** and **Verb**. **By type** selects types;
   **Under** reads containment; **Linked to** selects **Through**; **On related** selects
   **Related block**. Review **Matches on** and the offered **Options**. **Keep only
   matching records** narrows the returned records. A related filter also narrows the
   related block's items; **Score only matching items** limits which items contribute
   lookup scores. **Crosswalk** lets consumers ask for a target representation from
   that block. Enable only the choices the contract needs.
6. For a filter on connection values, use **On related**, choose the block, then **Matches on…**
   and a field under **Attributes of the relationship**. Keep only matching records if objects
   without a matching connection should disappear too. To score a carried value instead, use
   a text attribute in the related match's **First of**. Review **Schema** and **Message example**:
   only the connection with that value supplies a match, even when other records share its target.

![Filter dialog with verb-specific matching options](/docs/screens/model-consumer-add-filter.png)

Above: adding a filter to a consumer API in the reference model.

**Reference-data example:** the all-stops list can use an ordinary municipality filter to match Chur’s FSO number 3901. The stops list uses that filter name as its special parent scope and requires the municipality’s stable identity. Omitting the parent selection returns all stops. Review this distinction with the consuming team.

The stop number Exact rule scores Chur at 900 for its number 8509000. Matching Q663869 through its Wikidata system code instead scores 90. A tied top score stays ambiguous. The mode filter can further restrict results to Train. See [Lookups and batch answers](/docs/model/consumer-apis/#lookups-and-batch-answers) for how these choices fit together.

## Define notifications and review the contract

1. If every exposed type needs standard notifications for creation, update and deletion,
   enable **Events per type**. For a named event, use **Add custom event…**, then choose
   **Key**, **Types**, **Changes** and **Watches**. No Watches means any change to what
   consumers read, including related blocks. To report edits of carried values, include their
   related block in Watches and expose those values in the block. The reference event watches
   only main fields; it needs this extra choice to report connection-value changes.
   To report changes to the parent's selected values or related items, watch the parent
   output or leave Watches empty. One parent edit can update every child that shows it.
   Full event and webhook objects omit on-request blocks; notifications have no Include choice.
   This defines an event, not a delivery subscription.
2. Use **Describe…** to explain the API's purpose to consuming teams. Review **Issues**,
   **Schema**, **Message example** and the compatibility result. A **Not applied** notice
   means the attempted step was refused: correct its named problem, then review again.
   Specialist editing does not bypass validation.
3. If the editor says **Needs contract version …**, inspect the contract changes and
   [raise the contract version](/docs/guide/model/raise-a-contract-version/). The contract
   version is separate from the model release version. Renaming a public field, changing
   a related block's shape, removing an operation or reducing event coverage can require
   a higher version.
4. [Review and share the generated documents](/docs/guide/model/see-a-consumer-apis-documents/)
   before installing and activating the release. Draft edits do not change the live API.
   Agree changes with integrators and ask a security administrator to grant the consuming
   client this API in the workspaces it needs. Model authoring and other roles do not
   substitute for that grant.

**Reference-data example:** the reference notification watches code, name and validity dates. A name change produces an update naming the affected name output; changing latitude alone does not. See
[the event example](/docs/model/consumer-apis/#events-describe-changes-to-the-output).
The reference contract is version 1. When a draft based on its released definition raises it to 2, the editor keeps version 1 in **Earlier versions** by default. After activation both read current data, each in its own shape. Check the retained row and agree the changeover with consumers; see [Raise a contract version](/docs/guide/model/raise-a-contract-version/).

## Plan the earlier version’s lifetime

On **Types and related**, review **Earlier versions** after raising a released contract.
The editor keeps the base release’s definition even if you made breaking edits before raising;
it does not keep an unserved draft version. Review **Superseded** and optionally edit
**Sunset day** to announce an agreed end. Every retained version must still have the model
sources it reads. Keep those types, fields and relationships while its consumers need them.

The model administrator chooses the notice period. A sunset day does not stop service.
When the consuming teams are ready, follow
[Stop serving an earlier contract version](/docs/guide/model/stop-serving-an-earlier-contract-version/)
to remove the row, review the warning and activate the change. **Undo** restores a removal
in the draft; it does not reverse an already activated release.

## Refine a released API safely

Turning XREF off can ask **Stop offering XREF?** because its rules are removed and Resolve
stops too. Cancel to retain them, or confirm and inspect the contract difference. **Undo**
restores the step; switching XREF on again alone does not restore the old match rules.

Use **Rename…** for a display-name change. A new API shows **Key editable**; a released API
shows **Released: a new key moves its address**. Its key is the access point consumers
already use. **Change key…** is still offered, but after activation the old address answers
404, as if the API were removed, and the contract check warns about it. Removing the API
stops those reads after activation too. Coordinate any deliberate replacement and its access
grants with the consuming team.

*Source for the reference examples: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0.*

To remove an entire contract, choose **Remove consumer API**, read the warning and confirm
only when consumers are ready to lose that access after activation. Cancel keeps it. Undo
restores a saved draft removal. **Edit as JSON…** is a specialist alternative on the whole
API or an individual row; it saves one step and still needs validation and contract review.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/edit-:
---
title: Edit a draft as JSON
description: Save and validate a model document in the specialist draft workbench.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this task only when you maintain model documents. Ordinary browser modelling does not
require document syntax. You need **Model authoring**. See [The JSON view](/docs/model/json-view/).

1. Open the draft's **JSON** or **Open as JSON**. Check **Draft name** and the editable draft
   version before changing the **JSON model** text. Use **Export JSON** for a copy if needed.
2. Make the intended specialist edit. If **JSON syntax:** reports an error, correct it first.
   The summary alone is not proof that all references resolve.
3. Read **Authoritative validation**. Select a diagnostic to reach its location. Correct unknown
   references or conflicting definitions. Do not replace a referenced definition merely to silence an error.
4. Choose **Save draft**. This saves your text as a draft step, shown as **JSON edit** in
   History. If **A newer draft version exists** appears, choose **Copy local JSON** before
   **Reload saved version** when you need to keep your work. Review and reapply changes manually.
5. After saving, choose **Compile and compare**. Review **Canonical model**, its **Ready for
   review** or **Invalid** state and all semantic changes. Unsaved edits must be saved before compiling.
6. Choose **Open in editor** to inspect the same draft visually. To install without activating,
   use **Install immutable release…** where your permissions allow it and read **Install this
   model release?**. Confirm **Install release** only after review. It creates an inactive release.

![Syntax error in the specialist document editor](/docs/screens/model-json-syntax-error.png)

![Workbench actions including Save draft, Compile and compare and Export JSON](/docs/screens/model-json-workbench-actions.png)

For activation, follow [Install and activate a release](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/).
A successful save or compile alone does not check every workspace's data.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/reuse:
---
title: Reuse and change attributes
description: Attach a shared field and change its local rules or shared definition.
reader: model-admin
---

Work in a draft with **Model authoring**. Read
[Types, attributes and relations](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/) before changing a shared field.

1. Select the receiving type and open **Attributes**. Choose **Attach an existing attribute…**
   and select the field. Already attached fields are not offered. Choose **Required** only if
   every record of this type must supply it, then choose **Add attribute**.
2. Check **Shared with**. A shared attribute's name, value type and uniqueness are used by all
   attached types. Open **Attribute types** to inspect the common definition and its attachments.
3. In the type's table, select an editable **Required** or **Read-only** cell, choose **Yes**
   or **No**, then **Save**. The menu also offers **Make required** / **Make optional** and
   **Make read-only** / **Make editable**. These choices apply to this type's attachment.
4. To change the shared field, use **Rename…**, **Value type…**, **Make unique** or **Allow
   repeated values**. On the attribute type, **Features…** chooses **Searchable**, **Filterable**,
   **Sortable** and **Unique**. Inspect every attached type before applying a shared change.
5. Use **Move up** or **Move down** to order attributes. **Move to…**, or dragging a field onto
   a type in the model pane, moves the attachment; its columns and panel placement move with it.
   Check the destination rather than creating a duplicate attribute definition. For a released
   field, read **Needs a migration when installed**: moving the attachment removes its values
   from the original type's records. They cannot be carried onto a different type's records.
6. Review **Issues** and **History**. A released field change that affects stored data applies
   and is marked **Needs a migration**, with affected records, values and relationships.
   Installing the draft shows the migration to review. Check conversions, loss and records that
   break tighter rules before [confirming it](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/).
   Use **Undo** if the draft change is unwanted.

![Attach an existing shared attribute to a type](/docs/screens/model-attribute-attach-existing.png)

![Attribute operations including value type, local rules and list conversion](/docs/screens/model-attribute-menu.png)

**Detach from …** removes the attachment and its uses in that type's views and panels; it does
not mean remove the attribute from every type. Read the confirmation, or cancel to keep it.

## Set bounds and field guidance

1. Select the shared definition under **Attribute types**. For Whole number or Decimal number,
   edit **Minimum** or **Maximum** in **Settings**. Both open **Minimum and maximum…**. Enter
   either or both, or leave them empty to remove bounds, then **Save** in the popover. A minimum greater
   than the maximum is invalid. All uses of the shared field receive these bounds.
2. Edit **Hidden** or **Help text** in the same Settings table and **Save**. These are shared
   presentation choices. Hidden leaves the field off record forms without deleting its data.
3. To provide guidance for just one type, select that type’s **Attributes** table and edit
   **Hidden** or **Help text** there. A local help text replaces the shared help; clearing it
   returns to shared help. A field hidden by the shared definition remains hidden even when
   the local cell says No. Review a populated and an empty record in Preview.
4. Check Issues and the release comparison. Bounds apply to stored values too; saving the draft
   does not convert or fill data. Correct incompatible records or review a migration before
   activating the release.

![Shared attribute Settings with bounds, field guidance and a released-key migration notice](/docs/screens/model-attribute-settings.png)

*Above: Height (m) has a minimum of 0, a maximum of 4500, Hidden set to No and help text. Its facts say Released: a key change needs a migration.*

The shared definition’s **Attach to a type…** is another way to reuse it. **Change key…** is
also available after release, with a migration and a warning that integrations naming the key
must change. See [Rename or re-key an element](/docs/guide/model/rename-or-re-key-an-element/). **Remove attribute type** removes the common definition where
allowed; review its attachments and the confirmation. Detaching from one type is the smaller
change when other types still need it.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/insta:
---
title: Install and activate a release
description: Review a draft, choose one workspace and confirm installation and activation safely.
reader: model-admin
---

Apply a checked model to one workspace. You need model authoring to prepare the draft and
**Model release** in the target workspace; creating a new workspace also needs **Workspace
administration**. Read [Releases](/docs/model/releases/) and
[fix draft issues](/docs/guide/model/fix-issues-before-installing/) before confirming.

## Install from the editor

1. Open the draft and choose **Install and activate…**. Read the confirmation; opening it alone
   installs nothing.
2. Check **Release key**, **Version** and **Name**. Keep the key when releasing another version of
   the same model. The dialog proposes a version no release of this model holds. If you type one that is taken by
   different definitions, the refusal offers a **Use** button with the next free version. The draft's edit
   number is not this version.
3. Under **Activate into**, choose **An existing workspace** and select it, or **A new workspace**
   and complete its details. Read the workspace name carefully: another workspace may run another
   model. The choice affects this target alone.
4. Review **What changes against** the base release, **Valid**, stored-data compatibility and
   **Consumer APIs**. Resolve blocking issues before continuing. A different-model workspace may
   be checked only when activation is attempted; its selection is not a promise its records fit.
5. If **Activation needs a migration** appears, read the steps and what each part does.
   Review where records go, **records move**, **records created**, **relationships created**
   where shown, and **refused**. For a changed key, the warning names consumer APIs of the base
   release using it and says integrations naming the key must change. Coordinate those changes.
6. When a migration is needed, choose **Install … and preview the migration…**. This installs
   the release and opens the migration page with the draft's proposal filled in. The release
   is not active yet. Review **What the draft proposes**, its **Proposed** rows and all outcomes,
   including **Created** for a split or list conversion, then
   [confirm the migration](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) when acceptable.
7. Otherwise confirm **Install … and activate in …**, or **Install … and create …** for a new
   workspace. Wait for the outcome. **Cancel** in the install dialog leaves the draft saved
   without installing or activating it.

![Install and activate confirmation with release identity, workspace and compatibility checks](/docs/screens/model-install-dialog.png)

*Above: Guide draft proposes release 1.0.1 for Graubünden, adding Step-free access and Inspected by.
The captured dialog was cancelled: neither installation nor activation happened.*

![Install review with Activation needs a migration, moving-record counts and a preview action](/docs/screens/model-install-migration.png)

*Above: the draft proposes moving 12 Stop code records to the top level of Systems in Stops tidy-up, with zero refused. Install … and preview the migration… opens the record review; this captured dialog was cancelled.*

A successful installation fixes the release's content; the draft continues as the next editable
version. If the result says **Installed, not active**, keep the installed release and resolve the
reported activation problem. Do not assume installation was undone.


## Review earlier consumer contracts before activation

In **Consumer APIs**, check both the current version and every **Earlier versions** row in
the draft. Raising a contract normally keeps the base release’s previous definition. That
version continues reading current data in its original shape after activation. Installing
an older release alone does not keep any contract served; the workspace’s active release
must retain it.

A finding ending **a kept version is served as it was: restore it, or stop serving it**
means the retained contract would change. Restore that definition and its model sources,
or agree to stop serving it. Raising the current version again does not fix the finding.
The install review shows this explanation instead of a raise action for that retained version.

In the install review, and in the activation dialog of each workspace, a warning that
an API **stops serving version …** means that earlier version disappears
on activation. The review names the version and says its consumers get
`CONTRACT_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`; it does not say **Compatible** for that API. Confirm the removal with consuming teams, including webhook owners. Its
reads stop and affected webhooks need review before resuming on the current contract. A
**Sunset day** alone never stops a version. See
[Stop serving an earlier contract version](/docs/guide/model/stop-serving-an-earlier-contract-version/).

Read the removal warning in the install review before opening the confirmation. The API’s
**Schema › Against what consumers read now** lists the same finding.

Review the destination workspace’s contract check even when the draft’s base comparison
passes: another workspace may serve a different release or retain different versions.

## Apply from a workspace

1. On **Settings**, **Workspaces**, open the intended workspace and choose **Edit model**.
   Confirm **Applies to** in the editor header, make the changes and choose **Apply to this workspace…**.
2. Read the workspace's current model, **What changes in the model**, data compatibility and
   **Consumer APIs**. Expand **Becomes release** to review the release identity where shown.
3. Read **Change sets left on** the old version. They stay pinned to that release and cannot be
   published until moved to the new one or discarded. Check **Not changed** for the other workspaces.
4. If **Your records stay as they are** is shown, confirm **Apply to** the named workspace when ready.
   If **Activation needs a migration** appears, review the steps, destinations, counts and warnings
   about changed keys and the consumer APIs naming them. **Some records must move first** can
   appear when the compatibility check finds a migration without a draft proposal.
5. Choose **Preview what happens to the records…** when a migration is needed. It installs the
   release and opens a migration preview with the draft's choices where available. Inspect
   **What the draft proposes**, the **Proposed** rows and outcomes, including **Created** when
   records and relationships are created. The workspace keeps its current release until you
   [confirm the migration](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/).

![Workspace apply dialog showing changes, compatible data and change sets left behind](/docs/screens/model-workspace-apply-dialog.png)

*Above: applying Guide draft to Graubünden leaves Default unchanged and names December 2026 timetable
change as remaining on release 1.0.0. The dialog was cancelled.*

![Workspace Apply review with a proposed type move and Preview what happens to the records action](/docs/screens/model-apply-migration.png)

*Above: Apply to Stops tidy-up shows the same move of 12 Stop code records, with zero refused. Preview what happens to the records… opens the migration review. The captured dialog was cancelled.*

## Activate an already installed release

1. Open **Settings**, **Model**, choose the model, then **Releases** and the intended version.
2. Check its identity, workspace use and installation details. Use **Create draft from release**
   if its definitions need changing; the release itself is immutable.
3. Choose **Activate in a workspace…**, select the target and read its compatibility result and
   change sets left behind. A release can be activated only when that workspace's existing data fits.
4. Confirm **Activate** with the displayed version and workspace when ready. If activation is
   refused, correct the named issue and recheck. A stale-state refusal needs a refreshed workspace
   state and another review, not repeated confirmation of the old result.

![Installed release page with workspace use and activation and draft actions](/docs/screens/model-release-detail.png)

*Above: release 1.0.0 of the Graubünden model is immutable and already run by Graubünden.*

![Activation dialog checking one selected workspace and listing other workspaces unchanged](/docs/screens/model-release-activate-dialog.png)

*Above: the selected target is Default, which runs RDM Starter Model; Graubünden stays unchanged.
The captured activation was cancelled.*

After success, open the target workspace and check its applications and a changed type's page.
Other workspaces keep their models. If an already open page says its model changed, reload it
before editing records. Review any left-behind change sets through the
[change-set process](/docs/use/change-sets/) before their next publication.

## Read the activation result

| Result | Next action |
| --- | --- |
| Compatible with the workspace's data | Review the named workspace and confirm activation when ready. |
