| A migration is needed | From installation, choose **Install … and preview the migration…**; from Apply, **Preview what happens to the records…**. Review proposed destinations, created items, conversions, removals and items to fix before confirming the migration. |
| A different model | Review this destination carefully; compatibility is checked when activation is attempted. |
| A consumer API needs a higher contract version | Coordinate the contract change and raise its version in a draft before rechecking. |
| Could not be checked | Read the failure, correct its cause and check again; it is not a successful compatibility result. |

The install dialog says **Comparing with the base release** where the draft has one. That
comparison can differ from the target workspace's current release; read the separate data and
consumer checks too. Cancelling a migration preview leaves workspace data unchanged; a release
installed to start that preview remains installed. After a stale preview, review a fresh
one instead of confirming the old counts.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/edit-:
---
title: Edit a record page
description: Add panels and arrange fields, columns and regions on a draft record page.
reader: model-admin
---

Arrange a type's record page so people can read its fields and related records together.
You need **Model authoring** and an open draft. These changes affect the draft; people see
them after its release is activated in their workspace.

See [Record pages and tables](/docs/model/record-pages-and-tables/) for the page a type gets
before you arrange it.

## Open the layout

1. In the model editor, select the type in its application and choose **Preview**.
2. Choose **Edit layout**, then **Record page**. The layout shows **Main** and **Side**
   regions with frames for panels and fields.
3. If the type has no declared page, choose **Declare its page** first. This saves the
   generated page as a draft step so you can edit it. It includes **Details**, hierarchy
   where applicable, contained records and a panel for each relationship.

![Record layout with panels and field frames in Main and Side](/docs/screens/model-layout-record.png)

If the draft has errors, use **Show issues** and correct them before opening the layout.
For help choosing a workspace and record, follow [Preview a type](/docs/guide/model/preview-a-type/).

## Add a panel

1. At the foot of **Main**, choose **Add panel…**, beside **New field group**.
2. In **Add panel**, choose **What the panel shows**:
   - **Related records** lists the records reached through one relationship. It is offered
     when this type has relationships other than containment.
   - **Contained records** lists records inside the open record. It is offered only when
     the type contains types that this application lists. Select at least one **Contained types** choice.
   - **Fields** creates a group of this type's fields. Select **Fields**; chosen fields move
     from their current groups into the new one.
3. For **Related records**, select **Relationship**. The names read from this type's side
   of the relationship, including relationships pointing towards it. **(on the page)** means
   an existing panel already lists that relationship; it does not prevent another panel.
   Read the **Columns:** line beneath the choice to see the columns the new panel gets.
4. Choose **Region**: **Main** or **Side**. Review **Title**. For related or contained records,
   it starts from your choice and you can change it. For a field group, enter a title.
5. Choose **Add panel**. The panel appears in the chosen region as one draft step. Use **Undo**
   if it was not what you wanted. Adding the panel does not create or change records.

![Add panel with a relationship chosen, its proposed columns, region and title](/docs/screens/model-add-panel-relationship.png)

Above: a Stop page in the guide's Graubünden model, with **Is represented by system code**
chosen. The proposed columns include **Name**, **System**, **External code** and **Description**.

An existing page keeps its arrangement. To give an older page separate panels for its
relationships, add each one here rather than expecting **Declare its page** to replace it.

## Choose a panel's columns and sort

1. Open the menu of a related-record, contained-record or table panel and choose **Columns…**.
2. Select **Name** and the fields you need. Under **Where it sits**, select a containing type
   to show the containing record's name. This can be an ancestor further up the hierarchy,
   not just the immediate parent. **Type** is also offered when the panel lists several types.
3. Choose **Apply** and inspect the column frames. Keep at least one column.
4. On a related-record panel whose menu offers **Sort…**, choose it, select **Sorted by**
   and choose **Save**. The choices come from the panel's allowed sort fields.

![Panel Columns dialog with containing types under Where it sits](/docs/screens/model-panel-columns-where-it-sits.png)

Above: the **Has name translation** panel on a Stop page offers **Language** under
**Where it sits**. It shows each translation's language name. To show a field of that
language, such as **Language code**, use a
[table's related-field columns](/docs/guide/model/choose-table-columns-filters-and-sort/) instead.
Fields stored on the relationship itself cannot be columns.

## Arrange panels and fields

1. Open a panel's menu. **Move up**, **Move down** and **Move to Main** or **Move to Side**
   change its position. A grip can also drag it within a region or into the other region.
   On a phone, or with a keyboard, use the menu.
2. Choose **Rename…** to change **Title**. **Hide** keeps a panel in the layout but hides it
   from the record page; **Show** restores it. **Remove from page** takes it off the page,
   with **Undo** available afterwards. Stored records and values remain.
3. For a field, use **Move up**, **Move down** or **Move to …** to place it in a field group.
   **Remove from panel** takes it off that group. Dragging a field onto another group or
   field is another way to move it.
4. To make a field group in **Main**, choose **New field group**, give it **Title** and select
   **Fields**. Choose **Apply** in the popover. Selected fields move into it from their current positions.
   To add an omitted field to an existing group, use its **Add fields…** menu and select
   from **Fields not on the page**. This does not create a new field definition.

![Panel menu with ordering, visibility and field actions](/docs/screens/model-layout-panel-menu.png)

## Check the result

Return to preview and inspect a populated record and an empty record. Check the page with
records that have different relationships or parents. Review **Issues** before
[installing and activating the release](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/).
If an action shows **Not applied**, it has changed nothing: read the reason, correct the
choice and try again.

## Set the header and breadcrumbs

1. In **Record page**, choose **Header and breadcrumbs…**.
2. Select **Title of the record** from Name or an attached field. **Line under the title**
   adds a second field; choose **None** to remove it.
3. Choose **Show the type’s name in the header** as needed. **Breadcrumbs name the type**
   also shows the type in the header; **Breadcrumbs name the records above it** shows parents
   in the line above the title. That line starts with the list link when opened from a list,
   without an application entry. These choices do not change a record’s parent or name.
4. Choose **Save** and inspect the preview with a record that has parents. Undo restores the saved step.

![Record page Header and breadcrumbs dialog](/docs/screens/model-header-breadcrumbs.png)

## Change what a panel lists

1. Open the panel’s menu and choose **Settings…**. Fields groups have no extra settings.
2. For related records, select **Relationships listed** and **Listed from**. Choose **This
   record to the others**, **The others to this record**, or **Both ways**. Tick **Show which
   relationship joins each record** when one panel combines several meanings.
3. Select **Fields a reader can sort by** if people need a sort menu. Leaving these unchecked
   lists related records by name. A default sort no longer in the list moves to the first
   remaining choice, or is cleared when the list is empty.
4. For hierarchy, set **Show the parent** and **Show the records above the parent**. For a
   contained-record or table panel, choose **Rows on a page**. A table also offers **List
   only the records under this one**; clear it only when the page should show that type’s
   records beyond the open record’s direct children.
5. Choose **Save** and review columns, sorting and Issues. Changing settings does not rewrite stored
   connections. A panel with no matching records is empty; check its direction and selection
   before concluding that data is missing.

![Related-record panel Settings with relationship selection, direction and sort fields](/docs/screens/model-panel-settings.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/revie:
---
title: Review the assistant's workbook design
description: Check the proposed types, source coverage and record changes before accepting an assistant's load.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this task when a workbook needs a new or extended model. The assistant proposes how its
sheets, columns and records fit the workspace. You review that design before anything is
installed or loaded. For the manual editor route, use
[Start a draft from a workbook](/docs/guide/model/start-a-draft-from-a-workbook/).

You need **Use AI proposals**, **Bulk and import** and **Work in change sets** in the workspace.
Model changes also need **Model authoring**, **Model release** in the workspace and permission
to install model releases at instance level. The assistant and job creation must be enabled.

The whole file, your words and the workspace's model go to Claude Code. It reads workspace
records as needed. Assistant turns may incur charges; tasks and files normally remain for
90 days, and session files and transcripts remain while the task can continue. See
[About AI in refiroo](/docs/run/ai/) for the full account of permissions, costs, retention
and data leaving the instance.

## Give the file and its purpose

1. Open the intended workspace and its **⋯** menu beside the workspace selector. Choose
   **Import**. With the assistant enabled, **Load a workbook** opens first.
2. Choose an XLSX or CSV **Workbook**, or drop it onto the field. Check **Into** names the intended workspace.
3. In **Tell the assistant about this file (optional)**, explain whether this updates existing
   records or adds something new. Say which column identifies a record and how new types
   should relate to the existing ones, if you know. A stable key matters more than a row number.
   A list of records not yet held needs a key too; otherwise a later load can create them again.
4. Read what is sent, then choose **Read the workbook**. **Import without the assistant…**
   uses the manual import instead. **Cancel** sends nothing.
5. Wait on the task page. The bar below the top bar shows the current stage and next action.
   It follows you into the model editor and change set. **Stop** ends the current turn;
   it does not discard the task.

*Example: a file of stop names in several languages may extend the existing stop model with
related name records. Check that those names attach to the existing stops and that each
language column is accounted for.*

## Review the model before accepting

1. Read **The assistant’s proposal**, including each type's fields, relationships and record
   counts. The assistant can reuse the current model, extend it or propose a new one. Do not
   assume each sheet should become a separate type.
2. Read **Checks**, especially **Needs attention**, and **What the load does**. Compare new
   records with existing records matched: unexpected new records can mean an intended update
   did not find its records. Inspect **One name twice in one type** if shown; the finding says
   whether those records sit at the top level or under parents. Decide whether they represent
   different things or an unwanted duplicate. Checks and examples do not establish that the
   design means what you intended.
3. Read **Columns left out** and the questions with their assumed answers. Check every
   intentional omission. Conflicting workbook names or values are not automatically errors
   to normalise: explain whether they are intended.
4. Open **Show the model change**. Choose **Open in the model editor** to inspect the draft's
   types, fields and relationships, or edit them. The draft belongs to this task; a second task
   cannot write it while this task holds it. **Close** in the editor returns to the task.
   **No type, attribute or relationship changes** means the summary has no structural changes
   to list; the draft can still change views or layout. Open it in the editor to review those.
   For a task without a workbook or a model draft, the proposal says **No change to the model.**
   and has no model editor button.
5. Answer the questions or use **Tell the assistant what to change** under **Correct the model**.
   The same session revises the design and rereads your editor changes. Check the new proposal
   and its record and relationship counts again.

![Workbook proposal with type counts and an expanded table of model changes](/docs/screens/model-assistant-workbook-proposal.png)

*Above: the reference workbook proposal adds types and relationships, adds Step-free access
and Remark to Stop, and makes FSO number and System key optional. The expanded table shows
these changes.*

The assistant reads the workbook, the model and workspace records, then turns the file into
proposed records and relationships. It changes the draft where needed and asks the engine to
check every proposed record and relationship without saving them. It writes no import profile.
Review the resulting fields and counts: one source row need not mean one output record.
This does not edit your original workbook.

## Check the records and accept

1. Review **What the load does**: new records, existing records matched, new relationships,
   refused items and rows read. New relationships include the links of new records to their
   parents; the summary gives their count separately too. In the type table, compare **New**, **Matched**, **Changed**,
   **Refused** and **Linked to**. Open a type's row with a click, Enter or Space to see example
   records, their values, links and the cells they come from. These are examples, not every record.
2. Expand **Where each part of the file goes** to inspect the sheet and cell ranges that supply
   records or relationships. Compare them with the file and **Columns left out**. Read the
   reasons and source cells of refused items and tell the assistant what to correct.
3. Check how the assistant matched existing records. Explain which fields identify the same
   record when names repeat. Questions ask about choices the file and your instructions leave
   open; they do not ask you to design a loading mechanism.
4. If the draft changed after the check, the card warns you. Accepting checks every record and
   relationship again first. If any is refused, nothing is installed or loaded. Ask for a new
   proposal before accepting if your edit changes the result you want to review.
5. Choose **Accept and load to change set** when the design and proposed records are right. The engine installs
   a release if the model changed and loads exactly the checked records and relationships into
   a new change set as one batch, without another assistant turn. It activates and publishes
   nothing. If the batch refuses any item because the data changed, none of the batch is loaded
   and its change set is discarded. A release already installed can remain installed.
   Whole-type or partial reshapes follow [the model-move steps](/docs/guide/model/change-a-model-with-the-assistant/).
6. On the loaded page, compare the actual counts with the checked result. Both include parent
   links in the relationship total. Choose **Review the change set**, inspect its changes and
   validate. Follow the workspace’s approval rules. If the workspace runs a different model
   version, review offers **Move** followed by the workspace name, the proposed version and
   **and publish…**. Use it to preview the migration, then choose **Migrate and publish** to
   switch the workspace’s model and publish together. You need model-release and publication
   permission and any required approval. A separate activation first is not required; follow
   [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) for the preview and blockers.
   The assistant does not activate, approve or publish.

If the engine cannot apply the proposal, its reason appears on the page. Tell the assistant
what to change rather than accepting an unusable design. A failed turn can **Try again as it was**;
a stopped one can **Go on as it was**. If a required permission is lost, the page names what
is needed and offers a link to copy for the person who can load.

## Load another file, or correct a load

An assistant load saves no import profile. Send the next file of the same layout to the
assistant again, explaining how it should match the records already held.

A separately saved import profile can still let the engine recognise a layout before starting
a session. Its load confirmation can install and activate a changed model before importing;
review that confirmation even though this path makes no assistant call. If the saved layout
no longer fits, **Read it with the assistant** starts its reading. Before loading a saved
layout, **Back to the proposal** and the words box let you reconsider it.

![Loaded task with record counts, change-set review and correction actions](/docs/screens/model-assistant-workbook-loaded.png)

*Above: the reference workbook task has prepared records in a change set. Live data is
unchanged until publication.*

For a wrong load that is not published, enter a correction and choose **Discard and load again**.
Confirm only after reading that this removes the entire change set, including manual edits
in it. The assistant then revises the proposal and checks the records again. Review it and
choose **Accept and load to change set** before reviewing the replacement change set. **Discard the change
set** ends the task instead. A stopped load discards the change
set it was making and returns to the accepted proposal. Once published, the task offers new
work; it cannot discard that publication through this correction flow.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/split:
---
title: Split, merge and move types
description: Reshape draft types and their containment without confusing definitions with records.
reader: model-admin
---

Use these actions to reshape definitions in a draft. You need **Model authoring**. They do not
move live records merely by saving. Read [Types, attributes and relations](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/).

## Split a type

1. Select the type and choose **Split…** from its menu. It needs attributes to split.
2. Enter **New type’s name** and, where needed, **Plural name**. Choose **Attributes that move
   to it**. The selected attachments belong to the new type after the split.
3. Enter **Relation name** from the original type, **Reverse name** and **Cardinality** for the
   connection between them. Choose **Add type** and inspect both types, their relationship and layouts.
4. If stored data uses the released type, **History** marks the step **Needs a migration**.
   Installing proposes related records holding the moved values. In the preview, open **Created**:
   a source record with no moved value gets no new record; with **Many to one**, records holding
   identical moved values share one new record. Its name comes from the first moved value,
   or the source record's name if that value supplies no name.

![Split dialog with moved attributes and the connecting relationship](/docs/screens/model-type-split-dialog.png)

## Merge definitions

1. Select the type to absorb and choose **Merge into…**.
2. Choose **Into** carefully. Its attributes, relations and layout join the chosen type.
3. Choose **Save** in the popover and inspect the combined type and **Issues**. Use **Undo** if the result is unwanted.
4. When stored data uses the released type, review its **Needs a migration** mark in **History**.
   Installing proposes that its records become the receiving type, keeping their identities
   and history. Check the proposed destination and all outcomes in the migration preview.

![Merge dialog choosing the receiving type](/docs/screens/model-type-merge-dialog.png)

## Move a type

1. Choose **Move to…**. In **Find a target**, type a name, move with Up/Down and select with
   Enter. A destination can put the type under another type or at an application's top level.
2. For a contained destination, choose **Containment relation**, either a new relation or a
   suitable existing one. When several applications list the type, inspect **Take it out of**.
3. For a released type, read **Needs a migration when installed**. The notice explains where
   the records go: a top-level destination releases them from their old parent; under another
   type, records whose existing parent is not allowed are refused in the migration preview.
4. Confirm and check the type and the types under it. Dragging a type onto a type, an application
   or the space beside the tree opens the same decision. Use **Move to…** on a phone or by keyboard.
5. If stored data uses the type, the step applies with a **Needs a migration** mark in **History**.
   Installing shows the proposed destination application and placement. Review the migration:
   moving to the top level removes the old parent and its containment relationship. The records
   go to the named application even when several applications list the type.

![Move dialog with target search and containment relation](/docs/screens/model-type-move-to-dialog.png)

![Move dialog warning that a released type needs a migration when installed](/docs/screens/model-move-needs-migration.png)

*Above: Stop code is moving from under Stop in Network to the top level of Systems. The notice explains that its records move with it and become top-level records when the migration is confirmed.*

Saving any of these steps changes the draft only. Use **Install … and preview the migration…**
to review the proposed changes before [migrating the workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/).
Resolve items under **Must be fixed** and inspect any **Removed** items before accepting loss.
**Not moved** or **Not applied** explains an edit that could not be saved. **Stop listing in this application** only removes a listing;
**Remove type** removes its definition, views, page and relations at either end. Neither is a
shortcut for moving existing data between models; use [Copy and move](/docs/model/model-mappings/).
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/group:
---
title: Group collections in navigation
description: Group collections and relation matrices in the sidebar, order entries and choose opening views.
reader: model-admin
---

Arrange an application's sidebar so people can find related collections and open a matrix directly.
Work in a draft with **Model authoring**. See
[Applications and views](/docs/model/applications-and-views/) for grouping rules.

## Create and open a group

1. Select the application. Choose **Add a navigation group…** from its menu, or **Navigation
   group…** from **Add** and choose **Application**.
2. Enter **Label** and choose whether it is **Folded when the sidebar opens**. Choose **Add group** and check
   **Navigation groups** in the application panel. An empty group is allowed.
3. Choose the group's name in that table, or select it in the model pane. Its panel shows the
   application it belongs to, its starting state and entry count. The **Entries** table lists
   **Entry**, **Kind**, **Opens on** and **State**. A new group has no entries yet.

![Application navigation groups with their entries and starting states](/docs/screens/model-application-groups.png)

## Add collections and matrices

1. In the group panel, choose **Add to group…**. The popover lists **Collections** and
   **Relation matrices** separately. Entries already in this group are left out.
2. Use **Search collections and matrices** to find entries by name. Tick all the entries you
   want to add. Beside each, **Top of the sidebar** means an ungrouped collection;
   **Inside** followed by a type's name means a matrix available through that row collection.
   **In** followed by a group name means the entry is in another group. Ticking it changes
   that note to **Moves from** followed by the old group name.
3. Review those moves, then choose **Apply** in the popover. The same button saves selections made from the application's **Add to a group…** control. The entries appear in
   the group's table. A collection or matrix belongs to at most one group in this application;
   choosing a new group replaces its old placement. This does not move records under a parent.
4. Check the result. Adding several entries at once is one saved step: one **Undo** takes
   the whole addition back.

![Add-to-group dialog with collections and relation matrices selected and their current locations](/docs/screens/model-group-add-entries-dialog.png)

From the application panel, **In no group:** lists ungrouped collections. Its **Add to a group…**
opens the same popover with those collections ticked; choose **Group** and adjust the selection
before adding them.

You can also place one entry at a time. On a type listed in the application, choose
**Move to group…**. Select **Application** if offered, then **Group**.
**No group: the top of the sidebar** leaves the collection ungrouped. For a relation matrix,
find it in the application's **Views** table and choose **Move to group…** from its menu.
Choose a group, or the **No group: inside** option to keep it within its row collection.
Create a group first if the matrix's menu does not offer this action.

A grouped matrix has its own entry in the sidebar and on the group page. It uses the view's
name and a matrix symbol in its row type's colour, and opens the matrix directly. The row
collection stays where it was, and its view tabs still offer the matrix.

## Order entries and choose what opens

1. In **Entries**, drag a row by its grip to a new place, or open its menu and choose **Move up** or
   **Move down**. Collections and matrices share one order. The first entry cannot move up; the last cannot move down.
2. Choose **Move to another group…** to select a different **Group**. This action is available
   when another group exists. **Take out of the group** returns a collection to the top of the
   sidebar; a matrix returns to being available only through its row collection.
3. For a collection with several views, select its **Opens on** cell. Choose the view people
   should see when they open that collection, then **Save**. **Cancel** leaves it unchanged.
   With only one view there is no choice to edit. A matrix entry shows **Itself** and always
   opens that matrix.
4. Check the chosen view's name and kind in **Opens on**. It sets the collection's opening
   view in both the sidebar and the group page; people can still switch to its other views.
   Without a collection choice, refiroo uses the application's default view if it belongs to
   this collection, otherwise its table, otherwise its first view.

![Navigation group panel with a collection, a relation matrix and their opening views](/docs/screens/model-navigation-group-panel.png)

*Above: a group in the Graubünden model contains a collection and the Municipalities by system
relation matrix.*

## Adjust or remove the group

1. Use **Rename…** and **Start unfolded** / **Start folded** in the group panel to change its
   label and initial state. A person's later folding choice is remembered in their browser.
2. Drag a group's row by its grip in the application table, or use the group menu's **Move up** or
   **Move down**, to order groups. The table also lets you edit **Label** directly, and **Starts
   folded** is a box you click to change. **Change key…** is for unreleased keys only.
3. To remove the grouping, choose **Remove group**, read the confirmation and confirm.
   The confirmation says that its collections return to the top of the sidebar and, when the
   group holds relation matrices, that they go back inside their row type's entry; matrices
   remain available through their row collections. The views and records are kept. Check **Issues** and use **Undo** if needed.

![Navigation group menu with ordering and initial-state choices](/docs/screens/model-group-menu.png)

These are model defaults. The active workspace keeps its current navigation until the release
is activated. If an action says **Not applied**, correct the stated problem before retrying.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/turn-:
---
title: Turn an attribute into a list
description: Replace a field definition with a relationship to a reusable list type.
reader: model-admin
---

Use a list type when people should choose maintained records instead of entering a free value.
For example, a stop's operator may be a relationship to operator records. This is a modelling
choice, not a special value type. See [Types, attributes and relations](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/).

1. In a draft, select the type and open **Attributes**. Open the attribute's menu and choose
   **Turn into a list type…**. You need **Model authoring**.
2. Enter **List type’s name** and **Plural name**. Enter **Relation name** from the original
   type and **Reverse name** from the list records back to it.
3. Review **Which records may be chosen**. Leave it unrestricted to offer any list record,
   or add the offered criteria. A new list type initially offers criteria on its name.
4. Choose **Save** and inspect the new type and relationship. Check the original type's fields and
   layouts and resolve **Issues** before previewing or installing.
5. If the released attachment holds values, the step applies and **History** marks it
   **Needs a migration**. Saving the draft does not populate live list records. Use **Undo**
   to reverse an unwanted draft step.
6. When installing, review **Activation needs a migration** and choose **Install … and preview
   the migration…**. The preview includes the proposed list conversion. Open **Created** to
   inspect the list records and relationships it creates: one record per distinct value,
   named by the value, connected to every source record holding it. The values leave the
   source records. Review any loss or items to fix, then
   [confirm the migration](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) when acceptable.

![List conversion dialog with list names and relationship names](/docs/screens/model-attribute-list-type-dialog.png)

![Migration preview with split and list-conversion proposals and the Created outcome selected](/docs/screens/model-migration-created.png)

*Above: the draft splits Code system from Stop code and turns Code kind values into list records. Created lists 28 new records and relationships across both changes; nothing has changed in the workspace yet.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/raise:
---
title: Raise a model language version
description: Review and reopen a workspace whose model uses an older supported conversion path.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this task when a workspace says **Cannot be opened** because its model language is older
than this refiroo version reads. It changes the stored definition format, not the records.
You need permission to install models at the instance level. See
[Model language versions](/docs/model/model-language-versions/).

Before starting, you need an older-language release already stored in this installation,
usually retained through an engine upgrade. New drafts and imports on this version accept
only the current language, **0.10**; importing an older document does not create a release
for this task. The repair affects every workspace sharing the stored release. Arrange a
backup and coordinate with their owners before confirming it.

1. Open the affected workspace and read why it cannot open. A model written by a newer refiroo
   version needs that version; this repair is only offered for an older, raisable definition.
2. Under **Bring it up to date**, choose **Review the change…**. If the page says the model
   cannot be brought up to date automatically, ask the operator or a specialist model author.
3. Wait for the preview, then inspect **Schema language**, **Consumer APIs rewritten**,
   **Workspaces that return** and **Records, change sets, publications: unchanged**.
   Review every named workspace because they share this stored release.
4. Choose **Raise and reopen** only after reviewing that scope, or **Cancel** to leave it.
   This special recovery edits the stored release in place. It is an exception to ordinary
   immutable releases, available before the first stable release.
5. If **The change could not be made** appears, read the diagnostic. An invalid result or one
   equal to another release is refused. **Try again** rereads a failed preview. If the release
   changed after review, inspect the new preview before confirming.
6. After success, reopen the workspace and check its applications. Its records, history, change
   sets and publications stay as they were. This did not migrate or publish its data.

![Model language recovery preview with affected workspaces and unchanged records, change sets and publications](/docs/screens/model-language-raise-review.png)

If no workspace is available, the operator may need the offline procedure in
[Model releases and rollback](/docs/run/model-releases-and-rollback/).
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/add-a:
---
title: Add a relation matrix
description: Choose row, cell and column types and the actions people can use in a matrix.
reader: model-admin
---

Open a draft with **Model authoring**. A matrix needs row records related to cell records that
stand under column records. See [Applications and views](/docs/model/applications-and-views/).

1. Select an application and choose **Add a view…** from its menu. In **Kind of view**, choose **Relation matrix: rows and columns with the related records in the cells**. The form has a preview beside it.
2. Choose **Rows**, then **Each cell shows**. Read the explanation of the relationship offered.
   If a type is missing, check its allowed relationships and the cell type's parent structure.
3. Choose **Columns**. There is one column per record of a type the cell records sit under.
   Choose **Column heading** to identify those column records clearly.
4. Choose and order **Fields in a cell** and **Row columns**. Use the add, remove and up/down
   controls to inspect the intended order. The first text or number cell field is used for the
   cell display; if none is available, it uses the record name.
5. Set **What people can do in a cell** from the offered **Create**, **Edit**, **Link existing**
   and **Unlink** choices. Availability depends on the declared structure. A checked action
   still needs the person's record or relationship permissions at runtime.
6. Enter **Name**, inspect the preview and choose **Add view**. Review **Issues** before installing.
   A preview is a design aid, not proof that every user has permission to perform its actions.
7. For an existing relation matrix, open its row in **Views** and choose **Change…**. Use
   **Rename…** for its label or **Remove relation matrix** to remove the view. Removing the
   view does not delete the data it displayed. **Undo** can restore the draft step.

## Choose the cell actions

For an existing view, select the application, find the matrix in **Views**, open its menu and
choose **Change…**. In **What people can do in a cell**, select any offered combination:

- **Create** makes a record and connects it to the row. The creation form uses the relationship's rules and the groups already holding this view's
  records to suggest where it belongs under the column. It can propose a missing group,
  without a model change; the person checks the proposal or chooses another eligible group.
  See [Where new records go](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#matrix-cells-and-new-records). Create is offered only when **Fields in a cell**
  includes every required field, and creation needs no other required incoming relationship
  beyond the one this cell supplies. Parent containment is handled separately.
- **Edit** allows editing the displayed record fields. It is offered when at least one selected
  cell field is writable.
- **Link existing** connects a record already under the column. It is offered in the editor,
  but each candidate must satisfy the relationship rules when someone uses the matrix.
- **Unlink** removes a connection and keeps the record. It is not offered for a required
  relationship.

Choose **Save**, review **Issues**, then install and activate the release through your usual
[model release process](/docs/model/releases/). Check the actions after changing
row types or cell fields: dependent choices can be reset or removed when they no longer fit.

For a translation matrix, Create and Edit can support one name per language. For a mapping
matrix, Create and Link existing let people choose between a new code and reuse of an existing
code. Reuse creates another relationship to the same record, which keeps its identity for
connected systems after publication. These are model choices, not separate kinds of application.
A filled one-per-cell matrix suppresses Create even when the view enables it; see
[Relation matrices](/docs/use/relation-matrices/#what-you-can-change-from-a-cell).

![Relation matrix choices with ordered cell fields and a preview](/docs/screens/model-view-matrix-dialog.png)

*Example: Municipality rows connect to System code cells, which stand under System columns.*

A **Not applied** notice leaves the attempted change unapplied; read its reason and correct
the structure or choices. Saving this view in a draft does not change the live application.

Adding a matrix also adds any type listings it needs to the application in the same step.
Records retain their owning applications. Removing the matrix can remove listings needed only
by that view; a released listing in use can require migration. Inspect the removal confirmation
and Issues rather than assuming the view is the only affected definition.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/fix-i:
---
title: Fix issues before installing
description: Follow validation messages to their elements and check data compatibility before applying a draft.
reader: model-admin
---

Use this check before installing or applying a draft. **Model authoring** lets you correct it;
release access is needed to activate it. [Issues and dry runs](/docs/model/issues-and-dry-run/)
explains why a valid model, compatible stored data and accepted source rows are separate results.

## Follow and correct model issues

1. Open the draft and read the header's status. Expand **Issues and history**, then choose **Issues**.
   Read each message and its severity.
2. Use an issue's **Go to** link to open the affected type, application or view. Check the named
   setting against what that element actually contains.
3. Correct the cause using the element's controls. For a view referring to an unavailable field,
   remove that field from its selected columns, or attach the intended existing attribute to its
   type if it belongs there. If the last edit was a mistake, use **Undo** instead.
4. Save the correction and wait for validation. Reopen **Issues** and resolve the remaining errors.
   If **Another change came first** appears, read the newer steps, then choose
   **Apply mine again** or **Discard mine** after reviewing the current model.

![Draft validation error with a link to the affected view](/docs/screens/model-issues-error.png)

*Above: Guide draft contains a deliberate unavailable-field reference in the Municipalities view.
The issue points to Network's view rather than requiring the reader to search every type.*

Do not treat saving or closing as a successful check. An invalid draft can be saved, but its
errors still prevent installation. Read warnings too, especially when a workbook mapping is attached.

![Corrected draft showing Valid and no issues](/docs/screens/model-issues-none.png)

*Above: Guide draft's issue is fixed. The Issues tab now says the draft is valid and can be installed.*

## Check the selected workspace

1. Choose **Install and activate…**, or **Apply to this workspace…** in a workspace draft.
   Opening the confirmation performs checks without applying the model.
2. Check the named workspace and the differences from the base release. Read the stored-data
   result. If data does not fit, read the affected records and rules before deciding whether to
   correct data, revise the model or open the offered migration preview.
3. Review **Consumer APIs**. If a contract needs a higher version, coordinate that change and use
   the offered version action before checking again. A model release version increase alone does
   not resolve a consumer contract incompatibility.
4. Read the open change sets left on the current release. Plan how to move or discard them before
   their next publication. Use **Cancel** while further work is needed; the draft stays saved.

For an attached workbook, also wait for the latest **Dry run**, open refused-row figures and
resolve or explicitly account for them. **No issues** does not mean every source row is accepted.
Follow [Load a workbook](/docs/guide/model/start-a-draft-from-a-workbook/) for that check.

Once the intended model is valid and the target is suitable, follow
[Install and activate a release](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/).

Where an issue offers a fix, inspect its meaning before choosing it. **Use as the profile's key**
resolves a profile identity choice; it is not a change to a record's identifier. An issue for a
panel naming a removed field can offer to remove that panel. Recheck after either action. In a
workbook dry run, select each source tab, open refused-row counts and compare the **was** figures
with the previous check. A fix to one source does not establish that the other sources load.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/find-:
---
title: Find your way around the editor
description: Select definitions, open their actions and navigate the editor with the keyboard.
reader: model-admin
---

Open a [model draft](/docs/guide/model/create-a-model-draft/) in the editor. You need
**Model authoring**. See [The model editor](/docs/model/the-model-editor/) for saved steps and states.

1. Read the draft title. Select it to rename the draft. Open **About this draft** to check its
   base release, whether it is a new model, draft version and errors or warnings. The version
   increases with each step; **Close** keeps the saved draft.
2. In **Model**, unfold an application and select a type. Its centre panel shows **Attributes**
   and **Relations**. Selecting the application instead shows **Object types**, **Views** and
   **Navigation groups**. The same type can appear in more than one application.
3. Select **Attribute types** or **Relation types** to inspect reusable definitions. Select
   **Relationship matrix** to see permitted type pairs, with the from end down the rows.
   Use arrow keys in the grid and Enter to select a pair; its panel offers the pair's actions.
4. Use **Add** for **Application…**, **Object type…**, **Attribute type…**, **Relation type…**
   or **Navigation group…**. An empty draft asks you to add an application first.
   The **Consumer APIs** tab has its own add action.
5. Open an element's operations menu to change it. In the model pane, Up/Down and Home/End
   move focus, Enter or Space selects, Right/Left unfolds or folds, and Shift+F10 or the
   context-menu key opens that row's operations. A type an application lists only because one of its
   relation views needs it is shown with a dashed icon, in its group or under **From other
   applications**, and opens on the application that holds its records; types no view uses come last. A disabled action is not applied.
6. Expand **Issues and history** to inspect errors or saved steps. With a workbook, use
   **Issues, history and dry run** and the additional **Source** pane. Resize the pane dividers
   for space. On a phone, use the pane tabs; dragging is unavailable, so use the menus.

![Model editor showing the model pane, selected definition and history drawer](/docs/screens/model-editor-overview.png)

If an edit reports **Not applied**, read the reason before trying again. For a newer saved
version, follow [Work on a draft with others](/docs/guide/model/work-on-a-draft-with-others/).
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/move-:
---
title: Move records to another model
description: Review a proposed mapping, check every selected item and copy or move through change sets.
reader: model-admin
---

Copy or move records into another workspace when its model differs. Arrange **Copy and move**
access in the relevant workspaces and the data and change-set permissions needed for review and
publication. Background jobs and model administration must be enabled. See
[Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/) for matching rules and the difference between copy
and move.

## Open a mapping for the two workspaces

1. Open **Settings**, then **Copy and move**. Review **Mappings** and **Recent copies and moves**
   to avoid starting the same work twice.
2. Choose **New copy or move…**. Select **From workspace** and **To workspace**. Check the model
   and release displayed beside each name; source and target must be different workspaces.
3. Under **Mapping**, choose a saved mapping for these models or **A new mapping, proposed**.
   For a new mapping, fill **Name of the new mapping** so it can be recognised later.
4. Choose **Open the editor**. Wait for the proposal and dry run. This prepares the mapping and
   check; it does not copy records. **Cancel** leaves the dialog without starting the flow.

![Copy and move page with saved mappings and recent operations](/docs/screens/model-moves-list.png)

*Above: Guide mapping connects the Graubünden model to RDM Starter Model. Recent entries are dry
runs not started, not completed copies.*

![New copy or move dialog with source, target and mapping choices](/docs/screens/model-moves-new-dialog.png)

*Above: Graubünden is the source and Default the target. Guide mapping is selected, with A new
mapping, proposed offered below. The captured dialog was cancelled.*

## Complete the mapping

1. Review source types on the left and their mapped states. Select each mapping row and read
   **Why this step** and its evidence before accepting a suggestion; choose an alternative
   or change the row if the proposal does not represent your intended meaning.
2. Check the target type, every field and every relationship. **Not carried (reported)** leaves
   a value out. Choose that only when its loss is intended. Map a required target field or supply
   a meaningful default where the editor offers it.
3. Check **Parent** for contained records. A mapped child still needs a permitted parent in the
   target; carrying it under an incompatible parent causes a refusal.
4. Check **Records already in the target**. Decide whether to find only records moved before or
   also match by an offered unique field. Review existing target values before allowing updates.
5. Use **Undo** or **Redo** for mistakes. Wait for the refreshed dry run after a saved change.
   If saving is refused because the mapping changed elsewhere, reload it and review those changes.

![Proposed mapping and dry run with source and target types](/docs/screens/model-mapping-proposed.png)

*Above: the proposed Operators-to-Domains and Modes-to-Codelists choices need human review.
The dry run exposes substantial omissions; this is not a loss-free copy.*

## Choose the records and inspect the dry run

1. Choose **Copy** to keep source records, or **Move** to prepare their later deletion too.
2. Beside **What to copy** or **What to move**, choose **Change…**. Select **Every mapped type**,
   **The whole workspace**, **Chosen types**, or **One record and everything under it**. For chosen
   types, select the types and filters. For a subtree, choose its type and starting record.
3. Choose **Dry run this selection** and wait for the result. Check the source, target, mapping
   version and selection shown above the figures.
4. Review **Create**, **Update**, records that cannot go, and relationships carried or dropped.
   Open **What cannot be copied** or **What cannot move** to see reasons, counts and every affected
   item. Use an item's **Open the mapping** link to correct its choice, then check again.
5. Account for lost values too. A record may be copied without an unmapped value. Do not confirm
   merely because some records can go; resolve or deliberately accept each omission in scope.

![What to copy dialog with mapped types, whole workspace, chosen types and subtree choices](/docs/screens/model-mapping-selection-dialog.png)

*Above: Every mapped type is selected for Guide mapping. The captured selection dialog was cancelled.*

![Dry run reasons and affected items with links back to the mapping](/docs/screens/model-mapping-dry-run.png)

*Above: the example predicts 79 creates and lists missing values, invalid parents and dropped
relationships. Nothing has changed in either workspace.*

## Start and review the change sets

1. Choose **Start the copy…** or **Start the move…**. Read the confirmation's creates, updates,
   relationships and omissions, then fill **Name of the change set of workspace** for the target.
2. Confirm **Start the copy** or **Start the move**. Wait for the operation's result and inspect its
   actual counts and refusals. A changed mapping or model can prevent the start; refresh and review
   a new dry run before retrying. Nothing eligible to copy or move also prevents confirmation.
3. Open the target's produced change set. Review records, values and relationships, correct any
   remaining problems, validate, and publish through the normal approval process. Starting the
   copy alone has not made its records live.
4. For **Move**, also open the source deletion change set. Publish the target copy first, then
   review and publish the source deletions separately. Check any records kept because they changed
   since the dry run or because records staying behind depend on them. Do not assume every selected
   source record was deleted.

Follow [Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) for
review, validation and publication. Publishing either change set needs its own permissions and
any approvals required in that workspace.

Use **Mapping**, **Source**, **Target** and **Not copied** or **Not moved** to inspect the editor's
parts. Read the selected row's **Why this step**; evidence and alternatives explain a proposal,
without a numeric score. If a warning says the mapping names other releases, choose
**Use the releases the workspaces run**, review its rows and obtain a new dry run. Read-only
notices mean the deployment does not allow this flow; ask the operator before attempting a start.

Follow the started job to its result, inspect actual counts and any refusals, and open its
produced change sets. A finished job is not proof that every source item was copied or removed.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/raise:
---
title: Raise a contract version
description: Release a changed consumer contract while keeping the previous version available.
reader: model-admin
---

Raise a consumer contract version when consuming systems must read a changed shape or operation.
You need **Model authoring** to edit and **Model release** in the destination workspace to
activate. Read [Consumer APIs](/docs/model/consumer-apis/#keep-an-earlier-version-available)
for the rules. Agree the change and changeover with the consuming teams first.

## Keep the previous version available

1. Open a draft based on the release whose contract you are changing. Select **Consumer APIs**,
   then the API and **Types and related**. Check **Contract version**. If the draft says
   **Checked once the draft is valid**, fix its issues before relying on the contract check.
2. Review your changes to types, fields, related blocks, operations, filters and events.
   **Needs contract version …** lists what existing consumers would notice. Choose
   **Raise to version …**, or open the API menu and choose **Raise contract version to …**.
   Alternatively, edit **Contract version** in **Settings**, enter a higher whole number
   and choose **Save**. The menu advances it by one.
3. Inspect **Earlier versions**. When the draft’s base release served the previous version,
   the editor retains that release’s definition, even if you already made breaking edits
   in this draft. Your edits belong to the new current version. A new API, or a version
   never served by the base release, has no previous definition to retain. Check the row
   rather than assuming every increase adds one.
4. Check the retained **Version** and **Superseded** day. If you have agreed an end date,
   edit **Sunset day**, enter a calendar date in year-month-day form and **Save**. Clear it
   to withdraw the announcement. The date does not stop service automatically.
5. Review **Issues**, **Schema**, **Message example** and the generated operation document.
   [Share the documents](/docs/guide/model/see-a-consumer-apis-documents/) with consuming teams.
   Every earlier version must still have the types, fields and relationships it reads;
   raising the number cannot repair missing sources.
6. Open **Install and activate…** or **Apply to this workspace…**. Review **Consumer APIs**
   for the destination as well as the comparison against the draft’s base. Install and
   activate only when the retained contracts still fit that workspace’s active contract.

![Earlier versions table showing a new current version and its retained predecessor](/docs/screens/model-consumer-earlier-versions.png)

After activation, the new version is available and the retained version keeps reading current
data in its original shape. It is not an old data snapshot. Existing webhooks bound to the
retained version keep delivering in that version’s shape. Installing alone changes no workspace.
Other workspaces keep their own active releases.

## Raise without retaining the previous version

Use this only when consumers are ready to lose the version being replaced. In
**Needs contract version …**, **Raise and stop serving version …** raises the version without
keeping its predecessor. The API menu offers **Raise to … and stop serving …** with a
confirmation. This does not remove other versions already in **Earlier versions**.

Review the draft’s History; **Undo** restores the saved raise step before activation.
After activation, consumers of a version no longer served lose their reads, and its webhooks
need the receiver owner’s review before resuming on the current version. For a separate,
announced removal later, follow
[Stop serving an earlier contract version](/docs/guide/model/stop-serving-an-earlier-contract-version/).

## If the release is refused

- **A consumer API needs a higher contract version**: read the named contract and differences.
  Raise the changed current contract or undo the breaking change, then check again.
- **a kept version is served as it was: restore it, or stop serving it**: the retained
  version’s output would change. Restore that definition and its sources, or agree to
  stop serving it. Raising the current version again does not fix this finding.
- An issue naming an earlier version and a missing type, field or relationship needs that
  source restored or that version removed. A lower version, duplicate retained number,
  retained number at or above the current version, or invalid date must be corrected.

A model administrator chooses the notice period with the consuming teams. refiroo does not
schedule removal or impose its own software compatibility period on your consumer contracts.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/compa:
---
title: Compare releases
description: Choose a baseline and read the definitions added, changed or removed in an installed release.
reader: model-admin
---

Open **Settings › Model**, select a model, **Releases**, then the release to inspect.
See [Releases](/docs/model/releases/) for immutable definitions and permissions.

1. In **Release history**, find **Changes in this release**. Read **Before** and **After**;
   After is the open release. The suggested predecessor comes from activation history or the
   earlier installed release. It is not necessarily the workspace you currently have open.
2. Use **Compare with** to choose another baseline. A comparison may cross model families,
   so check both names and versions rather than assuming they share a lineage.
3. Read the changes table's **Kind**, **Path**, **Before** and **After**. These describe model
   definitions, not a history of record edits. Inspect removals as well as additions.
4. **No semantic changes** means the two documents define the same model. **No earlier release**
   means no predecessor is available; select another baseline if offered.
5. If **Comparison unavailable** names an unsupported model language, choose another release.
   Its metadata and **Export JSON** remain available for specialist inspection. A loading or
   failed comparison is not an empty comparison.

![Release history with baseline selector and semantic before and after changes](/docs/screens/model-release-compare.png)

The separate **Activation check** reads each workspace's data. A small or empty comparison alone
does not establish that activation in a chosen workspace is safe.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/check:
---
title: Check a workbook with a dry run
description: Read each source’s predicted changes and inspect refused rows before loading.
reader: model-admin
---

A dry run reads every mapped row without writing records. Model validity and row acceptance
are separate checks. Open a workbook draft with **Model authoring** and see
[Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/#issues-and-the-dry-run-answer-different-questions)
and [Issues and dry runs](/docs/model/issues-and-dry-run/) for the different results.

1. Expand **Issues, history and dry run**. Resolve blocking **Issues** in the model or profile
   first, then choose **Dry run**.
2. Check the draft version and comparison workspace. Wait for **Checking…** to finish.
   **Checked** is a completed check; **Failed** or **Stopped** is not. Read any failure and
   correct its cause before retrying or making the next mapping change.
3. Open each source tab. Read records created or updated, values, relationships, related
   records created and refused rows. These are different units, so do not add them as a row total.
4. Select a figure to inspect the rows behind it. Open the refused-row figure to read sheet,
   row number and reason. Correct an unresolved reference, wrong type or missing required value
   at its source or in the mapping. A valid draft can still refuse source rows.
5. After editing, wait for the new check. **was** compares with the previous result; it is not
   a count from an actual import. Use the result for the current draft version.
6. Account for every source and any remaining refusal before
   [loading into a change set](/docs/guide/model/load-a-workbook-into-a-change-set/).

![Dry run showing per-source predicted records, values and relationships](/docs/screens/use-wb-dry-run.png)

![Refused workbook rows with their sheet positions and reasons](/docs/screens/use-wb-dry-refused.png)

The eventual load can meet newer records or different workspace data. Review its actual result
and change set too; a dry run is neither an import nor a publication.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/propo: --- title: Propose again with a newer workbook description: Replace the draft source and review renewed proposals without losing manual decisions. reader: model-admin --- Use a saved workbook draft when a corrected file needs the same modelling work. You need **Model authoring**. See [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/) for proposal ownership. 1. Open the draft and read **History** before replacing its source. In **More actions**, choose **Upload a newer workbook…**. A draft without a source offers **Add a workbook…** instead. 2. Choose **Workbook**, an XLSX workbook or CSV file, or drop it onto the field. Review **Compare with the records of**. Upload and wait for the new source to be profiled. If it fails, read the file error and retry with a corrected file; do not rely on the previous source's counts. 3. Inspect every sheet, changed header and list range. Existing reading instructions may no longer fit the columns. Check your row keys and reference matching before accepting proposals. 4. Choose **Propose again…**. Review **A new application**, **A new model**, **Additions to the model** or **Nothing: I will map it by hand**, with **Application name** where offered. Apply the intended choice. **Proposing from the workbook** pauses editing until it finishes. 5. Only elements still as proposed follow the new proposal. Manual edits remain yours and undone proposals stay undone. Review conflicting column choices in **Issues**, rather than assuming the engine replaced your decision. 6. Inspect **Proposed because**, **Evidence** and **History**, then obtain a [new dry run](/docs/guide/model/check-a-workbook-with-a-dry-run/) before loading. ![Draft menu with upload-newer-workbook and propose-again actions](/docs/screens/use-wb-draft-menu.png) For routine uploads through an already installed profile, use **Settings › Import profiles**, **Upload the next version…** and its comparison instead. Review changed or missing columns, unknown values and missing-record choices before accepting the next file. ## Get the example update If you started with the [example workbook](/docs/guide/model/start-a-draft-from-a-workbook/#get-the-example-workbook), download Haltestellen_Busbetrieb_Nord_next.xlsx and select it in **Workbook** in step 2. This fictional update renames **UIC-Nr** to **UIC number** on **Haltestellen** and adds **Capture note**, filled with **Preview only** on the first five data rows. The other two sheets are unchanged. Use it to practise reviewing a renamed column and an extra column. It does not correct the workbook's unresolved references. Check the key and mappings again, decide whether to ignore **Capture note**, and run a new dry run before loading anything.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/see-a:
---
title: See a consumer API’s documents
description: Review the output shape, example and operations, then hand over the active contract.
reader: model-admin
---

Review the generated documents before asking another team to build a connection. The
schema describes the business object's fields; the message example illustrates that shape;
the OpenAPI document describes the offered requests and their responses. Together they
show what your consumer declaration produces. See
[Consumer APIs in the model](/docs/model/consumer-apis/) for how each choice affects the output.

You need access to the model draft to inspect its documents. Editing needs **Model authoring**.
Viewing a document is separate from giving a consuming client permission to read workspace data.

## Review the draft's output

1. In the model editor, select **Consumer APIs**, then the API. Check the selected API's
   name and **Contract version**. You are reviewing a draft; its changes are not yet live.
2. Open **Schema**. Compare the field names and types with **Fields**. Check required and
   nullable values, the parent and the shape of each related block. A single related
   record is an object or null; a many-valued relationship is an array. Review the whole
   object, because Get by ID, list items and lookup results share this shape.
3. Open **Message example**. It shows one object generated from the declared field types,
   not a record fetched from a workspace. Check that all intended fields and related
   blocks are present. Do not use the placeholder values as evidence that real records
   have those values, or that a lookup finds a particular record.
4. Use **Copy**, **Download schema.json** or **Download example.json** to share the
   selected document. Check the API and contract version before handing it over. After
   any draft edit, inspect the newly generated documents again.

![Generated schema tab for a draft consumer API](/docs/screens/model-consumer-tab-schema.png)

Above: the schema generated for Stops API in the reference model.

**Reference-data example:** the generated schema describes the stop number as an integer that can be empty. Its public name comes from **Output name** and its type from the selected source. It also describes operator as one object or empty and modes as a list. These are the shapes consuming teams rely on; ask the integrator to review the detailed document.

![Generated message example with placeholder values](/docs/screens/model-consumer-tab-example.png)

Above: the reference API's generated example. Its values illustrate types, not live data.

The example uses placeholder values based on field types. They do not prove that a real record exists or has those values. For comparison, the reference stop Chur has stop number 8509000. Use real records as a separate check when agreeing the contract with its consumers.

## Review the operations as well as the object

1. Return to **Schema** and find **Against what consumers read now**. Read any compatibility
   diagnostics. **Compatible: consumers of version … notice nothing they rely on** means
   this check found no incompatible change; it is not a live connection test.
2. Choose **download the draft's OpenAPI** beneath the compatibility information. This
   document includes the operations, parameters and response shapes, rather than just
   the business object. Share it with the integrator alongside the schema and example.
3. Compare the offered operations with **Operations** and their parameter names with
   **Filters**. Check list scope and ordering, lookup rules, events and contract version.
   An object schema alone cannot tell a consumer which list or filter to use.
4. If a change needs a higher contract version, follow
   [Raise a contract version](/docs/guide/model/raise-a-contract-version/), then download
   the documents again. Agree the new address and changeover with consuming teams before
   activation. Raising retains the base release’s previous definition by default. Check
   **Earlier versions** on **Types and related**; a new, unserved API has no previous
   version to retain. The draft tabs describe the current definition. Give the integrator
   each served version’s own document for the earlier contract review.

**Reference-data example:** an integrator checks that Stops API can read a known stop, list stops, look up its identifiers, resolve several inputs and follow the declared changes. The selected fields, related blocks, filters and notifications should match the agreement. Use [Consumer APIs for integrators](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/) for worked requests and answers. Every organisation’s declaration is its own contract; hand over your generated documents.

## Hand over the active contract

1. After the release is installed and activated, open **Settings › Connections › Consumer APIs**.
   This read-only page names the active release. Use **Open the release** to check it is
   the release you intended; it does not provide the draft's Schema and Message example tabs.
2. Find the API's section and version. Use **Base URL** and **OpenAPI document** to copy
   its addresses or open the document. The **Route** / **What it does** table lists its
   operations; a route description opens that operation in the API reference.
3. Give the integrator the active API's base address and operation document, the workspace
   they should read, and the agreed contract version. Ask the security administrator to
   confirm the client has this API's grant in that workspace. A model release does not
   create grants, and a role alone does not open consumer data.

![Active consumer API with release, version, base address, operation document and routes](/docs/screens/model-consumer-active-documents.png)

Earlier contracts are marked deprecated in their generated operation documents, with the
announced sunset day when one is set. Deprecated means still served: the administrator must
explicitly stop the version through a model release. Ask the integrator to check the
[version index and generated documents](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/#earlier-contract-versions)
for each required version. Do not assume an installed older release alone serves that version.

Opening the operation document does not require signing in. Reading data still requires the consuming client’s grant in the intended workspace. Share the addresses using the page’s copy controls; see [Consumer APIs for integrators](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/) for discovery and authentication.

## If a document is unavailable

- **The draft has issues** means the documents cannot be generated. Open **Issues**,
  correct the problem or undo the last step, then return to the document. Raising a
  contract version does not repair an invalid definition.
- A document load error is not a successful review. Read the message, correct the cause
  if it names a draft problem, then retry. If copying is unavailable, select the text
  or download the file instead.
- **The active release declares no consumer API** means the active model has none.
  Use **Open model** to inspect its definitions. A draft API is not live merely because
  its documents can be generated.
- If a live read is refused, check the workspace, API grant and active contract with the
  integrator. The OpenAPI document itself is readable without signing in; opening it
  successfully does not prove that the client can read data.

*Source for the reference examples: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0.*
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/delet:
---
title: Delete a model mapping
description: Remove a reusable copy-and-move mapping while keeping work already produced.
reader: model-admin
---

Delete a saved mapping when you no longer need its conversion choices. You need **Copy and move**
access. This removes its saved editing history and proposals too. Read
[Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/) before deleting one still used by other people.

1. Open **Settings**, **Workspaces and models**, **Copy and move**. Find the mapping under **Mappings**;
   check **From model**, **To model**, **Version** and **Updated**.
2. Choose its **Delete…**. The confirmation asks **Delete the mapping …?** and names both models.
3. Read the warning: copies and moves already made remain; new work needs a new mapping.
   Choose **Cancel** to keep it, or **Delete the mapping** to remove it. There is no Undo here.
4. Wait for the row to disappear. If deletion fails, read the message in the dialog. If another
   editor changed the mapping, refresh and review its new version before deciding again.

![Mappings list and Delete the mapping confirmation](/docs/screens/model-delete-mapping.png)

Deleting a mapping does not publish, undo or discard any change set from an earlier copy or
move. Review those change sets separately. When the Delete action is absent, ask an access
administrator about Copy and move access rather than trying to delete data to remove the mapping.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/add-a:
---
title: Add a record type and fields
description: Define where a type stands, add typed fields and reuse existing attributes.
reader: model-admin
---

Work in an editable draft with **Model authoring** access. If needed,
[create a draft](/docs/guide/model/create-a-model-draft/) first.
[The model editor](/docs/model/the-model-editor/) explains the panes and saved steps.

## Add the type

1. Select the application that should list the type. If the draft is empty, use **Application**
   to add one first, enter its name and choose **Add application**.
2. In the application's **Object types** section, choose **Object type**. In **Add an object type**,
   enter **Name** and, if needed, **Plural name**. Leaving the plural empty uses the name with an s;
   fill it explicitly when that would read incorrectly.
3. Choose **Stands**: **At the top level** for independent records, or **Under** a type for children.
   For children, choose the **Containment relation**. If creating one, fill both **Relation name
   (from the parent)** and **Reverse name (from the child)**. These describe the same connection
   from each end.
4. Choose **Add type**. The type appears in the model pane and application table. A new type gets
   a generated table view and record page. Check where it stands before adding fields. If Add type
   is unavailable, complete the required names and choices; read any refusal before trying again.

![Add an object type dialog showing its parent and containment relation fields](/docs/screens/model-hierarchy-dialog.png)

*Above: Platform is proposed Under Stop in Network. Both containment names still need filling;
the captured dialog was cancelled, so no Platform type was added.*

Containment defines record hierarchy, not merely indentation in the editor. Use **Move to…**
when you need to change placement; moving a released type used by data may need migration.

## Add fields with the right value types

1. Select the type and open **Attributes**. Review the existing rows before creating another field.
2. Choose **New attribute**. Enter **Name** and select **Value type**: for example **Text**,
   **Long text**, **Whole number**, **Decimal number**, **Yes or no**, **Date**, **Date and time**
   or **JSON** for structured values.
   Choose for the value's meaning, not its appearance in a spreadsheet. A code containing leading
   zeroes may need text, even if every character is a digit.
3. Review **Features**. **Searchable** includes the field in record search. **Filterable** allows
   filtering; the view decides which filter controls it shows. **Unique** prevents another record
   in the workspace from holding that attribute value. It is an attribute-wide rule, including
   other types that share the attribute. **Sortable** is still shown, but ordinary non-structured
   fields sort from list headers regardless of that checkbox.
4. Choose **Required** if records of this type must hold a value. Consider existing records:
   making a field mandatory does not fill it for them. Choose **Add attribute** and wait for the row.
5. Check its value type, Required and Unique settings. The new row is marked **New**, its type
   may be **Changed**, and the header's draft version advances. Expand **Issues and history**
   to see the saved step. No live record has acquired a value from adding the definition alone.

![New attribute dialog with name, value type, features and Required](/docs/screens/model-field-dialog.png)

*Above: Step-free access is being added to Stop as Yes or no, with Required unticked.*

![Attributes table showing the new field and the updated draft version](/docs/screens/model-field-added.png)

*Above: Step-free access is New, Stop is Changed and Guide draft has reached version 2.*

## Reuse or adjust a field

Choose **Attach an existing one…** when the same field definition already exists. Review **Shared
with** before changing its definition: renaming a shared attribute affects every type that uses it.
Required and Read-only can differ by type. Read-only prevents ordinary value editing; it does not
supply a value automatically.

Select an editable setting cell, choose the value and use **Save**, or **Cancel** to leave it
unchanged. A refusal on a released field means you must review its existing data and the migration
requirement rather than forcing the edit. The visual editor refuses a released field’s
value-type change when it affects stored values. Ask a specialist model author to prepare
that change in [the JSON view](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-draft-as-json/), save and compare
the draft, and install the target release. Then
[review the workspace migration](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) before converting
data. A draft save alone changes no stored record values.

![Required setting opened in place with Save and Cancel](/docs/screens/model-type-required-edit.png)

*Above: Abbreviation's Required choice is open on Stop. This capture was cancelled without changing it.*

Check [Issues](/docs/guide/model/fix-issues-before-installing/), then
[arrange the layout](/docs/guide/model/arrange-applications-and-views/) before releasing.

A list of allowed records is a relationship to a list type, rather than another field value
type. **Turn into a list type…** on an attribute asks for the relationship's name and which
records may be chosen. Configure its candidate criteria as described in
[Add a relationship](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relationship/#limit-which-records-can-be-chosen).
After adding fields, open the type’s **Settings**. Edit **Display attribute** to choose which
attached field names records in lists, links and titles, or choose **None: records are named
by their name**. Edit **At least one of** to select fields of which one must hold a value;
clear the selection to remove that requirement.

For business validity, attach two **Date** fields, then edit **Effective period**. Select
**Starts on** and **Ends on**, then **Save**. The fields must differ; the end is exclusive and
must be later than the start when both are filled. Empty dates leave that end open. Adding
the rule does not repair existing dates: review compatibility before activation.

![Type Settings with display attribute, effective period and grouped requirement](/docs/screens/model-type-settings.png)

Default values still need a specialist; see [the JSON view](/docs/model/json-view/).
Text-format and length rules are not offered by these controls.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/creat:
---
title: Create a workspace
description: Create an empty dataset and choose its installed model release.
reader: model-admin
---

You need **Workspace administration** and workspace administration enabled on the instance.
See [Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/) for permissions and lifecycle.

1. Open **Settings › Workspaces**. Search for the intended dataset before creating another.
   Choose **New workspace**.
2. Enter **Name** and review **Key**. The suggested key follows the name until you edit it.
   Use lowercase letters and digits separated by single hyphens. The key is permanent and
   identifies this workspace in links; renaming later does not change it.
3. Under **Model**, choose **The default workspace’s model** or **Another installed release**.
   For the latter choose **Installed release** and check the model name and version. The
   picker initially shows each model's newest usable release; reveal older versions if needed.
4. Choose **Add workspace**. The new workspace starts empty. It copies the selected definitions,
