guide/src/content/docs/model/application:
---
title: Applications and views
description: Organise shared types into applications, navigation groups and declared views.
reader: model-admin
---

Applications give people named places to work. A model decides which types and views each
application lists. Any application can use any supported view when its structure fits; an
application's name does not give it special capabilities. You need **Model authoring** to edit
these definitions. Start with [Arrange applications and views](/docs/guide/model/arrange-applications-and-views/).

## Listings and navigation

Select an application to inspect **Object types**, **Views** and **Navigation groups**.
The type table shows where records stand and their attribute and relation counts. **List an
existing type…** adds another listing of a shared definition; it does not copy records.
**Stop listing in this application** removes a listing where allowed. Moving containment or
removing the definition has a different effect; see [Types](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/).

![Application panel with its object types, views and navigation groups](/docs/screens/model-application-panel.png)

Navigation groups have a **Label**, ordered entries (collections and relation matrices) and an **Open**
or **Folded** starting state. A collection, or a relation matrix, can belong to only one group in an
application. A relation matrix placed in a group has an entry of its own, named after the view, and its
row type's entry stays. The matrix symbol uses the row type's colour, and opening the entry
goes directly to the matrix. The matrix also stays among the row collection's view tabs. Without
a group placement, it is available through that collection only. Ungrouped collections appear
at the top. An empty group is valid. Grouping does not change parents, data access or the type's
identity. Follow [Group collections in navigation](/docs/guide/model/group-collections-in-navigation/).

Navigation groups have one level: a group cannot contain another group. Its collection page
lets people search collection and matrix names; it does not show a record count for each entry.
Only collections with a view in this application can be placed in its groups. Group labels
and ordering change navigation without requiring a data migration.

A new navigation group starts open unless **Folded when the sidebar opens** is selected.
A person's later folding choice is remembered in their browser. Within an application, each
group has its own key, and a collection cannot be declared in two groups at once. If validation
names a collection outside the application, add a suitable view there or remove that group entry.

### The group panel

Choose a group in the model pane, or its name in the application's **Navigation groups**
table, to open its panel. It shows the application, starting state and entry count. **Entries**
lists collections and matrices together, in their sidebar order, with **Entry**, **Kind**,
**Opens on** and **State**. The application's group table also lists both kinds in **Entries**.

**Add to group…** lets you search and select several collections and matrices in one dialog.
Their location notes distinguish ungrouped collections, matrices inside a row collection and
entries in another group. Selecting an entry from another group moves it rather than copying
it. Entries already in the destination group are omitted. The whole addition is one history
step, so one **Undo** reverses it. In the application panel, **In no group:** offers
**Add to a group…** with the ungrouped collections already selected.

An entry's row menu offers **Move up**, **Move down**, **Move to another group…** and
**Take out of the group** where applicable. Taking a matrix out removes its separate entry;
it keeps the view in the row collection. A matrix's menu in the application's **Views** table
also offers **Move to group…** when a group exists. The group panel has **Rename…** and
**Start folded** / **Start unfolded**; the group menu orders or removes the group itself.

### A collection's opening view

**Opens on** chooses which of a collection's views opens from its sidebar entry or the group
page. Edit the cell in the group panel when the collection has more than one view, then
**Save**. The choice belongs to that collection in this application; it does not change
another collection's opening view or remove any view tabs. A separate matrix entry always
opens itself and shows **Itself** in this column.

Without a collection choice, refiroo uses the application's **Default view** if it is one of
that collection's views, otherwise its table, otherwise its first view. Choosing that same
fallback in **Opens on** returns the collection to following the default rather than keeping
a separate choice.

## Views

| View | What people use it for |
| --- | --- |
| Table | Read a collection with declared columns, filters and sorting. |
| Tree | Browse and move records through a declared hierarchy. |
| Mapping grid | Connect source and target records through a relationship. |
| Relation matrix | Read or edit related cell records at row and column intersections. |
| Relationships table | Show both ends and the connection’s own attributes in rows or a grid. |

A type created through the editor receives a table view. **Views** lists each view's kind,
what it shows and its state. Use its menu's **Rename…** for a label change.
Choose **Add a view…** in the application’s menu to add a Table, Tree, Mapping grid,
Relation matrix or **Relationships table: each relationship in a row, with its own attributes**. The kind list offers only views for which the model has suitable types and
relationships. Existing trees, mapping grids and relation matrices have **Change…**; ordinary collection table
layouts are arranged from the type’s Preview. A relationships table has its own **Layout…** action. Follow [Add a table, tree or mapping grid](/docs/guide/model/add-a-view/).

Application **Settings** has **Default view**, the view that opens first. Choose an existing
view and Save. A collection's **Opens on** choice takes precedence when opening that collection.
This changes the starting lens, not which types users can access. Icons,
colours and free-form presentation settings still need the [JSON view](/docs/model/json-view/).

## Relationships tables: columns and grouping

A relationships table reads one declared, directed relationship between two types. It shows
the from record, the to record and values carried by their connection. Containment is not
eligible. Both endpoint types are listed in the application when needed; adding the view
creates no records or relationships. Follow [Add a relationships table](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relationships-table/)
for the steps through **Add a view…**.

| Dialog field | What it controls |
| --- | --- |
| Relationships | The permitted pair and relationship, shown with an arrow from one type to the other. Changing this resets the field choices. |
| Columns of the from record | An ordered, non-empty choice of Name or scalar fields attached to the from type. The initial choice is Name and the first suitable unique field, if one exists. |
| Columns of the to record | The same choices for the to type. Their order is the displayed column order; the first labels each grid column group. |
| Attributes of the relationship | Attributes carried by this specific pair, rather than ordinary fields of either record. None is allowed. JSON values can be columns here. |
| Layout | **One row per relationship** lists existing connections. **Grid: each record once, a column group per related record** shows each from record once, with relationship attributes beneath each to-record group. |
| Head the rows by | **Nothing: one list**, **The from record** or **The to record**. Headings collect rows under the selected record. This choice is ignored by the grid. |
| Name | The label people see for this view. |

Endpoint columns cannot repeat and cannot hold JSON. Relationship columns must be declared
on the chosen pair and cannot repeat. The form derives filters from selected fields marked
Filterable, excluding JSON. Sorting includes both record names, selected scalar endpoint fields
and non-JSON relationship attributes. The initial sort is the from record's name and the
reading size is 20. A specialist can adjust filters, sorts and reading size (1–100) in the
[JSON view](/docs/model/json-view/#relationships-table-configuration).
Grid row ordering uses sorts on the from record.

If a saved declaration names a missing type, relationship, undeclared pair or unsuitable field,
**Issues** explains the failed reference. Correct that choice before installing; the
[specialist rules](/docs/model/json-view/#relationships-table-configuration) explain the diagnostic wording.
The view's **Layout…** changes only its presentation. **Remove relationships table** removes
the view and can stop listing types only it needed; read the confirmation. Stored connections
remain. The workspace sees draft changes only after release activation, and the view grants
no data permissions.

## A relation matrix needs a particular structure

Rows must connect to cell records; the cell records stand under column records. The form offers
only suitable choices. **Column heading**, ordered **Fields in a cell** and **Row columns**
determine what is shown. A cell displays its first text or number field, or its record name.
Open the matrix's menu in **Views** and choose **Change…** to set **What people can do in a
cell**. Any offered combination of **Create**, **Edit**, **Link existing** and **Unlink** can
be selected. These actions never grant access by themselves.

Create needs all required cell fields and no other required incoming relationship that the
cell cannot supply, apart from parent containment. Edit needs a writable selected cell field.
Link existing is offered, with individual candidates checked at runtime. Unlink is absent
when the relationship is required. Changing the structure or selected fields can remove
choices that no longer fit.

Create adds a record and its connection to the row. The relationship's candidate rules limit
where it may belong under the column. The form uses those rules first, then the groups already
holding this view's records, to suggest a place. It can also propose a missing group using
other columns as a pattern; accepting it needs no model change. The person reviews the place
and can choose another eligible group. See
[Relation matrices](/docs/use/relation-matrices/#what-you-can-change-from-a-cell). Link existing adds a connection to a shared
record, and Unlink removes only that connection. A filled cell offers Create alongside Link
existing unless a one-per-column uniqueness rule or the row's relationship cardinality limits
it to one. Empty, inactive and history-only cells can still offer Create. See
[Relation matrices](/docs/use/relation-matrices/) for counting states and change-set conflicts.

![Relation matrix form beside its structural preview](/docs/screens/model-matrix-view-dialog.png)

[Add a relation matrix](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relation-matrix/) walks through the form.
Do not confuse it with the editor's **Relationship matrix**, which defines permitted type pairs.
[Record pages and tables](/docs/model/record-pages-and-tables/) covers layout settings. A draft's
navigation and views become active only when its release is applied to the workspace.

## Application settings

The visual **Application…** form includes **Name** and **Description**. In an existing
application, **Settings** lets you change **Default view**. Application and type icons and
existing descriptions need a specialist in the [JSON view](/docs/model/json-view/).
Removing an application is a structural model change; retiring a workspace or release is a
separate administrative task. Check the removal confirmation for types only that application lists.

## Collections and their lenses

Views of the same source type appear as lenses of one collection. A table's source is the type
it lists. A mapping grid's source is the end chosen as its direction; a relation matrix's source
is its row type. A tree belongs to its first declared root type. Adding a second view for one
source type adds a way to work with that collection. Placing a relation matrix in a navigation
group adds a direct entry for that view while keeping the shared row collection.

## Mapping-grid declarations

A mapping grid chooses one permitted relationship and its two endpoint types. In the outgoing
direction its rows are sources choosing targets; in the incoming direction its rows are the
other end and the choices run back towards the source. Choose the direction before choosing
row and target-display fields. Both field lists must be non-empty and contain no repeats.
**Columns of a row** offers the row's own fields and, under **From the parents**, the types
it can stand beneath. Choosing a parent type adds a column headed by that type's name. It
shows the name of the row record's nearest parent of that type, including a parent several
levels above it. This gives context without changing the records being mapped. Row search
looks at source names and the source's displayed attributes; it does not search parent names.
**Columns of the matched record** offers that record's own fields, without parent columns.
Candidate search uses names or searchable attached fields of the type being chosen.

The configured relationship must be an optional association. Containment and required ownership
cannot be used, because replacing a mapping must not change a record's parent or orphan a
dependent. Saving one selected mapping replaces that source's mapping set; it does not change
the underlying relationship's cardinality for other clients.

A grid's model sets a page size of 1–100. The parent scope and coverage choices people select
while using it are temporary filters, not model settings. **Mapped**, **Unmapped** and
**Ambiguous** describe coverage for the configured relationship. **Add a view…** and the view’s **Change…** set its relationship, row end, display columns
and candidate search fields. New grids read 20 rows per page; changing that reading size
still needs the specialist view.

## Relation-matrix rules

A matrix uses one non-containment relationship, in either direction, between row and cell types.
The row, cell and column types must all be listed in the application. Its rows include records
of the row type in the workspace even when another application owns those records. Columns are
records of a type that can contain the cell type, directly or through intervening levels. A cell
record belongs to its nearest ancestor of that column type.

Choose unique, non-empty lists of **Row columns** and **Fields in a cell**. Row columns can include
fields of the row and its ancestor context. The column heading is the column record's name or a
non-JSON field attached to its type. Cell fields must be attached to the cell type. A specialist
can also declare row-search fields, using the name or searchable attached fields, and a page
size of 1–100.

| Cell action | Why it may be unavailable |
| --- | --- |
| Create | Every required cell field needs to be supplied or have a default. The cell must not require an additional owner relationship that the matrix cannot supply. |
| Edit | At least one displayed cell field must be editable. |
| Link existing | The chosen records must fit the binding, its candidate rules and number limits. |
| Unlink | A required owner relationship cannot be removed on its own. |

With no enabled cell actions, the matrix is read only. The form offers suitable actions; the
model's validation also rejects impossible declarations. Enabled actions still require each
person's data permissions. If Create is missing despite a default on a required field, ask a
specialist to inspect the declaration: the visual form checks that required fields are selected.

Uniqueness and conditional activity come from the relationship's rules, not a second rule on
the view. They describe the relationship's target end. An incoming matrix does not apply those
target-end rules to its cells, so it has no inactive or uniqueness-conflict states from them.
To inspect those states, use a suitable outgoing matrix. The matrix shows at most five cell
records as a preview with the full count; open a cell to inspect the rest.

## Tree declarations

A tree starts with parentless records of its root types. Every root type must also be a node
type and allow top-level creation. All shown node types must be listed in the application and
reachable from a root through containment using types the tree shows. A missing intermediate
type prevents that branch from being a valid tree. Recursive containment can show several levels
of the same type.

The main label is the name or a non-JSON field attached to every node type. An optional second
field can show identifying information, type, path, timestamps or another non-JSON field shared
by the node types. Child ordering is declared per type; without an entry, children sort by name.
Descending order is supported. Timestamp ordering falls back to name in change sets and
publications, which do not keep those live-only timestamps. Branches read 1–100 records at a time.

The declaration can offer creating children, renaming, moving and changing a Yes/No availability
field. With no actions it is read only. Create and Move need a containment possibility among
shown types. Rename cannot target a read-only label field. Availability needs an editable Yes/No
field attached to every node type, and that field cannot be declared without the availability
action. These choices enable controls; they do not grant permissions.

At runtime a node's menu offers allowed actions; F2 renames where enabled. Creating a child
offers only shown types the parent can contain. Move lists possible parents with unsuitable
choices disabled and their reasons. Search and opening a record reveal its path by loading
the relevant branches. **Add a view…** and **Change…** offer roots, a label, a second line, one shared child-order
field and an availability field. The editor includes reachable contained types already listed
in the application. New trees read 50 records per branch page. The form does not offer
separate ordering for each type, descending order, page size or the create, rename and move
actions: a specialist maintains those in the JSON view. Applying Change rebuilds the tree’s
action choices from the availability selection, so review previously declared actions afterwards.

guide/src/content/docs/model/model-chang:
---
title: Accounts of model changes
description: Understand the explanation of a proposed activation, its source facts and its limits.
reader: model-admin
---

Before activating a release or applying a workspace's draft, you can ask for a plain-language
account of what the change does. **What this change does** appears in the activation dialog and
in **Apply to this workspace** when an AI provider is available and you hold **Model release**
and **Use AI proposals** in that workspace. Follow
[Explain a model change](/docs/guide/model/explain-a-model-change/) to use it.

The account helps you read the change. It does not approve it, activate anything or remove a
blocking rule. Keep reading the data and consumer API checks alongside it.

## What is sent, charged and kept

Opening the dialog sends nothing to the AI provider. Only **Explain this change** asks it to
write an account. The request contains model changes and record counts, without record names
or values. The account is available at every configured send level. It needs the separate AI
provider; enabling the Claude Code assistant alone does not offer it.

A request can incur provider charges. refiroo records the call and its usage; request and answer
content is not kept in the call log unless the operator enables it. A successful account can
be reused for the same inputs within an hour without another provider call. It is a reading
aid, not part of the release or a permanent history entry. The provider's own retention is
separate. See [About AI in refiroo](/docs/run/ai/) for full access, costs and retention details.

## Facts first, wording second

refiroo supplies the facts that the provider puts into sentences:

- Differences between the model definitions.
- Rules the workspace's records would break, with counts.
- Changes that affect consumer APIs.
- Reasons activation is blocked, including a required migration or a consumer contract version change.
- Record counts for each affected type in the workspace.

The counts cover the whole relevant set of records. A release's differences are against the
workspace's running release. A draft's differences are against its base release; the data check
still uses the selected workspace. Check the workspace and baseline shown in the surrounding
dialog rather than assuming every comparison has the same starting point.

Each AI-written statement has numbers that lead to the facts it cites. **The facts** lists all
facts, initially showing ten; **Show the other …** reveals the rest. For a large change, the
provider receives at most 40 facts of each kind and the true totals. A **+** citation refers to
other facts of a kind. You still have the complete fact list in the dialog.

The note below the statements says the account was written by AI and can be wrong. A citation
shows the source; it does not prove the sentence interprets it correctly. Statements without
a valid source are removed, and the page reports how many were removed. If none remain, the
facts themselves are the account.

## Failure and limits

**The account could not be written** means the provider failed or returned an unusable answer.
The facts remain available because they do not depend on it. **Try again** makes another
attempt. A failure to request the account instead shows **The account could not be asked for**;
read its reason before retrying.

An invalid draft cannot be explained: fix its issues first. If a newer draft version exists,
reload and review it before asking again. A fresh compatibility check clears the old account.
Changed facts, including record counts, need a fresh request; failures and accounts with no
usable statements are not cached for reuse.

The browser account is in English. There is no follow-up conversation, and the account is not
shown in the install dialog or on the migration page. The [migration preview](/docs/model/migrations/)
lists its own conversions, removals and refusals; read those before confirming. An account saying
why activation is blocked is an explanation of the block, not permission to bypass it.
guide/src/content/docs/model/workbook-on:
---
title: Workbook onboarding
description: Understand the source file, model draft, proposals, dry run and loading into a change set.
reader: model-admin
---

Load a workbook when its sheets need to become records, fields and relationships, or extend a
model you already use. refiroo keeps the uploaded source with a model draft, proposes how to read
it, and checks the rows before you apply them. Follow [Start a draft from a workbook](/docs/guide/model/start-a-draft-from-a-workbook/)
for the screen-by-screen task.

This route starts in **Settings**, **Model** and needs model administration. Installing and
activating a release and loading records also need the corresponding permissions in the target
workspace. Ask an access administrator to check your grants if those actions are not available.
It is different from merely opening a file or pasting values into a collection.

## Source file and draft

**New from a workbook** accepts an Excel .xlsx workbook or CSV file. Convert older .xls
files to .xlsx first. Formula cells use their stored results; refiroo does not calculate formulas. You name the draft, choose what
to propose and choose the workspace whose records are used for comparison.

| Propose choice | Starting point |
| --- | --- |
| A new application | Add the proposed types and lists as another application in the model the draft starts from. |
| A new model | Start empty, without the active model's applications, and propose an application there. |
| Additions to the model | Match sheets and columns to existing types and attributes by name and records' values; propose the rest as additions. |
| Nothing: I will map it by hand | Leave the starting model untouched and map the columns yourself. |

![New from a workbook with the four proposal choices and comparison workspace](/docs/screens/use-wb-dialog.png)

*Above: the fictional operator workbook Haltestellen_Busbetrieb_Nord.xlsx is selected. The dialog
was cancelled in this capture; opening it alone creates nothing.*

The draft holds the model you are editing and an **import profile**: the instructions for reading
the file. Uploading does not change the original file on your computer. Splitting a cell's values,
replacing placeholders or ignoring a column changes those reading instructions; it does not repair
or rewrite the source spreadsheet. refiroo records are the result of that mapping, rather than a
copy of the workbook's presentation.

Storing the file starts a background job that reads every sheet and column before mapping
can use it. While it runs, **Source** says **Profiling [file name]: reading every sheet and
column…**. If **The workbook was not profiled** appears, read its reason and upload the file
again from the draft's menu. A check cannot use a file whose analysis has not finished.
Oversized files and formats other than XLSX or CSV are refused; reduce the file or convert it
before uploading again.

Once ready, **Source** shows a tab for each sheet, with its row count. On a sheet arranged as
several lists, select a list to inspect **Cells**, its header, **Under**, **Note** and **Loads**.
The cell preview shows the range with surrounding cells: loaded cells are shaded and the
header is darker. **Adjust list…** changes **Header row** and the range used for loading.
Sheet counts can include headers; check the actual list range and dry run before relying on them.

Select a column and read **Statistics**:

- **Filled** gives filled rows and distinct values. **no value twice: a candidate key** means
  every row is filled with a different value, not that it is the right business identifier.
- **Values read as** shows which value types the cells can be read as; **Most frequent values**
  lists common values and their counts.
- **Placeholders** and **Delimiters**, when present, help identify empty-value spellings and
  cells holding several values. Review them before choosing replacements or splitting.
- **Shares values with** names other workbook columns or fields and names of records in the
  comparison workspace, with shared-value counts and percentages. Shared values suggest a match;
  they do not prove a relationship or identity.

**Upload a newer workbook…** makes the earlier file superseded. The earlier copy remains for
the job retention period measured from replacement, then is deleted. For a saved profile,
replacement applies within the chosen workspace; it does not replace another workspace's file.
A profile's stored file can be used by its uploader and people with **Bulk and import** in
that workspace; files naming no workspace need that access at the instance. Keep the original
outside refiroo if you need a lasting archive.

![The workbook source pane beside the proposed model and selected type](/docs/screens/use-wb-editor.png)

*Above: the fictional operator workbook has three sheets. Haltestellen proposes a type with
fields and relationships; its source contains 51 data rows.*

## Proposed steps are decisions to review

**Proposed** identifies an element that still matches refiroo's suggestion. Select it to read
**Proposed because** and open **Evidence**. A column filled with a different value on every row
can be proposed as a key, but the statistics do not prove it is the identifier your organisation
intends. Review its meaning as well as its uniqueness.

![Evidence showing why a column was proposed as the record key](/docs/screens/use-wb-evidence.png)

*Above: UIC-Nr is filled and distinct on all 51 data rows of the fictional workbook.*

Select a column to inspect what it feeds and how it is read. **Map to…** on its menu changes that
mapping; dragging a column onto a type also starts mapping. Columns can supply names, fields,
parents or related records, or be ignored. Value maps can treat placeholders as empty. Check
whether unknown related values should be created or refused; a missing reference is not permission
to invent a record silently.

Each proposal or edit is a step in the draft's **History**. **Undo** and **Redo** let you revisit
steps. Editing a proposed element makes it yours and removes its Proposed mark. Closing the editor
keeps the saved draft and its proposals.

![The draft History with proposed steps and Undo actions](/docs/screens/use-wb-history.png)

*Above: the fictional workbook's draft has 16 proposal steps, including placeholder handling and lists.*

## Issues and the dry run answer different questions

**Issues** reports problems in the model and its mapping. **No issues** means the draft is valid;
it does not mean all source rows can load.

![Issues reporting that the draft is valid and can be installed](/docs/screens/use-wb-issues.png)

*Above: the fictional workbook's draft has no structural issues, although its dry run refuses nine rows.*

The **Dry run** reads the file against the draft's model and the comparison workspace without
writing records. It counts records created or changed, values, relationships, related records
created and refused rows. Each figure opens its underlying rows. A change to the mapping triggers
a new dry run; use the result for the current draft version. A result for an older version does
not establish what the current draft would load.

![Dry run counts for the first source, with nothing written](/docs/screens/use-wb-dry-run.png)

*Above: the fictional file's Haltestellen source would create 51 records, 97 values and 260
relationships, including 21 related records. These are predicted results, not completed writes.*

![Dry run with refused rows in the second source](/docs/screens/use-wb-dry-run-names.png)

*Above: the fictional workbook's Namen source would create four records but refuse nine rows.
The local-code sources are counted separately.*

Open refused rows to read their reasons. Correct the mapping or source, or decide explicitly which
rows cannot be loaded. **Checked** means the dry run checked the sources, not that it accepted
every row. A failed or stale check needs a new result before applying.

## Applying and keeping the work

**Load into a change set…** opens **Load the workbook**. Its summary identifies the dry-run
version and any refused rows. Review the three stages before starting:

| Stage | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Install and activate the model | Where needed, installs and activates the release and saves the import profile. Check Release key, Version and Name when a new release is being made. If no activation is needed, Keep the active model saves the profile without changing the model. |
| Open a change set | Creates the named change set in the Workspace you choose. This is the destination of the loaded records. |
| Load the rows | Reads the stored file through the saved profile. Records found are updated. |

![Load the workbook dialog with release details, change-set name, workspace and three stages](/docs/screens/wbload-dialog.png)

*Above: the fictional operator workbook is ready to load into Guide workbook test. The draft
changes the model, so the dialog proposes release 1.0.1 and offers Install, activate and load.*

Model activation changes the target workspace's definitions before the row load; it does not
wait for publication of the loaded records. These stages can stop separately: an installed
release may remain installed if activation fails. Read the reported stage and reason before
retrying. Do not assume a later failure undid an earlier stage.

The stages run in order. Completed steps are marked and the active step shows progress. The
action button changes to **Installing…**, **Opening the change set…** or **Loading…**. While the
stages run, the dialog's actions are unavailable; wait for the result before leaving it.

![Workbook load in progress with two completed stages and Loading under Load the rows](/docs/screens/wbload-running.png)

*Above: the model is active and the change set is open in Guide workbook test. The fictional
workbook's row load has started; 0 of 420 items have been processed at this moment.*

When finished, **Loaded into the change set** reports the actual counts for records and
relationships: **created**, **updated**, **unchanged** and **refused**. Created means new entries;
updated means changes to entries found by the profile; unchanged means no change was needed.
Refused items were not applied. A completed load can include refusals, so check the counts rather
than treating completion as acceptance of every row. These totals cover records and relationships,
not just the number of spreadsheet rows.

![Finished workbook load with counts and Open the change set review](/docs/screens/wbload-finished.png)

*Above: the fictional workbook load reports 258 created, 108 updated, 45 unchanged and 9 refused.
All stages are done, but nothing is live until the change set is published.*

**Open the change set review** opens the actual proposed differences. **Records** shows additions,
changes and removals; **Relationships** shows connection changes. Unchanged entries do not appear
as changes, and refused items are not successful additions. Use the dry run's refused-row details
to understand the known refusals; do not expect the change review to list unloaded rows.

![Loaded change set review listing added records with expandable details](/docs/screens/wbload-review.png)

*Above: the fictional workbook's review in Guide workbook test includes added lookup records
and local codes. Expand entries to inspect what was loaded.*

Choose **Back to change set** to inspect the records in their collections or correct the proposal.
The orange banner still names the change set. Validate and publish, or submit for approval, through
the normal [change-set process](/docs/use/change-sets/). Loading does not itself publish records.

![Loaded records in a collection under the open change-set banner](/docs/screens/wbload-records.png)

*Above: Haltestellens in the fictional workbook's application contains 51 records in Guide
workbook test. The banner identifies the open load change set; these are proposed records.*

The draft menu offers **Upload a newer workbook…**, **Propose again…** and **Delete draft…**.
Proposing again preserves your edits and leaves undone proposals undone; conflicts with how you
mapped a column become issues. Deleting asks for confirmation and removes the draft, its steps,
proposals and attached workbook. Installed releases are unaffected. It cannot be undone.

![Draft menu with newer workbook, propose again and delete actions](/docs/screens/use-wb-draft-menu.png)

*Above: the menu belongs to the draft made from the fictional operator workbook.*

![Delete draft confirmation describing removal of its steps and attached workbook](/docs/screens/use-wb-delete-draft.png)

*Above: the fictional workbook's draft can be deleted without removing installed releases.*

Once installed, the saved profile can be reused under **Settings**, **Import profiles** with
**Upload the next version…**. Review its comparison and dry run before loading: a new file can
change headers, introduce unknown values or omit records that still exist in refiroo.

## How a workbook is read

A workbook can describe a model explicitly, contain several lists laid out for people to read,
or repeat parent information on each row. The proposal can recognise key-and-name columns,
a code with a name, text lists, Yes/No flags, several values in a cell, names by row or column,
stable identifiers and placeholders. [How workbook proposals are made](/docs/model/workbook-proposals/) explains the recognition rules
and alternatives. These are suggestions about the file's shape; check that
the result means what you intend before installing it.

When a sheet contains lists, choose **Lists** in the source pane. Select each list to inspect
**Under**, **Cells**, **Note** and **Loads**. Use **Adjust list…** to correct **Header row**,
**Last row**, **First column** and **Last column**. Review the resulting range before applying.
**Don't load this list** excludes a list; **Load as a list…** chooses how a detected range is
read. For at least three lists with the same columns under one title (or none), a proposal can
offer **Read these N lists as one list under their headers**. It creates a list of headers and
a list of values beneath them; a value beneath two headers becomes two records. Translated
category names and a second header row's role are not loaded by this choice. Review the
alternative before taking it. These controls change reading instructions, not the workbook's cells. The list's menu and dialog are the way to
adjust its range; the outline is not dragged on the sheet grid.

## Map columns deliberately

1. Select a source column. Read its **Feeds**, **Read as**, **Matched by** and **Statistics**.
   Statistics include filled cells, frequent values, placeholders, delimiters and shared values.
2. Choose **Map to…**. Decide whether the column supplies a name, an attribute, a parent, a
   related record or a Yes/No relationship flag. Choose the destination type and any identifying
   column requested. **Ignore** leaves the column out of loading.
3. For an attribute, check **Attribute name** and **Value type**. For references, check
   **Matched by** and the chosen record or naming column. Enable creation of missing related
   records only if the file genuinely defines those new records.
4. Use **Split a cell on** for cells containing several values. **Do not split** keeps the
   whole cell. Under **Value map**, choose **Add a value map…** or **Edit value map…** and
   map **Text in the file** to **Becomes**. Removing a mapping row stops that replacement.
5. Use **Use as the key of the rows** only for a suitable unique identifier. A non-unique
   column explains why it cannot be the key. Check the refreshed dry run after each decision.

## Revisit proposals and files

From the draft's menu, **Propose again…** offers the same four proposal choices as creation.
Your manual edits are retained and undone proposals stay undone. Conflicting column choices
become issues to resolve. Wait while **Proposing from the workbook** pauses editing.
**Upload a newer workbook…** replaces the attached source; check **Compare with the records of**
again, then inspect changed headers, ranges, mappings and the new dry run before loading.

In **Dry run**, select each source's tab and open the counts, including refused rows with
sheet and row numbers. The **was** figures show what changed since the last dry run. Check the
current draft version, not an older successful result. The saved import profile belongs to this
model and can be used in workspaces running it; it cannot be used against another model.

For the final stages and review, follow
[Load a workbook into a change set](/docs/guide/model/load-a-workbook-into-a-change-set/).

## Focused tasks and refusal recovery

Use [Map a column](/docs/guide/model/map-a-column/),
[Read lists in a sheet](/docs/guide/model/read-lists-in-a-sheet/),
[Propose again with a newer workbook](/docs/guide/model/propose-again-with-a-newer-workbook/) and
[Check a workbook with a dry run](/docs/guide/model/check-a-workbook-with-a-dry-run/) for each part.

A profile key belongs to one model. If installing, activating or loading says the key belongs
to another model, use the offered **Use '…'** action for the free key, or change **Profile key**
in the source pane to a distinct one. Recheck Issues and the dry run before retrying; this is
not permission to overwrite another model's profile.

Every component of a combined row key must be bound and filled. Incomplete keys and ambiguous
matches need correction or an explicit skip choice in the profile. Repeated keys with compatible
filled values can contribute to one record; conflicting non-empty values refuse all contributing
rows. Inspect all affected rows rather than choosing the last value by spreadsheet order.

When missing records are to be deleted, the load must go into a change set for review. Examine
which records remain referenced before publishing deletions. For ordinary files using an existing
model, see [Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/).

## Reuse a saved profile with the next file

Open **Settings › Import profiles** and inspect the profile's model, still-valid status and
last load before **Upload the next version…**. Select the workspace deliberately: each workspace
keeps its own uploaded file and latest check. Checking and loading need the corresponding bulk
permission there. A file uploaded for one workspace does not replace another workspace's file.

Read the comparison's **Columns**, **Values**, **Records** and **Profile against the active release**.
**Accept rename** keeps the old binding on a recognised renamed column; **Ignore new column**
leaves an unwanted addition out. A missing bound column requires correction. Inspect new lookup
values and name drift instead of assuming that a matched key makes every name change harmless.
Open missing records before choosing **Keep the missing records** or the offered deletion choice.
Only an explicitly configured deletion profile deletes missing records, and only through a change
set. Refused rows do not make their identified records eligible for missing-record deletion.

A rename suggestion uses both column position and shared values; it is evidence to review, not
a certainty. Repeated headings stay separately addressable by numbered column names. Already
ignored sheets present in the earlier file need not invalidate an otherwise matching layout.
Skipped rows are distinct from refused rows; inspect the profile's figures, and check again if
the draft or profile changed after the result.

Model steps also update the draft's reading instructions: renamed references follow, moved or
split fields gain corresponding sources and merged types repoint them. A removal can leave a
column unmapped with a warning; inspect it rather than assuming it was safely ignored. A saved
profile is checked against the active release and names bindings that no longer resolve.

Only changes that affect loading replace the current workbook dry run. Label, navigation,
release-identity, layout and consumer-definition changes do not themselves restart it. Unfilled
rows and recognised heading or note rows do not create records. Skip-without-key instructions
require a declared key. A source replacement keeps the old file for retained job work; deleting
its owner also removes the attached files, so preserve any source you still need.

## Limits of workbook mapping

Use the profile for typed fields, lookups by an identifying value, delimiter-separated values,
relationship flags and related records. Value maps replace known spellings or placeholders; they
do not calculate new values. Value maps can be reused across columns. Each refused item identifies its sheet and row, so you
can find the original value. A load resolves references by their identifying values and orders
sources so that referenced records can be loaded first. Spreadsheet row order is not a substitute
for a reliable identifier.

If the file needs calculations, joins beyond an identifying-value lookup or custom procedural
logic, prepare it outside the editor or ask an integrator to use the
[bulk and import facilities](/docs/integrate/writing-in-bulk/). The editor is not a general spreadsheet programming tool.

For a single-choice lookup, changing the referenced value in a later file switches the existing
relationship to the new record. It does not add a second choice. Review relationship changes
alongside field changes in the change set, especially when a value has become empty.

## Have the assistant design the model

For a file whose meaning needs more than the workbook rules can infer,
[review the assistant's workbook design](/docs/guide/model/review-an-assistants-workbook-design/).
It proposes the model first and lets you correct it in words or in the editor before acceptance.
This is separate from the rules-based proposals described here.

## Leave out a whole sheet

Open a sheet’s menu in **Source** and choose **Ignore this sheet** when none of it should load.
This removes reading sources for that sheet and records it as ignored in the profile; it does
not delete the sheet from your file or delete live records. The action is unavailable when it
is already ignored. Review **History**, **Issues** and a fresh dry run afterwards, especially
if another source looked up records from that sheet. Use **Undo** for an unwanted saved step.
Ignoring one column or choosing **Don’t load this list** has a narrower scope.

---
title: The model editor
description: Find definitions, edit their structure, preview layouts and review the draft history.
reader: model-admin
---

Use the model editor to change a draft through named actions. Each saved action becomes a step
in its history. You need **Model authoring**; applying the result also needs release access.
See [Models](/docs/model/models/) for the stages and permissions.

## Find your way around

The header identifies the draft, its base release, draft version and validation state. **Undo**
and **Redo** act on saved steps. **Close** keeps the draft and its proposals. The main confirmation
is **Install and activate…**, or **Apply to this workspace…** when you came from a workspace.

The model pane lists applications and their types in a hierarchy, followed by **Relation types**,
**Attribute types** and **Relationship matrix**. A type listed in several applications still has
one definition. Select an element to see its details in the centre. Use the plus button to add
an element, or the selected element's menu for its operations.

![Draft editor with its header, model pane and Issues and history bar](/docs/screens/model-editor-overview.png)

*Above: Guide draft starts from the Graubünden release. The model pane lists Network, Systems and
Names; no element is selected in the centre.*

An application shows its types, where they stand, field and relationship counts, views and
navigation groups. A type shows **Attributes** and **Relations**. Select an editable cell to
change it with **Save**, or leave it with **Cancel**. Menus offer operations such as **Rename…**,
**Move to…**, adding fields and allowing relationships.

A short operation, such as renaming or choosing a value type, opens beneath its control in a small popover. Pick several items there with **Apply**; save a single setting with **Save**. Longer forms and forms needing a preview open beside the page as sheets. Adding uses **Add** followed by the thing's name; moving uses **Move**. Confirmations remain small centred dialogs. The same validation and draft **Undo** apply whichever form is shown.

| Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Released | The element is unchanged from the draft's base release. |
| New | The draft adds the element. |
| Changed | The element, or something within it, differs from the base release. |
| Proposed | The element still reflects the engine's suggestion from a source. Review it before relying on it. |

Renaming a label does not change its key. A released key can also change, but integrations
that name it must change with it. The element panel says **Released: a key change needs a migration**.

Removing, moving, splitting or merging a released type, converting a field to a list type,
or tightening a rule saves a draft step even when stored data uses the element. Menus warn
**Needs a migration when installed** where an action can need one. **Move to…** explains what
happens to the records or values when the migration runs. Changing the draft does not move
live records; review the migration before activating the release.

## Work with a navigation group

Select a group in the model pane, or choose its name in the application's **Navigation groups**
table. Its panel shows the application it belongs to, whether it starts open or folded, and how
many entries it holds. **Entries** lists **Entry**, **Kind**, **Opens on** and **State**.
Collections and relation matrices share this table and its order.

**Add to group…** opens a searchable list where you can tick several collections and matrices.
Location notes show what is at the top of the sidebar, inside a row collection or in another
group; choosing an entry in another group moves it. One addition, even with several entries,
is one saved step and one **Undo**. **Rename…** and **Start folded** / **Start unfolded** adjust
the group itself.

In an entry's menu, **Move up** and **Move down** change its position. **Move to another group…**
is offered when another group exists. **Take out of the group** returns a collection to the
sidebar's top level, or leaves a matrix available through its row collection without a separate
entry. These actions arrange navigation; they do not move records.

For a collection with several views, edit **Opens on** in place and **Save** the choice.
It decides which view opens from that collection's sidebar entry or the group page. Without a
separate choice, the application default is used when it belongs to the collection, then its
table, then its first view. Other view tabs stay available. A matrix entry shows **Itself**:
it always opens that matrix, using its view name and a matrix symbol in its row type's colour.
The row collection stays in navigation and still offers the matrix among its tabs.

The application panel's **Entries** column lists the collections and matrices in each group.
Its **In no group:** line offers **Add to a group…** with ungrouped collections ticked.
A relation matrix's menu in **Views** offers **Move to group…** when a group exists.
Follow [Group collections in navigation](/docs/guide/model/group-collections-in-navigation/)
for the steps. Navigation changes reach a workspace when the model release is activated.

## When there is a workbook

A workbook adds a **Source** pane with sheets, columns, mapping states and statistics. Select a
column to see what it feeds; select a type to see the columns that feed it. **Map to…** in the
column menu provides an alternative to dragging it onto the model. A proposal's **Proposed because**
explains the suggestion; **Evidence** opens the supporting observations. You can change or undo
proposals. The original workbook is not rewritten.

While profiling is running, wait for the sheets and columns. If profiling fails, read the reason
and upload the workbook again from the draft menu. Once columns are mapped, the **Dry run** tab
checks their rows after edits. Narrow screens present the panes as tabs.

For source selection, mapping and loading, follow
[Load a workbook](/docs/guide/model/start-a-draft-from-a-workbook/). The source pane is absent from a draft with
no attached workbook.

## Preview and layout

**Preview** on a type shows the draft's layout over records read live from a workspace running
its model. Its data controls are disabled: previewing writes nothing. Check the workspace and
record selectors; an empty preview for a new model does not mean the draft failed.

![Type preview with a workspace selector and disabled record controls](/docs/screens/model-type-preview.png)

*Above: Stop's draft layout is shown over a live Graubünden record. Step-free access is still a
draft addition, with no live value.*

**Edit layout** opens the layout editor. **Record page** arranges panels and fields in the main
and side regions. **Table** chooses columns, filters and the default sort. Layout changes are
saved draft steps too; they reach the workspace's record screens after activation.

Follow [Add a record type and fields](/docs/guide/model/add-a-record-type-and-fields/),
[Add a relationship](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relationship/) and
[Arrange applications and views](/docs/guide/model/arrange-applications-and-views/) for the actions.

## History, undo and other editors

Expand **Issues and history** and choose **History**. Steps appear newest first, with the action,
author, time and whether they are applied or undone. A single step may contain related actions,
such as creating an attribute and attaching it to a type.

A step that changes a released element used by stored data is marked **Needs a migration**,
with the counts of records, values and relationships using it. A released key change has the
mark even when no stored data uses it. Other changes to unused released elements have no mark.

![History showing two applied steps and their Undo actions](/docs/screens/model-history.png)

*Above: Guide draft records adding Step-free access and allowing Inspected by as two saved steps.*

**Undo** reverses a step in the draft; **Redo** restores an undone step. A new edit clears what
can be redone. If later steps depend on the step you undo, refiroo names them and offers to undo
them together. Read that list before confirming. Undoing a draft step never rewrites an installed
release or reverses already published record changes. Undo also takes the step's part out of
the draft's proposed migration; redo puts it back. The proposal follows the steps that are
currently applied.

If another administrator edits the draft first, your older edit can be refused. The **Another change came first** notice lists the steps applied since you opened it, and the
model below shows the newer version. Read those steps, then choose **Apply mine again** if your
change still belongs, or **Discard mine** to leave it out. A further intervening edit can refuse
the retry too.

## Compare before releasing

The install confirmation summarises changed applications, types, fields and relationships against
the draft's base release. A draft without a base is compared with the newest release of its own
model, if one exists; a wholly new model has no earlier definitions to compare.

Read those differences together with validation, stored-data compatibility and **Consumer APIs**.
A comparison of definitions does not prove that the workspace's existing records fit. The separate
checks are explained in [Issues and dry runs](/docs/model/issues-and-dry-run/).

When the selected workspace needs a migration, **Install and activate…** and **Apply to this
workspace…** show **Activation needs a migration**. Read the steps and the proposed changes:
which types records become, where they move, and whether they leave their parents. The figures
show records moving, records and relationships created where applicable, and refused items.
For each key change, the dialog warns that integrations naming the old key must change and
lists the consumer APIs of the base release that name it.

Choose **Install … and preview the migration…**, or **Preview what happens to the records…**
from **Apply to this workspace…**. This installs the release and opens the migration preview;
it does not activate the release in the workspace yet.

On the migration page, **What the draft proposes** is already filled in. Each type's row shows
**Records of**, **Become**, **In**, **Under** and **Records**, with a **Proposed** mark for the
draft's choice. Change **Become** to preview another choice without editing the draft.
Splits and list conversions can create records and relationships; inspect them under **Created**.
Fix refused items before confirming, and review and explicitly accept any removals.
The workspace keeps its current release until the migration is confirmed and succeeds.
See [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/) for what each kind of change carries or removes,
and follow [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) to complete the review.

## Header, keyboard and phone controls

Open **About this draft** for its base release (or **A new model**), edit version and validity.
The version increases with each saved step. Change the editable draft title to rename the draft;
this does not rename a release. **Saved as you go** means closing keeps the draft and proposals.

The **Add** menu offers **Application…**, **Object type…**, **Attribute type…**,
**Relation type…** and **Navigation group…**. In an empty draft, add an application first.
An operation opens a dialog; **Not applied** means the attempted step did not save. Correct its
reported cause, or cancel. **Delete draft…** in **More actions** asks for confirmation and removes
only the editable draft, its steps and attached source, leaving installed releases unchanged.

In the model pane, Up/Down and Home/End move focus; Enter or Space selects. Right and Left unfold
and fold sections. Shift+F10 or the context-menu key opens the selected row's operations.
On a phone, tabs replace the panes. Use the menus: model-editor drags are off on phones.
**Earlier steps** in History reads more than the initial saved-step list.

**Relationship matrix** shows every type as a row and column, with rows as the from end.
Cells list permitted relationships and their number limits; containment reads **contains**.
Move with arrow keys and select a pair with Enter. The selected pair's panel offers its existing
relations' menus and an action to allow another. It can be resized.

## Consumer contracts and the structured-document view

The **Consumer APIs** tab holds the contracts other systems read. Add a consumer API with its
name and the types to expose, then inspect **Types and related**, **Fields**, **Operations**,
**Filters**, **Schema** and **Message example**. Fields and related lists shape the public data;
operations choose what consumers can read. The compatibility status says whether a higher
contract version is needed. Raising that version is separate from numbering the model release.
Review breaking changes with the consuming teams before activation.

The header also offers **Open as JSON** for specialist model authors who maintain the complete
structured model document. Normal screen-based editing does not need it. Both routes edit the
same draft and record saved steps; document edits appear as **JSON edit** in History. Use
**Export JSON** there, or on an installed release, to download its document. If that view reports
a newer saved draft, preserve your local work with **Copy local JSON** before
**Reload saved version**. Reloading does not merge the two versions.

## Next tasks

Use [Find your way around](/docs/guide/model/find-your-way-around-the-editor/) for keyboard and phone
navigation, [Undo and review history](/docs/guide/model/undo-and-review-the-draft-history/) for saved
steps, and [Work on a draft with others](/docs/guide/model/work-on-a-draft-with-others/) for version
conflicts. [Delete a draft](/docs/guide/model/delete-a-draft/) removes only editable work.

[Types, attributes and relations](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/),
[Applications and views](/docs/model/applications-and-views/),
[Record pages and tables](/docs/model/record-pages-and-tables/) and
[Consumer APIs](/docs/model/consumer-apis/) explain each part of the editor.
The specialist [JSON view](/docs/model/json-view/) exposes the complete model document.

Draft comparison uses the base release where there is one, otherwise the latest installed
release of that model, otherwise an empty model. There is no automatic rebase or merge of a
draft onto a newer release. To start from different definitions, create a new draft from the
intended release and review the changes you carry across. A refused grouped operation applies
none of that step. Intermediate invalid drafts may be saved; Issues identifies what still needs work.

A navigation group's initial folded state is a model default; each browser can remember a
different state. A group page gathers its collection and matrix entries with search over their names. During a drag in the model
pane, moving near its upper or lower edge scrolls the pane. Keyboard and phone users use
**Move to…** and the ordering menus instead.

## Describe a change in words

You can also [ask the assistant to propose a model change](/docs/model/ai-model-changes/)
and open its draft in this editor. Review the proposal before accepting; direct edits here
are read again when the assistant continues.

guide/src/content/docs/model/managing-wo:
---
title: Managing workspaces
description: Create and manage independent datasets and choose which model each runs.
reader: model-admin
---

Manage datasets under **Settings › Workspaces**. You need **Workspace administration** for
workspace changes; reading data, changing models and granting access need their own permissions.
For everyday navigation, see [Workspaces](/docs/use/workspaces/).

## Find a workspace


Where your access permits it, **Manage workspaces** or **Settings**, **Workspaces** opens the
workspace list. It shows the model and release of each workspace and marks the default.

![Workspace management listing each workspace and its model release](/docs/screens/use-workspaces-manage.png)

*Above: Graubünden and Default run different models. This capture only views the list.*

Open a workspace row to inspect **Overview**, **Access**, **Approval** and **Activity**.
**Open workspace** returns to its data; **Activity** shows [history across records](/docs/use/history/).
The other actions require administrative permissions: **New workspace**, **Edit model**,
**Copy or move data…** and **Retire…** change the workspace or its configuration.
Opening the page does not perform them.

![A workspace detail with its actions and Overview, Access, Approval and Activity tabs](/docs/screens/use-workspaces-detail.png)

*Above: Graubünden's Overview shows its key, model, applications and default status.*

A retired workspace remains readable but refuses changes. Open it through workspace management,
rather than the active workspace selector. The default workspace cannot be retired or deleted;
an administrator must make another workspace the default first.

## Create or rename a workspace

1. Open **Settings › Workspaces**. Search the list before creating another dataset. Active
   workspaces appear first, then retired ones.
2. Choose **New workspace**. Complete its name and key. The key forms its address; choose it
   carefully. Use the default workspace's model, or choose another usable installed release.
3. Choose **Add workspace** and check the new workspace's **Overview**, model and applications. It has
   its own data; creation copies no records from the default workspace. Read any refusal before
   retrying. Cancel leaves the list unchanged.
4. To change its displayed name later, select the name where it stands, enter the new name and choose **Save**. The save notice offers **Undo**.
   Renaming does not change its key or create a new dataset.

## Retire, reactivate, make default or delete

- **Retire…** asks for confirmation. It removes the workspace from the active selector and
  refuses writes, keeping data, change sets, publications and history readable. Open it from
  this list later. **Reactivate** makes it available for work again.
- **Set as default** chooses the default destination. It neither copies data nor changes the
  models of other workspaces. Check the Default mark after the action.
- **Delete…** is only for an empty, never-published workspace with no change sets or webhook
  subscriptions. A workspace ever published can only be retired, even after its data is removed.
  The screen explains what prevents deletion. Confirm only after checking the name and key.

The default workspace cannot be retired or deleted. Make another active workspace the default
first. If another administrator changed the workspace or default while the page was open, review
the refreshed state and repeat only the action still needed.

## Tabs and model changes

**Overview** shows the workspace's facts and its model's applications; each application opens
in this workspace. **Access** lists grants for people, groups and clients. **Approval** holds
[publication policies](/docs/administer/approval-policies/). **Activity** lists changes newest
first, grouped by day, with filters; see [History](/docs/use/history/). Only tabs your access allows
are shown.

**Edit model** opens the saved draft for the workspace, reopening it on later visits. It needs
Model authoring, Model release and Browse, and an active workspace. Check **Applies to**, then
use **Apply to this workspace…** after editing. The confirmation lists model changes, data
compatibility, open change sets left behind and other workspaces left unchanged. If records must
move, review the separate preview before confirming. Follow
[Install and activate a release](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/).
**Copy or move data…** starts [a copy or move](/docs/guide/model/move-records-to-another-model/).

Workspace administration can also be switched off by the deployment. The page then stays read
only and names the setting; ask the operator to enable it if administration is needed.

## Workspace tasks

[Create a workspace](/docs/guide/model/create-a-workspace/),
[Edit its model](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-workspaces-model/),
[Make it the default](/docs/guide/model/make-a-workspace-the-default/) and
[Retire or delete it](/docs/guide/model/retire-or-delete-a-workspace/) give the steps.
To choose an installed release, use [Change a workspace's model](/docs/guide/model/change-a-workspaces-model/).

**Cannot be opened** on a workspace whose model language is unsupported needs the offered
model-language repair or operator help; see [Model language versions](/docs/model/model-language-versions/). A missing application
bookmark can instead mean **Not in this model**: open a collection declared by this workspace.
Editing the displayed name keeps the permanent key. A stale save asks you
to review newer state; it does not silently overwrite another administrator's edit.

## Permanent keys and changes made at the same time

A workspace key has at most 160 characters, using lowercase letters and digits separated by
single hyphens. Leading and trailing spaces are removed. Its key cannot be changed after
creation, and a retired workspace still reserves its key. Change **Name** to rename the dataset.

Retirement waits for a write already in progress to finish. Once retirement succeeds, later
live and change-set writes are refused. If two administrators change the default from the same
starting state, one succeeds and the other must refresh and review the new default.

Retiring also suspends active webhook subscriptions for this workspace. Reactivation makes the
workspace writable again but does not resume those subscriptions automatically. Ask their
administrator to review and resume them; undelivered events are kept only for their retention
period. See [Webhooks](/docs/administer/webhooks/) for delivery recovery.

guide/src/content/docs/model/json-view.m:
---
title: The JSON view
description: Use the specialist document workbench for definitions beyond the visual editor.
reader: model-admin
---

Most modelling tasks use the visual editor. The **JSON** view is the specialist workbench for
the complete model document, including settings without visual forms. Ask a specialist model
author to maintain those settings if you do not work with model documents. Both views edit the
same draft; neither directly changes the active workspace.

Open **JSON** in the editor header, or **Open as JSON** in its menu. The workbench has **Draft
name**, **JSON model**, **Authoritative validation**, a summary and **Compile and compare**.
You need **Model authoring** to save. See [Edit a draft as JSON](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-draft-as-json/)
for the workbench controls, without needing to learn document syntax here.

![Document workbench with draft name, validation and compile actions](/docs/screens/model-draft-json.png)

## Saving and checking

A syntax error prevents saving the text. Valid syntax does not prove that referenced definitions
exist or that the model is usable. **Authoritative validation** checks those rules and lets you
select a diagnostic to reach the affected text. Saving keeps the draft, including work still
needing model corrections. **Compile and compare** uses the saved version and shows **Canonical
model**, **Ready for review** or **Invalid**, a model hash and the semantic differences.

**Export JSON** downloads the current document. It does not install or activate it. **Install
immutable release…** separately confirms creation of an inactive release; activation still
requires a workspace compatibility check. The visual editor's **Install and activate…** combines
those stages. See [Releases](/docs/model/releases/).

## Other editors and unsupported visual settings

Unsaved text is local to this workbench until **Save draft**. If another author saves first,
**A newer draft version exists** preserves your text. **Copy local JSON** keeps it for review;
**Reload saved version** reads the saved draft without merging. Saved document edits appear
as **JSON edit** in History.

The document covers application descriptions and presentation settings; type display, placement
and effective periods; shared and relationship attributes; validation and uniqueness rules;
full view and panel declarations; consumer contracts; and import-profile instructions where
applicable. Visual controls cover only the options described on their pages. Do not infer that
an absent form means the model cannot declare a feature. Integrators use
[Integrate](/docs/integrate/overview/) for the model contract details rather than browser steps.

## Settings that still need a specialist

Use the named controls first. The type’s **Settings** now sets its display attribute,
effective period, grouped field requirement and parent relationships; attribute Settings
sets numeric limits, Hidden and Help text. Relationship **Carries**, application **Default
view**, **Add a view…**, **Header and breadcrumbs…** and panel **Settings…** also have forms.
See [Types](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/), [Views](/docs/model/applications-and-views/)
and [Record pages](/docs/model/record-pages-and-tables/) for those tasks.

These supported choices still require the complete document workbench:

| Choice | What to review with the specialist |
| --- | --- |
| Model title and description | The product wording used by the top bar comes from the default workspace’s model. A draft title alone does not change it. |
| Application or type icon | Choose an icon supported by refiroo; the visual editor displays it but has no icon picker. |
| Existing application, type or shared-field description | The new-application form takes a description; the element tables do not provide a general description editor. |
| Released field’s value type | A specialist can save the changed definition here when the visual editor refuses it. Compile and compare, install the release, then review the workspace migration before changing stored values. |
| Attribute default | A typed starting value used on creation, not a rule that refills cleared values. |
| Relationship uniqueness within an ancestor and its condition | Review the allowed type pair, ancestor and target field; these rules govern writes, not just one view. |
| Tree actions and detailed ordering | Create, Rename and Move, different ordering per child type, descending order and reading size. The visual tree form controls availability and one common child-order field. |
| Mapping-grid reading size | The visual form chooses endpoints, columns and candidate search, and new grids read 20 rows at a time. |
| Relation-matrix search and reading size | The matrix form sets structure, displayed fields and cell actions; additional row search fields and reading size need the workbench. |
| Full panel declarations | Creating a Table or Hierarchy panel directly, changing a table panel’s record type or a contained panel’s type list after creation. Existing hierarchy and table panels have Settings controls. |
| Detailed consumer declarations | The consumer editor has named forms for ordinary choices; a specialist can edit an entire API or item with **Edit as JSON…** when a combination has no form. |

Every saved change still needs validation. A free-form setting accepted in a document is not
proof that refiroo uses it. Ask the specialist to confirm the behavior and inspect the preview
and release checks before activation. Export preserves model definitions; it does not back up
workspace records, files, access settings or history. Use the operator’s
[backup and restore procedure](/docs/run/backup-and-restore/) for the installation.

## Relationships table configuration

Start with the [visual relationships-table form](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relationships-table/).
A specialist maintaining its configuration uses `fromColumns` and `toColumns` as ordered,
non-empty lists of `name` or scalar attribute keys attached to the respective endpoint type.
Each list must contain unique fields. `attributeColumns` is an ordered list of attribute keys
declared by that specific relationship binding; it may be empty but cannot repeat a key.
A JSON relationship attribute may be a column, but cannot be a filter or sort.

`groupBy` is `from`, `to` or null (no grouping). It heads the rows by the chosen record.
`layout` is `rows` by default, or `grid`: each from record once, with a column group per to
record, headed by the first `toColumns` field. The grid ignores `groupBy`; `from:` sorts
order its rows.

`filterFields` and `sortFields` identify the field's location as `from:<field>`, `to:<field>`
or `relation:<attribute>`. Endpoint fields must be `name` or attached scalar attributes;
relationship fields must be declared on the binding. Attribute filters require Filterable.
The visual form derives these lists from selected columns, excluding JSON; it starts
`defaultSort` at `from:name` and `pageSize` at 20. A specialist may declare other valid fields.
`sortFields` must be non-empty, `defaultSort` must name an entry (optionally prefixed with
`-` for descending), and `pageSize` must be 1–100.

Validation identifies the offending location. The following quoted diagnostic fragments are
from the validator; words in braces stand for the names in the affected declaration:

| Diagnostic wording | Correction |
| --- | --- |
| “references unknown object type '{key}'” / “references unknown relation type '{key}'” | Use existing definitions for both ends and the relationship. |
| “cannot use containment relation type '{key}'” | Choose a non-containment relationship. |
| “references a relation binding ({relation}, {from} → {to}) that is not declared in objectTypeRelations” | Declare the directed pair or choose a permitted one. |
| “View {list} must contain unique fields” | Remove repeats from the named column, filter or sort list. |
| “{list} references '{field}', which is not 'name' or a scalar attribute attached to '{type}'” | Use a field of the correct endpoint type. |
| “attributeColumns references '{field}', which binding ({relation}, {from} → {to}) does not declare in attributeTypeKeys” | Use an attribute carried by that pair. |
| “{purpose} field '{ref}' must be from:<field>, to:<field> or relation:<attribute>” | Qualify the filter or sort with its location. |
| “{purpose} field '{ref}': the binding does not declare attribute '{field}' in attributeTypeKeys” | Correct the relationship attribute reference. |
| “{purpose} field '{ref}': '{field}' is not 'name' or a scalar attribute attached to '{type}'” | Correct the endpoint reference. |
| “filter field '{ref}': attribute '{field}' is not filterable” | Remove the filter or enable filtering on that attribute. |
| “{purpose} field '{ref}' holds JSON and cannot be used” | Keep JSON as a relationship column only. |
| “defaultSort must name one of its sortFields” | Choose a declared sort field. |
