Once serving, use [Monitoring](/docs/run/monitoring/) to inspect workspace and process readiness,
background threads, connection pools and request diagnostics. During a database outage, a process
can remain live while unready. Restore connectivity and allow workers to recover; repeatedly
restarting healthy processes does not restore PostgreSQL. With several processes, follow
[Several processes](/docs/run/several-processes/) for their shared database and file storage.

Complete the recovery preparation with [Back up and restore](/docs/run/backup-and-restore/).
Restore a backup into a separate database and run the documented restore check there, then inspect
the recorded rehearsal outcome. The check must not target the live database. A failed rehearsal
is evidence to resolve before depending on that backup, rather than proof of a working restore.
Preserve the concise error and correlation references when escalating a failure.

## Check what a deployment runs and how it is configured

An operator identifies the running application version, supported model languages, model release
and source information before diagnosing a mismatch or planning maintenance.
[Monitoring](/docs/run/monitoring/) connects the deployment pages with process and workspace
information. [Configure refiroo](/docs/run/configure/) explains the settings catalogue, current
values, defaults, and whether a value came from the environment.

The pages inspect configuration; they do not edit environment settings. Change those in the
server or platform configuration and restart as documented. Secret settings show whether they
are present rather than revealing their values; the database address masks its password.
After a model activation, check the selected workspace's running release rather than assuming
all workspaces run the same one.

Use [Licence and source](/docs/run/licence-and-source/) to verify the running version's source
link, especially for a modified installation. If behaviour still disagrees with configuration,
return to [Troubleshooting](/docs/run/troubleshooting/) with the version, time, failing action,
workspace and diagnostic reference, excluding credentials and full environment files.

## Open a production installation over HTTPS

Start with [What you run](/docs/run/overview/) and
[Install with Compose](/docs/run/install-with-compose/), then choose automatic public
certificates, your organisation's certificate files or an existing HTTPS balancer in
[Serve over HTTPS](/docs/run/https/). Automatic issuance and renewal needs a public DNS name
and reachable port 443; port 80 is optional for redirects. Preserve certificate storage and
check renewal through the public address. Private names need a different certificate route.

[Set up sign-in and mail](/docs/run/sign-in-and-mail-setup/), test a complete sign-in and
recovery path, then complete the [production checklist](/docs/run/production-checklist/)
and [security checklist](/docs/run/security-checklist/). A healthy container does not establish
that every workspace, public sign-in, notification or receiver works. Keep the outcomes for
your installation and correct failed checks before admitting traffic.

## Upgrade and recover a failed cutover

Follow [Upgrades](/docs/run/upgrades/) to record the running source, supported model languages,
private configuration, backup and file archive before maintenance. Check the new deployment's
readiness, workspaces, sign-in and retained files before reopening writes. An unsupported stored
model needs the documented raising review; a database migration refusal needs its stated remedy.

[Model releases and rollback](/docs/run/model-releases-and-rollback/) distinguishes a compatible
model activation from application rollback. Restoring an older application requires its matching
pre-upgrade database and configuration; changing the bootstrap model file does not switch
existing workspaces. Do not repair a cutover by editing migration revision rows.

## Back up, rehearse and move to another host

[Back up and restore](/docs/run/backup-and-restore/) connects a consistent PostgreSQL and
job-file backup to its source version and protected keys. Rehearse the restore in an isolated
database and inspect the recorded result before relying on it. Include the public sign-in path
and file downloads when testing a replacement host; a database-only check does not establish those.

Use the same runbook's host-move sequence to stop writers, take the final consistent copy,
restore, verify and cut over the public address. Preserve the recovery material until the
replacement is proven. Retire the old host after cutover so it cannot resume competing work.
A missing sealing key prevents recovering stored secrets from their encrypted values alone.

## Replace secrets and watch growing storage

[Secrets and keys](/docs/run/secrets-and-keys/) identifies client credentials, signing material,
cursor keys and the sealing key before choosing the replacement procedure. Check which processes
share them and coordinate with the administrator and receivers. Retain the key matching a backup;
replacing a value blindly can make stored credentials unreadable or invalidate saved positions.

[The database](/docs/run/database/) covers connection budgets and growth. Combine it with
[Background jobs](/docs/run/background-jobs/), [Webhook delivery](/docs/run/webhook-delivery/)
and [Monitoring](/docs/run/monitoring/) to watch files, queues, delivery results and retained logs.
Change retention deliberately; it can remove diagnostic detail without removing reference data.
[Several processes](/docs/run/several-processes/) requires shared identity and file storage.
Measure the actual workload before making capacity or recovery-time promises.

## Enable optional AI or prepare a developer instance

Read [AI operation](/docs/run/ai/) before [Set up AI](/docs/run/set-up-ai/). Choose the provider,
built-in assistant and external-agent connection separately, set a send policy and credentials,
apply the configuration, then verify each enabled path. Inspect calls and task retention as well
as service readiness. Disabling a feature stops future use; it does not erase published records,
history or all retained task material. Follow the same page for replacement credentials or cleanup.

For local source work instead, follow [Developer instance](/docs/run/developer-instance/).
It has a different support boundary from the reference installation. Use
[Command-line tools](/docs/run/command-line/) for the documented maintenance commands, and
[Troubleshooting](/docs/run/troubleshooting/) to prepare concise diagnostics when a recovery fails.
guide/src/content/docs/journeys/shape-a-:
---
title: Shape a model
description: Connect model design, workbook loading, releases and workspace migrations.
reader: model-admin
---

These journeys are for model administrators shaping the types, fields, relationships and views
that people use. Applications are declared by the model; they can be changed, replaced or removed.
Start with [Models](/docs/model/models/) for the difference between a draft, an installed release
and the release running in a workspace.

Model authoring, model release and workspace administration permissions serve different purposes.
They do not automatically grant permission to read or change reference data. Each linked task
explains its required access and deployment settings.

## Create and activate an application-model release

A model administrator turns a reviewed design into the definitions a workspace runs.
[Releases](/docs/model/releases/) connects the lifecycle: create or import a draft, validate it,
compare its differences and stored-data compatibility, then install an immutable release.
[Install and activate a release](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/) takes that
release into the intended workspace. Saving, installing and activating are separate outcomes.

An incompatible release does not become active. Resolve its data problems or use the reviewed
[migration](#move-a-workspace-to-another-release) path. If another activation wins first, refresh
the state and review again. Use [Compare releases](/docs/guide/model/compare-releases/)
when checking differences, or [Export a release](/docs/guide/model/export-a-release/) to reuse it
elsewhere. Read-only inspection remains available when model administration is switched off.

## Administer workspaces

A workspace administrator, or an authorised integrator, creates a separate place for data,
gives it a stable key and a label, and chooses the release it runs.
[Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/) leads to
[Create a workspace](/docs/guide/model/create-a-workspace/) and
[Make a workspace the default](/docs/guide/model/make-a-workspace-the-default/).
Changing the default affects requests that omit a workspace; an explicit choice stays explicit.

When a workspace is no longer used, [retire or delete it](/docs/guide/model/retire-or-delete-a-workspace/).
Retirement preserves reads and refuses changes. The default cannot be retired; deletion also
requires an empty workspace with no publications. A refusal names what still prevents deletion.
Choose another default or retain the workspace for reading as appropriate.

## Define a consumer API in the model

A model author defines the business objects other systems should read without exposing their
storage structure. Start with [Consumer APIs](/docs/model/consumer-apis/), then
[define a consumer API](/docs/guide/model/define-a-consumer-api/) over the chosen types, fields,
related records, lists, lookup rules and events. Validate each reference and review the generated
[schema and message example](/docs/guide/model/see-a-consumer-apis-documents/).

Compare the consumer contract before installing and activating the release. A breaking change
needs a higher contract version; activation refuses it otherwise. An operation is available only
when declared. Coordinate changed contracts with integrators, who can then
[read through the consumer API](/docs/guide/integrate/read-through-a-consumer-api/).

**Example:** the reference model's stops consumer API exposes stops with names and codes drawn
from connected records. Another model can expose entirely different business objects.

## Design a model in the editor

A model administrator [creates a model draft](/docs/guide/model/create-a-model-draft/), then uses
[the model editor](/docs/model/the-model-editor/) to shape applications, types, reusable fields,
relationships, navigation and pages. Each edit has issues and a history; inspect them as the model
grows and [undo or review steps](/docs/guide/model/undo-and-review-the-draft-history/) where needed.
Preview pages before installation, without writing reference data from the preview.

A draft can temporarily be invalid, but an invalid draft cannot be installed. Released keys are
stable; a removal or structural change affecting stored data can require migration. If a colleague
changes the draft first, review their steps before retrying your edit. Finish through
[installation and activation](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/), then work with
records under the changed model to check the result.

## Onboard a workbook

A model administrator turns a workbook into a reviewed model and a repeatable loading profile.
Read [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/), then
[start a draft from a workbook](/docs/guide/model/start-a-draft-from-a-workbook/).
Inspect sheets, tables and lists; accept, change or reject proposals, or map columns by hand.
[Map a column](/docs/guide/model/map-a-column/) and
[read lists in a sheet](/docs/guide/model/read-lists-in-a-sheet/) explain the choices.
A proposal does not apply itself.

[Check the workbook with a dry run](/docs/guide/model/check-a-workbook-with-a-dry-run/) to inspect
what every row would do without writing records. Resolve missing values and mapping problems,
install and activate the model, then [load into a change set](/docs/guide/model/load-a-workbook-into-a-change-set/).
Review its differences and publish. Installation saves definitions and the loading profile;
it does not make the file's records live.

## Load the next version of a workbook

A steward or model administrator uses the saved profile to repeat the load without rebuilding
the mapping. [Load the next version of a workbook](/docs/guide/use/load-the-next-version-of-a-workbook/)
connects uploading the next file, inspecting differences, accepting column renames or ignoring
new columns, and checking again. Read the report before loading into a new change set.

Missing records are reported and kept unless the profile explicitly deletes them. A deleting
load needs a change set so the removals and their relationships can be reviewed. A changed model
release can invalidate a profile binding; fix the named binding rather than loading around it.
Finish by [reviewing the changes](/docs/guide/use/review-what-a-change-set-changes/) and publishing.

**Example:** a newer workbook of stop names or external codes can correct existing records and
add others. A stop absent from that file is not automatically deleted.

## Run a workspace on a model of its own

A model administrator installs the desired release and
[creates a workspace on it](/docs/guide/model/create-a-workspace/) or
[changes an existing workspace's model](/docs/guide/model/change-a-workspaces-model/)
after its compatibility review. Other workspaces keep their models. Switching workspace changes
the available applications and views as well as the records; shared labels do not imply shared data.

To evolve that workspace's definitions, [edit its model](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-workspaces-model/)
and apply the reviewed draft there. A page built under a replaced release must reload before
saving. If one workspace's model cannot be served, inspect its explanation and recovery options;
other workspaces can remain available. [Releases](/docs/model/releases/) also explains retiring
unused choices and deleting releases that nothing refers to.

## Move a workspace to another release

A model administrator uses [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/) when the target release needs
conversions or changes the existing data cannot adopt unchanged.
[Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) connects the preview, type and field
mapping, inspection of every loss, correction of blockers and explicit confirmation. Cancelling
changes nothing. The data conversion and release switch succeed together or neither does.

An intervening write makes the review stale: preview again instead of confirming an older result.
Open change sets stay on their release; move them separately or review a workspace migration with
publication as one operation. Existing publications keep their model and content. If a workspace
cannot open because its stored model uses an unsupported language version, follow the specific
recovery in [Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/); an ordinary migration and
raising an unsupported stored release are different operations.

## Move data between workspaces whose models differ

A model administrator or steward needs a mapping between the source and target definitions,
rather than assuming record types mean the same thing. Start with
[Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/), then
[move records to another model](/docs/guide/model/move-records-to-another-model/).
Complete the proposed mapping, choose the records, and inspect the dry run's created, updated and
refused items. Confirm a copy or move into the target's change set, then review and publish it.

A move also prepares reviewed deletion in the source; publish the target copy before that deletion.
Relationships whose other end stays behind are carried only when the counterpart can be found
in the target, otherwise they are dropped and reported. Matching and remembered counterparts let
later transfers update records rather than duplicate them. A changed mapping or release needs a
fresh review. Nothing rejected in the dry run should be treated as successfully moved.

## An account of a model change

A model administrator with **Model release** and **Use AI proposals** in the workspace can ask
for an explanation before activating a release or applying a draft. A configured AI provider
is required; enabling only the built-in assistant does not offer this account. Follow
[Explain a model change](/docs/guide/model/explain-a-model-change/).

Open the activation dialog or **Apply to this workspace** and read the compatibility checks.
Under **What this change does**, choose **Explain this change**. Nothing is sent before that
request. The provider receives the model's differences, rule failures, consumer-contract effects
and record counts, without record values or names. Requests can incur charges; the same facts
are reused for up to an hour. Call records remain; request text is kept only if enabled.
Read [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) for full access, disclosure, cost and retention rules.

Review the account and follow each numbered citation to the facts refiroo computed. These include
blocked activation and the counts of affected records, not a promise that the change is safe.
The explanation is English only, is not attached permanently to the release and takes no
follow-up question. It appears in activation and Apply, rather than installation or migration.
[Accounts of model changes](/docs/model/model-change-accounts/) explains its rules and limits.

![An account beside the model checks, with numbered citations and facts](/docs/screens/model-account-facts.png)

*Above: the Apply dialog for a change to the Graubünden reference model. The account cites the facts below it.*

If the provider fails, read the facts alone or choose **Try again**. Fix an invalid or newer draft
before asking again. Asking does not apply or activate anything, and an explanation cannot remove
a compatibility refusal. Continue through the normal activation review, or use
[the migration path](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) when the existing data needs conversion.

## Add types, fields and relationships

With **Model authoring**, [add a record type and fields](/docs/guide/model/add-a-record-type-and-fields/),
[reuse and change attributes](/docs/guide/model/reuse-and-change-attributes/) and
[add a relationship](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relationship/). A shared attribute change affects
all its attachments. Review required values, allowed parents and relationship candidates, then
[fix issues before installing](/docs/guide/model/fix-issues-before-installing/).
[Turn an attribute into a list](/docs/guide/model/turn-an-attribute-into-a-list/) when values
should become maintained records. Released values can need migration; a saved draft does not
populate that list or convert Live.

## Arrange navigation, views and record pages

[Find your way around the editor](/docs/guide/model/find-your-way-around-the-editor/), then
[arrange applications and views](/docs/guide/model/arrange-applications-and-views/) and
[group collections in navigation](/docs/guide/model/group-collections-in-navigation/).
[Add a view](/docs/guide/model/add-a-view/) for another way to read a collection, or
[add a relation matrix](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relation-matrix/) when its structure supports one.
Removing a navigation group keeps its collections; hiding a page panel keeps its stored values.

[Edit a record page](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-record-page/) to arrange fields and panels, and
[choose table columns, filters and sort](/docs/guide/model/choose-table-columns-filters-and-sort/)
for a view's defaults. [Preview a type](/docs/guide/model/preview-a-type/) against populated and
empty records before installation. Preview cannot write records. An invalid draft needs its
issues repaired first. [The specialist workbench](/docs/model/json-view/) owns supported
settings without visual forms; ask a specialist to
[edit that draft](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-draft-as-json/) where needed.

## Refine a draft without losing identity or colleagues' work

[Rename or re-key an element](/docs/guide/model/rename-or-re-key-an-element/) distinguishes a
label change from a stable identity: released keys are fixed even without records.
[Split, merge and move types](/docs/guide/model/split-merge-and-move-types/) reshapes definitions;
[remove an element](/docs/guide/model/remove-an-element/) first reviews affected uses and data.
Neither changes Live simply by saving the draft. Plan a migration when released data blocks a change.

[Work on a draft with others](/docs/guide/model/work-on-a-draft-with-others/) explains reviewing
a colleague's newer steps before retrying an edit. Use
[Undo and draft history](/docs/guide/model/undo-and-review-the-draft-history/) for an unwanted
saved step. [Delete a draft](/docs/guide/model/delete-a-draft/) only after preserving needed
work: its history and attached workbook go with it; installed releases stay.

## Recheck a workbook design or a saved mapping

[Propose again with a newer workbook](/docs/guide/model/propose-again-with-a-newer-workbook/)
keeps the distinction between design proposals, accepted draft edits and a fresh dry run.
Inspect changed columns and skipped sheets, then return to the normal loading and review path.

For transfers, [edit a mapping row](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-mapping-row/) and
[choose what moves](/docs/guide/model/choose-what-moves/) before reviewing a fresh complete dry
run. [Delete a model mapping](/docs/guide/model/delete-a-model-mapping/) only when future
transfers no longer need it; deletion does not undo earlier copies or moves.

## Maintain released contracts and definitions

[Raise a contract version](/docs/guide/model/raise-a-contract-version/) before activating a
breaking consumer change, and coordinate it with callers. This does not raise the model language:
[Raise a model language version](/docs/guide/model/raise-a-model-language-version/) is the
separate review for a stored model outside the supported window. Keep retained publications and
their definitions in the recovery plan.

[Retire or delete a release](/docs/guide/model/retire-or-delete-a-release/) hides unused choices
or permanently removes an unreferenced release. Existing references can prevent deletion.
Retirement does not stop workspaces already using a release. Review current use rather than
treating an older version as automatically disposable.
guide/src/content/docs/journeys/integrat:
---
title: Integrate a system
description: Discover contracts, read complete datasets, submit changes and follow events reliably.
reader: integrator
---

These journeys connect an integration's first contract read to ongoing synchronisation and
recovery. Use the management API to work with the model and records, or a model-declared consumer
API to read business objects. Start with [the integration overview](/docs/integrate/overview/)
and [signing in and tokens](/docs/integrate/signing-in-and-tokens/). Roles and consumer API grants
are separate; a token must also be intended for the API it calls.

The linked documentation explains sequences. Use the [API reference](/docs/api) for management
operations and their exact inputs and responses. Consumer API shapes depend on the model and are
explained with examples in [Consumer APIs](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/).

## Discover the model and the API

An integrator first checks what the deployment enables, its limits, and the workspace and model
release to use. [Discovering the model](/docs/integrate/discovering-the-model/) connects these
reads to types, attributes, relationships and permitted placements. Choose the data context before
reading metadata: a change set or publication can use a different release from Live.

Next open the [API reference documentation](/docs/integrate/api-reference/) and the
[management operations](/docs/api). Discover consumer APIs and their own generated contracts
rather than assuming all models expose the same paths. Stable public keys and record IDs identify
resources. If a model cannot be served, resolve the named workspace's problem instead of substituting
another workspace's definitions.

## Read a collection completely and resume

An integrator reads a bounded first page, processes it and follows the returned cursor until the
end. [Identifiers, paging and errors](/docs/integrate/identifiers-paging-and-errors/) explains
page positions, totals, reverse traversal and seeking where supported.
[Read a collection completely and resume](/docs/guide/integrate/read-a-collection-completely-and-resume/)
connects processing to saving a continuation point and restarting the same query.

Keep the query, workspace and context with that continuation. Reusing a cursor for a different
read is refused; do not construct or edit one. A page maximum is a page limit, not a limit on the
whole collection. A live traversal is not a frozen extract: choose a retained publication when the
integration needs a fixed snapshot. Browser readers can
[continue a long list](/docs/guide/use/continue-a-long-list/) through scrolling and position controls.

## Request the precise dataset an integration needs

An integrator selects types and a data context, combines typed field filters with hierarchy and
relationship criteria, chooses returned fields and related data, then pages the result.
[Reading records](/docs/integrate/reading-records/) explains the choices and links to the
[query operations](/docs/api). Use type-specific reads for model-declared fields; the cross-type
lookup serves the common fields it supports. A workspace relationship list answers questions
about connections rather than just records.

An invalid filter or sort is a refusal, rather than permission to return a broader dataset.
Correct the named criterion and restart with cursors for that query.

**Example:** read stops below chosen municipalities and include connected operators. Those types
and fields belong to the example model; the querying capability works over the selected model.

## Answer a business-date question

An integrator asks which records apply on a calendar date using a model-declared validity period.
[Business dates](/docs/integrate/business-dates/) explains inclusive starts, exclusive ends and
open boundaries. [Read as of a date](/docs/guide/integrate/read-as-of-a-date/) carries the date
through every page in the chosen live or published data.

A business date does not reconstruct an old database state or date every related record in a
projection. Check which types the answer actually dates. A type without a configured period cannot
answer a dated object or list read; mixed supported consumer lookups identify which types were
dated. Use a publication when you need a saved snapshot rather than validity on a date.

## Submit a bounded bulk change

An integrator sends a bounded group of record and relationship changes as one batch.
[Writing in bulk](/docs/integrate/writing-in-bulk/) leads to
[Submit a bulk change](/docs/guide/integrate/submit-a-bulk-change/) and the
[batch operations](/docs/api). Choose atomic execution for everything or nothing, or independent
execution when other items may succeed despite a refused item. Reference existing records by
ID or unique key and inspect each item's result before retrying.

Reuse the same idempotency key only for the same request: replay returns its original outcome;
changing the request under that key is refused. The ordinary model and version rules apply to
every item. Previewing a batch requires a background job; use the
[large-job journey](#run-a-large-background-job-and-recover) for work beyond inline limits.

## Run a large background job and recover

An integrator or exchange operator submits background work, keeps the returned job identity,
follows progress and reads item outcomes as execution advances.
[Jobs](/docs/integrate/jobs/) connects submission to completion, cancellation and recovery;
[Follow and cancel a job](/docs/guide/use/follow-and-cancel-a-job/) gives the browser view.
A preview can wait for explicit confirmation without having written the proposed changes.

After interruption, a worker resumes at the first unfinished item. Cancellation or failure of
independent work can leave committed chunks; atomic work rolls back together. A model, workspace,
permission or change-set change can stop work before the next chunk. Read the reason and applied
outcomes before resubmitting. Retention can remove detailed item results while keeping a summary,
so collect outcomes while they are available. Operators use
[Background jobs](/docs/run/background-jobs/) for worker recovery.

## Follow changes reliably

An integrator keeps another system current by processing a workspace's ordered change feed and
saving the last safely processed position. Read [Following changes](/docs/integrate/following-changes/),
then [load, then follow changes](/docs/guide/integrate/load-then-follow-changes/) to connect an
initial publication or consistent export with later changes. Feed entries identify changes and
their causes; they do not contain field values. Read records when the integration needs values.

Recognise replay by position and save progress only after processing succeeds. Keep following
continuation even through an empty filtered page until caught up. Unpublished edits and refused
writes do not appear. An expired position needs a fresh baseline and continuation from its stated
position; an ahead-of-head position needs investigation, including whether the wrong workspace
or a restored database was used. Do not silently skip to the current head.

## Exchange a supplier file

An exchange operator, steward or integrator identifies the destination, file layout and mapping,
then previews additions, updates and refused cells without changing data.
[Files, imports and exports](/docs/integrate/files-imports-and-exports/) leads to
[Exchange a supplier file](/docs/guide/integrate/exchange-a-supplier-file/) and its
[import and export operations](/docs/api). Browser workers can instead
[import a file](/docs/guide/use/import-a-file/) or
[export records](/docs/guide/use/export-records/). Choose the failure policy and inspect whether
the preview covered all execution items or only a sample before confirmation.

Read each applied or refused outcome, correct rejected rows and retry without duplicating applied
work. A changed profile, model or change set can require another preview. For a workbook intended
for people to edit, [edit in Excel and import back](/docs/guide/use/edit-in-excel-and-import-back/)
uses the carried mapping and versions; stale records are refused. A failed, cancelled or expired
export does not provide a partial download. Check a successful export's scope and position before
using it as a synchronisation baseline.

**Example:** exchange a workbook of stops and codes from other systems. The file's destination and
mapping determine what it changes; a similar column label does not establish identity.

## Read a business object through a consumer API

A consuming system discovers a declared contract and reads an object by its stable ID, or pages
a declared list. Start with [Consumer APIs](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/) and
[Reading business objects](/docs/integrate/reading-business-objects/), then
[read through a consumer API](/docs/guide/integrate/read-through-a-consumer-api/).
Declared parameters can narrow objects or their related blocks. The same object shape is used
across the contract's reads.

Live reads include saved live corrections, never unpublished proposals. Choose a publication for
a repeatable extract; its continuation stays with the starting snapshot even if a newer one
becomes current. An unsupported operation, wrong contract version or another workspace's record
is refused. Use the model's current contract documentation rather than guessing another path.

**Example:** the reference stops API combines a stop's fields with its names and external codes.
Those outputs are a declaration, not a fixed feature every model must expose.

## Resolve a business object through a consumer API

A consuming system starts with a code, name, ID or related value instead of a known record ID.
[Looking up and resolving](/docs/integrate/looking-up-and-resolving/) explains matching, scores,
ambiguity and translating into a target representation. [Resolve a file of codes](/docs/guide/integrate/resolve-a-file-of-codes/)
connects lookup to batch resolution and per-item found, missing, ambiguous or rejected outcomes.

Narrow ambiguous results using the definition's parameters; never pick an arbitrary tied match.
A unique best object can still have a missing or ambiguous target representation. Review those
separate outcomes before accepting a crosswalk. Use a publication to resolve the whole file
against a fixed dataset. The consumer documentation gives the contract-specific requests and
responses, including limits; broad or oversized lookups must be narrowed or divided.

## Follow a consumer API's changes

An integrator loads a publication, then follows the declared consumer events from its position.
[Consumer events and webhooks](/docs/integrate/consumer-events-and-webhooks/) connects full or
identity-only events, cursors, duplicate recognition and recovery after expiry. Process every
event at a position and keep its continuation; several events can share one raw change position.
Recognise repeated events by their event identity.

For pushed delivery, an authorised administrator [creates a webhook](/docs/guide/administer/create-a-webhook/)
and the integration [subscribes and verifies it](/docs/guide/integrate/subscribe-a-webhook-and-verify-it/).
Verify the signed request, process it safely and acknowledge successful receipt. Failures are
retried before later deliveries; inspect [webhook deliveries](/docs/administer/webhooks/) when
recovery is needed. Changed models, expired events or prolonged failures can suspend a subscription.
A reset skips missed events, so restore a baseline before treating the receiver as current.

Filters can hide the change by which an object leaves their scope. If your copy must remove such
objects, follow the necessary type-wide events and apply narrower criteria locally. This matters
for pull reads and webhook subscriptions alike.

## Automate a reviewed change and its approval handover

[Changes, approvals and publication](/docs/integrate/changes-approvals-and-publication/)
connects capture of an explicit base, versioned writes, complete validation and submission.
Present the differences and diagnostics to a person who may decide under the current policy.
Submission changes no Live data; approval publishes the reviewed version and can still refuse
competing live changes. Keep publication identity and feed position after success.

An open set is not a job that expires under item-result retention. To abandon it, withdraw a
submission where necessary and discard its prepared work. After losing a publication response,
read publication and change-set state before retrying. A consumed proposal can mean success.
Use approval events or inbox operations for review notifications; these are separate from the
data feed used for synchronisation. The page links to each [management operation](/docs/api).

## Administer models and transfer records through the API

[Model and release operations](/docs/integrate/model-and-release-operations/) connects draft
steps, validation, generated documents, installation and activation. Keep the model release
and record versions explicit. A data conversion needs a fresh migration preview with blockers
and losses presented for a person's confirmation; installing alone does not activate.

[Move records between models](/docs/guide/integrate/move-records-between-models/) follows a
saved mapping through selection, complete dry run and loading into change sets. Review omitted
values and dropped relationships as well as successful records. A move needs publication of
the target before source deletions. Changed releases or mappings invalidate an old review.
Use the linked [model operations](/docs/api) rather than editing stored definitions directly.

## Submit an assistant task from an integration

[Assistant tasks](/docs/integrate/assistant-tasks/) explains submitting instructions or a file,
following work, displaying checked changes and accepting a reviewed proposal. The requester
needs **Use AI proposals**, **Bulk and import**, and the permissions for model or change-set
work. This needs the built-in assistant and permission to send values, separately from an
external MCP connection.

Keep the task and job identities. Read current state before every action; distinguish a checked
proposal, a loaded change set and a migration requiring human confirmation. Session work cannot
approve, publish or activate. A matching saved-layout path can activate a draft with the right
permission, so show the actual path and result. Stopping, correcting or discarding can remove
an unpublished result and people's subsequent edits; show that consequence before acting.
Read its data, cost and retention rules, and link users to
[Work with an assistant](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/) for review and recovery.
guide/src/content/docs/journeys/manage-a:
---
title: Manage access
description: Connect sign-in, people, roles, system clients, key rotation and security review.
reader: access-admin
---

These journeys connect getting into refiroo with granting and reviewing access. People and
systems need permission for the work they do, in the workspace where they do it. An administrative
role does not automatically grant access to reference data. Start with
[People and access](/docs/about/people-and-access/) for the distinction between roles and grants.

## Sign in and work

A person opens refiroo, signs in by an offered method and returns to the page they wanted.
[Sign-in](/docs/administer/sign-in/) explains local passwords, an organisation's provider, passkeys
and second factors. [Account](/docs/use/account/) connects personal security settings, password
changes and sessions. Use the account menu to sign out when finished, or end other sessions from
your account when needed.

Repeated failed sign-ins are slowed. If a required second factor is unavailable, use a saved
recovery code or ask an administrator to
[help after a lost device](/docs/guide/administer/help-someone-who-lost-a-device/).
Where mail is configured, a forgotten-password request can provide a fresh one-use link; a reset
does not remove the second factor. If sign-in succeeds but no workspace opens, ask for Browse
access rather than resetting the password again.

## Manage who can do what

A security administrator [adds a person](/docs/guide/administer/add-a-person/), who sets their
password through the one-use link, or arranges the organisation's provider sign-in.
Next read [Roles and grants](/docs/administer/roles-and-grants/) and
[grant a role](/docs/guide/administer/grant-a-role/) directly or through a
[group](/docs/guide/administer/manage-a-group/). Choose the workspace and, when appropriate,
[narrow writes to record types](/docs/guide/administer/narrow-a-grant-to-record-types/).
Browse covers the workspace; narrowing writes does not hide other records there.

Review effective access, including grants inherited through groups and from the installation.
A Reader reads but cannot write; a Contributor proposes changes in change sets. Grants and
activation state take effect on the next request, and jobs recheck their requester's permissions.
The last security administrator cannot be removed. Use [Audit](/docs/administer/audit/) to check
who changed access and investigate a refusal against the action and workspace it names.

## A system calls with a client

An integration team asks a security administrator to create a separate identity for its system.
Read [Clients](/docs/administer/clients/), then
[create a client](/docs/guide/administer/create-a-client/) and save its secret when it is shown
once. Give it management roles for the work it must perform, or
[grant a consumer API](/docs/guide/administer/grant-a-consumer-api-to-a-client/) in the intended
workspace. One kind of grant does not imply the other.

The integrator then follows [system sign-in](/docs/integrate/signing-in-and-tokens/) and
[obtain system access](/docs/guide/integrate/get-a-token/) to connect the system under those grants.
Check allowed work and refused work before relying on it. Later,
[rotate the client secret](/docs/guide/administer/rotate-a-client-secret/) with an overlap when
needed, or deactivate the client to end its access. A deactivated client cannot keep working
with previously issued access. Keep a client separate from a person's browser account so its
activity and grants remain identifiable.

## Rotate a key

A security or integration administrator first identifies which credential needs replacement.
[Signing keys](/docs/administer/signing-keys/) explains ordinary replacement and emergency
retirement; [Rotate signing keys](/docs/guide/administer/rotate-signing-keys/) carries the chosen
action through verification. Normal replacement preserves existing access until expiry.
Emergency retirement ends access signed with the retired key immediately; browser sessions renew
and integrations must obtain fresh access.

For a delivery-signing key, [rotate a webhook key](/docs/guide/administer/rotate-a-webhook-key/)
from that webhook instead. Share the new key securely with its receiver and use the chosen overlap
to maintain verification during handover. These actions do not replace a client's secret.
Changing the encryption key used to store secrets is a separate operator procedure in
[Secrets and keys](/docs/run/secrets-and-keys/); coordinate that work with the operator.

## Check the security model

A security reviewer, administrator or integrator needs to understand where access is enforced
and how to assess the deployment. Begin with [Security, audit and privacy](/docs/about/security-and-trust/),
then compare the intended access with [Roles and grants](/docs/administer/roles-and-grants/) and
[Audit](/docs/administer/audit/). Include direct, group and installation-wide grants, writes
narrowed to types, background work and the separate grants for consumer APIs.

The service enforces permissions across browser and integration operations. Hiding a button is
not the security boundary. Deactivation and revoked permissions affect later requests and job
steps. Use the [Security checklist](/docs/run/security-checklist/) with the operator for HTTPS,
credential storage and deployment controls. Integrators can continue with
[the security model for integrations](/docs/integrate/security-model-for-integrators/).
This review connects the documented rules and evidence; it is not a separate security-checking
screen in refiroo.

## Move people to the organisation's sign-in provider

A security administrator [adds a sign-in provider](/docs/guide/administer/add-a-sign-in-provider/)
and tests complete sign-in, then [links an existing person](/docs/guide/administer/link-a-provider-person/)
where needed to preserve their grants and history. Review any provider-group mappings as well
as direct grants. Changing the provider's credentials requires coordination with its owner;
[Sign-in](/docs/administer/sign-in/) explains the recovery path.

[Require a second factor](/docs/guide/administer/require-a-second-factor/) for local accounts
and prepare recovery before losing a device. When provider sign-in is proven,
[turn off ordinary local sign-in](/docs/guide/administer/turn-off-local-sign-in/) only after
testing the retained local administrator route. That switch keeps accounts, roles and existing
second-factor requirements. Test both intended sign-in and recovery afterwards.

## Tailor a responsibility and remove access when it ends

[Create a custom role](/docs/guide/administer/create-a-custom-role/) from an existing role or
from nothing, choose its action groups, then grant it in the intended scope. Changing it later
affects every holder; copying a role does not keep the copy linked to its source. Review the
[permissions reference](/docs/administer/permissions-reference/) and the recipient's effective
access after changing it. Remove all grants before deleting an unwanted custom role.

When a person leaves, [People and groups](/docs/administer/people-and-groups/) connects
account deactivation, membership and retained attribution. Removing one grant can leave other
access in place. Deactivation stops the next request without erasing data history; refiroo
refuses changes that would remove the last active security administrator.

## Configure publication review and system delivery

[Set an approval policy](/docs/guide/administer/set-an-approval-policy/) with the workspace's
administrator, then use [Change with approval](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/) for an
actual proposal and decision. A changed policy affects waiting decisions too; inspect the
current policy rather than assuming the one used during preparation still applies.

For event delivery, [create a webhook](/docs/guide/administer/create-a-webhook/), agree its
signing key with the receiver and inspect a real delivery. If it stops,
[find out why a webhook paused](/docs/guide/administer/find-out-why-a-webhook-paused/) before
resuming or resetting. Reset can skip changes; restore the receiver's baseline when needed.
See [Webhooks](/docs/administer/webhooks/) for disabling, deleting and rotating delivery keys.

## Control assistant access and inspect AI use

[Manage agent access](/docs/guide/administer/manage-agent-access/) to inspect external-assistant
registrations, clients and call records, or stop an unwanted connection. Its read-and-prepare
ceiling still applies when the underlying person's grants are broader. Ending a personal
connection and blocking an assistant have different scopes.

With **Operations**, [check the AI provider](/docs/guide/administer/check-the-ai-provider/),
read the send policy and inspect calls and costs. Server settings are changed by the operator,
not by this page. [AI administration](/docs/administer/ai/) explains retained records and
separately enabled features; [Work with an assistant](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/)
connects them to their actual tasks.
guide/src/content/docs/journeys/index.md:
---
title: All user journeys
slug: journeys/index
description: Find a complete path through refiroo for data work, model design, access, integration and operations.
reader: evaluator
---

Choose the outcome you want, then follow its journey to the explanations and task guides in the
order you need them. A journey connects the whole task; the linked guides give the detailed steps.

The journeys cover people looking after data, model and access administrators, operators and
systems using the API. Permission and deployment settings determine which actions are available.
Applications and record types come from each workspace's model. Public transport stops, names and
codes from Graubünden are marked examples, rather than fixed applications everyone must use.

## Look after data

Find, maintain and connect records in the workspace you are working in. See [look after data](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/) for the complete paths.

- [Start from home](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#start-from-home).
- [Find and inspect a record](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#find-and-inspect-a-record).
- [Correct a record](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#correct-a-record).
- [Add a record where it belongs](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#add-a-record-where-it-belongs).
- [Delete a record and what depends on it](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#delete-a-record-and-what-depends-on-it).
- [Relate records and maintain their relationships](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#relate-records-and-maintain-their-relationships).
- [Build and change a hierarchy](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#build-and-change-a-hierarchy).
- [Reshape a hierarchy across types, and change a record back](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#reshape-a-hierarchy-across-types-and-change-a-record-back).
- [Review and replace a record's related records](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#review-and-replace-a-records-related-records).
- [See and fill relationship coverage across ancestors](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#see-and-fill-relationship-coverage-across-ancestors).
- [Change many records of a collection at once](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#change-many-records-of-a-collection-at-once).
- [See who changed what](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#see-who-changed-what).
- [Stop offering a value without deleting it](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#stop-offering-a-value-without-deleting-it).
- [Exchange a workbook and repeat the load](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#exchange-a-workbook-and-repeat-the-load).
- [Copy or move records to another workspace](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#copy-or-move-records-to-another-workspace).
- [Continue in a retired or unavailable workspace](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#continue-in-a-retired-or-unavailable-workspace).
- [Adjust the display and work with a keyboard](/docs/journeys/look-after-data/#adjust-the-display-and-work-with-a-keyboard).

## Change with approval

Prepare coordinated proposals, review them and bring them into Live safely. See [change with approval](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/) for the complete paths.

- [Prepare and publish a coordinated design](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/#prepare-and-publish-a-coordinated-design).
- [Continue live work while a change set is open](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/#continue-live-work-while-a-change-set-is-open).
- [Withdraw a publication and start reviewed changes from history](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/#withdraw-a-publication-and-start-reviewed-changes-from-history).
- [Review what a change set changes](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/#review-what-a-change-set-changes).
- [Prepare under the next model version while live keeps the current one](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/#prepare-under-the-next-model-version-while-live-keeps-the-current-one).
- [Propose and approve a change](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/#propose-and-approve-a-change).
- [Resume or abandon unfinished work](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/#resume-or-abandon-unfinished-work).

## Work with an assistant

Review machine-made proposals and keep control of what changes. See [work with an assistant](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/) for access, disclosure, costs, retention and review.

- [Use AI proposals](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/#use-ai-proposals).
- [Targets for unmapped values](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/#targets-for-unmapped-values).
- [Load a workbook, or change records, with the assistant](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/#load-a-workbook-or-change-records-with-the-assistant).
- [Reach refiroo from an assistant](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/#reach-refiroo-from-an-assistant).
- [An assistant reads](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/#an-assistant-reads).
- [An assistant prepares a change](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/#an-assistant-prepares-a-change).
- [Ask in words](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/#ask-in-words).
- [What changed in a period](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/#what-changed-in-a-period).
- [Reuse a checked layout or stop using AI](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/#reuse-a-checked-layout-or-stop-using-ai).

## Shape a model

Define applications and data rules, load workbooks and manage workspace releases. See [shape a model](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/) for the complete paths.

- [Create and activate an application-model release](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#create-and-activate-an-application-model-release).
- [Administer workspaces](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#administer-workspaces).
- [Define a consumer API in the model](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#define-a-consumer-api-in-the-model).
- [Design a model in the editor](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#design-a-model-in-the-editor).
- [Onboard a workbook](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#onboard-a-workbook).
- [Load the next version of a workbook](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#load-the-next-version-of-a-workbook).
- [Run a workspace on a model of its own](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#run-a-workspace-on-a-model-of-its-own).
- [Move a workspace to another release](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#move-a-workspace-to-another-release).
- [Move data between workspaces whose models differ](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#move-data-between-workspaces-whose-models-differ).
- [An account of a model change](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#an-account-of-a-model-change).
- [Add types, fields and relationships](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#add-types-fields-and-relationships).
- [Arrange navigation, views and record pages](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#arrange-navigation-views-and-record-pages).
- [Refine a draft without losing identity or colleagues' work](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#refine-a-draft-without-losing-identity-or-colleagues-work).
- [Recheck a workbook design or a saved mapping](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#recheck-a-workbook-design-or-a-saved-mapping).
- [Maintain released contracts and definitions](/docs/journeys/shape-a-model/#maintain-released-contracts-and-definitions).

## Integrate a system

Connect another system through complete reads, controlled writes and reliable change delivery. See [integrate a system](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/) for the complete paths.

- [Discover the model and the API](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#discover-the-model-and-the-api).
- [Read a collection completely and resume](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#read-a-collection-completely-and-resume).
- [Request the precise dataset an integration needs](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#request-the-precise-dataset-an-integration-needs).
- [Answer a business-date question](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#answer-a-business-date-question).
- [Submit a bounded bulk change](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#submit-a-bounded-bulk-change).
- [Run a large background job and recover](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#run-a-large-background-job-and-recover).
- [Follow changes reliably](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#follow-changes-reliably).
- [Exchange a supplier file](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#exchange-a-supplier-file).
- [Read a business object through a consumer API](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#read-a-business-object-through-a-consumer-api).
- [Resolve a business object through a consumer API](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#resolve-a-business-object-through-a-consumer-api).
- [Follow a consumer API's changes](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#follow-a-consumer-apis-changes).
- [Automate a reviewed change and its approval handover](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#automate-a-reviewed-change-and-its-approval-handover).
- [Administer models and transfer records through the API](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#administer-models-and-transfer-records-through-the-api).
- [Submit an assistant task from an integration](/docs/journeys/integrate-a-system/#submit-an-assistant-task-from-an-integration).

## Manage access

Sign in, grant people and systems access, and review its security. See [manage access](/docs/journeys/manage-access/) for the complete paths.

- [Sign in and work](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#sign-in-and-work).
- [Manage who can do what](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#manage-who-can-do-what).
- [A system calls with a client](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#a-system-calls-with-a-client).
- [Rotate a key](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#rotate-a-key).
- [Check the security model](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#check-the-security-model).
- [Move people to the organisation's sign-in provider](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#move-people-to-the-organisations-sign-in-provider).
- [Tailor a responsibility and remove access when it ends](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#tailor-a-responsibility-and-remove-access-when-it-ends).
- [Configure publication review and system delivery](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#configure-publication-review-and-system-delivery).
- [Control assistant access and inspect AI use](/docs/journeys/manage-access/#control-assistant-access-and-inspect-ai-use).

## Run the service

Start, inspect and recover the deployment. See [run the service](/docs/journeys/run-the-service/) for the complete paths.

- [Run the service, and recover from an expected refusal](/docs/journeys/run-the-service/#run-the-service-and-recover-from-an-expected-refusal).
- [Check what a deployment runs and how it is configured](/docs/journeys/run-the-service/#check-what-a-deployment-runs-and-how-it-is-configured).
- [Open a production installation over HTTPS](/docs/journeys/run-the-service/#open-a-production-installation-over-https).
- [Upgrade and recover a failed cutover](/docs/journeys/run-the-service/#upgrade-and-recover-a-failed-cutover).
- [Back up, rehearse and move to another host](/docs/journeys/run-the-service/#back-up-rehearse-and-move-to-another-host).
- [Replace secrets and watch growing storage](/docs/journeys/run-the-service/#replace-secrets-and-watch-growing-storage).
- [Enable optional AI or prepare a developer instance](/docs/journeys/run-the-service/#enable-optional-ai-or-prepare-a-developer-instance).

## Receive notices

Set up mail and choose how to hear about work and publications. See [receive notices](/docs/journeys/receive-notices/) for the complete paths.

- [Send mail](/docs/journeys/receive-notices/#send-mail).
- [Notification digests and following a workspace](/docs/journeys/receive-notices/#notification-digests-and-following-a-workspace).

If you are new to refiroo, start with [What is refiroo?](/docs/about/what-is-refiroo/) and
[How it works](/docs/about/how-it-works/), then choose a journey above.
guide/src/content/docs/journeys/change-w:
---
title: Change with approval
description: Prepare coordinated changes, review differences, obtain approval and publish safely.
reader: steward
---

Use these journeys when related changes must reach Live together, need review, or depend on a
model release. A change set holds the proposal; a publication preserves the result. Read
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) for their states and permissions. Work in change sets,
Publish and Approve publications are separate permissions; a reviewer does not automatically
have permission to decide or publish.

## Prepare and publish a coordinated design

A person preparing changes, or an integrator, starts a change set from current Live data or a
retained publication. Follow [Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/)
to name the proposal, make the ordinary record and relationship changes, review them, and validate
the whole result. Publish when validation, access and approval policy permit it. Then inspect the
new [publication](/docs/use/publications/) and its source.

Staged edits remain invisible to Live readers until publication. Publication applies all proposed
changes together, or none. A failed validation or conflict keeps the proposal for correction.
Installing a model or saving a record inside the proposal does not publish it.

**Example:** a coordinated change can update the validity dates of several stops for a timetable
change. The dates are data; publication is the act that makes the prepared changes live.

## Continue live work while a change set is open

A steward keeps routine corrections moving while colleagues prepare a larger proposal. Read
[how a change set works apart from Live](/docs/use/change-sets/#working-apart-from-live), then
[continue live work](/docs/guide/use/continue-live-work-while-a-change-set-is-open/) in the Live
context. Later publication applies only the proposal's changes: live additions and corrections to
untouched records survive.

If both sides changed the same record, publication stops and names it, even when different fields
were edited. Inspect the live record and the proposal before deciding how to revise the work.
Successful earlier validation does not reserve the live data.

## Withdraw a publication and start reviewed changes from history

A person responsible for publication, or an integrator, begins by
[browsing a publication](/docs/guide/use/browse-a-publication/) as it was saved. If the current
publication should no longer be designated current,
[withdraw it](/docs/guide/use/withdraw-a-publication/). Its snapshot and history remain readable;
Live is unchanged and no older publication becomes current automatically.

Next, [start from an earlier publication](/docs/guide/use/start-from-an-earlier-publication/),
prepare explicit corrections and return to review, validation and publication. Choosing an older
source does not roll back Live. Newer live records that the proposal leaves untouched are kept.
See [Publications](/docs/use/publications/) for the difference between Current, earlier and Withdrawn.

## Review what a change set changes

A reviewer or integrator opens the proposal to understand its effects before deciding.
[Review what a change set changes](/docs/guide/use/review-what-a-change-set-changes/)
connects record changes and relationship changes, their filters and the before-and-after details.
Inspect additions, removals, moves, changed types and fields across the complete lists.

“Before” is the proposal's starting data, including an older publication when that was its source.
The review explains the authored differences; validation and publication also check their combined
effect against current Live. If nothing matches a filter, clear it before assuming the proposal
is empty. Continue to [approval](#propose-and-approve-a-change) or direct publication as permitted.

## Prepare under the next model version while live keeps the current one

A person preparing a proposal works with a model administrator to use a candidate release before
Live switches to it. First [install the release](/docs/model/releases/) without activating it.
Then [prepare under the next model version](/docs/guide/use/prepare-under-the-next-model-version/).
The change set's forms and rules follow that release; Live and other proposals keep theirs.
Starting data must fit the chosen release.

Normal publication needs matching releases. Coordinate activation with the administrator.
If records require conversion, read [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/): either move the proposal
to the workspace's current release, or review a workspace migration combined with publication.
Each preview changes nothing, lists any losses and blockers, and must be refreshed if stale.
Moving a proposal alone changes no live data. A submitted proposal must leave its waiting state
before editing or changing its release; discarding remains an option for abandoned work.

## Propose and approve a change

A contributor prepares a change set, then submits it to someone allowed to approve publications.
Start with [Propose a change](/docs/guide/use/propose-a-change/), read
[Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/), and follow
[Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/) from submission to decision.
Submission validates and freezes the proposed version without changing Live. The approver opens
the notified request, reviews its differences and either approves and publishes or sends it back
with a required comment. The submitter receives the decision and can correct and resubmit returned work.

A workspace's [approval policy](/docs/administer/approval-policies/) determines whether approval
and a second person are required. With a second-person rule, the submitter cannot decide their own
request. To resume editing while waiting, the submitter or an authorised approver withdraws the
request; that keeps the proposed changes. Approval rechecks current data and can still refuse a
conflict. Reload and review the current request before another decision.

## Resume or abandon unfinished work

An open change set remains until published or discarded; job retention does not expire it.
Reopen it, check its context and review its current differences before continuing. Live or model
changes since the last visit can require fresh validation or a migration. See
[Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/).

If the proposal is no longer needed, withdraw a waiting submission before discarding it.
Discarding removes proposed work, while sending it back keeps it available for correction.
Neither undoes Live or removes a publication. After a lost publication response, inspect
publications and history before repeating the request: a consumed change set can mean that
publication succeeded. [Changes, approvals and publication](/docs/integrate/changes-approvals-and-publication/)
explains the corresponding integration recovery.
guide/src/content/docs/journeys/receive-:
---
title: Receive notices
description: Connect outgoing mail setup with personal email choices, digests and workspace following.
reader: steward
---

Use these journeys to hear about work that needs attention without continually opening each
proposal or job. Administrators provide outgoing mail; each person chooses email for their own
inbox. Inbox notices and workspace following also work without mail. These features do not require
an assistant or AI configuration.

## Send mail

A security administrator connects the instance to an outgoing mail server so people can receive
account links and the notices they choose. Start with [Mail](/docs/administer/mail/), then
[set up mail](/docs/guide/administer/set-up-mail/) and send a test message. Check that it reaches
the intended mailbox and that its application link points to the address people can open.
The server accepting a message does not prove it reached the inbox.

Ordinary messages wait for background delivery. Inspect waiting, sent and failed entries on the
Mail page; temporary failures retry, while permanent failures or exhausted retries need attention.
The reason distinguishes connection, secure connection, login and recipient problems. Correct the
cause with the mail administrator or operator. [Sign-in and mail setup](/docs/run/sign-in-and-mail-setup/)
explains the operator's part. Removing settings stops sending but does not immediately erase the
waiting queue. Stopping an individual message does not revoke a password link already created.

For a person receiving a new-account or reset link, follow it once to set a password and then sign
in. An expired or used link needs a fresh one; an existing second factor remains required.
Read [Account](/docs/use/account/) for personal sign-in security. For optional inbox email,
continue with the next journey.

## Notification digests and following a workspace

A person starts with [Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/) to understand the
notices and the work they open. Then read [Notification settings](/docs/use/notifications-settings/)
and [set up email notices](/docs/guide/use/set-up-email-notices/). Email starts off. Where mail
is configured and the account has an address, enable it and choose **At once**, **Digest** or
**Off** for each kind. These preferences do not remove notices from the inbox.

A digest can come every morning or on Mondays at 07:00 in the browser's time zone. Check the
saved zone and next digest time. It counts eligible unread, unhandled notices and lists the newest
50 with links; an empty digest is not sent. Reading or handling a notice before delivery can remove
it from the message. The email contains kinds, times, counts and links rather than record, workspace,
file or people's names. Digest notices do not use immediate mail's 24-hour cutoff.

To hear about another person's publication, [follow a workspace](/docs/guide/use/follow-a-workspace/)
from its Home card. Following needs Browse and adds inbox notices; email copies depend on your
choices above. Your own publications do not send you follower notices. Open a notice to inspect
its publication where it is still available and you still have access. The notice can remain after
its destination is no longer openable.

Stop following from Home or notification settings when no longer needed. Losing Browse or account
deactivation pauses notices while keeping the choice, so they can resume if access returns.
If email does not arrive, check the inbox, address, mail availability and saved choices before
assuming publication or approval failed. A refused settings change keeps the previous preferences.
guide/src/content/docs/about/three-kinds:
---
title: Three kinds of change
description: Choose between correcting live data, preparing coordinated changes and changing the model.
reader: evaluator
---

refiroo separates three kinds of change: a live edit, a coordinated change set and a model release. Daily work continues while related changes are prepared separately; approval policies can require review before publication. See [What refiroo is](/docs/about/what-is-refiroo/) for how these choices fit together.

| You need to… | Use… | What becomes different |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correct today's data | A live edit | The saved record is immediately current. |
| Prepare related data changes | A change set | Its changes become live together when published. |
| Change what the application allows | A model draft and release | The workspace uses the new definition when it is activated there. |

## Correct today's data

A person with permission can add, edit or delete live records without naming a change set. Saving records the change in history and protects against overwriting a newer version. It does not create a publication or a model release.

For example, correcting a stop's name in the Graubünden data is an ordinary live edit. Changing a model-defined availability field is also an edit: its business meaning is separate from publication status. See [Records](/docs/use/records/).

## Prepare related changes

A change set lets people prepare several changes away from Live. It starts from live data or an earlier publication and has its own proposed content. **Review changes** shows additions, changes and removals, including fields before and after. Validation checks the complete result without publishing.

Publishing applies the prepared changes over current Live data and creates the next read-only publication in the same operation. Unrelated live edits survive. A conflict or invalid result publishes nothing and keeps the prepared work. Review the reported conflicts; a new change set from current Live data is the way to prepare a fresh proposal when the old source no longer fits.

Where the workspace's approval policy requires it, the author submits the change set for a permitted reviewer to decide. The submitted content is frozen; withdraw the request before editing it. Approval publishes the reviewed content. See [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) and [Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/).

## Change what the application allows

A model administrator edits a model draft to add a field, change a relationship rule or offer another view. Validation checks the definition; a preview or dry run helps examine its effect. Installing makes an immutable model release. Activation selects it for a workspace, leaving other workspaces on their own releases.

Installing alone changes no workspace. A release that existing data does not fit cannot simply be activated: the administrator reviews a migration, including any potential loss, before confirming it. An unsupported model language or invalid definition must be corrected rather than overridden. See [Model releases](/docs/model/releases/) and [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/).

## Ask the right history question

| Question | Where to look |
| --- | --- |
| Who changed this record, and what changed? | [Record history](/docs/use/history/). Some older entries lack an author or a previous value. |
| What did a coordinated publication contain? | Its [publication](/docs/use/publications/), preserved even after later live edits. |
| Which fields and rules did a model define? | The installed [model release](/docs/model/releases/). |
| Which records were valid on a business date? | A [business-date read](/docs/integrate/business-dates/), for types whose model declares a validity period. |

A business-date read is not a reconstruction of everything stored on that date. A publication is not an archive of every intervening live edit. Withdrawing a publication removes its current designation without undoing data; starting a change set from it is not a full restore. Recovery of an entire dataset belongs to [backup and restore](/docs/run/backup-and-restore/).

## Keep something readable without offering it for new work

Changing a record's model-defined availability or validity dates can keep its identity and
history while ending its use under the agreed reading rules. It does not delete the record,
withdraw a publication or schedule publication for a future date. See
[Stop offering a value](/docs/guide/use/stop-offering-a-value/).

Retiring a model release instead hides it from future choices; workspaces already using it keep
working. Retiring a workspace preserves reading and stops changes. These choices have different
consequences from permanent deletion. See [Releases](/docs/model/releases/) and
[Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/).
guide/src/content/docs/about/how-it-work:
---
title: How refiroo works
description: Models give records their rules; workspaces hold live data, change sets and publications.
reader: evaluator
---

One engine, many applications: a model defines what people can keep and how they work with it. Connections keep their meaning through the model’s relationship rules. Each workspace holds its data under its own selected model release; several workspaces in one installation can share a model or use different ones. See [What refiroo is](/docs/about/what-is-refiroo/) for the overview.

## The model gives data its meaning

An **application model**, usually called a **model**, defines applications, record types, fields, relationships and views. An **application** groups relevant types and views into a working area.

A **record type**, also called an **object type** in the model editor, defines one kind of item. A **record** is an item of that type. A **field**, also called an attribute, holds a typed value: text, a number, a date or a yes/no value. Fields can be reused across types. A **binding** says where a reusable field or relationship may be used and which rules apply there.

The model determines which views an application offers. A table, tree, mapping grid or relation matrix is available because the model declares it and the data's structure supports it. See [Applications](/docs/use/applications/) and [Types, attributes and relations](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/).

## Connections carry meaning

A **relationship** is a named, directed connection between records. Its rules decide which types may connect, how many connections they may hold and whether a connection is required.

**Containment** is the parent/child relationship that gives a record its place in a hierarchy. Moving a record updates its parent and that relationship together; editing an ordinary relationship cannot move it. A **hierarchy editor** is a tree view for browsing and maintaining this structure.

A **mapping** connects a value to its equivalent or representation elsewhere. A mapping grid helps people find sources with no target or several possible targets. A **relation matrix** compares records against groups defined by an ancestor type, making missing connections visible as empty cells.

Translations are one use of records and relationships: a language-specific record connects to the thing it names and belongs to a language group. They are configured in a model, rather than built into every record. See the [translation example](/docs/examples/translations/).

Read more about [relationships](/docs/use/relationships/), [hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/), [mapping grids](/docs/use/mapping-grids/) and [relation matrices](/docs/use/relation-matrices/).

## One workspace, several views of its data

![One workspace holds editable Live data, change sets prepared separately, and read-only publications. Publishing applies a change set to Live and records a publication.](/docs/about/workspace.svg)

**Live** is the workspace's current data. A direct live edit takes effect when saved. A **record version** protects each save: if the record changed after it was read, the save is refused as a **conflict** so that newer work is not silently overwritten.

A **change set** holds coordinated changes away from Live. Its **candidate** is the proposed complete content: the source data with its prepared changes applied. Validate the change set to check that result, then publish it to apply its changes together over current Live data.

Publishing also creates a **publication**, an immutable snapshot. Immutable means its content cannot be edited afterwards. **Publication N** uses a number counted within the workspace; this continues across model releases and is separate from a record version. Later live edits do not rewrite publications.

Withdraw a publication to remove its current designation; this leaves Live and history unchanged. Retire a workspace to make its data, change sets and publications read-only. See [Workspaces](/docs/use/workspaces/), [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) and [Publications](/docs/use/publications/).

## Change the rules separately

A **model draft** proposes changes to the definition. Install a validated draft to create an immutable **model release**. Activate the release to use it in a workspace; installing alone does not switch the workspace. Existing data must fit the selected release, or an administrator must review a migration.

[Three kinds of change](/docs/about/three-kinds-of-change/) explains when to edit Live, prepare a change set or change the model. [Model releases](/docs/model/releases/) explains installation and activation.

## Shape the working screens

A model administrator uses [the model editor](/docs/model/the-model-editor/) to change a draft,
review its issues and history, and preview it against records without changing those records.
[Types, attributes and relations](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/) defines the reusable
fields, permitted parents, ownership and candidate rules behind the screens.

[Applications and views](/docs/model/applications-and-views/) chooses collections, navigation
groups and the table, tree, mapping-grid or relation-matrix views each collection offers.
[Record pages and tables](/docs/model/record-pages-and-tables/) arranges fields, related-record
panels, columns, filters and sort choices. Hiding a panel changes presentation; it does not
remove stored data or revoke access.

[Issues and dry runs](/docs/model/issues-and-dry-run/) distinguishes a valid definition from
one that also fits existing records or a proposed workbook load. [Workbook proposals](/docs/model/workbook-proposals/)
can help turn sheets and columns into a reviewed design. The [specialist workbench](/docs/model/json-view/)
handles supported definitions without visual forms; an absent form does not necessarily mean
the capability is unavailable.

For later changes, use [migrations](/docs/model/migrations/) to convert existing data under an explicit
loss review. A [model mapping](/docs/model/model-mappings/) describes how records transfer
between workspaces with different definitions. Neither installing a draft nor switching to
another workspace transfers records by itself.
guide/src/content/docs/about/accessibili:
---
title: Accessibility and devices
