description: Keyboard operation, display choices and narrow-screen layouts, with the limits of recorded accessibility evidence.
reader: evaluator
---

refiroo includes keyboard navigation, visible focus and layouts for narrow screens. Appearance choices let people adjust how much information they see and how it is displayed.

## Work with a keyboard

A **Skip to main content** link bypasses repeated navigation. Labelled regions, semantic tables and trees, and named controls provide structure. Menus and dialogs support keyboard operation; dialogs keep focus inside while open and restore it when closed. Editors guard against leaving unsaved input behind.

Trees support arrow-key navigation and record menus. **Move to…** provides an alternative to dragging records. Resizable panel separators can be focused and adjusted with arrow keys; Shift makes larger changes, and Home and End choose their limits.

Long lists load and draw a bounded part of their records. Use the collection's search to find records throughout the list: the browser's Find sees only rows currently drawn. See [Appearance and devices](/docs/use/appearance-and-devices/) for keyboard details and [Finding records](/docs/use/lists-and-filters/) for list navigation.

## Choose the display

**Settings → Appearance** offers **Current**, **Hearth**, **Studio**, **Instrument** and **Website purple** under **Theme**.
The separate **Light or dark** choice offers **System**, **Light** and **Dark**; System follows
the device's light or dark setting. Every theme works with either light or dark. **Table density** sets a comfortable or compact default; a table's own display choice can override it. **Type colours** offers two palettes, and **Edit pencil** controls whether edit hints appear on hover and focus or remain faintly visible. Touch screens always show the hints.

Choices take effect immediately without a Save button and are saved in that browser, so another
browser or device keeps its own settings. To reset them, choose **Current**, **System**,
**Comfortable**, **B: magenta and olive** and **On hover and focus** again. Panel widths can be adjusted where the layout offers a separator. See [Change how refiroo looks](/docs/guide/use/change-how-refiroo-looks/).

## Use a phone or touch screen

On a narrow screen, navigation moves into a drawer and panels can stack or use tabs. Workspace, application and Live, change-set or publication choices remain accessible in the band beneath the top bar. Tables can show fewer columns initially, with a control to reveal the rest.

![A collection on a phone, with workspace, application and Live choices, search, filters and a control to show all columns.](/docs/screens/list-phone.png)

Above: the Network application in the Graubünden workspace, showing stops on a phone-sized screen. This is one model's use of the same collection layout. Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02.

A tap opens a record. In an editable tree, holding a record still before moving begins a touch drag; moving sooner scrolls instead. The record's menu provides **Move to…** where dragging is inconvenient. See [Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/).

## What has been checked

The project has automated accessibility checks using axe and visual regression checks for main screens, including light and dark themes. Those checks help catch structural and appearance regressions. They do not prove that every task works with every assistive technology.

**No screen-reader user testing has been recorded.** No formal accessibility conformance claim is made here. Evaluate the workflows and assistive devices your team needs, and report barriers with the screen, action, browser and assistive technology involved.
guide/src/content/docs/about/how-it-is-b:
---
title: How refiroo is built
description: A web application and API service backed by PostgreSQL, with persistent background work.
reader: evaluator
---

One engine serves many model-defined applications through a web front end and an API service backed by PostgreSQL. The browser and integrations use the service; they do not write database tables directly. See [What refiroo is](/docs/about/what-is-refiroo/) for what this lets a team do.

## One service, shared rules

The service validates the model and uses it to interpret records, fields, relationships and views. It supplies the same data rules to ordinary edits, bulk jobs, imports and publication. The browser renders the views defined by the model rather than implementing a separate application for each domain.

The backend uses Python 3.14 and FastAPI, served by Uvicorn, with Pydantic 2 for typed inputs, SQLAlchemy 2 for database access and Alembic for database migrations. PostgreSQL holds model releases, reference data, history and operational state; the reference installation uses PostgreSQL 17 with ICU text collation. The web front end uses React and TypeScript, built with Vite.

Docker Compose runs the reference installation. Its nginx 1.28 web server serves the interface and forwards API requests to the engine. For [automatic HTTPS](/docs/run/https/), an optional Caddy 2 service obtains and renews certificates through ACME, using Let's Encrypt or ZeroSSL. An organisation can instead supply its own certificates or use its existing HTTPS proxy. The [operator overview](/docs/run/overview/) explains what to deploy.

## Standards and formats

People can sign in through an organisation's OpenID Connect provider or local accounts. Local accounts support WebAuthn passkeys and time-based one-time passwords (TOTP) from authenticator apps. External systems authenticate with OAuth 2.0 client credentials. See [Who can do what](/docs/about/people-and-access/).

The APIs publish OpenAPI 3.1 contract documents. Consumer webhooks use HMAC-SHA256 signatures and offer a native message format or CloudEvents 1.0 messages. File exchange supports Excel .xlsx workbooks and CSV; notifications use SMTP mail. Operators can collect Prometheus metrics. These connections are configured by the organisation; reading the interface does not require a hosted analytics service.

## Open-source components

refiroo uses the AGPL-3.0-or-later licence. Its dependencies have their own licences. FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, React, Vite, Astro, Starlight and the Scalar API-reference viewer use the MIT licence. Uvicorn and the WebAuthn verification library use BSD-3-Clause; the psycopg PostgreSQL driver uses LGPL-3.0-only. The repository's third-party notices list the bundled components and their licence texts, including libraries bundled with the driver.

See [Licence and compatibility](/docs/about/compatibility-and-licence/) for the running installation's source offer, and [Licence and source](/docs/run/licence-and-source/) for configuring it.

## Background work survives a restart

Larger imports, exports and data changes can run as background jobs. Job parameters, progress and outcomes are stored in the database. Workers in the service claim jobs and checkpoint their work. If a process stops, another worker can resume work whose claim has expired.

A completed part of an independent load remains applied; an all-or-nothing operation has different transaction rules. Jobs report what happened rather than treating cancellation as an undo. See [Background jobs](/docs/run/background-jobs/).

## Several processes can share the database

The standard container starts one API process. Several processes or servers can use the same PostgreSQL database. Database coordination protects startup, writes and job claims. Each request resolves the workspace's model release, so a release changed through one process is picked up by the others on their next request.

An operator must configure shared signing material and shared job-file storage where requests can reach different processes. Monitoring reports the processes and workspaces they serve. See [Several processes](/docs/run/several-processes/) and [Monitoring](/docs/run/monitoring/).

## Documentation stays with the installation

The guide is built with Astro and Starlight, with local Pagefind search, and bundled with the installation. Its pages, fonts and scripts are served locally, so reading it needs no outside service. The [API reference](/docs/api) also bundles its Scalar viewer by default and disables hosted extras. An operator can deliberately choose an externally hosted viewer script instead; that option needs internet access.

This local delivery concerns viewing documentation and the interface. Configured sign-in providers, mail servers and webhook receivers are separate connections chosen by the organisation.

## Operation includes recovery

Startup checks refuse unsafe database and model states with a reason and a recovery instruction. Health checks distinguish a process that answers from one ready to serve data. Operators can rehearse restoring a backup into a separate database and inspect the result.

Activating an older model release does not restore older data. See [Health and startup checks](/docs/run/health-and-startup-checks/) and [Backup and restore](/docs/run/backup-and-restore/).

## Plan the installation's lifetime

[Configuration](/docs/run/configure/) controls capability switches and limits; the
[command-line tools](/docs/run/command-line/) support operator maintenance without browser
access. [The database](/docs/run/database/) explains connection budgets and storage growth.
[Sign-in and mail setup](/docs/run/sign-in-and-mail-setup/) connects the public address to
identity providers and outgoing messages, and [webhook delivery](/docs/run/webhook-delivery/)
explains receiver failures, retries and recovery.

[Upgrades](/docs/run/upgrades/) covers software cutover and refusal recovery.
[Model releases and rollback](/docs/run/model-releases-and-rollback/) distinguishes choosing an
older compatible model from restoring the application's database. [Backup and restore](/docs/run/backup-and-restore/)
includes files and matching keys as well as PostgreSQL, and covers moving to a replacement host.
Deleting deployment storage is not a recovery procedure.

[AI operation](/docs/run/ai/) covers the optional provider, assistant and external-agent
connection; [Set up AI](/docs/run/set-up-ai/) gives the installation steps. A
[developer instance](/docs/run/developer-instance/) serves local code work and has a different
support boundary from the reference Compose installation.

The [production checklist](/docs/run/production-checklist/) brings together transport,
access, storage, monitoring and restore checks. Production sizing and recovery time depend
on the organisation's workload; these pages do not promise a measured capacity for it.
guide/src/content/docs/about/security-an:
---
title: Security, audit and privacy
description: How refiroo controls access, records activity and protects credentials.
reader: evaluator
---

Governed changes need a record of who changed what. refiroo requires people and systems to sign in before accessing reference data, checks permissions on each operation and records changes in history. Review comments can explain why a proposed change was approved or sent back. See [What refiroo is](/docs/about/what-is-refiroo/) for the overview.

## Access is checked by the service

Hiding an editing control is only a convenience. The service enforces roles and workspace grants on browser actions, file loads and API operations. Background jobs recheck the requester's rights as they run. A deactivated person or client loses access on the next request; ending a browser session also ends its use.

Public documentation, contract documents, sign-in services and health checks have deliberate exceptions to data authentication. Their availability does not make reference data public. See [Who can do what](/docs/about/people-and-access/) and [Sign-in](/docs/administer/sign-in/).

## Sign-in and credentials

Local accounts support TOTP authenticator codes and WebAuthn passkeys. An organisation's OpenID Connect sign-in provider brings its own sign-in policy. Repeated failed local sign-ins are slowed, and the failure message does not reveal whether the e-mail address or the password was wrong. People can inspect and end their sessions on [Account](/docs/use/account/).

Passwords are stored as hashes. Secrets that refiroo must use again, such as provider credentials and webhook signing keys, are encrypted in storage with an operator-managed key. Secrets are not ordinary reference-data fields and are not included in activity records. Protecting the encryption key and backups remains an operator responsibility; changing a key requires the documented recovery procedure.

For a public installation, refiroo provides [automatic HTTPS](/docs/run/https/): Caddy obtains a Let's Encrypt or ZeroSSL certificate and renews it before it expires. You do not need to buy a certificate, install certificate files or renew it by hand. The operator points the public name's DNS at the host, keeps port 443 reachable from the internet (port 80 is optional for redirects) and preserves the certificate storage volume. An organisation can instead use its own certificates or an existing HTTPS proxy.

Production installations also need protected database access and controlled operator credentials. See [Secrets and keys](/docs/run/secrets-and-keys/) and the [Security checklist](/docs/run/security-checklist/).

## Know who changed what

Data history names the person or client responsible, including the requester behind a job. Security activity separately records sign-ins, changes to people and clients, role grants and group membership. A security administrator can inspect that activity; data history remains limited to workspaces the reader may browse.

Attribution uses the person's or client's current name, even after deactivation. Older data changes without attribution show **Before sign-in**. History can expose names and previous reference-data values to authorised readers, so access and retention need to match your organisation's policy. See [History](/docs/use/history/) and [Audit](/docs/administer/audit/).

## Sharing creates another trust boundary

A webhook sends data to the configured receiver. Deliveries are signed so the receiver can verify their origin; signing does not encrypt their content. Production receivers use HTTPS. Operators and integration administrators must choose appropriate receivers and protect their signing keys.

Files and consumer APIs also disclose the data their reader is allowed to obtain. Grant only the access each integration needs. See [Consumer events and webhooks](/docs/integrate/consumer-events-and-webhooks/) and [Clients](/docs/administer/clients/).

## AI help stays under your control

AI is optional. Your operator can enable a provider for proposed mapping targets, questions turned
into list filters and explanations of changes. The built-in assistant uses Claude Code to prepare
models and records from your words or a workbook. These are enabled separately. External assistants
can connect through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) when agent access is enabled.

Built-in AI actions need **Use AI proposals**, as well as the permissions for the work itself.
The Data steward, Data owner, Model administrator, Workspace administrator and Integration
administrator roles include that permission. Access still depends on the workspace grant.
An external assistant uses its person's or client's grants, limited to reading and preparing
change sets; it cannot approve or publish, even when that person can.

### What may leave the instance

The operator chooses a send level for built-in AI help:

| Level | Information allowed to be sent |
| --- | --- |
| structure | Model names, field names, headers, types and counts, without stored record values. Your question is still sent. |
| samples | Also sample values within the operator's limit. A question in words can send a whole related list of at most 50 record names, including ancestor names, regardless of that sample limit. |
| values | The record values the task needs. This is required for mapping targets and the built-in assistant. |

The assistant receives your words, the workspace's model and the whole workbook if you attach one,
and reads records as needed within your access. A model-change explanation sends differences and
counts without record values. A history explanation includes names of records, people, change sets
and files only at values. Read the disclosure beside the action before asking.

An outside provider receives this information under your organisation's agreement with it. A
provider hosted inside your organisation can keep its requests there. Send levels do not govern
what an external MCP assistant does with permitted data after reading it. Check its service and
retention policy separately. [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) explains each feature's
information, access and limits.

### Review the proposal and its evidence

AI can misunderstand instructions, and text in reference data can mislead an assistant. Inspect
the proposed records, relationships and model, not just its explanation. Proposed mappings and
loads wait in a change set for your correction, approval and publication. The built-in assistant
cannot activate, approve or publish. A whole-type model migration has a different review: a person's
explicit migration confirmation changes live data and its model together.

Questions in words become editable filters rather than record changes. Explanations cite facts
computed by refiroo; follow those references before deciding. The explanation can be wrong, and
does not certify that a change is safe. If the provider fails, model and history facts remain
available. See [Work with an assistant](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/) for the complete paths.

A matching saved workbook layout can be loaded without an assistant session. That ordinary loading
path can also activate a changed draft when the requester has **Model release** permission. Review
the shown next steps rather than assuming every task ends in the same kind of proposal. See
[Loading with the assistant](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/).

### Costs and retained information

Requests and assistant turns can incur charges or consume a subscription allowance, including
failed or discarded work. Operations staff can inspect who asked, the purpose, outcome, tokens
and reported cost on **Settings › This instance › AI**. An absent cost is not proof of free use.
A saved workbook layout that fits the next file can avoid another assistant session.

Call records are kept. Request and answer text is absent from the call log by default; an
operator can enable it for a limited period, normally seven days. This does not remove the
separate assistant task: its instructions, proposal, checks and workbook normally remain for
90 days after completion or the last change. Session files and transcripts remain while the task
can continue, including after a stop or failure and while a loaded change set awaits publication.
They are cleaned up when finished work is next checked, or on expiry. Published data and history
remain. The provider's retention is separate. [Running AI](/docs/run/ai/) explains configuration,
retention and billing in full.

External assistant calls have a separate record of the caller, tool, argument names and outcome,
without argument values. You can end a personal assistant's session from your account. A security
administrator can block an assistant or deactivate its client; access stops on its next call.
See [Agent access](/docs/administer/agent-access/).

Report suspected vulnerabilities privately to **security@refiroo.org**, or use the repository's private reporting option described in its [security policy](https://github.com/refiroo/refiroo/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
guide/src/content/docs/about/people-and-:
---
title: Who can do what
description: Roles, workspace grants and sign-in keep responsibility separate from access.
reader: evaluator
---

Governed changes start with roles and grants: they control who may do what, while approval policies govern publication. Access can differ between workspaces, and a grant can narrow writes to particular applications or record types. Jobs and other systems face permission checks too. See [What refiroo is](/docs/about/what-is-refiroo/) for the overview.

## Roles describe work

refiroo includes nine general predefined roles. People can hold several, and an administrator can create custom roles from groups of actions.

| Role | Main responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Reader | Browse data without changing it. |
| Contributor | Prepare changes in change sets, without editing Live or publishing. |
| Data steward | Maintain Live data, prepare and publish change sets, and run bulk work. |
| Data owner | Stewardship plus publication approval, following changes, and copying or moving data. |
| Model administrator | Author, install and select model releases. |
| Workspace administrator | Manage workspaces and their default. |
| Integration administrator | Manage webhook subscriptions and follow changes. |
| Operator | Monitor the service and inspect deployment settings. |
| Security administrator | Manage people, groups, clients, roles and grants. |

The role's scope still matters. Model, workspace, integration, operations and security administration do not automatically include permission to browse or edit reference data. See [Roles and grants](/docs/administer/roles-and-grants/) for the full rules.

## Grants say where a role applies

A **grant** gives a role to a person, group or client, either across the instance or in one workspace where the role supports it. Group members inherit the group's grants. Several grants combine their permissions.

A workspace grant can narrow writes to selected applications or record types. This limits what the holder may change; it does not hide other types they may browse. A grant naming a type removed from the model grants nothing for that missing type.

The interface offers the actions the person can complete in the current workspace. A Reader has no editing controls. A Contributor can propose a change in a change set. **Settings → Account** shows **What you can do**, with roles and permissions by workspace. If an expected action is missing, check the workspace and this account summary, then ask a security administrator. Permission changes apply on the next request, so an action already open can still be refused.

## Approvals govern publication

A workspace can require publication approval and a different person to decide it. A submitted change set is frozen for review; an authorised person must withdraw the request before it is edited. Approval publishes the submitted content, while sending it back requires a comment.

Holding Publish alone does not bypass a required approval. The exact policy also determines whether someone holding both Publish and Approve may publish directly. See [Approval policies](/docs/administer/approval-policies/) and [Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/).

## People and systems sign in differently

People can use a local account or the organisation's configured OpenID Connect sign-in provider. Local accounts support an authenticator app, recovery codes and WebAuthn passkeys. Administrators can require a second factor. Provider-only accounts use the provider's security and cannot add local second factors or passkeys.

People can review and end their browser sessions on Account. A system uses its own **client**, with its own credentials and grants. Reading a consumer API requires a separate grant for that API in a workspace; no general role opens it, and these grants belong to clients, not people or groups.

See [Sign-in](/docs/administer/sign-in/), [Your account](/docs/use/account/) and [Clients](/docs/administer/clients/).

## Keep access current

[People and groups](/docs/administer/people-and-groups/) manages account details, memberships
and deactivation when someone leaves. [Roles and grants](/docs/administer/roles-and-grants/)
lets an administrator create a custom role where predefined responsibilities do not fit;
changing it affects everyone holding it. The [permissions reference](/docs/administer/permissions-reference/)
lists the actions each group permits. Removing one grant may leave access from another grant
or group. An unused custom role can be deleted only after its grants have been removed.

[Sign-in](/docs/administer/sign-in/) covers provider links, required second factors and recovery
after a lost device. An administrator can turn ordinary local password sign-in off after a
provider has successfully signed someone in, while preserving a tested local recovery route.
refiroo prevents removing the last active security administrator and protects the last retained
local sign-in route while ordinary local sign-in is off.

[Signing keys](/docs/administer/signing-keys/) separates routine replacement from emergency
retirement. [Agent access](/docs/administer/agent-access/) controls connections for external
assistants, and [AI administration](/docs/administer/ai/) shows built-in availability, send
policy and call records. [Mail](/docs/administer/mail/) provides outgoing delivery and its
failure queue; personal notification choices do not change permissions.

[Webhooks](/docs/administer/webhooks/) manages receivers, signing keys and delivery recovery.
[Approval policies](/docs/administer/approval-policies/) changes publication review for a
workspace. [Jobs and limits](/docs/administer/jobs-and-limits/) explains who can inspect or
cancel work. [About, Deployment and Operations](/docs/administer/deployment-pages/) identifies
the running service and its configuration, while [API and consumer documentation pages](/docs/administer/api-reference-and-consumer-api-pages/)
helps an administrator find contracts without granting access to their data.
guide/src/content/docs/about/data-qualit:
---
title: How refiroo protects data
description: Model rules, conflict protection and reviewed changes keep shared data dependable.
reader: evaluator
---

One set of rules applies on every path into refiroo. Browser edits, API calls and bulk loads meet the same model validation and permission checks. See [What refiroo is](/docs/about/what-is-refiroo/) for how these checks support shared reference data.

## Values keep their types and rules

A number stays a number, a date stays a date and a yes/no field stays distinct from text. The model can require a field, give it a default, make it read-only, limit a number's range or require at least one of several fields.

A unique field value cannot be assigned to another record in the same workspace. A separate relationship rule can allow only one counting related record beneath each ancestor of a chosen type; this is how a model can limit one active representation per owner and group. A required field cannot be emptied. A declared validity period must end after it starts. Correct the reported value, or ask a model administrator if the rule itself needs to change. See [Records](/docs/use/records/) and [Types, attributes and relations](/docs/model/types-attributes-relations/).

## Connections are checked too

The model decides which record types can connect, whether a connection is required and how many are allowed. A parent must be a permitted parent in the same application and workspace. A record cannot become its own ancestor.

The parent link is maintained with the record's position. Move the record to change its parent; ordinary relationship controls cannot alter that link. See [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/) and [Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/).

## A save cannot silently overwrite newer work

Changes carry the version the editor read. If someone else saved a newer version, refiroo refuses the stale save and keeps the attempted input available for review. Read the current information and decide how to apply the intended correction.

A change set also checks for competing live changes when published. Unrelated live edits survive, but a conflicting change publishes nothing. Validation before publication is useful; it does not reserve values or guarantee that Live stays unchanged afterwards. See [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/).

## Review changes with wider effects

Deleting a record first shows the impact: children, records it owns and relationships it would remove. Independent related records are disconnected rather than deleted. Review this preview before confirming.

Bulk changes and file loads offer previews showing what can be applied and what is refused. Their result depends on the chosen operation: publishing a change set is all-or-nothing, while a bulk job may apply independent items and refuse others. Cancellation cannot undo chunks an independent job already saved. Review the result rather than assuming every row succeeded. See [Changing many records](/docs/use/changing-many-records/) and [Imports and exports](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/).

## History makes changes accountable

Record history names who changed what and when, including the person or client behind a background job. Publication changes name their publication. Older entries without attribution say **Before sign-in**; some operations did not record the previous value. History is evidence of changes, not a substitute for a complete backup. See [History](/docs/use/history/) and [Security, audit and privacy](/docs/about/security-and-trust/).

## A limit is not an incomplete answer

Long collections are read in pages so people can continue through the complete matching list.
A page size does not limit the whole dataset. Bulk selections and file loads have separate
operation limits; exceeding one calls for a smaller operation, not an assumption that omitted
records succeeded. See [Lists, search and filters](/docs/use/lists-and-filters/) and
[Jobs and limits](/docs/administer/jobs-and-limits/).

Validation checks the rules the model declares. It cannot decide whether a real-world name or
code is correct, or whether a workbook's matching column identifies the right record. Review
proposed matches, omissions and losses before confirming a load or transfer. See
[Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/) and [Copying and moving](/docs/use/copying-and-moving/).
guide/src/content/docs/about/sharing-dat:
---
title: Sharing data with other systems
description: Read, load and follow shared reference data through governed interfaces.
reader: evaluator
---

refiroo is API first: everything the browser does is available through the API. Consumer APIs give other systems a common way to read agreed data, with a consistent shape within each contract. Systems can also load corrections and follow changes under the same model rules and permissions as browser work. See [What refiroo is](/docs/about/what-is-refiroo/) for the overview.

## Maintain data or consume it

The **management API** exposes the capabilities used by the browser: records, fields, relationships, models, workspaces, change sets, publications and history. Integrations can maintain reference data through it without automating screens.

A **consumer API** provides a read contract declared in the model. It presents the fields and related records a consuming system needs under agreed public names. Systems can read lists, look up values by their identifiers and resolve a code to another representation where the model declares that operation. A separate contract version protects consumers when the model evolves.

Consumer APIs share a consistent way to present data and read it. Within a contract, every kind of record comes in the same form, with its selected fields and related information together. A consuming system can reuse the way it reads lists, looks up a value, handles an error and follows changes across the consumer APIs your organisation declares. A new kind of record does not need its own reading process.

The model chooses what is shared; refiroo supplies the common patterns. Public names and available operations can differ between contracts, so the consuming system still needs to know the contract it reads. Its own contract version lets that agreement stay stable while the underlying model changes.

A client needs a grant for the particular consumer API in the particular workspace. A management role alone does not give consumer access, and a consumer grant does not permit management operations. See [Consumer APIs](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/) and [Who can do what](/docs/about/people-and-access/).

## Choose the state to read

Normal reads return Live data. A publication provides a fixed snapshot for an extract that must remain consistent while live editing continues. A publication read uses a compatible consumer contract; it cannot automatically be reinterpreted through any later contract.

Where a record type declares a validity period, an integration can ask which records are valid on a business date. This is a question about the data's declared dates, separate from asking what was stored in the past. See [Business dates](/docs/integrate/business-dates/) and [Reading records](/docs/integrate/reading-records/).

## Exchange files and larger loads

Scattered spreadsheets can become an agreed list: upload an existing workbook, map its columns through an import profile and check a preview before loading; a workbook can also start a model draft and load into a change set. See [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/) for that starting point.

Files let people review data in a workbook and bring changes back. Integration loads can create, update, connect and remove records in bulk, either together or with a result for each independent item. Background jobs report progress and refusals. A preview helps check the intended effect before applying it; an import is still subject to type, uniqueness, relationship and access rules.

See [Imports and exports](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/) for browser work and [Files, imports and exports](/docs/integrate/files-imports-and-exports/) for integration choices.

## Keep another system in step

The change feed records live changes in order. A system remembers where it stopped and continues from there. Prepared changes appear when published, rather than while someone is working on them. If the saved position has expired, the system must load a suitable publication and resume from its position.

Webhooks push model-declared events to a receiver. Deliveries are signed, retried on failure and may arrive more than once. Receivers must recognise repeated events and verify signatures. These events do not include the author's identity; management history does. See [Following changes](/docs/integrate/following-changes/) and [Consumer events and webhooks](/docs/integrate/consumer-events-and-webhooks/).

Start implementation in [Integrating with refiroo](/docs/integrate/overview/). The [API reference](/docs/api) describes the available operations and their exact contracts.

## Prepare a reliable connection

[Discovering the model](/docs/integrate/discovering-the-model/) lets an integration learn the
selected workspace's types, relationships and allowed placements. [System sign-in](/docs/integrate/signing-in-and-tokens/)
explains the system's identity, while [the security model for integrations](/docs/integrate/security-model-for-integrators/)
explains management roles, consumer grants and access that changes during a job.

[Reading records](/docs/integrate/reading-records/) covers precise queries over fields,
ancestors and related records. [Reading business objects](/docs/integrate/reading-business-objects/)
combines the data a consumer contract exposes; [looking up and resolving](/docs/integrate/looking-up-and-resolving/)
finds an object from a supplied value or translates it to another representation without hiding
missing or ambiguous results.

[Identifiers, paging and errors](/docs/integrate/identifiers-paging-and-errors/) explains complete
reads and continuation. [Versions and conflicts](/docs/integrate/versions-and-conflicts/) protects
record and model changes from competing edits. [Writing in bulk](/docs/integrate/writing-in-bulk/)
and [Jobs](/docs/integrate/jobs/) cover controlled batches, safe retries and item outcomes;
[changes, approvals and publication](/docs/integrate/changes-approvals-and-publication/) gives
automated proposals the same review path as browser work.

[Workspace contexts](/docs/integrate/workspaces-contexts-and-models/) keeps the chosen dataset
explicit, and [model and release operations](/docs/integrate/model-and-release-operations/)
supports automated model administration and reviewed transfers. [Compatibility](/docs/integrate/compatibility/)
explains which contract changes callers must tolerate.

## Connect an assistant

[Assistants and agents](/docs/integrate/assistants-and-agents/) lets an external assistant read
permitted data and prepare change sets through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), with a person
responsible for approval and publication. [Assistant tasks](/docs/integrate/assistant-tasks/)
lets an integration submit work to the separately enabled built-in assistant and follow its
proposal. Both require review; their data-sharing boundaries differ. See
[AI help stays under your control](/docs/about/security-and-trust/#ai-help-stays-under-your-control).
guide/src/content/docs/about/what-is-ref:
---
title: What refiroo is
description: One engine for shared reference data, shaped to your organisation and available to its systems.
reader: evaluator
---

refiroo is an engine for reference data: the fairly stable lists other systems depend on, such as codes, categories, names and the connections between them. A team defines its own reference-data applications with a **model**, without building separate software for each. refiroo supplies the screens, the API, validation, history, search, access control, approvals and publication.

## Bring scattered lists together

Reference data can be scattered across thousands of small spreadsheets, each team and system keeping its own copy, columns and version of the truth. People spend time reconciling those lists before they can use them together.

refiroo brings that work into one place. You can upload an existing workbook without first rebuilding its layout: an import profile says how its sheets and columns become records, fields and connections. A workbook can even be the starting point for a model. A model administrator reviews the proposed structure and mapping, checks issues and runs a dry run to see which rows can load and which need attention. Loading into a change set keeps the proposed data separate until it is reviewed and published. See [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/).

The agreed list then has a history, people responsible for it and connections to other lists. People edit it in the browser, export a workbook for colleagues and load their changes back; other systems read it through the API. Saved import profiles can read later versions of the original workbook. File loads meet the same rules as other changes. See [Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/).

## Give different codes a shared meaning

Consider the guide's example world: public transport stops in Graubünden, Switzerland. The same stop has a stop number, a SLOID identifier and a code in a ticketing system. Names are maintained in five languages. Without a shared place to connect them, each system keeps its own list, and people reconcile codes and names by hand.

With refiroo, a steward keeps the agreed meaning once, connects each system's code to it and supplies the names. Other systems read that agreed data. A code can change in one system without losing the connection to the stop it represents.

The guide uses public stop data and names, with a fictional ticketing system to show mappings. Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02; Wikidata, CC0. These are examples of records and relationships a model defines.

## What makes it different

**One engine, many applications.** A model defines record types, fields, relationships and views. A new reference-data domain can use another model. Every application has the same capabilities; its model chooses the views it offers. The shipped applications are optional examples you can replace or remove. See [How refiroo works](/docs/about/how-it-works/).

**Connections that keep their meaning.** A place in a hierarchy, an equivalent code in another system and a translation are different connections, each with its own rules. The model defines which records may connect and how. See [Connections carry meaning](/docs/about/how-it-works/#connections-carry-meaning).

**Three kinds of change.** A live edit corrects today's data when saved. A change set prepares related changes separately, with approval where required, then publishes them together as one consistent publication. A model release changes the structure and rules. Daily work continues while changes are prepared. See [Three kinds of change](/docs/about/three-kinds-of-change/).

**One set of rules on every path.** Browser edits, API calls and bulk loads meet the same validation and permission checks. Values keep their types, connections follow their rules and a stale save cannot silently overwrite newer work. See [How refiroo protects data](/docs/about/data-quality-rules/).

**API first.** Everything the browser does is available through the API. Model-defined consumer APIs give other systems a common way to read agreed data, with a consistent shape within each contract. See [Sharing data with other systems](/docs/about/sharing-data-with-other-systems/).

**Governed changes.** Roles and narrowed grants control who may change which data. Approval policies govern publication, and history records who changed what and when; review comments can explain why. See [Who can do what](/docs/about/people-and-access/) and [Security, audit and privacy](/docs/about/security-and-trust/).

**Workspaces with their own models.** An organisation can keep several working areas in one installation. Each workspace uses its own selected model release, so workspaces can share a model or use different ones. See [How refiroo works](/docs/about/how-it-works/).

## Who it helps

| Responsibility | What refiroo helps you do |
| --- | --- |
| Data steward | Correct shared values and organise lists. |
| Mapping or localisation steward | Connect equivalent codes and maintain names in different languages. |
| Integration team | Load, read and synchronise agreed data. |
| Workspace administrator | Provide working areas and keep old ones readable. |
| Model administrator | Change the structure and rules of the data. |
| Operator | Run, monitor, upgrade and recover the service. |

These are responsibilities. [Roles and grants](/docs/about/people-and-access/) decide what each person may actually do.

## Where it fits

refiroo serves reference data: relatively stable information used to describe, classify or connect other data. It is not intended to store transactions such as purchases or journeys, or to replace the systems that process them. Its approval controls govern reference-data publication; it is not a general workflow engine.


It is not a general data catalogue, business glossary, lineage scanner or enterprise governance
suite. A small product catalogue or a lightweight master-data use can fit when its needs can
be expressed through the same records, fields, relationships and views. These are uses you
model; they do not add fixed domain modules to refiroo.

## What you can do

Start with [Home](/docs/use/home/) to find workspaces, recent visits and work waiting for you.
Within the chosen workspace, these capabilities work with the types its model defines:

| Work | Where to read on |
| --- | --- |
| Find records | [Lists, search and filters](/docs/use/lists-and-filters/) combines search, typed conditions, sorting, related columns and navigation through long lists. |
| Maintain records | [Records](/docs/use/records/) covers names, typed fields, availability, validity dates and reviewed deletion. |
| Connect records | [Relationships](/docs/use/relationships/) describes associations, ownership and allowed candidates, including connections across applications. |
| Arrange parents and children | [Hierarchies](/docs/use/hierarchies/) supports browsing, moves and reviewed changes of type or level. |
| Connect equivalent values | [Mapping grids](/docs/use/mapping-grids/) shows missing connections and lets you review or replace targets. |
| Find gaps across groups | [Relation matrices](/docs/use/relation-matrices/) shows missing, filled, inactive and conflicting cells, with actions to fill them. |
| Change a collection | [Changing many records](/docs/use/changing-many-records/) previews changes to values, relationships or selected records before a job applies them. |
| Exchange workbooks | [Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/) supports repeatable profiles and workbooks people can edit and import back. |
| Transfer data | [Copying and moving](/docs/use/copying-and-moving/) prepares reviewed changes in another workspace using a mapping between models. |
| Follow background work | [Jobs](/docs/use/jobs/) shows progress, item results and cancellation, including work that only partly succeeded. |
| Coordinate and review | [Change sets](/docs/use/change-sets/) keeps proposals separate, [Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/) routes decisions, and [Publications](/docs/use/publications/) preserves results. |
| Understand a change | [History](/docs/use/history/) records changes to one record or across a workspace, including their authors and causes. |
| Hear about work | [Notification settings](/docs/use/notifications-settings/) offers immediate email, digests and following another person's publications in a workspace. |
| Ask for help | [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) explains optional list questions, proposed mapping targets, explanations and an assistant that prepares records or models for review. |

A capability can be disabled by the operator, an action can need permission, and a view can be
absent from a model. These are separate reasons an option might not appear. Begin with
[User journeys](/docs/journeys/) for the complete path through a task, or
[Applications](/docs/use/applications/) for the screens a model can offer.
guide/src/content/docs/about/compatibili:
---
title: Versions, compatibility and licence
description: Understand the compatibility commitment, model language window and source offer.
reader: evaluator
---

The software version, a model release and a publication number describe different things. **Settings → About** shows the running engine version, management API version, supported schema languages, licence, source address and active model release. A workspace's own model release determines the definition its data uses. About is available to
signed-in people; the additional Deployment and Operations pages need Operations permission. See
[About, Deployment and Operations](/docs/administer/deployment-pages/) for reading these details.

## What stays compatible

From 0.12.0, refiroo commits to additive evolution of its documented management API, consumer API contract versions, change events and webhook formats, sign-in contracts, deployment setting names and documented commands.

An addition preserves existing behaviour: for example, a new optional choice or an extra field in an answer. Integrations must tolerate additions they do not recognise. Removing a choice, changing a field's meaning or type, making an optional input required or refusing a previously accepted request is a breaking change.

For contracts published by refiroo, a breaking replacement must be offered alongside the old contract. The old version stays available for **at least twelve months and two minor releases after the deprecation announcement**. This protects existing callers while their owners arrange an update.

Your organisation’s consumer APIs are defined by its model administrator, who chooses the
notice period with the consuming teams. Earlier contract versions can remain available
beside the new one, reading current data in their original shape. An announced sunset day
does not stop service automatically: the administrator explicitly stops the version through
a model release. See [Consumer APIs in the model](/docs/model/consumer-apis/#keep-an-earlier-version-available).

The commitment does not freeze screen layouts and addresses, internal code or database tables. Integrations use the public contracts rather than the database. See [Compatibility for integrators](/docs/integrate/compatibility/) for caller responsibilities and [Upgrades](/docs/run/upgrades/) for operational planning.

## Model languages have a separate window

A model release versions the definition your team installed. Its **schema language** describes the format refiroo understands. Neither is a publication number or a record's editing version.

Before 1.0, each software release reads the schema language it writes; unused older languages can leave the supported window without the contract notice period. Stored models have a raising procedure, while an unsupported workspace may need administrator or operator recovery before it can be opened. Do not assume an old model remains usable merely because an API contract stays compatible.

From 1.0, a language version leaves the window only in a major release, with the notice period and an offline upgrader for stored releases and publications. See [Model language versions](/docs/model/model-language-versions/) for the currently supported window and recovery choices.

Before 1.0, only the latest minor software release receives security fixes. See the project's [security policy](https://github.com/refiroo/refiroo/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

## Licence and corresponding source

refiroo is offered under the **GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 or later**, shown as **AGPL-3.0-or-later**. The [licence text](https://github.com/refiroo/refiroo/blob/main/LICENSE) contains its terms, including the corresponding-source offer for people interacting with a modified version over a network in section 13.

The account menu offers **Source code**, and **Settings → About** shows the source address and licence. The default source address points to the running software's release tag. For a modified installation, its operator must point that offer to the corresponding modified source. Changing the address does not itself publish that source. Operator instructions are in [Licence and source](/docs/run/licence-and-source/).

Source availability and permission to use the refiroo name and artwork are separate: see the [trademark policy](https://github.com/refiroo/refiroo/blob/main/TRADEMARKS.md). Separate [commercial terms](https://github.com/refiroo/refiroo/blob/main/COMMERCIAL.md) are also offered.

## Taking part

Bug reports, questions and discussion are welcome. Outside code contributions are not currently merged while the contributor agreement is absent. Check the [contribution policy](https://github.com/refiroo/refiroo/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) before preparing code, and report security vulnerabilities privately through the security policy.
